                                 iv
                                             INTRODUCTION

        I, the Chairperson of the Joint Committee to which the Bill titled "The
Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026" was referred, having been
authorized by the Committee to submit the Report on their behalf, present this
Report along with the Bill as reported by the Joint Committee annexed thereto.

2. The Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 was introduced in Lok
Sabha on 23.03.2026. The Motion for reference of the Bill to a Joint
Committee of the House was moved in Lok Sabha on 23.03.2026 by the
Minister of Finance and Corporate Affairs (Appendix-I) and concurred by the
Rajya Sabha on 24.03.2026 (Appendix II).

3. As per the motion moved in the House, the Joint Committee was to
make a Report by the last day of the first week of the Monsoon Session, 2026.
The Committee were granted an extension of time once for presentation of the
Report. The extension for presenting the report by the last day of the Monsoon
Session of Parliament, 2026 was granted by the House as per the Motion
moved and adopted on 22.07.2026 (Appendix III).

4. According to its Statement of Objects and Reasons, the primary aim of
the bill is to simplify corporate legal procedures, ease compliance burdens,
and strengthen corporate governance in line with the Report of the Company
Law Committee (CLC) as well as the amendments carried out in 2015, 2017,
2019 and 2020 in the Companies Act, 2013. The amendments proposed in the
present Bill are focused on decriminalisation of various procedural defaults
under the Companies Act and the LLP Act by replacing criminal provisions
with civil penalties. Provisions of the Bill aim to provide relaxations related to
CSR provisions and strengthen the role of the National Financial Reporting
Authority to enhance corporate governance and protect investor interests. The
Bill also introduces a new mechanism allowing certain types of Trusts to
convert into LLPs to promote flexibility in fund structuring and improving ease
of doing business. Accordingly, the proposed legislation seeks to rationalize, in
the interest of promoting industry, existing statutory mechanisms within the
Companies Act, 2013 and the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008, while
introducing progressive, novel frameworks aligned with global best practices.

5. Keeping in view the importance of the Bill and its wide-ranging
implications, the Committee decided to invite memoranda to obtain the views
from experts/industry associations/organizations/stakeholders on the
provisions of the aforesaid Bill. With a view to give the widest publicity in
receiving stakeholders' suggestions, the Joint Committee had publicized its
advertisement through various modes. Firstly, a press release inviting

                                                        v
memoranda was issued on electronic media on 09.06.2026 through the Press
and Public Relations Wing, Lok Sabha Secretariat. The communiqué was also
sent to Sansad TV for display for a fortnight. Further, it was uploaded under
the `Press Release' tab on the Joint Committee homepage. Subsequently, for
a wider outreach, suggestions were also sought through email from major
Indian financial institutions, prominent law firms, professional accountancy
bodies, consulting and auditing giants, large corporate entities and key
regulatory/industry associations.

6. The Committee also engaged in substantive, in-depth deliberations with
officials from the Ministry of Corporate Affairs alongside eminent legal experts
and corporate law practitioners. This consultative process spanned key
government ministries and regulators, including Ministry of Corporate Affairs,
Ministry of Finance's Departments of Revenue, Economic Affairs, and
Financial Services, RBI, NITI Aayog, Ministry of Electronics and Information
Technology (MeitY), Ministry of Commerce and Industry (including DGFT,
DPIIT, and Invest India), the Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises,
and the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India.

7. To gather direct, ground-level insights, the Committee undertook a
targeted study visit to Mumbai on 02.07.2026 and 03.07.2026, where they
interacted with regional industry associations, regulatory bodies, capital
market infrastructure institutions, angel investors, startups, trusts, small
companies, alternative investment firms, corporate advisory consultancies,
and individual stakeholders. Additionally, the Committee consulted with key
banking institutions, including the State Bank of India, Bank of Baroda, and
Union Bank of India, to understand the financial sector's perspective on these
amendments.

8. The Committee received 130 memoranda in total through both physical
and digital modes, containing suggestions on the Bill from various
stakeholders, including 06 Members of the Parliament. The suggestions
received therein and during oral evidence were circulated to the Members of
the Committee. The same were also sent to the nodal Ministry i.e. Ministry of
Corporate Affairs and its comments were obtained. Important points
raised/suggestions made by the experts/stakeholders and the replies thereon
from the nodal Ministry were examined, discussed, considered and suitably
incorporated in the Report. All such suggestions, which were within the scope
of mandate of the Committee, were discussed and analysed in detail while
finalizing Recommendations of the Committee. There were many suggestions,
which were beyond the scope of the mandate of the Committee. All such
suggestions may later be evaluated and considered on merits in appropriate
forums.

                                                       vi
9. The Committee held 24 Sittings wherein they heard the
views/suggestions of the representatives from various experts/stakeholders
(83 in number) and Ministry of Corporate Affairs. The Committee completed
the clause-by-clause consideration of the Bill at their Sittings held on
16.07.2026 and 17.07.2026. Internal deliberations were held on 17.07.2026
and 23.07.2026 wherein in-depth discussion was held on pending concerns
and issues raised by the Committee members.

10. The Committee, in their 25th Sitting held on 31.07.2026, considered and
adopted the draft Report. The Bill, as reported by the Joint Committee, is
appended after the Report at Annexure. The Committee further authorized the
Chairperson to present the Report on their behalf. The Committee also
decided that one copy of the proceedings of the sittings of the Committee and
two copies each of the memoranda received by the Committee on the Bill from
various quarters may be placed in the Parliament Library after the Report has
been presented to Parliament, for reference of the Members of Parliament.

11. Two Notes/Minutes of dissent, received from 02 out of the 31 Members
of the Joint Committee, are attached at Appendix-IV.

12. During their examination of the Bill, the Committee heard a vast array of
conflicting viewpoints. Harmonizing these conflicting positions into a
framework acceptable to the majority, if not all, was a highly challenging
endeavour. This achievement was made possible only by the active
cooperation, steady support, and tireless efforts of everyone involved, with the
Members of the Joint Committee deserving special commendation for their
exceptional work. I extend my sincere thanks to all the Members of the Joint
Committee.

13. The Committee take this opportunity to express their deep appreciation
to the officials of the Ministry of Corporate Affairs for providing their valuable
inputs during the deliberations of the Joint Committee in connection with the
examination of the Bill. The Committee would like to place on record their
appreciation for the Ministry's collaborative and reform-oriented approach and
its readiness to work in close association with the Committee to refine the Bill.
Additionally, the Committee appreciate the Ministry for accepting many of the
suggestions voiced by multiple stakeholders concerning various provisions
including conversion of Trusts to LLPs, amendments to provisions of CSR,
changes in structure and powers of NFRA etc.

                                          REPORT

                                       CHAPTER - I

                                    INTRODUCTORY

         Corporate law in India governs the formation, operation, and dissolution of
companies, with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) providing the regulatory
framework to ensure corporates contribute effectively to national development.

1.2. The Companies Act, 2013 notified on 29th August, 2013, introduced major
reforms in disclosures to the stakeholders, accountability of the directors, auditors,
key managerial personnel, investor protection, corporate governance and an in-
house adjudication mechanism to adjudicate civil wrongs without involving criminal
courts.

1.3. Subsequent amendments in 2015, 2017, 2019, and 2020, based upon
recommendations of the Company Law Committee and suggestions received from
various stakeholders, further strengthened corporate governance, providing an
enabling framework for greater ease of doing business (EODB) to law abiding
corporates while decriminalising certain offences as EODB measures and de-
clogging the Special Courts and National Company Law Tribunal ("NCLT).

1.4 Parallelly, the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008 ("LLP Act") was notified
on 7th January, 2009 to facilitate doing business in the form of a new kind of entity
which has flexibility of a partnership firm but is constituted in the form of body
corporate structure with limited liability and perpetual succession. This Act was
amended in the year 2021 to facilitate ease of doing business and to decriminalise
certain offences.

1.5. In the current national and international context, there is a requirement for
simplifying corporate laws so that they are amenable to clear interpretation and
provide a framework that would facilitate faster economic growth. It is also
increasingly being recognized that the framework for regulation of corporate entities
has to be in tune with the emerging economic scenario, encourage good corporate
governance and enable protection of the interests of the investors and other
stakeholders. In the competitive and technology driven business environment, while
corporates require greater autonomy of operation and opportunity for self-regulation
with optimum compliance costs, there is a need to bring about transparency through

                                                        1
better disclosures and greater responsibility on the part of corporate owners and
managements for improved compliance.

Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026

1.6. The roots of the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 can be traced back
to the Company Law Committee constituted by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs
("MCA") in September 2019 under the chairmanship of Secretary, MCA to make
recommendations that are geared towards promoting greater ease of doing business
for law-abiding corporates and further improving the operational efficiency of
Companies Act 2013 and Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008 ("LLP Act, 2008").
The Committee submitted its last report in March 2022. The proposed Companies
(Amendment) Bill, 2026 represents a pivotal progression in India's corporate law
trajectory, designed to align the statutory regulatory regime with global governance.

1.7. As per the Bill, the proposed amendments are broadly aimed at--

        (i) promoting further ease of doing business and ease of living for
                corporates by decriminalising more provisions and amending certain
                other provisions;

        (ii) providing ease of compliance for One Person Companies, small
                companies, start-up companies and producer companies;

        (iii) streamlining existing regulatory practices to strengthen and improve the
                operational efficiency of the said enactments;

        (iv) recognising new concepts in light of rapidly evolving corporate landscape
                and changing business practices; and

        (v) carrying out drafting and clarificatory changes to remove ambiguities

1.8. Following earlier waves of de-criminalization under the 2020 reforms, the
2026 legislative intervention shifts focus toward reducing compliance burdens for
early-stage and medium enterprises, while elevating transparency and internal
controls for systemic financial stability. The Bill seeks decriminalisation of various
procedural defaults under the Companies Act and the LLP Act by replacing criminal
provisions with civil penalties. By decriminalising various minor default, the

                                                        2
enforcement philosophy shifts lesserrisk, procedural defaults to inhouse
adjudication with monetary penalties, reserving criminal sanctions for serious,
fraudlike or publicinterestheavy violations.

1.9. The Bill also seeks to bring wide-ranging changes to the CSR regime by
providing further relaxations for small companies by providing exemption from
mandatory Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR), requirements related to auditor
appointment for prescribed class of small companies, reduction in additional fees,
etc. (Objects and Reasons).

1.10. The Bill introduces a statutory framework to enable specified trusts, registered
by SEBI or IFSCA having prescribed activities to convert into LLPs. It facilitates the
adoption of the LLP structure by investment vehicles with provisions on eligibility and
the conversion process, thereby promoting flexibility in fund structuring and
improving ease of doing business. It also facilitates companies and limited liability
partnerships operating in International Financial Services Centres by allowing them
to issue and maintain share capital in foreign currency as permitted by the
International Financial Services Centres Authority.

1.11. The 2026 Bill embeds a digital-first governance framework by enabling hybrid
and fully virtual shareholder communications, electronic voting, and automated
filings. By permitting AGMs and EGMs through video conferencing while requiring at
least one AGM in physical mode, the legislature seeks to balance technological
efficiency with accountability and shareholder participation, ensuring modernized
governance without diluting transparency.

1.12. Aligned with the Ease of Doing Business objective, the Bill recalibrates
penalty structures by clearly differentiating technical, non-fraudulent lapses from
willful governance violations. Routine operational delays are channeled into civil
adjudication mechanisms rather than protracted court proceedings, ensuring
proportionate enforcement while alleviating the burden on judicial forums. This
measured framework delivers compliance certainty while upholding fairness and
efficiency in corporate regulation.

Methodology adopted by the Joint Committee of Lok Sabha on the Corporate
Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026.

1.13. Given the profound impact of Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 on the
multiple stakeholders and introduction of new measures viz. decriminalization of

                                                        3
offences, change in threshold w.r.t CSR, conversion of Trusts into LLPs etc., the
Committee in their first Sitting decided to invite views and suggestions from
experts/industry associations/organisations and stakeholders on the provisions of the
Bills. A Press Communiqué was issued through the Media and Public Relations
(MPR) Wing, Lok Sabha Secretariat on 09.06.2026 which was also disseminated
through the media and Social Media Platforms of Lok Sabha viz. LSS Facebook
page and LSS "X" handle giving a period of two weeks for stakeholders to submit
their suggestions. The Communique was also disseminated through a scrolling ticker
display on Sansad TV for a fortnight and uploaded on the Lok Sabha website. The
same was covered in several prominent newspapers. Subsequently, for a wider
outreach, suggestions were also sought through email from major Indian financial
institutions, prominent law firms, professional accountancy bodies, consulting and
auditing firms, large corporate entities and key regulatory/industry associations all of
whom are significant stakeholders or participants in India's legal, corporate, and
insolvency frameworks.

1.14. In response thereto, the Committee received 130 memoranda, containing
more than 900 suggestions on the Bill from various stakeholders, including 06
Members of the Parliament, which were tabulated and forwarded to the Ministry of
Corporate Affairs to obtain their views. A comprehensive list of Stakeholders/
Organisations/Associations/Individuals from whom Memoranda/ suggestions were
received, examined and considered by the Committee is given at Appendix - III.

1.15. The Committee held in-depth deliberations with officials from the Ministry of
Corporate Affairs. This consultative process spanned key government ministries and
regulators, including Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Ministry of Finance's Departments
of Revenue, Economic Affairs, and Financial Services, RBI, NITI Aayog, Ministry of
Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Ministry of Commerce and Industry
(including DGFT, DPIIT, and Invest India), the Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium
Enterprises, and the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India. The Committee also
drew up an exhaustive list of representatives, stakeholders, and institutions for
discussion which included the Valuers, NFRA, ICAI, National and Mid-level Industry
Associations, Public and Private Sector Banks, professional bodies, consulting firms,
Adjudicating Authorities, asset and finance companies, regulatory and quasi-judicial
bodies, and legal policy groups. During the discussions, submissions and
PowerPoint Presentations (PPTs) in a prescribed format were presented before the
Joint Committee. Thereafter, post-evidence replies on the queries posed by the
Members of the Joint Committee were also furnished which were circulated to the
Members of the Joint Committee. The Joint Committee also sought written replies on
specific issues from concerned Ministries/Departments for more clarity on the issues
raised by the domain experts/stakeholders during their deposition.

                                                        4
1.16. To gather direct, ground-level insights, the Committee undertook a targeted
study visit to Mumbai on 2nd and 3rd July, 2026, where they interacted with regional
industry associations, regulatory bodies, capital market infrastructure institutions,
angel investors, startups, trusts, small companies, alternative investment firms,
corporate advisory consultancies, and individual stakeholders. Additionally, key
banking institutions, including the State Bank of India, Bank of Baroda, and Union
Bank of India, were also consulted to understand the financial sector's perspective
on the proposed amendments. The Committee, thus, held extensive oral
evidence/discussions with various government bodies, financial institutions, industry
experts, chambers of commerce, and legal authorities, culminating in the drafting of
the Report.

1.18. In the process of examination of the Bill, the Committee obtained Background
Notes, Written Replies, Post-Evidence Replies, Information, Clarification, Detailed
Notes and other requisite documents from the Ministry of Corporate Affairs. The
Committee took the Oral Evidences of the representatives of Ministry of Corporate
Affairs on the Suggestions/Memoranda received from various Stakeholders on the
provisions of the Bill during four sittings of the Joint Committee held on 16.07.2026
and 17.07.2026. The representatives from Ministry of Law and Justice (Legislative
Department and Department of Legal Affairs) were also present throughout all
Sittings of the Committee to provide their legal and constitutional expertise. Detailed
internal deliberations of the Joint Committee was also held on 23.07.2026 to discuss
clause by clause the provisions of the Bill. The Committee considered and adopted
the draft Report and the amended Bill during the 25th Sitting held on 31.07.2026.

                                                        7
1.19. Thus, based on the written and oral depositions of both official and non-official
Witnesses and the Memoranda received from various Stakeholders and also from
the Members of the Joint Committee, the Committee have examined the Bill
exhaustively and given their considered views as enumerated in the succeeding
Chapter-II which deal with the Clause-by-Clause examination of the amendments
proposed in the Bill.
1.20. During the course of extensive hearings, a large number of suggestions were
received by the Committee. All such suggestions, which were within the mandate of

recommendations of the Committee. There were many suggestions, which were
beyond the mandate of the Committee. All such suggestions may later be evaluated
and considered on merits in appropriate forums.
1.21. The Bill as reported by the Joint Committee is placed at Annexure to the
Report.

                                                        8
                                       CHAPTER - II

 CLAUSE BY CLAUSE EXAMINATION OF THE CORPORATE LAWS
                             (AMENDMENT) BILL, 2026

                                                CLAUSE - 1

1. Clause 1 of the Bill seeks to provide for short title and commencement
of the proposed legislation.

1.1 Provisions proposed in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

(1) This Act may be called the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Act, 2026.

(2) It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by
notification in the Official Gazette, appoint; and different dates may be appointed for
different provisions of this Act, and any reference in any provision to the
commencement of this Act shall be construed as a reference to the coming into force
of that provision.

1.2 Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

1.2.1 The Committee note that Clause 1 of the Corporate Laws (Amendment)
Bill, 2026 seeks to provide for the short title and commencement of the
proposed legislation. The Committee observe that the Clause empowers the
Central Government to bring the provisions of the proposed legislation into
force on such date as may be notified in the Official Gazette. Further, it enables
different provisions of the proposed legislation to be brought into force on
different dates, and provides that any reference in any provision of the Act to
its commencement shall be construed as a reference to the date on which that
particular provision comes into force.

         The Committee are of the view that such an enabling provision would
provide the necessary flexibility to the Government to implement the various
provisions of the Act in a phased manner, in accordance with administrative

                                                        9
and operational requirements. The Committee, therefore, recommend that
Clause 1 of the Bill be accepted without any amendment.

                                                       10
      CLAUSE - 2

2. Clause 2 seeks to amend Section 2 of the Limited Liability Partnership
Act, 2008.

2.1 Provisions proposed in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

         In the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008 (hereafter in this Chapter referred
to as the principal Act), in section 2, in sub-section (1), 

(i) after clause (m), the following clauses shall be inserted, namely: --

         `(ma) "International Financial Services Centre" shall have the same
meaning as assigned to it in clause (g) of sub-section (1) of section 3 of the
International Financial Services Centres Authority Act, 2019;

         (mb) "International Financial Services Centres Authority" means the
Authority established under sub-section (1) of section 4 of the International
Financial Services Centres Authority Act, 2019;';

(ii) after clause (q), the following clause shall be inserted, namely: --

         `(qa) "permitted foreign currency" means a currency which may be
specified by the International Financial Services Centres Authority in
consultation with the Central Government;';

(iii) after clause (ta), the following clause shall be inserted, namely: --

         `(tb) "Specified International Financial Services Centre LLP" means a
limited liability partnership which is set up in an International Financial
Services Centre and regulated by the International Financial Services Centres
Authority;'.

2.2 Relevant provisions of the Principal Act (The Limited Liability
Partnership Act, 2008):

2. Definitions. - (1) In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires, --

*  *  *           *  *                                                     *

         11
         (m) "foreign limited liability partnership" means a limited liability
partnership formed, incorporated or registered outside India which establishes
a place of business within India;

*     *     *      *     *     *

         (q) "partner", in relation to a limited liability partnership, means any
person who becomes a partner in the limited liability partnership in
accordance with the limited liability partnership agreement;

*     *     *      *     *     *

         (ta) "small limited liability partnership" means a limited liability
partnership--

            (i) the contribution of which, does not exceed twenty-five
   lakh rupees or such higher amount, not exceeding five crore rupees, as
   may be prescribed; and

            (ii) the turnover of which, as per the Statement of Accounts
   and Solvency for the immediately preceding financial year, does not
   exceed forty lakh rupees or such higher amount, not exceeding fifty
   crore rupees, as may be prescribed; or

            (iii) which meets such other requirements as may be
   prescribed, and fulfils such terms and conditions as may be prescribed;

   *     *     *      *     *     *

2.3 Reasons/justification furnished by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs for
the proposed provisions:

         "These definitions are necessary to operationalise the IFSC-specific LLP
regime introduced by the Bill. They adopt the meanings of "International Financial
Services Centre" and "International Financial Services Centres Authority" from the
IFSCA Act, 2019, empower the IFSC Authority to specify permitted foreign currencies
in consultation with the Central Government, and create a distinct category of
"Specified International Financial Services Centre LLP" to which the special IFSC
provisions apply."

               12
2.4 Important views/suggestions given by experts/stakeholders:

2.4.1 The specification of a "permitted foreign currency" has direct legal
consequences for capital contribution, accounting and filings. Requiring specification
by gazetted notification ensures publicity, legal certainty and judicial noticeability, and
mirrors the drafting in the proposed section 43A(5)(c) of the Companies Act, 2013.
Therefore, it is recommended that the clause (qa) be retained, subject to the
following clarification: in the proposed clause (qa), for the words "which may be
specified by the International Financial Services Centres Authority in consultation
with the Central Government", substitute "which may be specified, by notification, by
the International Financial Services Centres Authority in consultation with the Central
Government";

2.4.2 Expand the definitions of Specified International Financial Services Centre
LLP and permitted foreign currency to expressly include Virtual Digital Asset Service
Providers (VASPs), Tokenisation Platforms, DLT Operators, Digital Asset Custodians
and Blockchain Infrastructure Providers licensed by IFSCA. It would remove
ambiguity and provides legal certainty for emerging digital asset businesses, create a
new legal category for regulated IFSC LLPs and enable blockchain startups to
operate under IFSCA;

2.4.3 Since the concept of "permitted foreign currency" and related procedural
matters are to be specified by IFSCA in consultation with the Central Government, it
is suggested that such subordinate frameworks be evolved in close inter-ministerial
coordination so as to remain aligned with India's broader trade, investment and
external sector policy objectives;

2.4.4 Clause (tb) has been inserted with a view to define the Specified IFSC LLP.
However, rather than defining the same under the LLP framework, this definition
merely relies on the IFSCA framework. Similar to how Small LLPs have been defined
under Section 2(1)(ta), Specified IFSC LLPs can also be defined within the LLP
framework by specifying the turnover or contribution threshold. The Committee may
consider redefining this definition. The current definition could be broadened by
bringing in parameters like contribution of the LLP, and the attempt should be to
define it from an LLP perspective and not merely from IFSC perspective.

2.5 Examination by the Committee:

2.5.1 Explaining about the specification of permitted foreign currency, the Ministry
placed on record the following:

                  "Section 20 of the International Financial Services Centres Authority
         Act, 2019 provides that every transaction of financial services in an

                                                       13
         International Financial Services Centre shall be in such foreign currency as
         may be specified by regulations in consultation with the Central Government.
         Section 28 provides that the Authority may, by notification, make regulations
         consistent with this Act and the rules made thereunder for carrying out the
         provisions of this Act. Section 3(1)(i) provides that "notification" means a
         notification published in the Official Gazette, and the expressions "notified"
         and "notify" shall be construed accordingly. Thus, regulations of the IFSCA
         under International Financial Services Centres Authority Act, 2019 are
         required to be notified in the Official Gazette.

                  Therefore, for the purpose of the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill,
         2026, the "permitted foreign currencies" would be ones which are specified by
         IFSCA through regulations made in consultation with the Central Government.
         There are also provisions for the conversion of monetary value of share
         capital/contribution into permitted foreign currencies. The framework for the
         same will be specified by IFSCA through regulations in consultation with the
         Central Government. The regulations made by IFSCA will be duly notified as
         noted above."

2.5.2 Concerning the suggestion that the specification of "permitted foreign
currency" may be issued by gazette notification in order to ensure publicity, legal
certainty and judicial noticeability, and also to mirror the drafting in the proposed
section 43A(5)(c) of the Companies Act, 2013, the Ministry stated that the word
"specify" denotes specified by regulations and the regulations are always published
in the Gazette.

2.5.3 On the issue of explicitly inserting the words "by notification" in the proposed
clause (qa), the Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs deposed before the
Committee as under:

                  "Everything which has to come has to come through regulation, and
         regulation has to be notified in the Gazette. This is clear. It also happens that
         where there is no regulation, then it comes as a notification in the Gazette. But
         we are saying that specify means it has to be done in consultation with the
         Central Government and then through a notification."

2.5.4 Explaining about the process to be followed by IFSCA for specifying the
permitted foreign currency, the representative of the Ministry of Corporate Affairs
deposed before the Committee as under:

                                                       14
                  "    ,     
               ,       
                         
              ,       "

2.5.5 With respect to the suggestion that the definition may be expended to
expressly include Virtual Digital Asset Service Providers (VASPs), Tokenisation
Platforms, DLT Operators, Digital Asset Custodians and Blockchain Infrastructure
Providers licensed by IFSCA, the Ministry clarified that Virtual Digital assets are not
to be treated as a foreign currency.

2.5.6 The Ministry noted the suggestion that subordinate framework with respect to
"permitted foreign currency" may be evolved in close inter-ministerial coordination so
as to make it aligned with India's broader trade, investment and external sector
policy objectives, and submitted as under:

                  "This would be appropriately dealt with during framing of subordinate
         legislation. The suggestion pertains to the manner in which the regulatory
         framework governing permitted foreign currency and related procedural
         requirements is to be operationalised. Since these matters are proposed to be
         prescribed through subordinate legislation and regulations, the issue of inter-
         ministerial consultation and coordination would be addressed at the stage of
         formulation of the relevant Rules."

2.5.7 In response to a suggestion that Specified IFSC LLPs should be defined from
an LLP perspective and not merely from IFSC perspective, the Ministry of Corporate
Affairs furnished the following:

                  "An IFSC LLP cannot be defined based on financial thresholds. It is
         defined based on its registered office alone. Such thresholds can only be set
         by the IFSCA for its purpose."

2.6 Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

2.6.1 The Committee note that Clause 2 of the Corporate Laws (Amendment)
Bill, 2026 seeks to amend sub-section (1) of Section 2 of the Limited Liability
Partnership Act, 2008, wherein definitions of the terms "International Financial

                                                       15
Services Centre", "International Financial Services Centres Authority",
"permitted foreign currency" and "Specified International Financial Services
Centre LLP" are proposed to be inserted. The Committee observe that the
Clause intends to adopt the meanings of "International Financial Services
Centre" and "International Financial Services Centres Authority" from the
International Financial Services Centres Authority Act, 2019, thereby ensuring
consistency and uniformity across the legislative framework. Further, it
empowers the IFSCA to specify permitted foreign currencies in consultation
with the Central Government and creates a distinct category of "Specified
International Financial Services Centre LLP" to which the special IFSC
provisions apply.

         Keeping in view the justifications provided by the Ministry of Corporate
Affairs, examination of the suggestions received from various stakeholders
and experts, and after thorough deliberations on the amendments proposed
under Clause 2, the Committee are of the opinion that the proposed
amendments are required in order to provide the necessary definitional
framework for implementation of the special regulatory regime applicable to
Limited Liability Partnerships operating in International Financial Services
Centres. The Committee, therefore, accept the proposed insertion of clauses
(ma), (mb), (qa) and (tb) in sub-section (1) of Section 2 of the Limited Liability
Partnership Act, 2008.

2.6.2 Further, the Committee note that Clause 18 of the Bill proposes to
amend Section 2(28) of the Companies Act, 2013, by substituting the words
"the Cost and Works Accountants" with the words "the Cost Accountants"
within the definition of "Cost Accountant". The Committee observe that this
amendment is intended to align the definition with current statutory
terminology, without altering the substantive effect of the provision.
Furthermore, the Committee note that an identical definition of "Cost
Accountant" exists in Section 2(1)(h) of the Limited Liability Partnership Act,
2008, which similarly requires alignment with the correct statutory
nomenclature. Therefore, the Committee recommend the following

                                                       16
amendments in section 2, sub-section (1) of the Limited Liability Partnership
Act, 2008:

    `in clause (h), for the words "the Cost and Works Accountants", the words
    "the Cost Accountants" shall be substituted.';

2.6.3 With respect to the proposed rule-making powers conferred upon the
concerned Authority under Clause 2, the Committee observe that the concept
of "permitted foreign currency" and related procedural matters are to be
specified by the International Financial Services Centres Authority in
consultation with the Central Government. The Committee feel that the
effective implementation of the proposed framework would depend
substantially upon the timely formulation of clear and comprehensive rules,
regulations and procedural guidelines. Moreover, the formulation of such
regulatory framework should be undertaken in close consultation and
coordination with the concerned Ministries, regulatory authorities and other
stakeholders so as to ensure that the regulatory framework governing
permitted foreign currencies remains consistent with the country's overall
macroeconomic priorities, foreign exchange management, international trade
obligations, investment facilitation measures and broader external sector
policy objectives. Accordingly, the Committee recommend that the Ministry of
Corporate Affairs and the International Financial Services Centres Authority
should ensure that the subordinate legislative framework is formulated in a
timely, transparent and consultative manner, with due regard to inter-
ministerial coordination and policy coherence, so as to facilitate the effective
implementation of the proposed provisions.

                                        CLAUSE - 3

3. Clause 3 seeks to amend Section 11 of the Limited Liability Partnership
Act, 2008.

3.1 Provisions proposed in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

In section 11 of the principal Act, --

         (a) in sub-section (1), for clause (c), the following clauses shall be
substituted, namely: --

         "(c) there shall be filed along with the incorporation document, a
statement in such form, as may be prescribed, by any one person who
subscribed his name to the incorporation document that all the requirements
of this Act and the rules made thereunder have been complied with, in respect
of incorporation and matters precedent and incidental thereto;

         (d) a declaration in the prescribed form by an advocate, a chartered
accountant, cost accountant or company secretary in practice, where a limited
liability partnership engaged such professionals in its formation or
incorporation.";

         (b) in sub-section (2), in clause (c), the following proviso shall be inserted,
namely: --

         "Provided that a Specified International Financial Services Centre LLP
shall state its objects to undertake financial services activities, as permitted
under clause (e) of sub-section (1) of section 3 of the International Financial
Services Centres Authority Act, 2019 and any matter considered necessary in
furtherance thereof, in accordance with the regulatory requirements specified
by the International Financial Services Centres Authority;".

3.2 Relevant provisions of the Principal Act (The Limited Liability
Partnership Act, 2008):

11. (1) For a limited liability partnership to be incorporated, --

*                                       *           *  *            *  *

                                           18
(c) there shall be filed along with the incorporation document, a
statement in the prescribed form, made by either an advocate, or a
Company Secretary or a Chartered Accountant or a Cost Accountant,
who is engaged in the formation of the limited liability partnership and
by anyone who subscribed his name to the incorporation document,
that all the requirements of this Act and the rules made thereunder
have been complied with, in respect of incorporation and matters
precedent and incidental thereto.

(2) The incorporation document shall--

   *     *     *                           *                    *      *

(c) state the proposed business of the limited liability partnership;

*     *     *                           *     *                        *

3.3 Reasons/justification furnished by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs for
the proposed provisions:

         "The amendment restructures section 11 (1) to make professional certification
at the time of incorporation optional rather than mandatory. While a declaration by a
subscriber to the incorporation document continues to be required, the declaration by
a practising professional is required only where such professional has been
engaged. This seeks to reduce compliance burden and facilitate ease of doing
business, by providing flexibility to companies and LLPs in the incorporation process.

         Further, the amendment introduces a specific requirement for a Specified
International Financial Services Centre LLP to undertake financial services activities
as permitted under IFSCA framework."

3.4 Important views/suggestions given by experts/stakeholders:

3.4.1 For LLPs exceeding a prescribed paid-up capital or turnover threshold,
professional certification should continue to remain mandatory as professional
certification acts as a quality-control mechanism at the incorporation stage,
enhances compliance standards, reduces regulatory risk, and promotes
accountability in larger LLPs where stakeholder interests are significant;

3.4.2 The Bill does not address the tax consequences of converting from a trust to
an LLP, or clarify how income earned by an AIF established as an LLP will be
characterised. Uncertainty on whether conversion triggers a taxable event, and

                                                       19
whether fund income through the LLP route is treated as business income, would
constitute a practical barrier to adoption of the LLP structure. Change in Corporate
structure of AIFs from Trust to LLPs should be tax neutral;

3.4.3 The word `and' should be added at the end of clause (c) to ensure that a
declaration from the professionals, if any, who were part of the formation and
incorporation process shall be filed along with the incorporation document;

3.4.4 In clause (d), the contents of the declaration were not specified, hence the
same should be redrafted to include the phrase, `certifying the particulars of the
incorporation documents to be true'. While the clause mentions that the declaration
must be in such form as may be prescribed, it is necessary to either detail out the
kind of contents required for each professional or prepare and annex the form to the
delegated legislation in such manner as it becomes clear what contents are required
within the declaration;

3.4.5 A clarification is required whether declarations are from all of the professionals
or any one of the professionals. This is important because the wording of the
amendment appears ambiguous on this. Hence, clause (d) should be redrafted to
convey that the declaration needs to be from one of the professionals who were
engaged and not by all;

3.4.6 The wording of the clause (d) opens a loophole. The declaration under (d) has
to be filed by a professional who is engaged in the formation and incorporation
process. If an LLP does not engage a professional, then they will not have to submit
the declaration. Be that as it may, this is a critical loophole particularly for the
Specified International Financial Services Centre LLP owing to the nature and
purpose of such entities. Hence, the following proviso has to be added to ensure that
the formation and incorporation of such entities is subject to a higher compliance
requirement:

                  "Provided that a Specified International Financial Services Centre LLP,
         shall engage the services of an advocate or a chartered accountant, or a cost
         accountant, or a company secretary in its formation or incorporation who shall
         make such declaration, as prescribed under clause (d)."

3.4.7 As many blockchain firms provide infrastructure rather than regulated financial
services, permit "financial technology, blockchain infrastructure, tokenisation, digital
asset platforms, programmable finance, smart contracts and ancillary technology
services" as permissible objects;

3.4.8 Substitute Clause 3(b) as:

                                                       20
                  "Provided that Specified International Financial Services Centre LLP
         shall clearly and specifically state, as its objects, the undertaking of financial
         services activities permitted under clause (e) of Section (1) of Section 3 of the
         International Financial Services Centres Authority Act, 2019 and shall
         undertake such activities strictly in accordance with the regulatory
         requirements, guidelines and directions issued by the International Financial
         Services Centres Authority from time to time";

3.4.9 At present, the provisions governing the incorporation of a limited liability
partnerships mandatorily requires a statement from a practicing professional, namely
an Advocate, Chartered Accountant, Cost Accountant, or Company Secretary, that all
the requirements of the Act and the rules made thereunder have been complied with,
in respect of incorporation and matters precedent or incidental thereto. The aforesaid
provision implies that for the incorporation of a limited liability partnership,
engagement of a professional is mandatory. The proposed amendment appears to
make it optional for the limited liability partnerships to engage a professional for the
incorporation of the limited liability partnerships. The related rules and forms should
be modified simultaneously so as to ensure that limited liability partnerships can be
incorporated without a statement or certification by the professional.

3.5 Examination by the Committee:

3.5.1 In response to the suggestion that for LLPs exceeding a prescribed paid-up
capital or turnover threshold, professional certification should continue to remain
mandatory, the Ministry of Corporate Affairs submitted as under:

                  "This is an amendment brought about to facilitate ease of living for
         corporates and other stakeholders. The main aim of the amendments is to
         ease compliance requirements and foster ease of doing business. It is in light
         of these goals, that the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 has made the
         requirement of appointing a professional optional at the time of incorporating a
         limited liability partnership."

3.5.2 Explaining about the reasons for making professional certification at the time
of incorporation of a limited liability partnership optional, the Secretary, Ministry of
Corporate Affairs deposed before the Committee that:

                  ", , ,
          So, this was one of the suggestions that came as part of the DPIIT
         consultation."

                                                       21
3.5.3 With respect to a suggestion that the change in corporate structure of AIFs
from Trust to LLPs should be tax neutral, the Ministry furnished the following:

                  "Suggestion pertains to Tax laws. The proposed amendment creates an
         enabling provision for conversion of Trust into LLP. All consequent effects and
         impact will be regulated by respective laws."

3.5.4 About the requirement for specifying the content of the declaration in the Bill
itself, as suggested in para 3.4.4, the Ministry stated that the details of the
certification will be addressed in the rules and forms.

3.5.5 For the request that "financial technology, blockchain infrastructure,
tokenisation, digital asset platforms, programmable finance, smart contracts and
ancillary technology services" may be included as permissible objects, the Ministry
explained that:

                  "LLP Act does not provide permission to any form of business. It only
         refers to lawful business with an object to profit. Such provisions cannot be
         included in the LLP Act."

3.5.6 Concerning the suggestion that the related rules and forms should be
modified simultaneously so as to ensure that limited liability partnerships can be
incorporated without a statement or certification by the professional, the Ministry
made the following submissions:

                  "Rules will be amended as soon as the Corporate Laws (Amendment)
         Bill, 2026 is passed by the Parliament. Forms are part of the rules and the
         revision in the forms will also take place simultaneously."

3.5.7 Further explaining about the proposed rule making powers under Clause 3,
the Ministry placed on record that:

                  "Clause 3 of the Bill empowers the Central Government to prescribe,
         under clause (c) and (d) of sub-section (1) of section 11 of the Limited Liability
         Partnership Act, 2008, the form of the statement to be filed along with the
         incorporation document, by any one person who subscribed his name to the

                                                       22
         incorporation document and the form of declaration to be filed by an advocate,
         a chartered accountant, cost accountant or company secretary in practice,
         where a limited liability partnership engaged such professionals in its
         formation or incorporation. This kind of delegation is procedural in nature and
         does not affect the substantive conditions."

3.6 Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

3.6.1 The Committee note that Clause 3 of the Bill seeks to amend clause (c)
and insert a new clause (d) in sub-section (1) of section 11 of the Limited
Liability Partnership Act, 2008. The proposed amendment provides that the
requirement for a declaration by an advocate, chartered accountant, cost
accountant or company secretary in practice at the time of formation or
incorporation of an LLP shall apply only where such professional has been
engaged for the purpose of incorporation. The Clause also seeks to insert a
new proviso in clause (c) of sub-section (2) to provide that a Specified
International Financial Services Centre LLP shall undertake only such financial
services activities, as are permitted under the framework of the International
Financial Services Centres Authority.

         The Committee observe that while the declaration by a subscriber to the
incorporation document shall continue to remain mandatory, the requirement
of a declaration by a practicing professional has been made conditional upon
the engagement of such professional, thereby making professional
certification at the time of incorporation optional. The Committee are of the
view that the proposed amendment strikes an appropriate balance between
maintaining necessary safeguards and reducing procedural requirements. It
would ease the incorporation process by providing greater flexibility to LLPs,
thereby facilitating the ease of doing business without compromising the
integrity of the incorporation process. Further, the Committee note the
submission of the Ministry of Corporate Affairs that the proposed amendment
emanated from the consultations held with the Department for Promotion of
Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) and the same is intended to align India's

                                                       23
regulatory framework with international best practices, which is expected to
have a positive bearing on global business and competitiveness rankings.

         Accordingly, taking into account the justifications and clarifications
furnished by the Ministry, the views and suggestions received from
stakeholders and experts, and deliberations held by the Committee, the
Committee recommend that Clause 3 be accepted without any amendment.

      CLAUSE - 4

4. Clause 4 seeks to amend Section 13 of the Limited Liability Partnership
Act, 2008.

4.1 Provisions proposed in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

         In section 13 of the principal Act, in sub-section (1), the following proviso shall
be inserted, namely: --

         "Provided that a Specified International Financial Services Centre LLP
shall have its registered office at an International Financial Services Centre, at
all times.".

4.2 Relevant provisions of the Principal Act (The Limited Liability
Partnership Act, 2008):

13. (1) Every limited liability partnership shall have a registered office to
which all communications and notices may be addressed and where they
shall be received.

*  *  *           *  *                                                 *

4.3 Reasons/justification furnished by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs for
the proposed provisions:

         "The amendment requires Specified IFSC LLPs to maintain their registered
office within an IFSC, thereby ensuring alignment with the regulatory framework
applicable to such entities and their operation within the IFSC jurisdiction."

4.4 Important views/suggestions given by experts/stakeholders:

4.4.1 Allow approved disaster recovery (DR) sites and technology centres outside
IFSC, while maintaining principal office in GIFT City as modern blockchain
infrastructure is cloud native and geographically distributed.

      25
4.5 Examination by the Committee:

4.5.1 In response to a suggestion to allow approved disaster recovery (DR) sites
and technology centres outside IFSC, while maintaining principal office in GIFT City,
the Ministry of Corporate Affairs clarified as under:

                  "There is no restriction in the law regarding maintenance of DR sites
         (which are not registered office) outside IFSC jurisdiction. Such matters would
         be governed by the regulatory framework of IFSCA."

4.6 Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

4.6.1 The Committee note that Clause 4 of the Bill seeks to insert a new
proviso in sub-section (1) of section 13 of the Limited Liability Partnership Act,
2008, to provide that a Specified International Financial Services Centre LLP
shall, at all times, have its registered office within an International Financial
Services Centre. The Committee also note the clarification furnished by the
Ministry of Corporate Affairs that the amendment relates only to the location of
the registered office and does not restrict the maintenance of disaster
recovery (DR) sites or other operational facilities outside the IFSC.

         Having considered the justification furnished by the Ministry, the views
and suggestions received from stakeholders and experts, and the
deliberations held thereon, the Committee observe that the proposed
amendment is intended to ensure that Specified IFSC LLPs remain within the
regulatory jurisdiction of the International Financial Services Centre and
operate in accordance with the applicable regulatory framework. Therefore, the
Committee accept the Clause 4 of the Bill as proposed.

      CLAUSE - 5

5. Clause 5 seeks to amend Section 15 of the Limited Liability Partnership
Act, 2008.

5.1 Provisions proposed in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

         In section 15 of the principal Act, in sub-section (1), the following proviso shall
be inserted, namely: --

         `Provided that a Specified International Financial Services Centre LLP
shall have the suffix "International Financial Services Centre LLP" as part of
its name.'.

5.2 Relevant provisions of the Principal Act (The Limited Liability
Partnership Act, 2008):

15. (1) Every limited liability partnership shall have either the words
"limited liability partnership" or the acronym "LLP" as the last words of its
name.

*  *  *           *  *                                                 *

5.3 Reasons/justification furnished by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs for
the proposed provisions:

         "The amendment is intended to identify Specified IFSC LLPs by requiring their
IFSC status to form part of their name."

5.4 Important views/suggestions given by experts/stakeholders:

5.4.1 The proviso to Section 15 of the LLP Act (principal Act), as proposed to be
inserted by Clause 5 of the Amendment Bill, be modified to read as follows:

         "Provided that a Specified International Financial Services Centre LLP
shall have the suffix "International Financial Services Centre LLP" or the
acronym "IFSC LLP" as part of its name."

      27
                  The proposed modification is intended to promote ease of doing
         business by permitting the use of the shorter acronym "IFSC LLP" as an
         alternative suffix, thereby reducing administrative burden associated with
         lengthy entity names while ensuring continued identification of such LLPs as
         entities operating within IFSC.

5.5 Examination by the Committee:

5.5.1 While accepting the suggestion regarding permitting the use of the shorter
acronym "IFSC LLP" as an alternative suffix, the Ministry of Corporate Affairs made
the following submission:

                  "Since "IFSC" is a widely recognised and statutorily accepted acronym
         used throughout the IFSC legal and regulatory framework, permitting the suffix
         "IFSC LLP" would preserve the objective of identifying Specified IFSC LLPs,
         while reducing the practical burden associated with lengthy entity names.
         Hence, the suggestion may be incorporated in the Amendment Bill.
         Accordingly, Clause 5 may be revised."

5.6 Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

5.6.1 The Committee note that Clause 5 of the Bill seeks to amend sub-section
(1) of section 15 of the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008 by inserting a
proviso requiring every Specified International Financial Services Centre LLP
to include the suffix "International Financial Services Centre LLP" as part of its
name. The Committee observe that the underlying objective of the proposed
amendment is to ensure that LLPs operating under the special regulatory
framework applicable to International Financial Services Centres (IFSCs) are
readily distinguishable from other LLPs, thereby promoting ease of
identification for regulators, investors and other stakeholders. However, during
the course of examination, various stakeholders and experts raised the
concern before the Committee that the mandatory use of the full suffix
"International Financial Services Centre LLP" may result in unduly long entity
names, creating practical difficulties in business communications, branding
and other commercial operations. The Committee further observe that the
acronym "IFSC" has acquired widespread regulatory and commercial

                                                       28
recognition and it has been consistently used in the regulations and circulars
issued by the International Financial Services Centres Authority. In view of its
established legal and commercial acceptance, the Committee are of the
considered opinion that permitting the abbreviated suffix "IFSC LLP" would
equally achieve the legislative objective of clearly identifying Specified IFSC
LLPs, while at the same time reducing the practical burden associated with
lengthy names and enhancing operational convenience.

         Therefore, the Committee recommend that Clause 5 of the Bill should be
modified to provide that a Specified International Financial Services Centre
LLP may use either the suffix "International Financial Services Centre LLP" or
the suffix "IFSC LLP" as part of its name. Accordingly, the Clause 5 be
amended as under:

         In section 15 of the principal Act, in sub-section (1), the following
proviso shall be inserted, namely: --

                  `Provided that a Specified International Financial Services Centre
         LLP shall have the suffix "International Financial Services Centre LLP"
         or "IFSC LLP" as part of its name.'.

              CLAUSE - 6

(2) The limited liability partnership agreement and any changes, if any,

6.3 Reasons/justification furnished by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs for
