              30
6.4 Important views/suggestions given by experts/stakeholders:

6.4.1 Add confidentiality/non-public filing for investor information. Accordingly, a
proviso may be inserted as:

                  "Provided further that in case of a class or classes of limited liability
         partnerships regulated by the Securities and Exchange Board of India, or by
         the International Financial Services Centres Authority, as may be prescribed,
         details of partners admitted or recognised as investors, their contribution or
         commitment particulars, profit-sharing or economic rights, and such other
         information, as may be prescribed, may be filed and accessed in such
         manner, as may be prescribed, such that the said contents are accessible
         only to the Central Government, Registrar, Securities and Exchange Board of
         India, International Financial Services Centres Authority, income-tax
         authorities and such other authorities, as may be prescribed."

                  The relaxation in filing frequency is useful but incomplete. Investor
         details and commercial economics should not become publicly searchable
         MCA records. Confidential filing preserves regulatory access while addressing
         investor privacy concerns, particularly for sovereign funds, institutions, family
         offices and strategic investors;

6.4.2 Expressly include Category I and Category II Alternative Investment Funds
within the "prescribed class" of LLPs eligible for annual reporting and foreign-
currency-capital relief. Without an express inclusion, the relief intended for VC/PE
funds structured as LLPs remains contingent on future notification rather than
automatic;

6.4.3 Clause 6 may be substituted as:

                  "Provided that, in the case of such class or classes of limited liability
         partnerships, as may be prescribed, which are regulated by the Securities and
         Exchange Board of India or the International Financial Services Centres
         Authority, the requirement of filing any changes in the limited liability
         partnership agreement shall be such, as may be prescribed.";

6.4.4 The relevant rules should clearly identify the class of eligible entities and
preserve transparency of beneficial ownership and control, so that compliance
simplification does not create ambiguity for entities beyond the intended regulatory
perimeter.

                                                       31
6.5 Examination by the Committee:

6.5.1 While accepting the suggestion regarding maintenance of confidentiality of
investor information, the Ministry of Corporate Affairs stated that the necessary
amendment may be made to ensure that such details are not open for inspection.

6.5.2 Further explaining about the need to maintain confidentiality of investor
information, the Ministry furnished the following:

                  "Since AIFs are privately pooled vehicles raising funds from
         sophisticated investors, confidentiality of fund documents (incorporation
         documents, annual return, Statement of Account) along with investors'
         information, is a critical requirement for globally competitive AIFs. There are
         express provisions for confidentiality in Fourth Schedule of the AIF
         Regulations. SEBI has also requested for a specific overall exemption for AIF
         LLPs from public inspection, by way of insertion of proviso under Section 36 of
         the LLP Act. In any case, this information will be available with the
         depositories and MCA."

6.5.3 On being asked about the power of registrar to reject registration/filing of
changes in LLP agreement, the Ministry submitted that:

                  "All such filings are processed online on the MCA21 system. The
         Registrar is required to give ample opportunity to the applicant, to rectify the
         mistakes, if any, by clearly specifying them. Rejections happen only after the
         opportunity of rectification has been exhausted. While rejecting any
         application, the detailed reasons for such rejections have to be clearly
         specified."

6.5.4 Regarding a suggestion for inclusion of Category I and Category II Alternative
Investment Funds within the "prescribed class" of LLPs eligible for annual reporting
and foreign-currency-capital relief, the Ministry clarified that the necessary inclusion
will take place through the rules, after due consultation with SEBI, IFSCA and all
other stakeholders.

                                                       32
6.5.5 In pursuance of a suggestion that relevant rules should clearly identify the

class of eligible entities and preserve transparency of beneficial ownership and

control, the Ministry placed on record the following:

                  "This would be appropriately dealt with during framing of subordinate
         legislation. The suggestion relates to the prescription of eligibility criteria and
         compliance requirements for the proposed framework. The identification of
         eligible entities and the manner of ensuring transparency regarding beneficial
         ownership and control would be appropriately addressed through the relevant
         Rules."

6.5.6 Further explaining about the proposed rule-making powers under Clause 6,

the Ministry made the following submissions:

                  "Clause 6 of the Bill empowers the Central Government to prescribe,
         under the proviso to sub-section (2) of section 23 of the Limited Liability
         Partnership Act, 2008, the class or classes of limited liability partnerships
         regulated by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), or by the
         International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA), and the
         requirement of filing changes in the limited liability partnership agreement to
         the Registrar, by such limited liability partnerships. The use of "class or
         classes" is a well-established legislative device in corporate law, enabling
         dynamic calibration without frequent statutory amendments. The essential
         policy, i.e., that differential compliance may be warranted, is determined by the
         legislature; only the identification and periodic revision of such classes is
         delegated. This form of delegation does not amount to conferral of unguided
         discretion, but the same is based upon objective criteria of the specified
         regulator regulating such LLP."

6.5.7 Explaining about the rationale for the words "as may be prescribed", the

representative of the Ministry of Corporate Affairs deposed before the Committee

that:

                  "At present, all LLPs are required to file any changes made to the LLP
         Agreement within 30 days. There has been a request from the industry,
         supported by SEBI, IFSCA and DEA. In such AIFs, partners join and exit in
         large numbers almost every month, resulting in frequent changes to the LLP
         Agreement. That is also one of the reasons why the number of AIFs in the
         form of LLPs is very low. The request is that this requirement may be modified
         so that filing can be done once a year or once in six months. That is why the
         words `as may be prescribed' have been proposed. This amendment will apply
         only to those IFSC LLPs and AIFs which are regulated by IFSCA."

                                                       33
6.6 Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

6.6.1 The Committee note that Clause 6 of the Bill seeks to insert a new
proviso to sub-section (2) of section 23 of the Limited Liability Partnership Act,
2008, to provide that, in case of such class or classes of LLPs regulated by the
Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) or the International Financial
Services Centres Authority (IFSCA), the requirement relating to filing of
changes in the LLP agreement shall be governed by such manner and
procedure, as may be prescribed in the rules. The Committee also note that the
proposed provision is aligned with the broader policy objective reflected in the
amendments proposed under Clauses 7, 12, 13 and 17 of the Bill, which
intends to facilitate the establishment and functioning of regulated entities,
including Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs), in the form of LLPs.

         The Committee take note of the submission made by the Ministry of
Corporate Affairs that at present, all LLPs are required to file any changes
made in the LLP agreement with the Registrar within a period of 30 days. The
Committee understand that this requirement has been identified as one of the
factors contributing to the limited adoption of the LLP structure by AIFs, as
AIFs typically witness frequent changes in their partner composition due to
entry and exit of large number of investors almost every month, which
necessitates corresponding changes in the LLP agreement. Further, the
Committee note that stakeholders, including industry representatives, SEBI,
IFSCA and the Department of Economic Affairs (DEA), have suggested that the
filing requirement may be rationalized by permitting such filings on a periodic
basis, such as annually or once in six months, instead of requiring filing of
every individual change within 30 days.

         The Committee are of the view that a periodic filing mechanism would
reduce procedural burden on regulated LLPs, while ensuring that necessary
information remains available with the regulatory authorities. The Committee,
therefore, recommend that the Clause 6 be suitably modified to provide for
annual filing of changes in the LLP agreement in respect of such class or

                                                       34
classes of LLPs regulated by SEBI or IFSCA. Accordingly, the Committee
recommend that Clause 6 of the Bill be amended as under:

         In section 23 of the principal Act, in sub-section (2), the following
proviso shall be inserted, namely: --

                  "Provided that in case of a class or classes of limited liability
         partnerships regulated by the Securities and Exchange Board of India,
         or by the International Financial Services Centres Authority, as may be
         prescribed, the requirement of filing any changes in the limited liability
         partnership agreement shall be on an annual basis, in such form and
         manner, as may be prescribed.".

6.6.2 Further, during the course of examination of the Bill, the Committee
received suggestions from various stakeholders and experts regarding the
need to ensure confidentiality of investor-related information. The
stakeholders expressed the view that details of investors should not become
publicly searchable records, and confidential filing mechanisms would enable
regulators to access necessary information, while protecting the privacy and
commercial interests of investors, particularly sovereign funds, institutional
investors, family offices and strategic investors.

         The Committee appreciate the concerns raised by the stakeholders and
are of the view that while regulatory transparency and compliance
requirements are essential, adequate safeguards should also be maintained to
protect sensitive investor information. The Committee, therefore, are of the
opinion that suitable changes should be made in the Act to provide for
confidentiality of the details filed by IFSC LLPs. Accordingly, the Committee
recommend that section 36 of the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008,
which provides for public inspection of documents kept by Registrar, be
amended as under:

      In section 36 of the principal Act, the following proviso shall be inserted,
namely: --

                                                       35
                  "Provided that the requirements related to inspection of
         documents under this section shall not apply in case of a class or
         classes of limited liability partnerships registered and regulated by the
         Securities and Exchange Board of India, or by the International Financial
         Services Centres Authority, as may be prescribed.".

6.6.3 Moreover, the Committee observe that several documents filed with the
Registrar contain personal information of partners, designated partners,
investors, managers and other individuals and many of these documents are
available for public inspection under the Limited Liability Partnership Act,
2008. The Committee are of the view that while transparency and public access
to statutory records are essential for maintaining corporate accountability,
such access should be balanced with the need to safeguard personal data and
protect the privacy of individuals. Therefore, there is a need to ensure that
personal data contained in documents filed with the Registrar of Companies is
collected, processed, stored, disclosed and made available for inspection in a
manner that is consistent with the provisions and principles of the Digital
Personal Data Protection Act, 2023.

         The Committee also observe that LLPs should be provided with an
appropriate mechanism to rectify clerical, arithmetical, typographical or factual
errors or omissions in documents or information filed with the Registrar. The
Committee are of the opinion that permitting such rectification through a
prescribed application process would facilitate correction of inadvertent
errors, reduce unnecessary compliance burden and ensure accuracy and
reliability of statutory records maintained by the Registrar.

         Further, the Committee feel that LLPs should also be provided with an
appropriate provision for seeking refund of fees paid for registration or filing
of any form or document in cases where such form or document could not be
registered or filed due to technical reasons. At present, such matters are
governed by the refund manual issued by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.
Therefore, the Committee are of the view that incorporating a specific statutory
provision for refund of fees in such cases would provide greater clarity and

                                                       36
certainty to LLPs and prevent avoidable financial burden, particularly where
the filing could not be completed due to technical issues.

         In view of the above, the Committee recommend that the Limited
Liability Partnership Act, 2008 should be amended as under:

         After section 69 of the principal Act, the following sections shall be
inserted, namely: --

         "69A. Refund of fees or any other payment.

         For refund of fees or any other payment, the provisions of section 403A
of the Companies Act, 2013 (18 of 2013) shall mutatis mutandis apply."

         "69B. Rectification in documents filed with the Registrar.

         For rectification of the documents filed with the Registrar, the provisions
of section 398A of the Companies Act, 2013 (18 of 2013) shall mutatis mutandis
apply."

         "69C. Application of the provisions of Digital Personal Data Protection
Act, 2023.

         All the provisions of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and
the rules made thereunder relating to consent and processing of digital
personal data, in so far as they are not inconsistent with this Act, shall apply in
relation to the records in electronic form specified in sections 36 and 68 of this
Act."

6.6.4 The Committee note the submission made by the Ministry of Corporate
Affairs that inclusion of Category-I and Category-II Alternative Investment
Funds within the "prescribed class" of LLPs eligible for annual reporting and
foreign currency contribution-related reliefs, would be undertaken through the
rules, after due consultation with SEBI, IFSCA and other relevant stakeholders.

                                                       37
         The Committee observe that the inclusion of such regulated entities
within the "prescribed class" would provide greater clarity and certainty
regarding the applicability of the proposed provisions and would facilitate
wider adoption of the LLP structure by Alternative Investment Funds. The
Committee are of the view that the rules framed under the proposed provisions
should be finalized in consultation with all concerned regulators and
stakeholders to ensure that the compliance framework is practical, balanced
and aligned with the regulatory requirements governing such entities.

         The Committee, therefore, recommend that the Ministry of Corporate
Affairs should consider specifically including Category-I and Category-II
Alternative Investment Funds within the "prescribed class" of LLPs, while
framing the rules under the proposed provisions.

                                                       38
              CLAUSE - 7

7. Clause 7 seeks to amend Section 25 of the Limited Liability Partnership
Act, 2008.

7.1 Provisions proposed in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

         In section 25 of the principal Act, in sub-section (2), the following proviso shall
be inserted, namely: --

         "Provided that in case of a class or classes of limited liability
partnerships regulated by the Securities and Exchange Board of India, or by
the International Financial Services Centres Authority, as may be prescribed,
there shall be a requirement to furnish the details of such changes to the
Registrar on an annual basis, in such form and manner, as may be
prescribed.".

7.2 Relevant provisions of the Principal Act (The Limited Liability
Partnership Act, 2008):

25. (1) *  *  *                              *  *

(2) A limited liability partnership shall--

   (a) where a person becomes or ceases to be a partner, file a notice
   with the Registrar within thirty days from the date he becomes or
   ceases to be a partner; and

   (b) where there is any change in the name or address of a partner,
   file a notice with the Registrar within thirty days of such change.

*  *       *  *                              *  *

7.3 Reasons/justification furnished by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs for
the proposed provisions:

         "The amendment facilitates the use of LLP structures for entities such as
Alternative Investment Funds by permitting a periodic reporting framework for
partner-related changes for LLPs regulated by SEBI or the IFSCA. This is part of the
Amendment Bill's broader regulatory framework for such entities through

                                                       39
amendments to section 23, 58, and insertion of section 57A and Schedule V of the
LLP Act."

7.4 Important views/suggestions given by experts/stakeholders:

7.4.1 Subject to change in the definition of LLP partners, the data of the
Contributors should not be publicly available for the reason of confidentiality. Investor
level information in each fund should remain accessible only to regulators and not be
publicly searchable, in order to safeguard investor privacy and security;

7.4.2 Expressly include Category I and Category II Alternative Investment Funds
within the "prescribed class" of LLPs eligible for annual reporting and foreign-
currency-capital relief. Without an express inclusion, the relief intended for VC/PE
funds structured as LLPs remains contingent on future notification rather than
automatic;

7.4.3 The existing requirement under section 25(2) of the limited liability
partnerships Act to report the changes in partners within 30 (thirty) days ensures that
the records maintained by the Registrar, including those displayed on the portal of
the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, accurately reflect the current constitution of a limited
liability partnership. The reporting of such changes only on an annual basis for
certain limited liability partnerships would result in outdated records on the portal of
Ministry of Corporate Affairs. Therefore, the proposed proviso may be amended as
under:

                  "Provided that in case of a class or classes of limited liability
         partnerships regulated by the Securities and Exchange Board of India, or by
         the International Financial Services Centres Authority, as may be prescribed,
         the particulars of any change under this sub-section shall be furnished to the
         Registrar, within such period and in such form and manner as may be
         prescribed."

The revision retains the obligation to promptly update the records of Registrar, while
providing flexibility to prescribe a different reporting period for such classes of limited
liability partnerships regulated by SEBI or IFSCA;

7.4.4 While any routine/ordinary changes, such as details of a partner or
replacement of a limited partner with its affiliate, may be reported annually, however,
time-bound reporting should remain mandatory for designated partners change,
control change and beneficial ownership change. This would balance transparency
with ease of compliance. In UK, partnership changes are required to be notified
within 14 days;

                                                       40
7.4.5 The amended Section 25(2) applies to LLPs regulated by SEBI or the IFSCA
(mainly AIFs and fund-management entities structured as LLPs). Where such an LLP
holds a dematerialised account, the move from event-based to annual reporting of
changes in partners/designated partners may, in the interim, leave the authorised-
signatory record unverified at the Registrar level. Therefore, it is recommended to
issue a Note on Clauses (or enabling rule) clarifying that the operation of such a
demat account in the interim is governed by the depositories' Bye-Laws and
Operating Instructions under the depository framework, pursuant to which the
depository may prescribe acceptable interim documentation (such as the LLP's
resolution, the LLP agreement and an authority letter) to evidence the authorised
signatory pending the annual filing; and that the filing requirements prescribed by the
Central Government for such LLPs be reconciled with the reporting required of them
by SEBI or the IFSCA, to avoid duplication;

7.4.6 LLP law treats every contributor of capital as an LLP partner with attendant
statutory rights and obligations, with no separate category for a passive financial
contributor. The Committee may consider introducing a distinct 'contributor' category
for AIF-LLPs, enabling investors to hold an economic interest without being
designated as an LLP partner with attendant statutory rights and obligations. It
should be aligned with the existing SEBI AIF framework to avoid unintended
consequences. AIF investors are financial contributors, not co-managers of the fund.
This distinction clearly separates fund managers, who should be designated as LLP
partners with governance responsibilities, from contributors, who should hold
economic interests as limited partners without being treated as administrative or
working partners under LLP law;

7.4.7 Requiring identical fund level information to be filed separately with different
authorities should be avoided. AIF-LLPs would be required to report similar
information separately to both the Ministry of Corporate Affairs and SEBI under their
respective frameworks. The Committee may consider enabling information already
filed with SEBI to be shared with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, thereby avoiding
duplicate regulatory filings for AIF-LLPs and reducing compliance burden;

7.4.8 The relevant rules should clearly identify the class of eligible entities and
preserve transparency of beneficial ownership and control, so that compliance
simplification does not create ambiguity for entities beyond the intended regulatory
perimeter.

7.5 Examination by the Committee:

7.5.1 While accepting the suggestion regarding maintenance of confidentiality of

investor information, the Ministry of Corporate Affairs stated that the necessary

amendment may be made to ensure that such details are not open for inspection.

                                                       41
7.5.2 Regarding a suggestion for inclusion of Category I and Category II Alternative
Investment Funds within the "prescribed class" of LLPs eligible for annual reporting
and foreign-currency-capital relief, the Ministry clarified that the necessary inclusion
will take place through the rules, after due consultation with SEBI, IFSCA and all
other stakeholders.

7.5.3 In response to a concern that reporting of changes on an annual basis for
certain limited liability partnerships would result in outdated records on the portal of
the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, the Ministry submitted as under:

                  "The amendment is aimed at streamlining the compliance requirement
         of the AIF LLPs. As such, if the details are otherwise required, there are
         adequate provisions to obtain them, such as Registrar's power to call for
         information under section 38 of the LLP Act. Besides this, the respective
         regulators may also obtain information."

7.5.4 With reference to the view that time-bound reporting should remain mandatory
for designated partners change, control change and beneficial ownership change,
the Ministry furnished that:

                  "The present provision does not pertain to reporting of changes of
         designated partners, which is covered by section 9. Even AIF LLPs will have
         to report changes in the designated partners in a timely manner in 30 days."

7.5.5 Concerning the issue that lag between a change in the authorised partners
and the annual filing could leave the demat account's signatory record temporarily
unverified, the Ministry clarified as under:

                  "Designated partners are the authorised signatories of an LLP. The
         amendment does not relax the requirement of intimating the changes in
         appointment or removal of designated partner, which is governed by section 9
         of the LLP Act. Thus, the demat account's signatory record would not remain
         unverified."

                                                       42
7.5.6 On the request regarding introducing a distinct 'contributor' category for AIF-
LLPs so as to enable investors to hold an economic interest without being
designated as an LLP partner, the Ministry placed on record the following:

                  "The rights and the obligations of the partners can be altered through
         the LLP agreement itself, subject to the provisions of the Chapter V of the LLP
         Act, which covers situations like fraud. This provides for sufficient flexibility
         and as such no amendment is required."

7.5.7 In pursuance of a suggestion about enabling the information already filed with
SEBI to be shared with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, thereby avoiding duplicate
regulatory filings for AIF-LLPs and reducing compliance burden, the Ministry stated
that the filing related aspects will be addressed at the time of making rules, which will
involve detailed consultations.

7.5.8 With respect to a suggestion that relevant rules should clearly identify the
class of eligible entities and preserve transparency of beneficial ownership and
control, the Ministry made the following submissions:

                  "This would be appropriately dealt with during framing of subordinate
         legislation. The suggestion relates to the prescription of eligibility criteria and
         compliance requirements for the proposed framework. The identification of
         eligible entities and the manner of ensuring transparency regarding beneficial
         ownership and control would be appropriately addressed through the relevant
         Rules."

7.5.9 Further explaining about the proposed rule-making powers under Clause 7,
the Ministry placed on record that:

                  "Clause 7 of the Bill empowers the Central Government to prescribe,
         under the proviso to sub-section (2) of section 25 of the Limited Liability
         Partnership Act, 2008, the class or classes of limited liability partnerships
         regulated by the SEBI, or the IFSCA, and the form and manner of furnishing
         the details of changes in partners to the Registrar on an annual basis, by such
         limited liability partnerships. The use of "class or classes" is a well-established
         legislative device in corporate law, enabling dynamic calibration without
         frequent statutory amendments. The essential policy, i.e., that differential
         compliance may be warranted, is determined by the legislature; only the
         identification and periodic revision of such classes is delegated. This form of

                                                       43
         delegation does not amount to conferral of unguided discretion, but the same
         is based upon objective criteria of the specified regulator regulating such LLP."

7.6 Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

7.6.1 The Committee note that Clause 7 of the Bill seeks to insert a new
proviso to sub-section (2) of section 25 of the Limited Liability Partnership Act,
2008, so as to provide that in case of prescribed class or classes of LLPs
regulated by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) or the
International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA), the requirement for
furnishing details of changes in partners to the Registrar shall be on annual
basis, in such form and manner, as may be provided by rules.

         The Committee observe that the proposed amendment intends to
facilitate the adoption of the LLP structure by regulated entities, including
Alternative Investment Funds, by introducing a simplified and periodic
reporting framework for changes in partners. Further, the proposed relaxation
is limited to reporting of changes in partners and does not affect the existing
requirement under section 9 of the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008,
relating to timely filing of changes in the appointment or removal of designated
partners. Accordingly, even Specified IFSC LLPs would be required to intimate
changes in designated partners within the prescribed period of 30 days.

         The Committee are of the view that the proposed periodic reporting
mechanism would reduce procedural burden, while ensuring continued
regulatory oversight by the concerned authorities. The Committee, therefore,
recommend that Clause 7 of the Bill be accepted without any amendment.

7.6.2 With respect to the concerns regarding confidentiality of investor-
related information, the Committee have recommended suitable amendments
in Section 36 of the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008, as detailed in
paragraph no. 6.6.2 of this Report.
