13.5.4.  On the issue of conversion of a Trust to an LLP and the liability of the

investors of the Trust after conversion, the Representatives of Gujarat International

Finance Tec-Company Limited (GIFTCL), deposed before the Committee and

submitted as follows:

"Here we have defined the `investor' means an investor in the hands of the specified
trust in accordance with the relevant regulations. However, as far as the trust is
concerned, we have beneficiaries for the trust. We are suggesting that clarification
may be made that the investor of the funds or beneficiaries of the fund may be
included. So, in several SEBI and IFSC registered framework including investment
funds and pooling vehicles, participants hold interest as beneficiaries rather than
direct investors. So, this clarification should be there that we should include
beneficiaries as well.

Similar suggestion is in terms of clause 17.3. Here also the reference is given to the
trustees. Here also, we are suggesting that instead of the trustees, the beneficiary
should be there because the trusts are formed for a specific purpose where the
trustees merely hold the legal title in a fiduciary capacity while the beneficiaries
constitute the true economic participants. So, the word `beneficiary' should be used.

The next point is with regard to the conversion of the trust to a limited liability
partnership. A lot of information is already sought. We are requesting that only one
additional statement needs to be included that should give the list of beneficiaries
and their beneficial interest in the specified trust and the list of designated partners.
So, that additional statement should also be sought.

                                                       81
Then the last point is with regard to clause 17.16. Here again, we are saying the
partners liable for liability is an obligation of trust. Every trustee of a specified trust
has converted into a limited liability. Their personal liability should remain. So, again
this clause is against the very existence or the structure of a trust. So, here also we
need to either have the beneficiaries included or the designated partners of the LLP
through which the liability can be transferred but not the trustees."

13.6. Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

The Committee note that Clause 13 of the Bill substitutes Section 58 of the
Principal Act. The Committee find that this amendment expands the scope of
conversion into LLPs to include specified trusts by incorporating a new
Schedule V and aligning section 58(1) accordingly. It facilitates the use of the
LLP structure for Alternative Investment Funds by providing a statutory
pathway for their conversion, while also providing post-registration intimation
requirements.

The Committee also note the suggestion that the word `Trustees' must be
replaced with `Investors' and `Manager' since Trustees are custodial/fiduciary
intermediaries and not economic stakeholders. Investors (LPs) are the
beneficial owners and capital contributors and therefore must become LLP
partners. Agreeing in principle with the suggestion the Committee find that the
investors (beneficiaries) indeed possess the substantive economic interest,
reap the financial benefits, and ultimately assume the risk. In contrast, the
trustees generally act in a purely fiduciary, administrative, or professional
capacity. The investors cannot be allowed to hide behind the trustees. Because
the investors reap the economic benefits, they, in addition to the trustees,
should be bound by the rules governing the conversion. Moreover, since
Managers are responsible for all investment decisions and compliance and
they must be made liable in the scheme of conversion as well.

Accordingly, in view of the above, the Committee recommend that under
Clause 13, Section 58 (2) be reframed as follows:

"(2) Upon such conversion, the partners of the firm, the shareholders of
private company or unlisted public company, or the trustees, investors and
managers of the specified trust, as the case may be, the limited liability
partnership to which such firm or such company or such specified trust has
converted, and the partners of the limited liability partnership, shall be bound

                                                       82
by the provisions of the Second Schedule, the Third Schedule, the Fourth
Schedule or the Fifth Schedule, as the case may be, applicable to them."

15.4.2.  "It is recommended that the clause be modified as follows: for "to such

16.6. Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

The Committee note that Clause 16 of the Bill seeks to insert new subsections
after Sub-Section (1) and Sub-Section (9), in section 76A of the principal Act.
The new Sub-Section 1A provides a statutory mechanism enabling a limited
liability partnership, or its partner or designated partner, to make an
application for adjudication of penalty under section 76A of the Principal Act.
The new sub-section 10 is intended to clarify that the above decriminalisation
shall have a retrospective effect and the relevant details (i.e. manner of

                                                       93
withdrawal of complaint/prosecution, manner of transfer of such matter for
adjudication), shall be provided through a scheme to be notified by the Central

The Committee note the suggestion to retain the Clause, provided that the

commencement and laid before both Houses of Parliament. The Committee
further observe that the Ministry agrees with this suggestion, finding it
consistent with the proposed amendment, and has stated that the Scheme will
be released following due consultation.

The Committee are of the opinion that apart from the limited liability
partnership, its partner or designated partner, `any other person' may also be
allowed to file the application for adjudication of penalty under section 76A of
the Principal Act. This step will be in support of reducing compliance burden
and providing flexibility in procedural aspects of adjudication process to LLPs
and their partners.

Accordingly, the Committee recommend that in Clause 16 (1A) the words `any
other person' be added and the Clause be amended as follows:

"In section 76A of the principal Act, --

(a) after sub-section (1), the following sub-section shall be inserted,
namely: --

     "(1A) A limited liability partnership or its partner or designated partner or
any other person may make an application in such form and manner and on
payment of such fees, as may be prescribed, under this section for
adjudication of penalty.";

17.  Clause 17 of the Bill seeks to insert a new Schedule (Fifth Schedule)

to the LLP Act, 2008 regarding conversion from specified Trust into Limited

Liability Partnership.

17.1 Provision proposed in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

After the Fourth Schedule to the principal Act, the following Schedule shall be
inserted, namely: --

                                 `THE FIFTH SCHEDULE

                                      (See section 57A)

CONVERSION FROM SPECIFIED TRUST INTO LIMITED LIABILITY
PARTNERSHIP

17.2 Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (Limited Liability Partnership Act,
2008):

A new provision has been proposed in the Bill by inserting the Fifth Schedule under
Section 57A of the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008, to regulate the conversion
of specified trusts into limited liability partnerships.

17.3 Reasons / Justification given by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs for the
proposed provision:

"This is the corresponding schedule to the amendments proposed in section 23, 25,
and 58."

17.4 Important Views/Suggestions given by Experts/Stakeholders:

The Stakeholder supported the proposed framework while suggesting certain
modifications. It was recommended that the proposed conversion framework under
the Fifth Schedule be strengthened by providing greater clarity on investor consent
requirements, regulatory oversight, stakeholder protection, post-conversion rights
and liabilities, and implementation procedures. In particular, consideration may be

                                                       95
given to prescribing a value-based investor consent threshold, requiring prior
approval or intimation to SEBI/IFSCA, introducing a coordinated SEBI-MCA
framework for such conversions, ensuring compliance certification by a practising
professional, providing an opportunity of hearing and reasoned orders before refusal
of registration, clarifying the status and rights of investors/beneficiaries and trustees
post-conversion, and prescribing clear procedures and timelines for asset vesting,
mutation, and updating of statutory records.

17.5    Examination by the Committee:

17.5.1  On the suggestion relating to strengthening the proposed conversion

framework under the Fifth Schedule, the Ministry submitted the following:

"The Schedule V is proposed to be amended to propose that a prior NOC from
SEBI/IFSCA would be required. Value based investor consent is also being
incorporated. The process of conversion will be completely online and adequate
opportunity will be given to the applicant to rectify any mistakes."

17.5.2  During the examination of the Bill, the Committee expressed their

concern regarding the extent of delegated legislation proposed under the Bill. They

observed that certain substantive matters, even where the legislative intent was

already clear, had been left to be prescribed through rules instead of being expressly

incorporated in the Bill itself. The Committee, therefore, sought a detailed note from

the Ministry of Corporate Affairs explaining the rationale for such delegation. In

regard to Clause 17, the Ministry submitted as follows:

"Clause 17 of the Bill empowers the Central Government to prescribe, under
paragraph 4 (a) of the Fifth Schedule of the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008,
the form and manner, and such fee for the statement by all of its trustees, containing
the particulars as given under paragraph 4(a). It further empowers the Central
Government to prescribe, under paragraph 5 of the Fifth Schedule, the form and
manner in which the limited liability partnership shall inform the concerned authority
about the conversion and of the particulars of the limited liability partnership.

It proposes to prescribe form and manner, and fee for the statement by all trustees
containing the particulars as given under paragraph 4(a). Also, it proposed to
prescribe form & manner in which the LLP shall inform concerned authority about
conversion & of particulars of LLP. These kinds of delegations are procedural in
nature."

                                                       96
17.5.3  Further, during the oral evidence, the representative of the Ministry of

Corporate Affairs elaborated upon the proposed amendments relating to conversion

of specified trusts into limited liability partnerships, as follows:

"Sir, in the LLP amendments, one of the clauses that attracted the highest number of
suggestions is this one. Section 57A provides for the conversion of a specified trust
into a limited liability partnership. This is basically aimed at enabling AIF trusts
registered with SEBI or IFSCA to convert into AIF LLPs. The major suggestions were
as follows. ..... That is why we proposed that the trustees would affect the conversion
and become partners initially. Subsequently, the investors in the AIF would become
partners in the LLP. However, stakeholders requested that all possible options be
provided. Accordingly, after discussions with IVCA, the industry body, along with
DEA, IFSCA, and SEBI, we agreed to make the necessary changes. Apart from
trustees, we also proposed to include investors and managers. Thus, the managers,
investors, or trustees can affect the conversion, leaving the decision to the particular
AIF. ..... That is why we made the provision more flexible."

17.6 Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

17.6.1  The Committee observe that the Clause 17 of the Bill seeks to

insert a new Schedule (Fifth Schedule) to the LLP Act, 2008 referred to in

section 57A to specify the conditions which would need to be fulfilled before

conversion of a specified trust into a limited liability partnership. The

provisions of Fifth Schedule are similar to conditions provided under Second,

Third and Fourth Schedules to the Act. This amendment will facilitate

conversion of Alternative Investment Funds formed as trusts into LLPs.

The proposed Fifth Schedule comprises 17 paras governing the conversion of
specified trusts into limited liability partnerships and providing for a smooth
transition upon such conversion. The Committee, after close scrutiny and
examination of Clause 17, taking into consideration the views and suggestions
received from various stakeholders and their own deliberations, accept the
Clause subject to the amendments recommended in respect of the relevant
paras of the proposed Fifth Schedule under it.

        97
The Committee have examined each of the paras of the proposed Fifth
Schedule separately and their observations and recommendations are
contained in the succeeding paras of this Report.

17.6.2  On the issue of delegation of legislative powers proposed under

Clause 17, the Committee examined the justification furnished by the Ministry.

The Ministry has submitted that the matters proposed to be prescribed under

para 4(a) of the Fifth Schedule relate to the form, manner and fee for filing the

statement containing the prescribed particulars while the matters proposed

under para 5 relate to the form and manner in which the resulting limited

liability partnership is required to intimate the concerned authority of the

conversion and furnish the particulars of the limited liability partnership. It has

been further stated that these delegations are procedural in nature and are

intended only to prescribe the operational modalities for implementation of the

proposed provisions. The Committee, after examining the justification

furnished by the Ministry, are satisfied that the proposed delegation relates

only to procedural and operational matters.

17(1) Para 1 of the Clause 17 proposes to provide for definitions of key terms.

17(1).1 Provision proposed in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

1. Interpretation. --In this Schedule, unless the context otherwise requires, -- (a)
"convert", in relation to a specified trust converting into a limited liability partnership,
means a transfer of the property, assets, interests, rights, privileges, liabilities,
obligations and the undertaking of the specified trust to the limited liability partnership
in accordance with this Schedule;

(b) "investor" means an investor to the funds of the specified trust in accordance with
the relevant regulations made by the Securities and Exchange Board of India, or by
the International Financial Services Centres Authority, as the case may be; and

(c) "specified trust" shall have the meaning assigned to it in the Explanation to
section 57A.

        98
17(1).2  Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (Limited Liability

Partnership Act, 2008):

A new provision has been proposed in the Bill by inserting the Fifth Schedule under
Section 57A of the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008, to regulate the conversion
of specified trusts into limited liability partnerships.

17(1).3  Reasons / Justification given by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs

for the proposed provision:

"This is the corresponding schedule to the amendments proposed in section 23, 25,
and 58."

17(1).4  Important Views/Suggestions given by Experts/Stakeholders:

17(1).4.1 Regarding clause, 17(1)(b), the definition of investors should be
expanded to also include beneficiaries of the specified trust. Proposed suggestion
"investor means an investor of the funds or beneficiaries to the fund of the specified
trust in accordance with the relevant regulations made by the Securities Exchange
Board of India, or by the International Financial Services Centres Authority, as the
case be;" The definition of "investor" should also expressly include beneficiaries of
the specified trust, as trust-based structures fundamentally distinguish between legal
ownership and economic interest, with trustees holding legal title and beneficiaries
representing the true economic stakeholders. In several SEBI- and IFSCA-regulated
frameworks, including investment funds and pooling vehicles, participants hold
interests as beneficiaries rather than direct investors in a corporate sense, and their
rights and entitlements arise from such beneficial interest. A narrow formulation
limited only to "investors to the funds" may therefore create interpretational ambiguity
and fail to capture the full spectrum of stakeholders, particularly in structures
involving nominee arrangements or layered participation. Including beneficiaries
ensures that the definition aligns with the substantive economic reality of trust
structures, is consistent with regulatory practice, and enables appropriate recognition
and protection of all stakeholders--particularly in the context of conversion, where
continuity of rights and interests is critical.

17(1).4.2 Specified trusts definition to include any private trusts (not only
SEBI/IFSCA trusts); and (ii) permit conversion of such trusts into LLPs and/or
companies (including Section 8 companies) Proposed Section 57A to be revised to
state:

"...the term "specified trust" means a trust established under the Indian Trusts Act,
1882 or under a Central Act or State Act (including such trusts registered with

                                                       99
Securities and Exchange Board of India, or by the International Financial Services
Centres Authority) and (may be deleted: registered by the Securities and Exchange
Board of India, or by the International Financial Services Centres Authority, as the
case may be, having such activities as may be prescribed.)" Introduce similar
provision in the Companies Act, 2013.

[Note: The enabling regime must be trust-appropriate including permitting scheme-
level (not whole-trust) conversion.]

The current definition excludes private trusts limiting the Bill's scope for such entities.
A company is governed under the framework of the Companies Act, 2013 as
compared to a private trust having no such robust governance framework.
Conversion of any trust to a company will result in extending the same governance
framework to the former.

17(1).5  Examination by the Committee:

17(1).5.1 In regard to the suggestion to expand the definition of "investor" so as
to include beneficiaries, the Ministry, in its written reply, stated as follows:

"Such nominee arrangements will have to be disclosed in case of LLPs. Even in
those cases, the nominee is required to act on the directions of the nominator
(beneficiary). The interests of beneficiaries are always exercised through the
nominees. There would be no interpretational ambiguity, as there are provisions
under the LLP rules to disclose the status of the nominee, where such arrangements
exist. All LLPs are required to maintain a register of partners, including the details of
the nominees as per rule 22A of the Limited Liability Partnership Rules, 2009."

17(1).5.2 On the suggestion relating to the expansion of the definition of

"specified trust" and the extension of the conversion framework to other trusts, the

Ministry stated as follows:

"The amendment envisages conversion of trust to LLP and not to a company. The
definition of trust is aligned with the applicable regulations of SEBI."

17(1).6  Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

17(1).6.1 The Committee note that para 1 of the proposed Fifth Schedule
seeks to define the key expressions governing the proposed framework for

                                                      100
conversion of specified trusts into limited liability partnerships. During the
examination of the Bill, stakeholders suggested that the manager/fund
manager should also be recognized in the proposed conversion framework.

The Committee are of the view that, once the manager is proposed to be
assigned a role under the Fifth Schedule, the expression `manager' or `fund
manager' should also be specifically defined with reference to the applicable
SEBI and IFSCA regulations to ensure legal certainty and consistency with the
regulatory framework governing Alternative Investment Funds.

The Committee, therefore, accept the para 1 of the proposed Fifth Schedule
subject to the following amendments. Insert the following clause after clause
(b):

"(ba) "manager" means a manager as defined under the Securities and
Exchange Board of India (Alternative Investment Funds) Regulations, 2012
made under the Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992 and includes
fund manager or fund management entity as defined under the International
Financial Services Centres Authority (Fund Management) Regulations, 2025
made under the International Financial Services Centres Authority Act, 2019;"

17(1).6.2 As a consequential amendment, the word "and" occurring
immediately after the words "may be;" may be omitted to maintain
grammatical continuity.

17(2) Para 2 of Clause 17 seeks to provide for the conversion of specified
trusts into Limited Liability Partnerships in accordance with the proposed Fifth
Schedule

17(2).1 Provision proposed in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

2. Conversion from specified trust into limited liability partnership. --

(1) A specified trust may convert into a limited liability partnership by complying with
the requirements as to the conversion set out in this Schedule.

                                                      101
(2) Upon such conversion, the trustees of the specified trust shall be bound by the
provisions of this Schedule that are applicable to them.

17(2).2  Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (Limited Liability

Partnership Act, 2008):

A new provision has been proposed in the Bill by inserting the Fifth Schedule under
Section 57A of the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008, to regulate the conversion
of specified trusts into limited liability partnerships.

17(2).3  Reasons / Justification given by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs

for the proposed provision:

"This is the corresponding schedule to the amendments proposed in section 23, 25,
and 58."

17(2).4  Important Views/Suggestions given by Experts/Stakeholders:

17(2).4.1 The stakeholder has suggested that the proposed text of Paras 2(2)
and 3 of the Fifth Schedule may be as follows: 2.(2) Upon such conversion, the
partners of the firm, the shareholders of private company or unlisted public company,
or the trustees investors and the manager (as defined by the Securities and
Exchange Board of India or International Financial Services Centres Authority) of the
specified trust, as the case may be, [...] shall be bound by the provisions of the
Second Schedule, the Third Schedule, the Fourth Schedule or the Fifth Schedule, as
the case may be, applicable to them.

17(2).4.2 "Many Category I AIFs operate multiple Investments (schemes) under
a single SEBI registration as a Fund. Legislative clarification that this structure may
continue following conversion to LLP would avoid uncertainty and support
implementation. A SEBI registered AIF invests in multiple start-ups and keeps record
of each investment from inception to exit. Thus, in the LLP structure same should be
permitted."

17(2).4.3 "Fifth Schedule, Paragraph 3 (as proposed): "A specified trust, and its
schemes, may apply to convert into limited liability partnership(s) in accordance with
this Schedule, only if the partners of the limited liability partnership into which the
specified trust is to be converted are the (word may be deleted: trustees) Investors of
such specified trust and the Manager of the Alternative Investment Fund, who shall
be admitted as a Designated Partner, and no one else."

                             102
a. The current draft's "and no one else" language, when combined with "trustees,"
would exclude both the investors and the Manager from the converted LLP. This
makes the conversion practically impossible: the trust converts into an LLP whose
only partners are the former trustees, while the actual capital contributors and the
managing entity have no legal standing in the new vehicle.

b. The one-trust-to-one-LLP model is fundamentally incompatible with the multi-
scheme architecture of AIFs. A single AIF trust may operate 3, 5, or more schemes,
each with different investors, different vintages, different investment mandates, and
different lifecycles. A trust with five active schemes must be able to convert into five
separate LLPs, each corresponding to one scheme. Any other approach would
require forced consolidation of distinct investor pools, which would breach the terms
of the Private Placement Memoranda, Contribution Agreements, and side letters
governing each scheme.

c. If schemes cannot separately convert, AIFs face a dilemma: either (a) they do not
convert at all, forgoing the significant benefits of the LLP structure including limited
liability, and international LP familiarity; or (b) they attempt to consolidate schemes
before conversion, which has no framework under the Income Tax Act, 2025 or
SEBI/IFSCA Regulations.

d. The proposed Section 47(xiic) of the Income Tax Act provides capital gains tax
exemption on conversion. However, the actual assets being portfolio company
securities, debt instruments, and other investments, are held at the scheme level. If
conversion does not operate at scheme level, the tax neutrality benefit is rendered
illusory: the trust entity converts tax-free, but the scheme-level assets would need to
be separately transferred, triggering capital gains tax and defeating the legislative
intent.

e. All third-party contractual relationships - portfolio company shareholder
agreements, subscription agreements, lender facility agreements, escrow
arrangements, and co-investment documentation - are entered into at the scheme
level. Conversion at scheme level would allow these contracts to vest in the
successor LLP by operation of law under the Fifth Schedule, without the need for
individual novation, assignment, or third-party consents. A trust-only conversion
would leave all scheme-level contracts orphaned, requiring thousands of individual
transfers across the AIF industry.

f. The requirement that the Manager be admitted as a Designated Partner is a
structural necessity. Under Section 7(1) of the LLP Act, 2008, every LLP must have
at least two Designated Partners, at least one of whom must be a resident in India.
The Manager, as the entity with operational control, regulatory accountability, and
investment decision-making authority, is the only entity that can meaningfully
discharge the Designated Partner's compliance obligations under the LLP Act.
Without this, the converted LLP would need to appoint an unrelated Designated
Partner with no connection to the fund's management - an absurd outcome that

                                                      103
would compromise governance standards.

g. This amendment would bring Indian fund structuring in line with the global
standard. Jurisdictions that have enacted similar conversion or re-domiciliation
frameworks--including Singapore (VCC re-domiciliation under the VCC Act),
Mauritius (conversion under the Limited Partnerships Act 2011), and the UK
(migration under the Limited Partnerships Act 1907)--all permit the fund manager to
assume the role of general or managing partner and allow sub-fund or scheme-level
conversion. India's framework should be no less sophisticated."

17(2).5  Examination by the Committee:

17(2).5.1 The Ministry, in regard to the suggestion relating to inclusion of
investors and the manager among the persons bound by the provisions of the Fifth
Schedule upon conversion, has stated:

"Suggestion received is being examined in consultations with DEA, SEBI, IFSCA."

17(2).5.2 Regarding suggestion relating to continuation of the existing multi-
scheme structure following conversion into a limited liability partnership, the Ministry
has stated:

"The basic LLP structure will remain intact. It will have one set of partners for the
whole of the LLP. Separate schemes with separate partners cannot be run under a
single LLP."

17(2).5.3 In regard to the suggestion relating to the eligibility, procedural
requirements and scope of conversion of specified trusts into limited liability
partnerships, the Ministry has stated:

"An amendment is being proposed whereby, the AIF trust is proposed to be given
option to convert either through all trustees, or through all managers or through
partners. There is also a requirement of prior NOC of SEBI/IFSCA. Where the
conversion takes place through trustees or managers, there will be an obligation to
onboard all the investors within 30 days. The amendment does not envisage
conversion of those trusts which have multiple schemes in them. Largely most AIF
trusts run with a single scheme. The amendment will cater to the conversion of such
trusts into LLPs."

                                                      104
17(2).5.4 When sought clarification whether Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs)
having multiple schemes would be eligible for conversion under the proposed Fifth
Schedule, and if not, how such AIFs would be able to avail of the proposed
conversion framework. In reply, the representative of the Ministry of Corporate Affairs
during the oral evidence on the 16th July, 2026, explained to the Committee as
follows:

"Right now, IFSCA does not allow multiple schemes in their AIFs. In IFSCA, the
structure is each trust will have only one scheme. So, there is no problem. They said
that the present formulation is absolutely fine with them. In SEBI, out of 1,900
according to the data provided, only 160 AIFs are having two schemes. We will
submit, we will provide the details also. 49 are having three schemes, 23 are having
four, 12 are having five and rest around nine, six etc. The numbers are very less.
Almost majority of the AIFs are in the form of single and the average number of
schemes per trust is 1.2. That is the reason the trust is having a registration. For
example, in a trust which is having three schemes, three schemes are having unique
number because the information is filed with SEBI. It is only for SEBI. But these
schemes are not having an illegal structure. Any registration with SEBI happens for
the trust. That is the reason to allow conversion. For example, if a particular trust is
having ten schemes, then that will become ten LLPs. It will become a problem
because how the registration will be handled; the SEBI will give another ten different
registrations."

17(2).5.5 On the same issue of AIF having multiple schemes, Secretary, Ministry
of Corporate Affairs further explained as follows:

"They can have separate trusts for that and then they can come here directly. That is
the reason. It is because the number of trusts is very few, because of which it will
make the law very complex. Even the administration becomes very complex..... ",
               
     Then we can have further discussion on that."

17(2).5.6 The Ministry, through a written submission, has further stated on the
issue of conversion of AIFs with multiple schemes:

"IFSCA has informed that they have one scheme per trust. In case of SEBI also,
most of the trusts have a single scheme. Each scheme of a multi-scheme trust
operates as a segregated pool of assets and liabilities with different sets of investors.
An LLP, by contrast, is a single legal entity with one common pool of assets bound
by a single agreement. The statutory vesting mechanism is not designed to provide

                                                      105
for multiple, scheme-wise LLPs."

17(2).6  Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

17(2).6.1 The Committee note that para 2 of the proposed Fifth Schedule
provides the enabling framework for conversion of a specified trust into a
limited liability partnership and specifies the persons who shall be bound by
the provisions of the proposed Schedule upon such conversion. The
Committee further note that the Ministry has accepted the suggestion to
broaden the category of persons bound by the provisions of the Fifth Schedule
and has agreed to suitably amend the provision in consultation with the
Department of Economic Affairs, the Securities and Exchange Board of India
and the International Financial Services Centres Authority.

The Committee are of the view that such amendment would ensure consistency
with the revised conversion framework by extending the application of the
proposed Fifth Schedule to all persons through whom the conversion may be
effected and would appropriately reflect the operational structure of Alternative
Investment Funds.

Accordingly, the Committee propose following amendment:

In paragraph 2(2) of the proposed Fifth Schedule, for "the trustees of the
specified trust", shall be substituted with "the trustees, investors and
managers of the specified trust".

17(2).6.2 The Committee note that the proposed framework does not clearly
address the conversion of multi-scheme Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs)
into limited liability partnerships. The Committee also note the clarification
furnished by the Ministry that the proposed framework is intended primarily to
facilitate conversion of specified trusts having a single scheme and that the
substantial majority of Alternative Investment Funds registered with SEBI, or
regulated by IFSCA, fall within this category. The Ministry has explained that an
individual scheme of a multi-scheme Alternative Investment Fund does not

                                                      106
possess a separate legal identity distinct from the trust and that permitting
scheme-wise conversion would give rise to complexities. The Committee,
however, are of the view that there is a need to provide enabling framework for
conversion of specified trust with multiple schemes also.

The Committee, therefore, recommend that the Government should provide for
a carve out, by way of an enabling framework for conversion of such specified
trust as are registered or regulated by SEBI or IFSCA, and which operate or
maintain multiple schemes. Further, keeping in view the larger aim to facilitate
conversion of specified trust to LLP, the Committee recommend that the
Government may provide a detailed framework to address the consequential
issues arising out of such conversion, like filing taxation, capital gains, stamp
duty implications, etc. If required, suitable amendments may be carried out in
the relevant Acts.

Accordingly, the following sub-para may be inserted after sub-para (2) of para 2
of the Fifth Schedule:

         "(2A) Notwithstanding anything contained in this Schedule, where a
         specified trust operates or maintains multiple schemes, or such other
         structure which is not already covered under this Schedule, a framework
         may be provided for conversion of such trusts into a limited liability
         partnership, subject to such conditions, and procedure, as may be
         prescribed.

         (2B) The Central Government may, in consultation and coordination
         with the Ministries, Departments and regulatory authorities concerned,
         notify a comprehensive framework to facilitate the conversion of
         specified trusts into limited liability partnerships, including provisions
         relating to taxation, capital gains, stamp duty, transfer and vesting of
         assets and liabilities, filing and compliance requirements, continuation
         of rights and obligations, and other consequential or incidental matters
         arising from such conversion.

         (2C) The Central Government may also undertake or recommend
         suitable amendments to the relevant laws, wherever necessary, to
         ensure a smooth and seamless implementation of such conversion."

                                                      107
Subject to the amendments recommended above, the Committee accept the
para 2 of the Fifth Schedule.

17(3) Para 3 of Clause 17 seeks to prescribe the eligibility conditions for
conversion of a specified trust into a Limited Liability Partnership.

17(3).1 Provision proposed in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

3. Eligibility for conversion.-- A specified trust may apply to convert into a limited
liability partnership in accordance with this Schedule, only if the partners of the
limited liability partnership into which the specified trust is to be converted, are
trustees of such specified trust and no one else.

17(3).2  Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (Limited Liability

Partnership Act, 2008):

A new provision has been proposed in the Bill by inserting the Fifth Schedule under
Section 57A of the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008, to regulate the conversion
of specified trusts into limited liability partnerships.

17(3).3  Reasons / Justification given by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs

for the proposed provision:

"This is the corresponding schedule to the amendments proposed in section 23, 25,
and 58."

17(3).4  Important Views/Suggestions given by Experts/Stakeholders:

17(3).4.1 Regarding clause 17(3), the eligibility for conversion should be for
beneficiaries of the specified trust and not for the trustee of the specified trust.
Proposed suggestion: "Eligibility for conversion. --A specified trust may apply to
convert into a limited liability partnership in accordance with this Schedule, only if the
partners of the limited liability partnership into which the specified trust is to be
converted, are beneficiaries of such specified trust and no one else." The eligibility
condition, as currently worded, appears conceptually misaligned with the nature of
trust structures. Restricting partners of the resulting LLP to only the trustees does not
appropriately reflect the economic ownership and stakeholder interests in a trust,
where trustees merely hold legal title in a fiduciary capacity, while the beneficiaries
constitute the true economic participants. Accordingly, the eligibility criteria for

                                                      108
conversion should be anchored to the beneficiaries of the specified trust, as they are
the ultimate holders of beneficial interest and bear the economic rights and risks
associated with the trust property.

17(3).4.2 "Only 'Individuals' and 'Body corporates' may be partners. Challenges
for HUFs / AOPs / select investor categories to participate in an LLP structure. The
Bill enables conversion but does not clarify whether all eligible AIF investors can
become partners. Insert a proviso deeming `Any person permitted to invest under
SEBI / IFSCA rules' eligible to be admitted or recognized as a Partner of the
converted LLP, in the prescribed manner. AIF investors include HUFs, Family
Offices, Trusts, Offshore Funds and Institutions. Without including them, Funds will
find it difficult to adopt the "conversion''.

17(3).4.3 "Proposed Fifth Schedule on `Conversion from Specified Trust into
Limited Liability Partnership' identifies `Trustees' as the persons who would become
`Partners' on conversion. However, trustees are independent fiduciaries holding no
economic interest in AIFs. `Investors' are the beneficiary owners of the trust-AIF and
the `Manager' discharges all its operational obligations. Hence, the investors and the
Manager of AIFs should be made `Partners' upon such conversion, and not trustees."

17(3).4.4 "Lower the 75% investor-consent threshold, coupled with a dissenter
exit right; tighten the indemnity provision in Fifth Schedule para 16 to limit residual
trustee liability; and (for onward reference to the Ministry of Finance/States) confirm
tax and stamp-duty neutrality on conversion. Most Indian AIFs are structured as
trusts. The conversion option introduced by the Bill remains theoretical unless the
consent threshold is workable, trustee liability is bounded, and the conversion is tax-
neutral."

17(3).4.5 "HUFs constitute an established and large category of investors under
the SEBI AIF framework. This investor category has played an important role in
channeling long term capital into startups and should continue to be supported within
the revised framework. Aligns with existing SEBI framework and removes regulatory
inconsistency. The HUFs should be continued to be allowed to participate under the
LLP structure as Contributors/Limited Partners but not be made the Administrative in
an LLP as may be required by law."

17(3).4.6 "Fifth Schedule, Paragraph 3 (as proposed): "A specified trust, and its
schemes, may apply to convert into limited liability partnership(s) in accordance with
this Schedule, only if the partners of the limited liability partnership into which the
specified trust is to be converted are trustees Investors of such specified trust, its
schemes and authorised representatives of Manager of the Alternative Investment
Fund, who shall be admitted as a Designated Partner, and no one else."

1. Where an AIF is established in the form of a trust, the trustee plays a role in its
governance and overall supervision and day to day operations are delegated to

                                                      109
Investment Manager. Upon conversion of such a trust into an LLP, the trustee
structure would cease to exist, and accordingly, trustees would no longer have any
role in the functioning of the AIF.

2. The current draft's "and no one else" language, when combined with "trustees,"
would exclude both the investors and the Manager from the converted LLP. This
makes the conversion practically impossible: the trust converts into an LLP whose
only partners are the former trustees, while the actual capital contributors and the
managing entity have no legal standing in the new vehicle.

3. The requirement that the Manager be admitted as a Designated Partner is a
structural necessity. Under Section 7(1) of the LLP Act, 2008, every LLP must have
at least two Designated Partners, at least one of whom must be a resident in India.
The Manager, as the entity with operational control, regulatory accountability, and
investment decision-making authority, is the only entity that can meaningfully
discharge the Designated Partner's compliance obligations under the LLP Act.
Without this, the converted LLP would need to appoint an unrelated Designated
Partner with no connection to the fund's management - an outcome that may
compromise governance standards."

17(3).4.7 "Replace Para 3: on conversion, the trustee, sponsor or manager
becomes (or nominates) a Designated Partner, and the investors are admitted as
Partners other than Designated Partners, with flexibility for a Manager or Sponsor to
also hold an investor interest.

Replace paragraph 3 with: "A Specified Trust may apply to convert into a Limited
Liability Partnership in accordance with this Schedule if, upon conversion, the
trustee, sponsor, investment manager, manager or such other person, as may be
prescribed, becomes or nominates a Designated Partner, and the investors of the
specified trust are admitted or recognised as partners other than Designated
Partners, in accordance with the limited liability partnership agreement and
applicable regulations or approvals of the Securities and Exchange Board of India or
the International Financial Services Centres Authority, as the case may be. Provided
that nothing contained in this paragraph shall prevent any trustee, sponsor,
investment manager, manager, Designated Partner or their nominees or affiliates
from also holding an investor interest or other economic interest in the limited liability
partnership, where permitted under the limited liability partnership agreement and
applicable regulations or approvals of the Securities and Exchange Board of India or
the International Financial Services Centres Authority, as the case may be.

"Trustees and no one else" leaves investors out of their own fund. It is suggested
that investors are admitted as non-designated partners, making the conversion route
more feasible for a Fund."

17(3).4.8  Suggested modification to the section as follows: 3. Eligibility
                                               110
Justification for conversion.--A specified trust may apply to convert into a limited
liability partnership in accordance with this Schedule, only if the partners of the
limited liability partnership into which the specified trust is to be converted, are
investors of such specified trust and no one else. Trustees primarily act in a fiduciary
and managerial capacity and do not ordinarily hold the beneficial economic interest
in the trust property. The investors (or beneficiaries), on the other hand, are the
persons who possess such economic interest and are therefore the appropriate
persons to become partners upon conversion. This approach is also consistent with
the conversion framework for companies under the Fourth Schedule to the LLP Act,
where the shareholder, the owners of the company, become partners of the LLP,
rather than the directors, who merely manage the affairs of the company. On the
same principle, upon conversion of a specified trust into an LLP, the beneficiary
investors, and not the trustees, should be eligible to become partners of the LLP.

17(3).4.9 The Fifth Schedule requires that partners of an LLP converted from a
specified trust be only the trustees. This vests the entire AIF corpus with a fiduciary
holding no economic interest, and where a single corporate trustee administers the
fund, the converted LLP falls below the statutory minimum of two partners. It is
suggested that the permitted partners be widened to also include the sponsor, the
investment manager, and contributors of the fund who consent to be admitted as
partners.

17(3).4.10 "The new Section 57A inter alia proposes that a 'specified trust'
registered with SEBI or IFSCA may convert into LLP in accordance with the new
Fifth Schedule. Suggestion: In Paragraph 3 of the Proposed Fifth Schedule, the word
"trustees" may be replaced with "investors" and also "Managers" may be permitted to
become "Partners". Proposed revised draft clause: Para 3 of the proposed Fifth
Schedule: "Eligibility for conversion.--A specified trust may apply to convert into a
limited liability partnership in accordance with this Schedule, only if the partners of
the limited liability partnership into which the specified trust is to be converted, are
investors in such specified trust and the manager of such specified trust and no one
else."

(i) Under the Indian Trusts Act, 1882, a trust is a legal obligation where an owner (the
settlor) transfers property to a trustee. The trustee holds this property to manage it
for the exclusive benefit of a third party, known as the beneficiary. Hence, the
appointment of trustees is a statutory requirement for establishing a trust under the
Indian Trusts Act, 1882.

(ii) In terms of SEBI (AIF) Regulations, 2012, a "trust" means a trust established
under the Indian Trusts Act, 1882 or under an Act of Parliament or State Legislation.

(iii) Furthermore, in terms of AIF Regulations, 2012, the `Manager' means any person
or entity who is appointed by AIF to manage its investments. Manager is entrusted
with running the AIF as per SEBI and IFSCA Regulations.

                                                      111
(iv) Investors are the actual beneficiaries of a trust because they hold the financial
interest in the trust's assets. Hence, investors are the rightful persons who should
continue as partners in the subsequent LLP upon the conversion of the trust vehicle
into LLP.

(v) Para 3 of the proposed Fifth Schedule provides that only `trustees' can become
partners of the LLP upon conversion. This would leave `investors' (actual
beneficiaries) in trust, and `manager' (entrusted with the management) out of the LLP
structure.

(vi) Accordingly, it is suggested that word "trustees" may be replaced with "investors"
and "Managers" may be allowed to become partners in LLP upon conversion."

17(3).4.11 Typically, in the case of Alternate Investment Funds (AIFs), the
trustees do not have any capital to contribute and therefore, this mechanism/
eligibility where trustees need to become partners may need a change. Our
suggestion would be to have the General Partner to be the Designated Partners
(DPs), including a nominee (where there is one) with the other investors inducted as
partners upon conversion. Alternatively, if Trustees or Manager of the AIF are to be
included as DPs, then there should be suitable amendments to the LLP Act to
include no capital commitments by such DPs. The proposal to ensure that the
current construct from an AIF/ Fund perspective is taken into consideration.

17(3).4.12 "Paragraph 3 requires that partners of the resulting LLP be the trustees
"and no one else", which, absent an express bridge, casts doubt on when economic
investors may become partners - the very purpose of the conversion for AIF
structures."

17(3).5    Examination by the Committee:

17(3).5.1 In regard to the suggestion at para 17(3).4.1 relating to inclusion of
beneficiaries/investors as eligible partners in the converted limited liability
partnership, the Ministry has stated:

"The provision was made in the context of providing ease of incorporation and
conversion of such trusts into LLPs. This would obviate the requirement of
conducting KYC of all the investors at the time of incorporation of an LLP, which may
be a large number. The investors could then be onboarded by an amendment in the
LLP agreement consequent to the incorporation. Suggestion received is being

17(3).5.2  In regard to the suggestion at para 17(3).4.2 relating to eligibility of all
                                               112
categories of AIF investors, including Hindu Undivided Families (HUFs) and similar
entities, to become partners in the converted limited liability partnership, the Ministry
has stated:

"Rule 22B of the LLP Rules, 2009 caters to such situations, which allows a
person/entity to hold beneficial interest in the contribution without being a partner,
provided adequate disclosures are made in this regard."

17(3).5.3 In regard to the suggestion at para 17(3).4.3 relating to recognising
investors and the Manager as partners in the converted limited liability partnership,
the Ministry stated:

"Suggestion received is being examined in consultations with DEA, SEBI, IFSCA."

17(3).5.4 In regard to the suggestion at para 17(3).4.4 relating to providing value-
based investor consent, investor onboarding and tax neutrality in the conversion
framework, the Ministry has stated:

"The threshold for consent is being changed 3/4th in terms of value. The AIF trust is
proposed to be given option to convert either through all trustees, or through all
managers or through partners. There is also a requirement of prior NOC of
SEBI/IFSCA. Where the conversion takes place through trustees or managers, there
will be an obligation to onboard all the investors within 30 days. Necessary

17(3).5.5 In regard to the suggestion at para 17(3).4.5 relating to continuation of
participation of Hindu Undivided Families (HUFs) in the converted limited liability
partnership, the Ministry has stated:

"Rule 22B of the LLP Rules, 2009 caters to such situations, which allows a
person/entity to hold beneficial interest in the contribution without being a partner,
provided adequate disclosures are made in this regard."

17(3).5.6 In regard to the suggestions contained in paras 17(3).4.6 to 17(3).4.12
relating to participation of trustees, managers and investors in the conversion
framework, recognition of managers and investors as partners, appointment of

                                                      113
designated partners, onboarding of investors after conversion and other
consequential changes to facilitate the conversion of specified trusts into limited
liability partnerships, the Ministry has stated:

"An amendment is being proposed whereby, the AIF trust is proposed to be given
option to convert either through all trustees, or through all managers or through
partners. There is also a requirement of prior NOC of SEBI/IFSCA. Where the
conversion takes place through trustees or managers, there will be an obligation to
onboard all the investors within 30 days."

17(3).5.7 Further, during the oral evidence of the Ministry of Corporate Affairs on
16th July, 2026, the representative of the Ministry elaborated upon the rationale for
the proposed amendments to the conversion framework for specified trusts and
clarified its revised position as follows:

"Sir, in the LLP amendments, one of the clauses that attracted the highest number of
suggestions is this one. Section 57A provides for the conversion of a specified trust
into a limited liability partnership. This is basically aimed at enabling AIF trusts
registered with SEBI or IFSCA to convert into AIF LLPs. The major suggestions were
as follows. As I already mentioned, we had initially proposed that the trustees would
become partners and effect the conversion. Normally, an AIF has many investors. If
all of them had to complete KYC requirements during conversion, it would become
cumbersome for the AIF trust to convert into an AIF LLP. That is why we proposed
that the trustees would affect the conversion and become partners initially.
Subsequently, the investors in the AIF would become partners in the LLP. However,
stakeholders requested that all possible options be provided. Accordingly, after
discussions with IVCA, the industry body, along with DEA, IFSCA, and SEBI, we
agreed to make the necessary changes. Apart from trustees, we also proposed to
include investors and managers. Thus, the managers, investors, or trustees can
affect the conversion, leaving the decision to the particular AIF. For example, if a
trust has 200 investors, it may decide to undertake the conversion through the
manager or the trustees, and later amend the LLP agreement to include all the
partners. That is why we made the provision more flexible."

17(3).5.8 When the Committee sought clarification regarding the requirement of
consent for conversion under the proposed framework particularly where a specified
trust has trustees, managers and investors and desired to know how the conversion
would be effected in the event of a difference of opinion among them. The
representatives of the Ministry clarified as follows:

                                                      114
"In the initial the initial schedule, we mentioned that the trustee will affect the transfer.
The requirement is 75, approval from 75 per cent of the investors. A suggestion has
come, do no put as "investors", you put us "value of the investors". It is because 75
per cent of the value is mentioned for all approvals in AIF in SEBI and IFSCA
regulations. So, we have already included it. The second thing which I would like to
mention is this. You rightly said, Sir, then the particular trust will decide, they will do
this particular conversion through manager or investors or trustees. That is up to
them. But the requirement of approval, even whatever may be the methodology they
are going to adopt, either to the trustee or manager or investor, the requirement of
approval is always 75 per cent of the value of the investors. So, that is going to
remain the same. When the conversion happens through investors, for example, all
the investors want to become partners. In the conversion time itself, all the investors
will become partners. Some of the AIF can take a decision. They want to do the
transfer that affects the conversion through trustee. Once the trustee becomes
partner in the LLP, then they will modify the partnership agreement and then include
all the investors as partners. That is already provided. There is no problem in that.
So, that is how it is being. It has been discussed with the stakeholders and also, they
all agreed with this formulation."

17(3).6  Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

17(3).6.1 The Committee note that para 3 of the proposed Fifth Schedule
prescribes the eligibility conditions for conversion of a specified trust into a
limited liability partnership. The Committee have carefully considered the views
of the stakeholders, the written replies furnished by the Ministry and the
clarifications given during the oral evidence. The Committee also note that the
original provision restricted eligibility for conversion to cases where the
partners of the resulting limited liability partnership were only the trustees of
the specified trust.

17(3).6.2 During the examination of the Bill, several stakeholders submitted
that the proposed restriction did not adequately reflect the operational
structure of Alternative Investment Funds. They further stated that limiting
eligibility only to trustees excluded managers and investors from the
conversion framework at the threshold stage, thereby making the proposed
conversion mechanism less practical and flexible. The Committee are of the
considered view that omission of the said restriction would provide the
necessary flexibility in the conversion process and substantially address the
concerns expressed by the stakeholders. Accordingly, the Committee

                                                      115
recommend that para 3 of the proposed Fifth Schedule be amended by omitting
the following:

"only if the partners of the limited liability partnership into which the specified
trust is to be converted, are trustees of such specified trust and no one else."

17(3).6.3 The Committee further are of the view that requiring a prior No
Objection Certificate from the Securities and Exchange Board of India or the
International Financial Services Centres Authority, as the case may be, would
ensure that the conversion process remains subject to appropriate regulatory
oversight. Accordingly, the Committee recommend that para 3 of the proposed
Fifth Schedule be amended by inserting, after the words "in accordance with
this Schedule", the following:

"only if the Securities and Exchange Board of India, or by the International
Financial Services Centres Authority, as the case may be, has given their no
objection to such conversion"

17(4) Para 4 of Clause 17 seeks to specify the statements, documents and
investor consent required for conversion.

17(4).1 Provision proposed in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

4. Statements to be filed.--A specified trust may apply to convert into a limited
liability partnership by filing with the Registrar,--

(a) a statement by all of its trustees in such form and manner and accompanied by
such fee, as may be prescribed, containing the following particulars, namely:--

(i) the name and registration number, if applicable, of the specified trust;

(ii) the date on which the specified trust was established under the Indian Trusts
Act, 1882 (2 of 1882) or under a Central Act or State Act;

(iii) the date on which the specified trust was registered with the Securities and
Exchange Board of India, or by the International Financial Services Centres
Authority, as the case may be, in terms of the relevant regulations issued in this

                                                      116
regard; and

(iv) the consent of three-fourths of the investors of the trust; and

(b) the incorporation document and statement referred to in section 11.

17(4).2      Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (Limited Liability

Partnership Act, 2008):

A new provision has been proposed in the Bill by inserting the Fifth Schedule under
Section 57A of the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008, to regulate the conversion
of specified trusts into limited liability partnerships.

17(4).3      Reasons / Justification given by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs

for the proposed provision:

"This is the corresponding schedule to the amendments proposed in section 23, 25,
and 58."

17(4).4      Important Views/Suggestions given by Experts/Stakeholders:

17(4).4.1 Pertaining to Clause 17(4), the statements that need to be filed should
also include the list of beneficiaries and their beneficial interest in the specified trust,
list of designated partner(s) and such other information as maybe required by the
Registrar. The inclusion of the list of beneficiaries and their respective beneficial
interests is essential to ensure continuity of economic ownership and transparency in
the conversion process, given that beneficiaries represent the true economic
stakeholders in a trust structure. This disclosure enables the Registrar to verify that
the conversion appropriately reflects underlying ownership and that stakeholder
interests are preserved. Further, requiring details of the designated partners ensures
regulatory clarity on governance and control of the resulting LLP post-conversion.

17(4).4.2 It was recommended that the clauses be retained, subject to the
following modifications: (i) in paragraph 4(a)(iv) of the Fifth Schedule, for "the
consent of three-fourths of the investors of the trust", substitute "the consent of
investors holding not less than three-fourths in value of the interests in the trust"; (ii)
insert an enabling paragraph permitting admission of investors as partners
simultaneously with, or immediately upon, conversion, subject to conditions as may
be prescribed; and (iii) the Committee may recommend to the Government that
consequential amendments be moved to section 47 of the Income-Tax Act, 2025, to
confer tax neutrality on such conversion, without which the provision may remain a

                                                      117
dead letter. (i) A head-count consent test is unworkable for widely-held AIFs and
inconsistent with the value-based approach the Bill itself adopts in Clause 69.

17(4).5  Examination by the Committee:

17(4).5.1 Regarding suggestion relating to inclusion of the list of beneficiaries,
their beneficial interests and the designated partners among the statements required
to be filed for conversion, the Ministry has stated:

"Suggestion received is being examined in consultations with DEA, SEBI, IFSCA. As
regards, the disclosure of beneficial interest, there are separate requirements in the
LLP rules for its disclosure, which may take place consequent to incorporation."

17(4).5.2 On the suggestion relating to prescribing value-based investor consent
for conversion under paragraph 4(a)(iv), the Ministry has stated:

"Value based consent of the investors is being considered."

17(4).6  Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

17(4).6.1 The Committee note that para 4 of the proposed Fifth Schedule
prescribes the statements and documents required to be filed for conversion of
a specified trust into a limited liability partnership. After considering the views
expressed by the stakeholders, the written replies furnished by the Ministry
and the clarifications given during the oral evidence, the Committee
recommend that para 4 of the proposed Fifth Schedule be adopted subject to
the following amendments.

The Committee are of the opinion that the application for conversion should be
filed only by a person duly authorised by investors holding not less than three-
fourths in value. Such a requirement would ensure that the application is
instituted only with the authority of the investors competent to approve the
proposed conversion. Accordingly, the Committee recommend that in
paragraph 4(a) of the proposed Fifth Schedule, for the words "a statement by
all of its trustees", the words "a statement by the applicant duly authorised by

                                                      118
the investors representing not less than three-fourth in value of the
investments in the specified trust" shall be substituted.

17(4).6.2 The Committee are also of the view that conversion of specified
trusts regulated by the Securities and Exchange Board of India or the
International Financial Services Centres Authority should remain subject to
appropriate regulatory oversight. In view of the Committee's recommendation
that conversion should be undertaken only after obtaining a prior No Objection
Certificate from the concerned regulator, the Committee consider it necessary
that the application for conversion should also be accompanied by a copy of
such No Objection Certificate. Accordingly, the Committee recommend that
paragraph 4(a) of the proposed Fifth Schedule be amended by inserting the
following new clause after clause (ii):

"(iia) a copy of the no objection referred to in paragraph 3;

17(4).6.3 The Committee feel that the application should clearly disclose the
period from which the specified trust has remained subject to the regulatory
framework of the Securities and Exchange Board of India or the International
Financial Services Centres Authority, as the case may be. Such disclosure
would facilitate verification of the regulatory status of the specified trust at the
time of conversion.

The Committee, therefore, recommend that in the clause relating to the
regulatory registration of the specified trust, the provision be amended to
substitute the words "the date on which the specified trust was registered
with" with the words "the date from which the specified trust has been
registered and regulated by".

17(4).6.4 The Committee further note that stakeholders had suggested that
investor consent for conversion should be determined on the basis of the value
of their interests rather than merely their numerical strength. The Committee
are of the considered view that requiring the consent of investors holding

                                                      119
three-fourths in value would better reflect the economic interests of investors
and provide a more appropriate basis for determining investor consent in the
case of specified trusts regulated as Alternative Investment Funds.

Therefore, they recommend that in clause (a)(iv) relating to investor consent
"the consent of three-fourths of the investors of the trust;" shall be substituted
with "the consent of three-fourths of the investors in value of the trust;"

The Fifth Schedule (inserted by Clause 17) permits the Registrar to refuse

17(6).5  Examination by the Committee:

refusal before the Tribunal and also empowers the Registrar to require
verification of the prescribed documents. The Committee further note the
concern expressed by a stakeholder that despite the facility of resubmission,
an applicant may be apprehensive of refusal of registration without a reasoned
order. The Committee also note the Ministry's clarification that there is a
mechanism for resubmission of forms in cases of deficiencies. The Committee,
therefore, are of the opinion that the proposed provision, read with the
appellate remedy before the Tribunal, provides adequate safeguards.
Accordingly, the Committee recommend that para 6 of the Fifth Schedule may

17(7).2  Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (Limited Liability

Partnership Act, 2008):

A new provision has been proposed in the Bill by inserting the Fifth Schedule under
Section 57A of the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008, to regulate the conversion
of specified trusts into limited liability partnerships.

17(7).3  Reasons / Justification given by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs

for the proposed provision:

"This is the corresponding schedule to the amendments proposed in section 23, 25,
and 58."

17(7).4  Important Views/Suggestions given by Experts/Stakeholders:

                                   123
17(7).4.1 The current language under clause 7(b) of the Fifth Schedule refers
that the assets, interests, etc. of the Trust shall be transferred to and shall vest in the
LLP. We suggest including language which only states that the conversion of the
Trust to the LLP is only change of legal form and all other changes due to the
change of the structure should be considered accordingly. Considering the words
`transfer' from an income tax perspective can have different implications, the use of
language as suggested could reduce any ambiguity when such structures are
eventually implemented.

17(7).4.2 "Conversion of specified trusts to LLPs is a welcome step for flexibility.
In particular, guidance is needed on how to handle fiduciary duties when, say, an
investment trust or securitization trust converts to an LLP. For example, if a trust held
assets on behalf of investors (as in Alternative Investment Funds or securitization
vehicles), upon conversion to an LLP: How are the beneficial ownership and trustee
obligations preserved? Trust structures are commonly used in financial markets (for
securitization, mutual funds, REITs/InvITs, etc.) precisely because they can ring-
fence assets and define duties in a certain way. Allowing their conversion to LLPs
may be beneficial (e.g., for operational flexibility or tax reasons), but without clear
rules, such conversions might lead to legal ambiguities. Stakeholders need to know
that, for instance, a debenture trustee trust converting into an LLP will not
compromise the security interest of lenders or that investors in an AIF structured as a
trust won't lose protections when it becomes an LLP. By clarifying these points, the
law will ensure market confidence isn't affected by the transition. It will also likely
encourage uptake of this provision, knowing that critical rights (like those in trust
deeds) remain intact post-conversion. In summary, specifying how fiduciary roles
and investor/creditor rights carry over to the successor LLP will make this reform
workable and beneficial in practice."

(7).4.3  Conversion of a firm/company into an LLP enjoys conditional tax

neutrality under section 47(xiiib) of the Income-Tax Act; the absence of a

corresponding provision for trusts would trigger capital gains and stamp implications

that defeat the reform. The vesting, continuity and trustee-liability provisions

(paragraphs 7-16) are otherwise well-drafted and consistent with the Third and

Fourth Schedules.

17(7).5  Examination by the Committee:

17(7).5.1 Regarding suggestion relating to treating conversion as a change in
legal form rather than a transfer of assets and interests, the Ministry has stated:

"Taxation related aspects cannot be clarified in this Bill. There are clear provisions to
suggest that the vesting upon conversion is by operation of law, without requiring any
execution of deed."

                   124
17(7).5.2 On the suggestion relating to the conversion framework for specified
trusts, the Ministry has submitted as follows:

"The AIF trust is proposed to be given option to convert either through all trustees, or
through all managers or through partners. There is also a requirement of prior NOC
of SEBI/IFSCA. Where the conversion takes place through trustees or managers,
there will be an obligation to onboard all the investors within 30 days. Necessary
amendment is being made in the Schedule."

17(7).6  Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

17(7).6.1 The Committee note that the para 7 of the Fifth Schedule under
Clause 17 seeks to provide that upon registration of conversion, all tangible
and intangible property, assets, interests, rights, privileges, liabilities and
obligations of the specified trust shall vest in the resulting limited liability
partnership by operation of law and that the specified trust shall stand
dissolved. The Committee further note the Ministry's clarification that such
vesting takes place by operation of law without requiring execution of any
separate deed. Having considered the views expressed by the stakeholders
and the response of the Ministry, the Committee are satisfied that the proposed
provision adequately provides for the legal consequences of conversion. In
view of this, the Committee accept para 7 of the proposed Fifth Schedule
without any modification.

17(7).6.2 The Committee, however, recommend that the Central Government
may frame suitable Rules, in consultation with the Securities and Exchange
Board of India (SEBI), the International Financial Services Centres Authority
(IFSCA) and the Registrar of Companies to ensure time-bound processing of
applications for conversion and seamless coordination amongst the concerned
authorities to facilitate timely updation of record, so as to prevent delays in
processing and to avoid hardships for entities.

17(14)  Para 14 of Clause 17 seeks to provide for continuation of existing
        appointments, authorities and powers after conversion.
