                                               CLAUSE - 32

32. Clause 32 of the Bill seeks to amend section 96 of the Companies Act,
2013.

32.1 Provision proposed in The Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

In section 96 of the principal Act, after sub-section (2), the following sub-section shall
be inserted, namely: --

"(3) A company may hold its annual general meeting physically, or through video
conferencing or other audio-visual means, either wholly or partly, in such manner
and subject to such terms and conditions, as may be prescribed:

Provided that if the number of members referred to in sub-section (2) of section 100
requisition the meeting to be held in a hybrid mode, the company shall hold the
meeting in such mode:

Provided further that every company shall hold its annual general meeting in physical
mode at least once in every three years.".

32.2 Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (The Companies Act, 2013):

96. Annual general meeting.

(1) Every company other than a One Person Company shall in each year hold in
addition to any other meetings, a general meeting as its annual general meeting and
shall specify the meeting as such in the notices calling it, and not more than fifteen
months shall elapse between the date of one annual general meeting of a company
and that of the next:

Provided that in case of the first annual general meeting, it shall be held within a
period of nine months from the date of closing of the first financial year of the
company and in any other case, within a period of six months, from the date of
closing of the financial year:

Provided further that if a company holds its first annual general meeting as aforesaid,
it shall not be necessary for the company to hold any annual general meeting in the
year of its incorporation:

                                                      245
Provided also that the Registrar may, for any special reason, extend the time within
which any annual general meeting, other than the first annual general meeting, shall
be held, by a period not exceeding three months.

(2) Every annual general meeting shall be called during business hours, that is,
between 9 a.m. and 6 p.m. on any day that is not a National Holiday and shall be
held either at the registered office of the company or at some other place within the
city, town or village in which the registered office of the company is situate:

Provided that annual general meeting of an unlisted company may be held at any
place in India if consent is given in writing or by electronic mode by all the members
in advance:

Provided further that the Central Government may exempt any company from the
provisions of this sub-section subject to such conditions as it may impose.

Explanation. --For the purposes of this sub-section, "National Holiday" means and
includes a day declared as National Holiday by the Central Government.

32.3 Reasons/Justification given by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs for the
proposed provision:

"This clause seeks to amend section 96 to enable companies to hold annual general
meetings (AGMs) physically, or through video conferencing or other audio-visual
means for ease of doing business."

32.4 Important Views/Suggestions given by Experts/Stakeholders:

Some of the important suggestions received from stakeholders are given below: -

32.4.1 Stakeholders, in separate submissions, expressed broad support for the
proposed amendment, as facilitating modern, flexible corporate governance and
reducing compliance costs, particularly for MSMEs and small companies.

32.4.2 "It is suggested that every company should continue to hold at AGM in
physical mode, while retaining the option to provide VC/OAVM facilities in addition
thereto."

                                                      246
32.4.3 "(i) Insert a statutory proviso to Section 96 mandating "Minimum Digital
Governance Standards" including mandatory two-way audio-visual communication,
anti-spoofing authentication protocols (biometric liveness and MFA), and a 25%
platform outage automatic adjournment threshold. (ii) Modify the third proviso to let
companies hold AGMs through VC or OAVM completely at their option/discretion,
rather than forcing a physical meeting once every three years."

32.4.4 "In section 96 of the principal Act, after sub-section (2), the following sub-
section shall be inserted, namely:-- "(3) A company may hold its annual general
meeting physically, or through video conferencing or other audio-visual means, either
wholly or partly, in such manner and subject to such terms and conditions, as may be
prescribed: Provided that if the number of members referred to in sub-section (2) of
section 100 requisition the meeting to be held in a hybrid mode, or the company is a
listed company, the company shall hold the meeting in such mode: Provided further
that every company shall hold its annual general meeting in physical mode at least
once in every three years.". As an alternate, if this addition is not acceptable, it can
be prescribed that in any company where institutional investors hold more than 5%
share capital, the meeting must be held in hybrid mode."

32.4.5 "Support the formal recognition of virtual and hybrid general meetings but
recommend greater flexibility: private companies should be exempted from the rule
of holding a physical AGM once every three years; for public or listed companies, a
physical (or hybrid) meeting should be mandated only if a substantial number of
shareholders explicitly request one; and Rules should include clear minimum
standards for electronic meetings, such as real-time two-way interaction, secure
participant authentication, and automatic adjournment if a quarter of participants lose
connection due to technical problems."

32.4.6 "AGM and EGM may continue to be conducted in virtual or hybrid mode as
applicable. The requirement of holding one physical meeting every three years is
difficult to comply with, given that the company is a Canadian joint venture; there is
no difficulty in conducting meetings virtually, as it is more convenient for the
stakeholders located abroad."

32.4.7 "Rules under these sections be framed in consultation with SEBI and aligned
with SEBI (LODR) Regulations, prescribing uniform norms for hybrid/virtual
meetings, quorum determination and verification in electronic settings, and
recording/disclosure/archiving of proceedings, along with integrity safeguards for
remote e-voting. The RTA of a company and its e-voting service provider should be
separate and independent entities, with no common control, to preserve secrecy,
integrity, non-repudiation and independent auditability; the role of depositories as
secure, auditable e-voting and authentication infrastructure providers should also be
expressly recognised."

32.4.8 "The requirement of holding the AGM in physical mode atleast once in every
three years be deleted altogether, so that companies have full flexibility to determine

                                                      247
the mode of AGM (physical/virtual/hybrid) based on their own operational and
shareholder considerations."

32.4.9 "A narrow exception to the triennial physical-AGM proviso for a wholly-owned
subsidiary, a One Person Company, or a company that has obtained the consent of
all voting members, while leaving the requisition right and the flexibility otherwise
introduced by the Bill untouched. Separately recommends that rules be framed to let
a remote shareholder attend, vote, and ask a question, with a reliable record, and a
clear process for a lost connection during a vote, plus model formats and FAQs."

32.4.10 "Recommends removal of the residual mandatory-physical-meeting
requirement (once in three years) specifically for private companies with fewer than
50 members, as one of ARIA's four clause-specific ease-of-doing-business
suggestions."

32.4.11 "Requests reconsideration of the mandatory-physical-AGM-once-in-three-
years requirement in the second proviso to new Section 96(3), on the basis that
members already have a statutory right to request a hybrid meeting."

32.4.12 "The blanket physical-AGM requirement (once in every three years) be
limited to a prescribed class of companies; the Central Government may be
empowered to exempt closely-held entities (e.g., closely-held private companies,
wholly-owned subsidiaries and joint venture companies with a small shareholder
base) from convening the physical AGM mandatorily."

32.4.13 "A proviso may be inserted inter-alia stating: "Provided that the interval
between two consecutive physical annual general meetings shall not exceed a
period of two calendar years.""

32.4.14 "The proposed second proviso may be reviewed and companies should be
permitted to determine the appropriate mode of conducting their AGMs, subject to
adequate safeguards for shareholder participation and voting, without a mandatory
requirement to hold a physical AGM once every three years."

32.4.15 "Companies with fewer than 100-200 members be permitted to hold AGMs
through VC/OAVM on a permanent basis, unless members holding at least 10% of
voting power require a physical meeting; that listed and other prescribed large public
companies be mandated to provide a hybrid meeting facility; that a comprehensive
statutory framework govern electronic attendance, e-voting, digital proxies and digital
inspection of statutory records; and that electronic proof of delivery generated
through MCA-recognised systems be deemed conclusive evidence of service unless
rebutted by the recipient. (The related suggestion on penal consequences for minor
procedural deviations is dealt with separately under Clause 33.)"

                                                      248
32.4.16 "For listed companies: hybrid AGMs should form part of the minimum
meeting standard, rather than depending on shareholders first meeting a requisition
threshold; virtual-only AGMs should be permitted only in genuinely exceptional
circumstances (such as public health, safety or emergency) that make a physical or
hybrid meeting impracticable, with a clear board explanation; any authority to hold
virtual-only AGMs should be subject to independent shareholder approval, be time-
bound and periodically renewed, and be accompanied by clear disclosure of when it
may be used. Safeguards should include the ability to ask questions and vote in real
time, clear procedures for verifying shareholder identity and ownership, equal
treatment of online and in-person participants, real-time video of directors and
management, transparent rules on question moderation and disclosure of questions
and answers after the meeting, contingency plans for technology failure, and secure
and reliable authentication, voting and record-keeping systems. Voting should also
remain open throughout the meeting so that members who participate can vote once
the discussion has concluded."

32.4.17 "It is suggested that companies should have an option to conduct all annual
general meetings through virtual or hybrid means."

32.4.18 "Recommends amendments to sections 96, 99, 100 and 101 of the
Companies Act, 2013 to embed express safeguards for hybrid/virtual meetings,
including real-time questions, transparency on questions put forward, and
contingency planning for platform malfunction, with voting kept open during the
meeting, and strongly urges against reducing the notice period for any shareholder
meeting, including wholly virtual AGMs or EGMs, from 21 days to seven days."

32.4.19 "Exempt closely-held private companies and small companies from
mandatory physical AGM."

32.4.20 "The Second Proviso to the proposed amendment should be deleted."

32.4.21 "Decision of holding AGM by physical, virtual or hybrid mode should be left
to the discretion of the Board, subject to requisition by shareholders."

32.4.22 "Recognise cryptographically signed digital minutes and video recordings as
the original legal record of board proceedings."

32.4.23 "Remove the requirement for at least one physical AGM every three years
for private companies with fewer than 50 members."

32.4.24 "Allow secure blockchain-based e-voting, digital identity verification and
smart-contract voting."

                                                      249
32.4.25 "The requirement to mandatorily conduct one physical AGM every 3 years
may be dispensed with. Companies may be provided with the flexibility to decide on
the mode of conducting general meetings (physical, virtual or hybrid), left entirely to
the discretion of the company, subject to the shareholder right to requisition a hybrid
meeting, as proposed. Certain basic standards for virtual meetings, two-way audio-
visual communication with safeguards, authentication measures to prevent identity
fraud, and automatic adjournment if a prescribed percentage of shareholders lose
connection, should be prescribed in the law itself, rather than left entirely to the
rules."

32.4.26 "Leave the mode of AGM, physical, virtual or hybrid, to the Board's
discretion. Change the mandatory physical AGM from once in 3 years to once in 5
years. It is also suggested that a clear timeline be prescribed for receipt of
requisitions from members under the proposed first proviso to Section 96(3): listed
public companies within 30 days from the end of the financial year; unlisted public
companies and private companies within 60 days from the end of the financial year."

32.4.27 "Procedures left to Rules. Codify quorum, voting, inspection in Act."

32.4.28 "Electronic service of documents reduces compliance burden but legal
certainty depends on establishing dispatch, receipt, integrity and authenticity. Rules
may prescribe electronic acknowledgement, proof of delivery, electronic logs,
preservation of records, and handling of delivery failures. MeitY supports the
initiative, subject to robust technological safeguards including participant
authentication, prevention of impersonation, secure e-voting, audit logs and
cybersecurity protections."

32.4.29 "AGMs and EGMs may be held physically, virtually, or in hybrid mode, at the
company's discretion. Mandatory physical AGM (once every three years) may be
omitted; shareholders holding the Section 100(2) threshold may requisition a hybrid
meeting as the operative safeguard. The 7-day notice period proposed for fully virtual
EGMs may be extended to virtual AGMs as well. The postal-ballot voting window
may be decreased from 30 to 15 days. Minimum digital safeguards, two-way audio-
video, authentication, and auto-adjournment if over 25% of participants are
disconnected, may be codified."

32.4.30 "It is recommended that the clauses be retained, subject to the following
modifications: (i) insert an Explanation that the three-year period for a physical AGM
shall be reckoned from the last AGM held in physical or hybrid mode; (ii) the rules
under section 101 shall provide that a seven-day notice for a wholly-electronic EGM
shall be permissible only where e-voting or postal ballot is offered to all members;
and (iii) hybrid mode be the default prescription for the top listed companies,
consistent with SEBI's direction of travel."

                                                      250
32.4.31 "For small companies, particularly family run MSMEs, Board and ownership
often coincide and decisions are taken continuously in the course of operations.
Stakeholders therefore have requested that the formal Board meeting requirement
be rationalised."

32.4.32 "The objective should be to ensure universal shareholder participation while
maintaining the integrity of the voting process. Instead of restricting the use of
electronic voting due to connectivity challenges in certain areas, suitable facilitative
measures may be prescribed by the Government or the regulator to address such
practical difficulties."

32.4.33 "The mandatory requirement to hold a physical AGM once in three years
imposes additional compliance and administrative costs on companies, including
expenses related to venue, logistics, travel, security, and other arrangements,
particularly for companies with a geographically dispersed shareholder base, and
may also restrict wider participation by members unable to attend due to
geographical, health, professional, or other constraints."

32.4.34 "Delete only the newly inserted second proviso requiring every company to
hold an AGM in physical mode at least once in every three years, since the newly
inserted first proviso already enables members to requisition the meeting to be held
in a hybrid mode. It is also suggested that the e-AGM notice specify the detailed
procedure for holding the AGM through VC/OAVM and voting, and a query is raised
on the SOP or methodology for conducting an Annual General Meeting through
VC/OAVM."

32.4.35 "The rules under these sections be framed in consultation with SEBI and
aligned with SEBI (LODR) Regulations, prescribing uniform norms for hybrid/virtual
meetings, quorum determination and verification in electronic settings,
recording/disclosure/archiving of proceedings, and integrity safeguards for remote e-
voting. The RTA of a company and its e-voting service provider should be separate
and independent entities, with no common control; the role of depositories as secure,
auditable e-voting and authentication infrastructure providers should be expressly
recognised."

32.4.36 "Recommends confining the mandatory once-in-three-years physical AGM to
listed and large unlisted public companies, exempting small companies, OPCs, start-
ups and wholly closely-held private companies, noting that Delaware, Singapore and
the UK impose no periodic physical-meeting mandate at all."

32.4.37 "Clauses 32 and 34 enable companies to hold AGMs/EGMs wholly or partly
through video conferencing but do not comprehensively protect the interests of
virtual attendees. It is suggested that shareholders be guaranteed a reasonable
opportunity to see, listen, speak and vote at virtual meetings, that the technology
used be capable of accommodating effective participation irrespective of the number

                                                      251
of participants, that video recordings, chat logs and transcripts of such meetings be
made mandatorily available to members, and that statistics on virtual versus in-
person participation be maintained and disclosed regularly."

32.5 Examination by the Committee:

Replies of the Ministry corresponding to the suggestions are as follows:

32.5.1 The Ministry acknowledged that several stakeholders, as recorded at
paragraph 32.4.1 above, were in support of the proposed amendment, and stated
that it did not call for any change.

32.5.2 Responding to a suggestion at paragraph 32.4.2 above that every company
should continue to hold its AGM in physical mode, with VC/OAVM facilities to be
provided only in addition thereto, the Ministry, in its written submission, stated that
the proposed amendment gives companies the flexibility to hold AGMs physically, via
VC/OAVM, or in hybrid mode, thereby reducing compliance costs and easing
burdens on companies and shareholders; that adequate safeguards for shareholder
engagement are already built in, since the first proviso allows members themselves,
through the existing requisition mechanism under sub-section (2) of section 100, to
require a hybrid-mode meeting where desired; and that the provision may
accordingly be retained without any change.

32.5.3 Addressing suggestions at paragraphs 32.4.3, 32.4.4, 32.4.5 and 32.4.13
above, through separate submissions seeking statutory Minimum Digital Governance
Standards for virtual meetings, extension of the hybrid-mode requirement to listed
companies or wherever institutional investors hold more than 5% of share capital,
exemption of private companies from the triennial physical-AGM requirement, and a
cap of two calendar years on the interval between two physical AGMs, the Ministry,
in its written submission, stated that this would be appropriately dealt with during the
framing of subordinate legislation, since sub-section (3) of the amended section 96
already provides that a company may hold its AGM through VC/OAVM "in such
manner and subject to such terms and conditions, as may be prescribed", enabling

                                                      252
the Central Government to prescribe technical and procedural safeguards as
required; and that, as regards the third proviso, section 96 would be amended to
allow virtual/hybrid AGMs "in such manner...as may be prescribed", subject to every
company holding its AGM in physical or hybrid mode at least once in every three
years.

32.5.4 On the suggestions at paragraphs 32.4.6, 32.4.8 to 32.4.12, 32.4.14 and
32.4.15 above, each seeking that the requirement of a mandatory physical AGM
once every three years be relaxed, limited to a prescribed class of companies, or
removed altogether, leaving companies flexibility to determine the mode of the AGM
subject to the shareholders' right to requisition a hybrid meeting, the Ministry noted
that section 96 would be amended to allow virtual/hybrid AGMs "in such manner...as
may be prescribed", subject to every company holding its AGM in physical or hybrid
mode at least once in every three years, and that the Bill would be modified
accordingly.

32.5.5 On the suggestion at paragraph 32.4.17 above, that companies should have
an option to conduct all annual general meetings through virtual or hybrid means, the
Ministry noted that section 96 would be amended to allow virtual/hybrid AGMs "in
such manner...as may be prescribed", subject to every company holding its AGM in
physical or hybrid mode at least once in every three years, and that the Bill would be
modified accordingly.

32.5.6 In response to a suggestion at paragraph 32.4.7 above that rules for
hybrid/virtual meetings be framed in consultation with SEBI and aligned with SEBI
(LODR) Regulations, that the RTA and the e-voting service provider be kept
independent of each other, and that depositories be expressly recognised as
authentication infrastructure providers, the Ministry, in its written submission, stated
that section 96 would be amended to allow virtual/hybrid AGMs "in such manner...as
may be prescribed", subject to every company holding its AGM in physical or hybrid
mode at least once in every three years, and that the Bill would be modified
accordingly; and that the procedural and operational framework for electronic and
hybrid meetings, remote e-voting and associated technological safeguards would be

                                                      253
appropriately addressed through the Rules and other applicable regulatory
framework, in consultation with the concerned regulators, wherever necessary.

32.5.7 Responding to a suggestion at paragraph 32.4.16 above that, for listed
companies, hybrid AGMs form the minimum meeting standard rather than depending
on a requisition threshold, that virtual-only AGMs be permitted only in genuinely
exceptional circumstances subject to safeguards, and that EGMs of listed companies
conducted wholly by video conferencing or OAVM be called on a notice of not less
than fifteen days rather than seven (a related concern also raised under Clause 35),
the Ministry, in its written submission, stated that, for listed companies, EGMs held
wholly by video conferencing or OAVM under the new section 100(7) would be
required to be called by giving a notice of not less than fifteen days or such other
period as may be prescribed, and that the Bill would be modified accordingly.

32.5.8 Addressing a suggestion at paragraph 32.4.18 above, submitted by a
stakeholder, favouring hybrid meetings over virtual-only meetings, subject to defined
participation safeguards, and opposing any reduction of the notice period for
shareholder meetings to seven days, the Ministry noted that the suggestion
regarding participation safeguards for virtual/hybrid meetings is duly noted and will
be considered at the appropriate rule-making stage; and that, as regards the notice
period, for listed companies, an extraordinary general meeting held wholly through
video conferencing or other audio-visual means under the new section 100(7) would
be called by giving a notice of not less than fifteen days, or such other period as may
be prescribed.

32.5.9 With respect to suggestions at paragraphs 32.4.19, 32.4.21, 32.4.22, 32.4.24,
32.4.26 and 32.4.27 above, seeking exemption of closely-held private and small
companies from the mandatory physical-AGM requirement, deletion of the second
proviso, and that the mode of the AGM be left to the Board's/company's discretion,
the Ministry, in its written submission, stated that section 96 would be amended to
allow virtual/hybrid AGMs "in such manner...as may be prescribed", subject to every
company holding its AGM in physical or hybrid mode at least once in every three
years. In respect of the suggestion at paragraph 32.4.30 above, the Ministry

                                                      254
additionally noted that the suggestion regarding standards for virtual meetings would
be considered appropriately during the framing of subordinate legislation.

32.5.10 In response to suggestions at paragraphs 32.4.23, 32.4.25 and 32.4.28
above, seeking recognition of cryptographically signed digital minutes and
blockchain-based e-voting as legal records, and codification of quorum, voting and
inspection procedures in the Act itself, the Ministry noted that this suggestion would
be considered appropriately during the framing of subordinate legislation, since sub-
section (3) of the amended section 96 already provides that a company may hold its
AGM through VC/OAVM "in such manner and subject to such terms and conditions,
as may be prescribed".

32.5.11 Responding to a suggestion at paragraph 32.4.28 above that, while
electronic service of documents reduces the compliance burden, the Rules should
prescribe safeguards for participant authentication, secure e-voting, audit trails and
cyber security, the Ministry, in its written submission, stated that this suggestion
would be considered appropriately during the framing of subordinate legislation,
since the proposed amendments provide an enabling framework for holding general
meetings electronically and for the electronic service of documents; and that the
stakeholder's suggestions, relating to the operational aspects of the provision, would
be considered as appropriate while framing the relevant Rules, the provision being
retained without change.

32.5.12 Addressing suggestions at paragraphs 32.4.29 and 32.4.30 above, seeking,
inter alia, that the mode of AGMs/EGMs be left to the company's discretion, that the
mandatory triennial physical AGM be omitted, and clarifications on notice periods for
electronic meetings, the Ministry, in its written submission, stated that section 96
would be amended to allow virtual/hybrid AGMs "in such manner...as may be
prescribed", subject to every company holding its AGM in physical or hybrid mode at
least once in every three years; that, as regards EGMs, the suggestion would be
considered appropriately during the framing of subordinate legislation; and that, as
regards the applicability of a seven-day notice period to AGMs, since the business
transacted at an AGM includes matters of "Ordinary Business", the existing twenty-

                                                      255
one-day notice period would be retained irrespective of the mode in which the AGM
is held.

32.5.13 In reply to suggestions at paragraphs 32.4.31 to 32.4.34 above, seeking the
option to conduct all AGMs virtually or in hybrid mode, rationalisation of Board-
meeting requirements for small/family-run MSMEs, facilitative measures for
connectivity challenges in e-voting, and reconsideration of the mandatory physical-
AGM requirement generally, the Ministry submitted that it is proposed to amend
section 96 to permit companies to hold AGMs in physical, virtual, or hybrid mode,
with the requirement that every company hold an AGM in physical or hybrid mode at
least once every three years.

32.5.14 With respect to a suggestion, similar to that at paragraph 32.4.7 above, that
rules for hybrid/virtual meetings be framed in consultation with SEBI and aligned with
SEBI (LODR) Regulations, with functional separation between the RTA and the e-
voting service provider and express recognition of depositories as authentication
infrastructure providers, the Ministry clarified that this would be appropriately dealt
with during the framing of subordinate legislation.

32.5.15 On the suggestion at paragraph 32.4.36 above that the mandatory once-in-
three-years physical-AGM requirement be confined to listed and large unlisted public
companies, exempting small companies, OPCs, start-ups and wholly closely-held
private companies, the Ministry noted that it accepted the suggestion in principle and
proposed to amend section 96 to permit companies to hold AGMs in physical, virtual,
or hybrid mode, with the requirement that every company hold an AGM in physical or
hybrid mode at least once every three years, and that a new proviso would be
inserted to provide for a gap of at least two years between such AGMs.

32.5.16 In response to a suggestion at paragraph 32.4.37 above that shareholders
attending virtual meetings under Clauses 32 and 34 be guaranteed a reasonable
opportunity to see, listen, speak and vote, that recordings, chat logs and transcripts
of such meetings be made available to members, and that statistics on virtual versus
in-person participation be maintained and disclosed, the Ministry noted that the

                                                      256
proposed provisions enable companies to hold general meetings through electronic
means, with the detailed procedural requirements and safeguards to be prescribed
under the relevant rules.

32.5.17 During the Clause-by-Clause examination of the Bill held with the Ministry of
Corporate Affairs on 16.7.2026, Secretary, MCA informed the Committee that AGMs
and EGMs could already be held via video conferencing under a COVID-era circular,
and the Bill now gives this statutory recognition, permitting virtual, hybrid or physical
modes; the mandatory triennial physical-AGM requirement was recast to
physical/hybrid, given the difficulty for companies with large or geographically
dispersed shareholder bases, while retaining the safeguard that a hybrid meeting
must be held if shareholders so demand.

32.5.18 On the Committee's query regarding `Minimum Digital Governance
Standards' for virtual/hybrid meetings, given uneven internet connectivity including in
the North-Eastern States, the Secretary, MCA clarified that such standards, including
the role of an independent scrutiniser and voting through NSDL/CDSL-certified
agencies, are already defined under the Companies (Management and
Administration) Rules, with immediate declaration of voting results, and that the
framework could be further improved over time.

32.5.19 On the Committee's query on whether shareholders could waive the triennial
physical-AGM requirement and whether the proviso was redundant given the existing
physical/hybrid option, the Secretary, MCA clarified that the amendment mandates a
physical AGM once every three years, but that the Ministry, in view of stakeholders'
difficulties, had agreed to provide a physical/hybrid option instead, with the
corresponding formulation to be worked out accordingly.

32.5.20 The Committee sought for further assurance of a minimum technical
reliability standard for hybrid/virtual voting and attendance. In response, the
Secretary, MCA clarified that such operational matters are already addressed in the
Rules, which govern e-voting and postal/physical ballot procedures, including
timelines, the definition of a secure electronic system, and record security; an

                                                      257
independent scrutiniser and voting only through NSDL/CDSL-certified agencies, with
periodically renewed certification, serve as key safeguards, and the Ministry would
consider further improvements.

32.5.21 On the Committee's suggestion that requirements be differentiated for small
and large companies, given that shareholder-protection concerns arise more acutely
in larger companies, the Secretary, MCA submitted that flexibility already exists,
since it is for each company to decide whether to meet physically, virtually, or in
hybrid mode, and noted that around fifteen interrelated suggestions on removing the
triennial requirement had been received in total.

32.6 Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

32.6.1 The Committee note that Clause 32 inserts a new sub-section (3) in
section 96 permitting a company to hold its annual general meeting physically,
or through video conferencing or other audio-visual means, either wholly or
partly, subject to two conditions: (i) the meeting be held in hybrid mode where
requisitioned by the number of members referred to in section 100(2), and (ii)
every company hold its annual general meeting in physical mode at least once
in every three years.

32.6.2 Acknowledging the widespread support for the enabling framework,
and recognizing its role in advancing ease of doing business and modernizing
corporate governance the Committee concur with the Ministry's explanation
that adequate safeguards for shareholder engagement already exist through
the requisition mechanism under section 100(2).

32.6.3 The Committee note that numerous stakeholders have urged
relaxation of the triennial physical-meeting mandate, highlighting the need for
flexible formats to reflect evolving technology and reduce compliance
burdens. Taking note of the Ministry's acceptance, the Committee observe that

                                                      258
the requirement may now be met through either a physical or hybrid meeting,
with a gap not exceeding two years between such meetings.

32.6.4 The Committee recognize that mandating an exclusively physical
meeting once in three years does not reflect contemporary corporate
governance practices, given the growing adoption of digital and hybrid modes
of shareholder engagement. Accordingly, the Committee recommend that the
second proviso to Section 96(3), as inserted by Clause 32, be modified to
require every company to hold its annual general meeting in physical or hybrid
mode at least once in every three years, with a gap not exceeding two years
between such meetings, consistent with the Ministry's accepted formulation.
The modified second proviso shall read as under:

"Provided further that every company shall hold its annual general meeting in
physical or hybrid mode at least once in every three years with a gap, which
shall not be more than two years between two such meetings."

32.6.5 The Committee further recommend that the revised provision be
implemented with clear guidance to companies, ensuring that hybrid meetings
are conducted in a manner that guarantees equitable participation and
transparency for all shareholders.

32.6.6 The Committee note the suggestion that Rules for hybrid/virtual
meetings be framed in consultation with SEBI and aligned with SEBI (LODR)
Regulations, and the Ministry's statement that the procedural and operational
framework for such meetings, remote e-voting and associated technological
safeguards would be appropriately addressed through the Rules, in
consultation with the concerned regulators, wherever necessary. Accordingly,
the Committee recommend that the Ministry ensure that the Rules under
section 96(3) are framed in consultation with SEBI and other concerned
regulators, wherever necessary, so as to facilitate the effective implementation
of the proposed provisions.

                                                      259
32.6.7 Subject to the modification set out in paragraph 32.6.4 above, the
Committee accept the remaining provisions of Clause 32 as proposed.

                                                      260
                                               CLAUSE - 33

33. Clause 33 of the Bill seeks to amend section 99 of the Companies Act,
2013.

33.1 Provision proposed in The Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

In section 99 of the principal Act, --

(a) in the marginal heading, for the words and figures "Punishment for default in
complying with provisions of sections 96 to 98", the words and figures "Penalty for
default in complying with provisions of section 96" shall be substituted;

(b) the words and figures "or section 97 or section 98 or in complying with any
directions of the Tribunal" shall be omitted;

(c) for the words "punishable with fine which may extend to one lakh rupees and in
the case of a continuing default, with a further fine which may extend to five
thousand rupees for every day during which such default continues", the words
"liable to a penalty of one lakh rupees and in case of continuing default, with a further
penalty of five thousand rupees for each day during which such default continues,
subject to a maximum of two lakh rupees in case of a company and fifty thousand
rupees in case of an officer who is in default" shall be substituted.

33.2 Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (The Companies Act, 2013):

99. Punishment for default in complying with provisions of sections 96 to 98.

If any default is made in holding a meeting of the company in accordance with
section 96 or section 97 or section 98 or in complying with any directions of the
Tribunal, the company and every officer of the company who is in default shall be
punishable with fine which may extend to one lakh rupees and in the case of a
continuing default, with a further fine which may extend to five thousand rupees for
every day during which such default continues.

33.3 Reasons/Justification given by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs for the
proposed provision:

                                                      261
"The amendment restructures section 99 by limiting its scope to defaults under
section 96 and replacing the existing fine-based punishment with a fixed penalty
framework, including caps for continuing defaults. This amendment is part of the
broader decriminalisation exercise under the Bill."

33.4 Important Views/Suggestions given by Experts/Stakeholders:

Some of the important suggestions of the stakeholders in this regard are furnished
below:

33.4.1 Stakeholders, in separate submissions, expressed broad support for the
proposed amendment: supporting the enabling provisions for holding AGMs and
EGMs in physical, hybrid or video conferencing mode as progressive and expected
to reduce compliance cost and improve ease of participation, particularly for small
companies and emerging enterprises; and recommending that the clause be
retained, as it recasts section 99 to confine the provision to defaults under section 96
(omitting references to sections 97, 98 and Tribunal directions) and converts the fine
into a capped civil penalty.

33.4.2 "It is suggested that a lower maximum cap of 50,000 be prescribed for Small
Companies and One Person Companies (OPCs), while retaining the proposed cap of
2 lakh for other companies, consistent with the principle of proportional regulation
for smaller corporate entities."

33.4.3 "In the same submission recommending flexibility for AGMs of small
companies, it is further suggested that minor procedural deviations, such as
technical disruptions during VC/OAVM not affecting the validity, quorum or voting at
a meeting, should not attract penal consequences if rectified within the prescribed
period."

33.4.4 "Sections 96, 99, 100 and 101 of the Companies Act, 2013 should embed
express safeguards for hybrid/virtual meetings, including real-time questions,
transparency on questions put forward, and contingency planning for platform
malfunction, with voting kept open during the meeting; and the notice period for all
shareholder meetings, AGMs as well as EGMs, should be kept at not less than
twenty-one days."

33.4.5 "Electronic service of documents reduces compliance burden, but legal
certainty depends on establishing dispatch, receipt, integrity and authenticity; MeitY
supports the initiative, subject to robust technological safeguards including
participant authentication, prevention of impersonation, secure e-voting, audit logs
and cybersecurity protections."

                                                      262
33.4.6 "AGMs and EGMs may be held physically, virtually, or in hybrid mode, at the
company's discretion. Mandatory physical AGM (once every three years) may be
omitted; shareholders holding the Section 100(2) threshold may requisition a hybrid
meeting. The 7-day notice period proposed for fully virtual EGMs may be extended to
virtual AGMs as well. The postal-ballot voting window may be decreased from 30 to
15 days. Minimum digital safeguards, two-way audio-video, authentication, and auto-
adjournment if over 25% of participants are disconnected, may be codified."

33.4.7 "It is recommended that the clauses be retained, subject to the following
modifications: (i) insert an Explanation that the three-year period for a physical AGM
shall be reckoned from the last AGM held in physical or hybrid mode; (ii) the rules
under section 101 shall provide that a seven-day notice for a wholly-electronic EGM
shall be permissible only where e-voting or postal ballot is offered to all members;
and (iii) hybrid mode be the default prescription for the top listed companies,
consistent with SEBI's direction of travel."

33.5 Examination by the Committee:

The Ministry in their written replies to the corresponding suggestions above have
submitted as under:

33.5.1 The Ministry acknowledged that several stakeholders, as recorded at
paragraph 33.4.1 above, were in support of the proposed amendment, and stated
that it did not call for any change.

33.5.2 In response to a suggestion at paragraph 33.4.2 above that a lower maximum
cap of 50,000 be prescribed for Small Companies and One Person Companies,
while retaining the proposed cap of 2 lakh for other companies, the Ministry, in its
written submission, stated that section 446B of the Companies Act, 2013 already
provides that penalties prescribed for One Person Companies, Small Companies,
start-up companies and Producer Companies (and their officers) cannot exceed one-
half of the penalty specified for other companies; that, by implication, the maximum
applicable penalty for contraventions of section 99 would accordingly be fifty
thousand rupees for such companies; and that the provision may therefore be
retained without any change.

                                                      263
33.5.3 Responding to a suggestion at paragraph 33.4.3 above that minor procedural
deviations during VC/OAVM meetings, if rectified within the prescribed period, should
not attract penal consequences, the Ministry noted that this was accepted on the
same basis as recorded in response to the corresponding suggestion under Clause
32, there being no separate reply specific to the penalty aspect of this suggestion on
record.

33.5.4 Addressing a suggestion at paragraph 33.4.4 above that sections 96, 99, 100
and 101 embed express safeguards for hybrid/virtual meetings and that the notice
period for all shareholder meetings be kept at not less than twenty-one days, the
Ministry, in its written submission, clarified that the suggestion regarding participation
safeguards for virtual/hybrid meetings is duly noted and will be considered at the
appropriate rule-making stage; and that, as regards the notice period, for listed
companies, an extraordinary general meeting held wholly through video conferencing
or other audio-visual means under the new section 100(7) would be called by giving
a notice of not less than fifteen days, or such other period as may be prescribed.

33.5.5 With respect to a suggestion at paragraph 33.4.5 above that electronic service
of documents be supported by Rules prescribing safeguards for dispatch, receipt,
integrity and authenticity, the Ministry, in its written submission, stated that this
suggestion would be considered appropriately during the framing of subordinate
legislation, since the proposed amendments provide an enabling framework for
holding general meetings electronically and for the electronic service of documents;
and that the stakeholder's suggestions, relating to the operational aspects of the
provision, would be considered as appropriate while framing the relevant Rules, the
provision being retained without change.

33.5.6 On the suggestion at paragraph 33.4.6 above that AGMs and EGMs be held
physically, virtually or in hybrid mode at the company's discretion, that the seven-day
notice period proposed for virtual EGMs be extended to virtual AGMs, and that the
postal-ballot voting window be shortened, the Ministry, in its written submission,
stated that section 96 would be amended to allow virtual/hybrid AGMs "in such
manner...as may be prescribed", subject to every company holding its AGM in

                                                      264
physical or hybrid mode at least once in every three years; that, as regards EGMs,
the suggestion would be considered appropriately during the framing of subordinate
legislation; and that, as regards the applicability of a seven-day notice period to
AGMs, since the business transacted at an AGM includes matters of "Ordinary
Business", the existing twenty-one-day notice period would be retained irrespective
of the mode in which the AGM is held.

33.5.7 In response to a suggestion at paragraph 33.4.7 above that the clauses be
retained subject to an Explanation on how the three-year period for a physical AGM
is to be reckoned, a condition on the seven-day EGM notice, and hybrid mode as the
default for top listed companies, the Ministry, in its written submission, stated that
section 96 would be amended to allow virtual/hybrid AGMs "in such manner...as may
be prescribed", subject to every company holding its AGM in physical or hybrid mode
at least once in every three years; that, as regards EGMs, the suggestion would be
considered appropriately during the framing of subordinate legislation; and that, as
regards the applicability of a seven-day notice period to AGMs, since the business
transacted at an AGM includes matters of "Ordinary Business", the existing twenty-
one-day notice period would be retained irrespective of the mode in which the AGM
is held; it further clarified that the three-year period for a physical or hybrid AGM
would be reckoned from the date of the last AGM held in physical or hybrid mode.

33.5.8 During the Clause-by-Clause examination of the Bill held with the Ministry of
Corporate Affairs on 16.7.2026, Secretary, MCA explained the rationale for the
amendment as follows:

"Sir, this is decriminalisation exercise. This is for default in conducting AGM and
EGM.                 
              "

33.6 Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

33.6.1 The Committee note that Clause 33 recasts section 99 to confine its
scope to defaults under section 96 (removing references to sections 97, 98 and

                                                      265
Tribunal directions, which are separately addressed through the Tribunal's
contempt powers under section 425). The Committee further note that the
provision converts the existing fine into a capped civil penalty, as part of the
Bill's wider decriminalisation exercise.
33.6.2 The Committee also note stakeholder suggestions for prescribing a
lower ceiling of fifty thousand rupees for Small Companies and OPCs, and the
Ministry's clarification that Section 446B of the Act already secures this
outcome by capping penalties for such companies at one-half of the penalty
applicable to other companies.
33.6.3 The Committee recognize that the recasting of Section 99 is aligned
with the Bill's objective of rationalising penalties and reducing criminal liability
for procedural defaults. The Committee concur with the Ministry's argument
that the proportionality concern raised by stakeholders is already addressed
under Section 446B, which ensures reduced penalties for Small Companies,
OPCs, start-ups and Producer Companies.
33.6.4 The Committee, therefore, accept Clause 33 as proposed, without any
modification.

                                                      266
                                               CLAUSE - 34

34. Clause 34 of the Bill seeks to amend section 100 of the Companies Act,
2013.

34.1 Provision proposed in The Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

In section 100 of the principal Act, after sub-section (6), the following sub-section
shall be inserted, namely: --

"(7) A company may hold its extraordinary general meeting physically, or through
video conferencing or other audio-visual means, either wholly or partly, in such
manner and subject to such terms and conditions, as may be prescribed:

Provided that if the number of members referred to in sub-section (2) requisition the
meeting to be held in a hybrid mode, the company shall hold the meeting in such
mode.".

34.2 Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (The Companies Act, 2013):

100. Calling of extraordinary general meeting.

(1) The Board may, whenever it deems fit, call an extraordinary general meeting of
the company.

Provided that an extraordinary general meeting of the company, other than of the
wholly owned subsidiary of a company incorporated outside India, shall be held at a
place within India.

(2) The Board shall, at the requisition made by, --

(a) in the case of a company having a share capital, such number of members who
hold, on the date of the receipt of the requisition, not less than one-tenth of such of
the paid-up share capital of the company as on that date carries the right of voting;

(b) in the case of a company not having a share capital, such number of members
who have, on the date of receipt of the requisition, not less than one-tenth of the total
voting power of all the members having on the said date a right to vote, call an

                                                      267
extraordinary general meeting of the company within the period specified in sub-
section (4).

(3) The requisition made under sub-section (2) shall set out the matters for the
consideration of which the meeting is to be called and shall be signed by the
requisitionists and sent to the registered office of the company.

(4) If the Board does not, within twenty-one days from the date of receipt of a valid
requisition in regard to any matter, proceed to call a meeting for the consideration of
that matter on a day not later than forty-five days from the date of receipt of such
requisition, the meeting may be called and held by the requisitionists themselves
within a period of three months from the date of the requisition.

(5) A meeting under sub-section (4) by the requisitionists shall be called and held in
the same manner in which the meeting is called and held by the Board.

(6) Any reasonable expenses incurred by the requisitionists in calling a meeting
under sub-section (4) shall be reimbursed to the requisitionists by the company and
the sums so paid shall be deducted from any fee or other remuneration under
section 197 payable to such of the directors who were in default in calling the
meeting.

34.3 Reasons/Justification given by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs for the
proposed provision:

"This clause seeks to amend section 100 to enable companies to hold extraordinary
general meetings (EGMs) physically, or through video conferencing or other audio-
visual means for ease of doing business."

34.4 Important Views/Suggestions given by Experts/Stakeholders:

Some of the important suggestions of the stakeholders in this regard are furnished
below:

34.4.1 Stakeholders, in separate submissions, expressed broad support for the
proposed amendment: conveying broad policy concurrence with the enablement of
holding EGMs via virtual or hybrid platforms; recommending and supporting the
expansion of the digital ecosystem to allow general corporate meetings, including
EGMs, to operate seamlessly through virtual or hybrid infrastructure; supporting the
enabling provision allowing EGMs to be held virtually or through audio-visual means;

                                                      268
supporting the reform, with modification/clarification, as converting pandemic-era
practices into durable law; and supporting the enabling provisions for AGMs and
EGMs in physical, hybrid or video-conferencing mode as progressive, expected to
reduce compliance cost and improve ease of participation, particularly for small
companies and emerging enterprises.

34.4.2 "(i) Insert a statutory proviso to Section 100 mandating "Minimum Digital
Governance Standards" (two-way audio-visual communication, anti-spoofing
biometric/MFA protocols, and a 25% technical outage automatic adjournment
threshold). (ii) Requisition meetings (EGMs convened on requisition of shareholders)
should explicitly be permitted to be held in electronic mode."

34.4.3 "It is suggested that sub-section (7) to section 100 as proposed to be inserted
may be amended to also allow the shorter notice period under sub-section (1) of
section 101 for extraordinary general meetings held physically or in hybrid mode, and
not only for those conducted wholly through video conferencing."

34.4.4 "In section 100 of the principal Act, after sub-section (6), the following sub-
section shall be inserted, namely:-- "(7) A company may hold its extraordinary
general meeting physically, or through video conferencing or other audio-visual
means, either wholly or partly, in such manner and subject to such terms and
conditions, as may be prescribed: Provided that if the number of members referred to
in sub-section (2) requisition or the company is listed the meeting to be held in a
hybrid mode, the company shall hold the meeting in such mode.""

34.4.5 "Support the formal recognition of virtual and hybrid extraordinary general
meetings but recommend greater flexibility: for public or listed companies, a physical
(or hybrid) meeting should be mandated only if a substantial number of shareholders
explicitly request one; and Rules should include clear minimum standards for
electronic meetings, ensuring robust two-way communication, secure participant
authentication, and automatic adjournment safeguards if major technical issues
occur."

34.4.6 "Rules under these sections be framed in consultation with SEBI and aligned
with SEBI (LODR) Regulations, prescribing uniform norms for hybrid/virtual
meetings, quorum determination and verification in electronic settings, and
recording/disclosure/archiving of proceedings, along with integrity safeguards for
remote e-voting; the RTA of a company and its e-voting service provider should be
separate and independent entities, with no common control; and the role of
depositories as secure, auditable e-voting and authentication infrastructure providers
should also be expressly recognised."

34.4.7 "Rules address a members' requisition for a hybrid meeting, and mechanisms
ensuring remote shareholder authentication and reliable participation, alongside
model formats and FAQs to help companies apply the reform consistently."

                                                      269
34.4.8 "Suggests removal of the residual mandatory-physical-meeting requirement
(once in three years) specifically for private companies with fewer than 50 members,
consistent with its corresponding suggestion under Clause 32."

34.4.9 "Sections 96, 99, 100 and 101 of the Companies Act, 2013 should embed
express safeguards for hybrid/virtual meetings, including real-time questions,
transparency on questions put forward, and contingency planning for platform
malfunction, with voting kept open during the meeting; and the notice period for all
shareholder meetings, AGMs as well as EGMs, should be kept at not less than
twenty-one days."

34.4.10 "Allow secure blockchain-based e-voting, digital identity verification and
smart-contract voting."

34.4.11 "It is suggested that the requirement to mandatorily conduct one physical
AGM every 3 years may be dispensed with, with the mode of conducting general
meetings left entirely to the discretion of the company, subject to the shareholder
right to requisition a hybrid meeting; certain basic standards for virtual meetings, two-
way audio-visual communication with safeguards, authentication measures to
prevent identity fraud, and automatic adjournment if a prescribed percentage of
shareholders lose connection, should be prescribed in the law itself, rather than left
entirely to the rules."

34.4.12 "Procedures left to Rules. Codify quorum, voting, inspection in Act."

34.4.13 "Electronic service of documents reduces compliance burden, but legal
certainty depends on establishing dispatch, receipt, integrity and authenticity; MeitY
supports the initiative, subject to robust technological safeguards including
participant authentication, prevention of impersonation, secure e-voting, audit logs
and cybersecurity protections."

34.4.14 "AGMs and EGMs may be held physically, virtually, or in hybrid mode, at the
company's discretion. Mandatory physical AGM (once every three years) may be
omitted; shareholders holding the Section 100(2) threshold may requisition a hybrid
meeting. The 7-day notice period proposed for fully virtual EGMs may be extended to
virtual AGMs as well. The postal-ballot voting window may be decreased from 30 to
15 days. Minimum digital safeguards, two-way audio-video, authentication, and auto-
adjournment if over 25% of participants are disconnected, may be codified."

34.4.15 "It is recommended that the clauses be retained, subject to the following
modifications: (i) insert an Explanation that the three-year period for a physical AGM
shall be reckoned from the last AGM held in physical or hybrid mode; (ii) the rules
under section 101 shall provide that a seven-day notice for a wholly-electronic EGM
shall be permissible only where e-voting or postal ballot is offered to all members;

                                                      270
and (iii) hybrid mode be the default prescription for the top listed companies,
consistent with SEBI's direction of travel."

34.4.16 "Concern regarding the increasing use of the expression "as may be
prescribed" is not directed against delegated legislation per se, but arises where
substantive policy decisions and essential legislative functions are left to subordinate
legislation without adequate guidance in the parent statute; matters involving
substantive rights, obligations, scope of applicability, exemptions, penalties and
regulatory jurisdiction should be specified in the Act itself, while only procedural and
implementation-related matters may be left to Rules."

34.4.17 "It is humbly recommended that the rules under these sections be framed in
consultation with SEBI and aligned with SEBI (LODR) Regulations, prescribing
uniform norms for hybrid/virtual meetings, quorum determination and verification in
electronic settings, recording/disclosure/archiving of proceedings, and integrity
safeguards for remote e-voting; the RTA of a company and its e-voting service
provider should be separate and independent entities, with no common control; and
the role of depositories as secure, auditable e-voting and authentication
infrastructure providers should be expressly recognised."

34.5 Examination by the Committee:

The Ministry in their written replies to the corresponding suggestions above have
submitted as under:

34.5.1  In response to the suggestion at paragraph 34.4.1 above, expressing

general support for the proposed amendment, the Ministry noted that it agreed with

the proposed amendment and did not call for any change.

34.5.2  Responding to a suggestion at paragraph 34.4.2 above to insert a

statutory proviso to section 100 mandating Minimum Digital Governance Standards,

and to explicitly permit requisitioned EGMs to be held in electronic mode, the

Ministry, in its written submission, stated that Clause 34 enables companies to hold

EGMs through video conferencing or other audio-visual means, with the manner and

terms and conditions to be prescribed through Rules rather than fixed in the Act

itself, and that the suggestion accordingly does not require any amendment to the

Companies Act, 2013 and would be considered at the rule-making stage.

        271
34.5.3  Addressing a suggestion at paragraph 34.4.3 above that the shorter

notice period proposed for wholly-electronic EGMs also be extended to physical or

hybrid EGMs, the Ministry, in its written submission, stated that the proposed

amendment to section 101 provides for a notice period of seven days or such period

as may be prescribed by the Central Government, that the proviso to sub-section (1)

of section 101 already provides for calling of a general meeting after giving shorter

notice where consent from members as prescribed is accorded, and that a separate

provision did not appear necessary.

34.5.4  In reply to a suggestion at paragraph 34.4.4 above to insert sub-section

(7) to section 100 to enable EGMs to be held physically, through video conferencing

or otherwise, with a hybrid-mode requisition safeguard, the Ministry, in its written

submission, stated that the proposed amendment gives companies the flexibility to

hold AGMs physically, via VC/OAVM, or in hybrid mode, thereby reducing

compliance costs and easing burdens on companies and shareholders; that

adequate safeguards for shareholder engagement are already built in, since the first

proviso allows members themselves, through the existing requisition mechanism

under sub-section (2) of section 100, to require a hybrid-mode meeting where

desired; and that the provision may accordingly be retained without any change.

34.5.5  With respect to a suggestion at paragraph 34.4.5 above supporting the

formal recognition of virtual and hybrid EGMs but recommending that a physical or

hybrid meeting be mandated only where a substantial number of shareholders

explicitly request one, together with minimum standards for electronic meetings, the

Ministry, in its written submission, stated that this would be appropriately dealt with

during the framing of subordinate legislation, since sub-section (3) of the amended

section 96 already provides that a company may hold its AGM through VC/OAVM "in

such manner and subject to such terms and conditions, as may be prescribed",

enabling the Central Government to prescribe technical and procedural safeguards

as required; and that, as regards the third proviso, section 96 would be amended to

allow virtual/hybrid AGMs "in such manner...as may be prescribed", subject to every

company holding its AGM in physical or hybrid mode at least once in every three

years.

                                     272
34.5.6  In response to a suggestion at paragraph 34.4.6 above that rules for

hybrid/virtual EGMs be framed in consultation with SEBI and aligned with SEBI

(LODR) Regulations, with functional separation between the RTA and the e-voting

service provider, the Ministry, in its written submission, stated that section 96 would

be amended to allow virtual/hybrid AGMs "in such manner...as may be prescribed",

subject to every company holding its AGM in physical or hybrid mode at least once in

every three years, and that the Bill would be modified accordingly; and that the

procedural and operational framework for electronic and hybrid meetings, remote e-

voting and associated technological safeguards would be appropriately addressed

through the Rules and other applicable regulatory framework, in consultation with the

concerned regulators, wherever necessary.

34.5.7  Responding to a suggestion at paragraph 34.4.7 above that rules

address members' requisition for a hybrid meeting and mechanisms for remote

shareholder authentication, alongside model formats and FAQs, the Ministry, in its

written submission, stated that the proposed amendment is an enabling provision,

and that the procedural and operational aspects relating to hybrid EGMs, including

members' requisitions, shareholder authentication, participation mechanisms and

other implementation details, would be considered, as appropriate, while framing the

Rules.

34.5.8  Addressing a suggestion at paragraph 34.4.8 above that the residual

mandatory-physical-meeting requirement be removed for private companies with

fewer than 50 members, the Ministry noted that section 96 would be amended to

allow virtual/hybrid AGMs "in such manner...as may be prescribed", subject to every

company holding its AGM in physical or hybrid mode at least once in every three

years, and that the Bill would be modified accordingly.

34.5.9 In reply to a suggestion at paragraph 34.4.9 above that sections 96, 99, 100
and 101 embed express safeguards for hybrid/virtual meetings and that the notice
period for all shareholder meetings be kept at not less than twenty-one days, the
Ministry, in its written submission, clarified that the suggestion regarding participation
safeguards for virtual/hybrid meetings is duly noted and will be considered at the

                                                      273
appropriate rule-making stage; and that, as regards the notice period, for listed
companies, an extraordinary general meeting held wholly through video conferencing
or other audio-visual means under the new section 100(7) would be called by giving
a notice of not less than fifteen days, or such other period as may be prescribed.

34.5.10  With respect to suggestions at paragraphs 34.4.10 and 34.4.12 above,

for secure blockchain-based e-voting and digital identity verification, and for codifying

quorum, voting and inspection procedures in the Act, the Ministry noted that this

suggestion would be considered appropriately during the framing of subordinate

legislation, since sub-section (3) of the amended section 96 already provides that a

company may hold its AGM through VC/OAVM "in such manner and subject to such

terms and conditions, as may be prescribed".

34.5.11  On the suggestion at paragraph 34.4.11 above that the mandatory

triennial physical AGM be dispensed with, leaving the mode of meeting to the

company's discretion subject to the shareholder right to requisition a hybrid meeting,

and that basic standards for virtual meetings be prescribed in the Act itself, the

Ministry, in its written submission, stated that section 96 would be amended to allow

virtual/hybrid AGMs "in such manner...as may be prescribed", subject to every

company holding its AGM in physical or hybrid mode at least once in every three

years; it further stated that the suggestion regarding standards of virtual meetings

would be considered appropriately during the framing of subordinate legislation.

34.5.12  Responding to a suggestion at paragraph 34.4.12 above that electronic

service of documents be supported by Rules prescribing safeguards for dispatch,

receipt, integrity and authenticity, the Ministry, in its written submission, stated that

this suggestion would be considered appropriately during the framing of subordinate

legislation, since the proposed amendments provide an enabling framework for

holding general meetings electronically and for the electronic service of documents;

and that the stakeholder's suggestions, relating to the operational aspects of the

provision, would be considered as appropriate while framing the relevant Rules, the

provision being retained without change.

                                          274
34.5.13  Addressing a suggestion at paragraph 34.4.13 above that AGMs and

EGMs be held physically, virtually or in hybrid mode at the company's discretion, that

the seven-day notice period proposed for virtual EGMs be extended to virtual AGMs,

and that the postal-ballot voting window be shortened, the Ministry, in its written

submission, stated that section 96 would be amended to allow virtual/hybrid AGMs

"in such manner...as may be prescribed", subject to every company holding its AGM

in physical or hybrid mode at least once in every three years; that, as regards EGMs,

the suggestion would be considered appropriately during the framing of subordinate

legislation; and that, as regards the applicability of a seven-day notice period to

AGMs, since the business transacted at an AGM includes matters of "Ordinary

Business", the existing twenty-one-day notice period would be retained irrespective

of the mode in which the AGM is held.

34.5.14  In reply to a suggestion at paragraph 34.4.14 above that the clauses be

retained subject to an Explanation on how the three-year period for a physical AGM

is to be reckoned, a condition on the seven-day EGM notice, and hybrid mode as the

default for top listed companies, the Ministry, in its written submission, stated that

section 96 would be amended to allow virtual/hybrid AGMs "in such manner...as may

be prescribed", subject to every company holding its AGM in physical or hybrid mode

at least once in every three years; that, as regards EGMs, the suggestion would be

considered appropriately during the framing of subordinate legislation; and that, as

regards the applicability of a seven-day notice period to AGMs, since the business

transacted at an AGM includes matters of "Ordinary Business", the existing twenty-

one-day notice period would be retained irrespective of the mode in which the AGM

is held; it further clarified that the three-year period for a physical or hybrid AGM

would be reckoned from the date of the last AGM held in physical or hybrid mode.

34.5.15  With respect to a suggestion at paragraph 34.4.15 above that matters

involving substantive rights, obligations, scope of applicability, exemptions, penalties

and regulatory jurisdiction should be specified in the Act itself, with only procedural

and implementation-related matters left to Rules, the Ministry, in its written

submission, stated that the procedural requirements relating to the holding of

meetings are being considered for detailed treatment in the Rules, so as to provide

                                       275
the necessary flexibility to make quick amendments as requirements arise from time
to time, and that these procedural aspects may not be considered essential features.

34.5.16      On the suggestion at paragraph 34.4.16 above that rules under these

sections be framed in consultation with SEBI and aligned with SEBI (LODR)

Regulations, with functional separation between the RTA and the e-voting service

provider, the Ministry clarified that this would be appropriately dealt with during the

framing of subordinate legislation.

34.5.17      Secretary, MCA at the sitting held on 16.7.2026 explained the provision
as follows:

",  100              
           96         
   AGM          ,  EGM    
Already EGM is happening through this mode. We are just codifying it."

34.5.18      On being asked whether a minimum notice period exists for the

extraordinary general meeting. Clarifying this at the sitting held on 16.7.2026, the

Secretary, MCA stated that while the standard requirement is seven days, in the

case of listed companies, SEBI mandates fifteen days, and the Ministry was in

agreement with this position.

34.5.20      Addressing queries on unifying the rules for Sections 96 and 100, the

Secretary, MCA, clarified that while AGMs and EGMs share technical parameters for

VC/OAVM, they serve distinct purposes. Furthermore, the Secretary noted that

suggestions for a 15-day notice period for listed companies have been accepted,

technical details will be prescribed through rules, and Section 101 already permits

notices as short as two or three days with 95% shareholder consent.

                                     276
34.6 Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

34.6.1 The Committee note that Clause 34 inserts a new sub-section (7) in
section 100 to enable companies to hold extraordinary general meetings
physically, through video conferencing or other audio-visual means, or in
hybrid mode, mirroring the flexibility extended to annual general meetings
under Clause 32.

34.6.2 The Committee further note that the enabling framework was welcomed
in several submissions, whose suggestions relate principally to the content of
the subordinate legislation rather than to the text of Clause 34 itself, and which
the Ministry has agreed to examine at the rule-making stage.

34.6.3 The Committee note the suggestion, linked to Clause 32, for
dispensing with the triennial physical-meeting requirement for small, closely-
held private companies, and the Ministry's acceptance of the corresponding
modification under Clause 32.

34.6.4 The Committee also note the suggestion for extending shorter notice
to physical/hybrid EGMs. The Committee concur with the Ministry's
clarification that the existing proviso to Section 101(1) already allows shorter
notice with the consent of members, and therefore a separate provision is not
warranted.

34.6.5 Taking note of the suggestion that Rules for hybrid/virtual EGMs be
framed in consultation with SEBI, the Committee record the Ministry's
assurance that the procedural and operational framework for such meetings
would be appropriately addressed through the Rules, in consultation with the
concerned regulators, wherever necessary, and recommend that the Rules
under section 100(7) be framed accordingly.

                                                      277
34.6.6 The Committee, therefore, accept Clause 34 as proposed, without any
modification, while recommending that the Ministry have due regard to the
suggestions noted above at the stage of framing the Rules.
