35. Clause 35 of the Bill seeks to amend section 101 of the Companies Act,
2013.

35.1 Provision proposed in The Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

In section 101 of the principal Act, in sub-section (1), --

(a) in the proviso, for the words "Provided that", the following words shall be
substituted, namely: --

"Provided that the extraordinary general meetings conducted wholly through video
conferencing or audio-visual means under sub-section (7) of section 100, may be
called by giving a notice of not less than seven days, or such other period, and in
such manner, as may be prescribed:

Provided further that";

(b) in the second proviso, for the words "Provided further", the words "Provided also"
shall be substituted.

35.2 Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (The Companies Act, 2013):

101. Notice of meeting.

(1) A general meeting of a company may be called by giving not less than clear
twenty-one days' notice either in writing or through electronic mode in such manner
as may be prescribed:

Provided that a general meeting may be called after giving shorter notice than that
specified in this sub-section if consent, in writing or by electronic mode, is accorded
thereto--

(i) in the case of an annual general meeting, by not less than ninety-five per cent. of
the members entitled to vote thereat; and

(ii) in the case of any other general meeting, by members of the company--

                                                      279
(a) holding, if the company has a share capital, majority in number of members
entitled to vote and who represent not less than ninety-five per cent. of such part of
the paid-up share capital of the company as gives a right to vote at the meeting; or

(b) having, if the company has no share capital, not less than ninety-five per cent. of
the total voting power exercisable at that meeting:

Provided further that where any member of a company is entitled to vote only on
some resolution or resolutions to be moved at a meeting and not on the others, those
members shall be taken into account for the purposes of this sub-section in respect
of the former resolution or resolutions and not in respect of the latter.

* * * * *

35.3 Reason/Justification given by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs for the
proposed provision:

"This amendment seeks to facilitate conduct of extraordinary general meetings
through video conferencing or other audio-visual means."

35.4 Important Views/Suggestions given by Experts/Stakeholders:

Some of the important suggestions of the stakeholders in this regard are furnished
below:

35.4.1 Stakeholders, in separate submissions, expressed broad support for the
proposed amendment, welcoming the reduction of the EGM notice period from
twenty-one to seven days and the enabling provisions for AGMs and EGMs in
physical, hybrid or video-conferencing mode as progressive, expected to reduce
compliance cost and improve ease of participation, particularly for small companies
and emerging enterprises.

35.4.2 "The proposed amendment enabling EGMs through video conferencing/audio-
visual means with a shorter notice period of 7 days is welcome; however, it is
recommended that the postal ballot mechanism under Section 110 of the Companies
Act, 2013 be altogether deleted and replaced with e-voting facility."

35.4.3 "EGMs be allowed to be called at shorter notice, just like AGMs, if members
give written consent."

                                                      280
35.4.4 "In section 101 of the principal Act, in sub-section (1), it is suggested that the
shorter notice period for EGMs conducted wholly through video conferencing or
audio-visual means not be made applicable to listed companies; either the
amendment be dropped, or the notice period for such EGMs of listed companies be
kept at not less than fifteen days."

35.4.5 "The proposed reduced notice period of 7 days for virtual EGMs should also
be extended to AGMs and resolutions passed through Postal Ballot."

35.4.6 "Proposed to amend the proviso to insert an exception for listed companies,
ensuring their notice period cannot be cut down to 7 days, and instead be kept at not
less than fifteen days."

35.4.7 "Rules under these sections be framed in consultation with SEBI and aligned
with SEBI (LODR) Regulations, prescribing uniform norms for hybrid/virtual
meetings, quorum determination and verification in electronic settings, and
recording/disclosure/archiving of proceedings, along with integrity safeguards for
remote e-voting; the RTA of a company and its e-voting service provider should be
separate and independent entities, with no common control; and the role of

should also be expressly recognised."

35.4.8 "Recommends rules ensuring a reliable voting record and a clear process for
connection failures during a poll conducted at a wholly-virtual EGM called on the
shortened 7-day notice."

35.4.9 "For listed entities, EGMs conducted wholly through video conferencing/audio-
visual means should be called on notice of not less than 15 days, not 7 days."

35.4.10 "In the same submission on safeguards for listed-company AGMs, it is
further recommended, on notice periods for electronic extraordinary general
meetings, that the current 21-day notice period be retained for all general meetings
regardless of format; at a minimum, listed companies should continue to be subject
to a 21-day notice requirement, whether through the Act or SEBI's listing rules."

35.4.11 "Requests that the reduced 7-day notice period be extended to AGMs
conducted wholly through video-conferencing/audio-visual means as well, and not
confined to EGMs."

35.4.12 "Sections 96, 99, 100 and 101 of the Companies Act, 2013 should embed
express safeguards for hybrid/virtual meetings, including real-time questions,
transparency on questions put forward, and contingency planning for platform
malfunction, with voting kept open during the meeting; and the notice period for all

                                                      281
shareholder meetings, AGMs as well as EGMs, should be kept at not less than

35.4.13 "Electronic service of documents reduces compliance burden, but legal

supports the initiative, subject to robust technological safeguards including
participant authentication, prevention of impersonation, secure e-voting, audit logs
and cybersecurity protections."

35.4.14 "AGMs and EGMs may be held physically, virtually, or in hybrid mode, at the
company's discretion. Mandatory physical AGM (once every three years) may be
omitted; shareholders holding the Section 100(2) threshold may requisition a hybrid
meeting. The 7-day notice period proposed for fully virtual EGMs may be extended to

35.4.15 "It is recommended that the clauses be retained, subject to the following
modifications: (i) insert an Explanation that the three-year period for a physical AGM
shall be reckoned from the last AGM held in physical or hybrid mode; (ii) the rules
under section 101 shall provide that a seven-day notice for a wholly-electronic EGM
shall be permissible only where e-voting or postal ballot is offered to all members;
and (iii) hybrid mode be the default prescription for the top listed companies,
consistent with SEBI's direction of travel."

35.4.16 "Rules under section 101 shall provide that a seven-day notice for a wholly-
electronic EGM shall be permissible only where e-voting or postal ballot is offered to
all members."

35.4.17 "Given the immediacy and efficiency enabled by VC/OAVM platforms, the
proposed reduced notice period of 7 days for virtual EGMs may also be extended to
virtual AGMs. The voting period in case of postal ballot may be kept at 15 days from
the date of dispatch of notice for both remote e-voting and voting by way of physical
ballot."

35.4.18 "It is suggested that (i) the notice period for AGMs conducted wholly through
video conferencing or audio-visual means be reduced to 14 days instead of the
existing 21 days; and (ii) postal ballots be substituted by remote e-voting for listed
entities, with the voting period suitably shortened to 14 days instead of the existing
30 days."

35.4.19 "It is humbly recommended that the rules under these sections be framed in
consultation with SEBI and aligned with SEBI (LODR) Regulations, prescribing
uniform norms for hybrid/virtual meetings, quorum determination and verification in

                                                      282
electronic settings, recording/disclosure/archiving of proceedings, and integrity
safeguards for remote e-voting; the RTA of a company and its e-voting service
provider should be separate and independent entities, with no common control; and
the role of depositories as secure, auditable e-voting and authentication
infrastructure providers should be expressly recognised."

35.5 Examination by the Committee:

The Ministry in their written replies to the corresponding suggestions above have
submitted as under:

35.5.1  The Ministry acknowledged that several stakeholders, as recorded at

paragraph 35.4.1 above, were in support of the proposed amendment, and stated

that it did not call for any change.

35.5.2  In response to a suggestion at paragraph 35.4.2 above that the postal

ballot mechanism under section 110 be deleted altogether and replaced with e-

voting, the Ministry, in its written submission, stated that the current definition of

`postal ballot' under section 2(65) of the Companies Act, 2013, `means voting by post

or through any electronic mode', already encompasses voting via post and electronic

means, and that retaining the term also ensures that companies which have already

adopted a postal ballot method can continue to use it without incurring additional

costs in setting up new methods of voting.

35.5.3  Addressing a suggestion at paragraph 35.4.3 above that EGMs be

allowed to be called at shorter notice, just as AGMs are, where members give written

consent, the Ministry, in its written submission, stated that the proposed amendment

to section 101 provides for a notice period of seven days or such period as may be

prescribed for an EGM held wholly via VC or OAVM. It was also submitted that the

proviso to sub-section (1) of section 101 already provides for calling a general

meeting after giving shorter notice where members' consent is accorded, making a

separate provision unnecessary; and that section 101 applies to EGMs as it does to

AGMs, with the first proviso already providing sufficient flexibility for holding EGMs.

                                      283
35.5.4  In reply to suggestions at paragraphs 35.4.4, 35.4.6, 35.4.9 and

35.4.10 above, each proposing that the shortened notice period for wholly-electronic

EGMs not apply to listed companies, and that such companies instead be subject to

a notice period of not less than fifteen days, the Ministry, in its written submission,

stated that, for listed companies, EGMs held wholly by video conferencing or OAVM

under the new section 100(7) would be required to be called by giving a notice of not

less than fifteen days or such other period as may be prescribed, and that the Bill

would be modified accordingly.

35.5.5  With respect to suggestions at paragraphs 35.4.5 and 35.4.17 above,

that the reduced seven-day notice period for virtual EGMs also be extended to AGMs

and to resolutions passed through postal ballot, the Ministry, in its written

submission, stated that the business transacted at an AGM includes matters of

"Ordinary Business", consideration of financial statements, declaration of dividend,

and appointment of directors and auditors, apart from any special business the

company may decide to transact. The existing twenty-one-day notice period is

accordingly retained irrespective of the mode in which the AGM is held. A company

retains the option to call an EGM for urgent and time-sensitive matters, for which a

seven-day notice period applies where held wholly in virtual mode, except for listed

companies, where the notice period is fifteen days. The existing timelines prescribed

for postal ballots already provide adequate opportunity for shareholder participation

and would accordingly be retained.

35.5.6  In response to a suggestion at paragraph 35.4.7 above that rules for

hybrid/virtual EGMs be framed in consultation with SEBI and aligned with SEBI

(LODR) Regulations, with functional separation between the RTA and the e-voting

service provider, the Ministry, reiterating its response to the identical suggestion

raised under Clause 32, stated that section 96 would be amended to allow

virtual/hybrid AGMs "in such manner...as may be prescribed", subject to every

company holding its AGM in physical or hybrid mode at least once in every three

years, and that the Bill would be modified accordingly; and that the procedural and

operational framework for electronic and hybrid meetings, remote e-voting and

associated technological safeguards would be appropriately addressed through the

                                    284
Rules and other applicable regulatory framework, in consultation with the concerned
regulators, wherever necessary.

35.5.7   Responding to a suggestion at paragraph 35.4.8 above for rules

ensuring a reliable voting record and a clear process for connection failures during a

poll at a wholly-virtual EGM called on shortened notice, the Ministry, in its written

submission, stated that the rules to be prescribed for virtual or hybrid meetings would

address a reliable voting record and a process for connection failures, and that these

matters would be considered at the rule-making stage.

35.5.8 Addressing a suggestion at paragraph 35.4.11 above that the reduced seven-
day notice period be extended to AGMs conducted wholly through video-
conferencing/audio-visual means, and not confined to EGMs, the Ministry, in its
written submission, stated that the business transacted at an AGM is generally
ordinary business -- including consideration of financial statements, declaration of
dividend, appointment of directors and auditors, as well as any special business the
company may decide to transact -- and that, accordingly, the existing twenty-one-
day notice period is retained irrespective of the mode in which the AGM is held.

35.5.9 In reply to a suggestion at paragraph 35.4.12 above that sections 96, 99, 100
and 101 embed express safeguards for hybrid/virtual meetings and that the notice
period for all shareholder meetings be kept at not less than twenty-one days, the
Ministry, in its written submission, clarified that the suggestion regarding participation
safeguards for virtual/hybrid meetings is duly noted and will be considered at the
appropriate rule-making stage; and that, as regards the notice period, for listed
companies, an extraordinary general meeting held wholly through video conferencing
or other audio-visual means under the new section 100(7) would be called by giving
a notice of not less than fifteen days, or such other period as may be prescribed.

35.5.10  With respect to a suggestion at paragraph 35.4.13 above that

electronic service of documents be supported by Rules prescribing safeguards for

dispatch, receipt, integrity and authenticity, the Ministry, in its written submission,

stated that this suggestion would be considered appropriately during the framing of
                                                      285
subordinate legislation, since the proposed amendments provide an enabling
framework for holding general meetings electronically and for the electronic service
of documents; and that the stakeholder's suggestions, relating to the operational
aspects of the provision, would be considered as appropriate while framing the
relevant Rules, the provision being retained without change.

35.5.11  On the suggestion at paragraph 35.4.14 above that AGMs and EGMs

be held physically, virtually or in hybrid mode at the company's discretion, that the

seven-day notice period proposed for virtual EGMs be extended to virtual AGMs, and

that the postal-ballot voting window be shortened, the Ministry, in its written

submission, stated that section 96 would be amended to allow virtual/hybrid AGMs

"in such manner...as may be prescribed", subject to every company holding its AGM

in physical or hybrid mode at least once in every three years. As regards EGMs, it

was submitted that the suggestion would be considered appropriately during the

framing of subordinate legislation; and that, as regards the applicability of a seven-

day notice period to AGMs, since the business transacted at an AGM includes

matters of "Ordinary Business", the existing twenty-one-day notice period would be

retained irrespective of the mode in which the AGM is held.

35.5.12  Responding to a suggestion at paragraph 35.4.15 above that the

clauses be retained subject to an Explanation on how the three-year period for a

physical AGM is to be reckoned, a condition on the seven-day EGM notice, and

hybrid mode as the default for top listed companies, the Ministry, in its written

submission, stated that section 96 would be amended to allow virtual/hybrid AGMs

"in such manner...as may be prescribed", subject to every company holding its AGM

in physical or hybrid mode at least once in every three years; that, as regards EGMs,

the suggestion would be considered appropriately during the framing of subordinate

legislation; and that, as regards the applicability of a seven-day notice period to

AGMs, since the business transacted at an AGM includes matters of "Ordinary

Business", the existing twenty-one-day notice period would be retained irrespective

of the mode in which the AGM is held. It was further clarified that the three-year

period for a physical or hybrid AGM would be reckoned from the date of the last

AGM held in physical or hybrid mode.

                                      286
35.5.13        Addressing a suggestion at paragraph 35.4.16 above that the rules

under section 101 provide that a seven-day notice for a wholly-electronic EGM be

permissible only where e-voting or postal ballot is offered to all members, the

Ministry noted that this would be considered appropriately during the framing of

subordinate legislation.

35.5.14        In reply to a suggestion at paragraph 35.4.18 above that the AGM

notice period be reduced to fourteen days for fully virtual meetings, and that postal

ballots be replaced with remote e-voting for listed entities with the voting period

shortened to fourteen days, the Ministry, in its written submission, stated that the

business transacted at an AGM includes matters of "Ordinary Business", and that the

existing twenty-one-day notice period is accordingly retained irrespective of the

mode in which the AGM is held; and that a company retains the option to call an

EGM for urgent matters, for which a seven-day notice period applies where held

wholly in virtual mode, except for listed companies, where the notice period would be

fifteen days.

35.5.15        With respect to a suggestion at paragraph 35.4.19 above that rules

under these sections be framed in consultation with SEBI and aligned with SEBI

(LODR) Regulations, with functional separation between the RTA and the e-voting

service provider, the Ministry clarified that this would be appropriately dealt with

during the framing of subordinate legislation.

35.5.16        Responding to the Committee's query on hybrid meeting quorums, the

Secretary, MCA, clarified that physical and online attendance would be combined for

quorum purposes, while the existing proxy framework and all three participation

modes--physical, online, and postal ballot--would remain available.

35.5.17        Addressing concerns regarding the shortened seven-day EGM notice

period and potential asset-stripping risks, the Secretary, MCA, clarified that while the

general notice period remains seven days, the Ministry accepted SEBI's

recommendation of a 15-day notice period for listed companies to allow adequate

review time. It was noted that asset-stripping and fraud concerns are typically
                                                      287
handled through separate regulatory enforcement, with the Ministry undertaking to
consult SEBI further on this specific risk.

35.5.18  In its written submission, the Ministry further stated that the position at

35.5.17 above was based on SEBI's recommendation, having regard to the nature of

resolutions typically placed before an EGM of a listed company -- including schemes

of arrangement such as mergers, demergers and amalgamations, material related-

party transactions, and the appointment or remuneration of directors -- each of

which may involve complex legal, financial or valuation considerations requiring

shareholders and SEBI-registered proxy advisors adequate time to review scheme

documents, valuation reports and fairness opinions before casting an informed vote

35.5.19  The Committee were also apprised that, as per the OECD Corporate

Governance Factbook 2025, which surveys the corporate governance framework

across fifty-two jurisdictions, only nineteen per cent of surveyed jurisdictions

prescribe a notice period for general meetings of under twenty days, and that even

these jurisdictions typically prescribe fourteen or fifteen days rather than seven; and

that certain jurisdictions, including Singapore, the United Kingdom and Hong Kong,

prescribe differentiated notice periods depending on the type of resolution or meeting

involved, rather than a uniform shorter period across all general meetings.

35.5.20  Based on the global notice-period data, the Ministry submitted that a

15-days minimum notice period as suggested by SEBI, strikes a more balanced

approach and aligns with the global benchmarks while allowing reasonable speed in

corporate decision-making. The suggestion along with existing shorter-notice

mechanism under Section 101 with 95% shareholder consent, provides sufficient

flexibility for exceptional circumstances, addressing both urgency and strong

safeguards for shareholder protection and market integrity in case of listed company.

35.6 Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

         288
35.6.1 The Committee note that Clause 35 amends the proviso to section
101(1) to permit a shorter notice period, not less than seven days, or such
other period as may be prescribed, uniformly for extraordinary general
meetings conducted wholly through video conferencing or audio-visual means
under the new section 100(7).

35.6.2 The Committee note that the Ministry had accepted the suggestion,
based on SEBI's recommendation, and agreed to provide that for listed
companies such EGMs would require a notice period of not less than fifteen
days rather than seven, having regard to the nature of resolutions typically
placed before an EGM, such as schemes of arrangement, material related-party
transactions and appointment of directors, which may require shareholders
and proxy advisors additional time for scrutiny.

35.6.3 During deliberations, concern was raised that an extraordinary general
meeting is, by definition, meant for extraordinary or urgent situations, and that
a longer notice period of fifteen days could give a company additional time to
divert funds before shareholders are able to act; even for listed companies, the
notice period should accordingly remain at seven days.

35.6.4 The Committee note SEBI's clarification that, in situations involving
fraud, diversion of funds or serious governance failure, it is unlikely that the
management responsible for such conduct would itself convene an EGM to
address its own misconduct, and that the existing proviso to section 101(1),
which permits an EGM to be called at shorter notice where members holding
not less than ninety-five per cent of the voting power have consented, already
provides a safeguard for genuine emergencies.

35.6.5 The Committee further note SEBI's submission, with reference to the
OECD Corporate Governance Factbook 2025, that only nineteen per cent of
surveyed jurisdictions prescribe a notice period of under twenty days, and that
comparator jurisdictions such as Singapore, the United Kingdom and Hong
Kong prescribe differentiated notice periods depending on the type of

                                                      289
resolution or meeting involved. Having regard to the nature of resolutions
typically placed before an EGM of a listed company, and to the safeguard
already available under section 101(1) for genuinely urgent matters, the
Committee are of the view that the case for a differentiated, fifteen-day notice
period for listed companies has been sufficiently made out, and recommend
that Clause 35 be modified accordingly.

35.6.6 The Committee take note of the suggestions regarding, respectively,
shorter notice for physical/hybrid EGMs and the postal ballot mechanism
under section 110, and the Ministry's clarifications that the existing statutory
framework already accommodates these concerns; the Committee see no need
for further amendment on these points.

35.6.7 The Committee note the suggestions for extending the shortened
notice period to wholly virtual AGMs, and the Ministry's clarification that AGM
business is ordinarily routine in nature and warrants the existing twenty-one-
day notice regardless of meeting mode; the Committee concur with this
distinction between AGMs and EGMs.

35.6.8 The Committee note the Ministry's position that the procedural and
operational framework for hybrid/virtual EGMs, including the matter raised in
the suggestion that Rules be framed in consultation with SEBI, would be
appropriately addressed through the Rules, in consultation with the concerned
regulators, wherever necessary, and recommend that the Rules under this
Clause be framed accordingly.

35.6.9 The Committee, therefore, recommend that Clause 35 of the Bill be
modified as follows:

" In section 101 of the principal Act, in sub-section (1),--

                                                      290
(a) in the proviso, for the words "Provided that", the following words shall be
substituted, namely:--
"Provided that the extraordinary general meetings conducted wholly through
video conferencing or audio-visual means under sub-section (7) of section
100, may be called by giving a notice of not less than seven days, or such
other period, and in such manner, as may be prescribed:
Provided further that in the case of a listed company, an extraordinary general
meeting conducted wholly through video conferencing or other audio-visual
means under sub-section (7) of section 100 shall be called by giving a notice of
not less than fifteen days, or such other period as may be prescribed:
Provided also that";
(b) in the second proviso, for the words "Provided further", the words
"Provided also" shall be substituted."
35.6.10 Subject to the above modification, the Committee accept Clause 35 as
proposed.

                                               CLAUSE - 36

36. Clause 36 of the Bill seeks to amend section 124 of the Companies Act,
2013.

36.1 Provision proposed in The Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

In section 124 of the principal Act, --

(a) in sub-section (5), after the words "seven years from the date of such transfer",
the words, brackets and figure ", along with any dividend which has not been paid or
claimed where such shares have been transferred by the company under sub-
section (6)," shall be inserted;

(b) in sub-section (6), --

(i) after the word "Fund", the word "Authority" shall be inserted;

(ii) in the proviso, after the word "Fund", the word "Authority" shall be inserted;

(iii) in the Explanation, after the word "Fund", the word "Authority" shall be inserted.

36.2 Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (The Companies Act, 2013):

124. Unpaid Dividend Account.

(5) Any money transferred to the Unpaid Dividend Account of a company in
pursuance of this section which remains unpaid or unclaimed for a period of seven
years from the date of such transfer shall be transferred by the company along with
interest accrued, if any, thereon to the Fund established under sub-section (1) of
section 125 and the company shall send a statement in the prescribed form of the
details of such transfer to the authority which administers the said Fund and that
authority shall issue a receipt to the company as evidence of such transfer.

(6) All shares in respect of which dividend has not been paid or claimed for seven
consecutive years or more shall be transferred by the company in the name of
Investor Education and Protection Fund along with a statement containing such
details as may be prescribed:

                                                      292
Provided that any claimant of shares transferred above shall be entitled to claim the
transfer of shares from Investor Education and Protection Fund in accordance with
such procedure and on submission of such documents as may be prescribed.

Explanation. --For the removal of doubts, it is hereby clarified that in case any
dividend is paid or claimed for any year during the said period of seven consecutive
years, the share shall not be transferred to Investor Education and Protection Fund.

36.3 Reasons/Justification given by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs for the
proposed provision:

"This amendment is proposed to clarify that all pending or unclaimed dividends,
irrespective of the year to which they pertain, shall also be transferred to the Investor
Education and Protection Fund at the stage when the corresponding shares are
transferred to the Fund. It also introduces references to the `Authority' administering
the Fund."

36.4 Important Views/Suggestions given by Experts/Stakeholders:

Some of the important suggestions of the stakeholders in this regard are furnished
below:

36.4.1 "It is suggested that the reference to the "Investor Education and Protection
Fund" in Section 124 be replaced with the "Investor Education and Protection Fund
Authority", for consistency with the corresponding terminology used in Section 125,"

36.4.2 "It is suggested that the proposed amendment to section 124(5) be suitably
re-drafted as under: "along with any dividend which has not been paid or claimed
where such shares have been transferred or are due for transfer by the company
under sub-section (6),", so as to avoid ambiguity where the transfer of unpaid
dividends and of the corresponding shares are not completed simultaneously."

36.4.3 "Section 124(5) and 124(6): it is suggested that a mechanism be introduced
for removal of non-existent or untraceable shareholders after due notice and
verification by the ROC/NCLT."

                                                      293
36.5 Examination by the Committee:

The Ministry in their written replies to the corresponding suggestions above have
submitted as under:

36.5.1 In response to a suggestion at paragraph 36.4.1 above that the reference to
the "Investor Education and Protection Fund" in section 124 be replaced with the
"Investor Education and Protection Fund Authority", the Ministry clarified that the
reference to the Investor Education and Protection Fund in section 124 relates to the
Fund itself, and not to the Investor Education and Protection Fund Authority.

36.5.2 Responding to a suggestion at paragraph 36.4.2 above that the proposed
amendment to section 124(5) be re-drafted to expressly cover shares that are due
for transfer under sub-section (6), the Ministry, in its written submission, stated that
the suggested clarification may not be required, since the proposed amendment to
section 124(5) already clarifies that any dividend remaining unpaid or unclaimed in
respect of shares transferred under section 124(6) is also required to be transferred
to the Investor Education and Protection Fund. The provision sufficiently addresses
the intended objective without giving rise to the ambiguity highlighted; and no further
modification was accordingly considered necessary.

36.5.3 Addressing a suggestion at paragraph 36.4.3 above for a statutory
mechanism to remove non-existent or untraceable shareholders after due notice and
verification by the ROC/NCLT, the Ministry noted that a mechanism already exists
under section 59 for rectification of the register of members upon an application to
the NCLT.

36.5.4 Secretary, MCA at the sitting held on 16.7.2026 explained that Clause 36
seeks to correct an omission whereby the Investor Education and Protection Fund
Authority was not expressly named as the `Authority' in the Act; the Secretary further
explained that the amendment addresses an inconsistency in practice, since some
companies transferred unclaimed dividends after only four years while others waited

                                                      294
the full seven years. It was further explained that the amendment brings uniformity by
requiring that, once shares are transferred after seven years, all unclaimed dividend
relating to those shares, whether outstanding for one, two, three or seven years, be
transferred at the same time.

36.5.5 Responding to queries on compliance safeguards, the Secretary, MCA,
explained that existing measures include inspector appointments, an amnesty
scheme allowing companies to clear filing defaults by paying 10% of the additional
fees to avoid strike-off, and Section 454A, which imposes double the penalty for
repeat defaults within a three-year period.

36.6 Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

36.6.1 The Committee note that Clause 36 seeks to amends Section 124(5) so
that unpaid or unclaimed dividend is also transferred to the Investor Education
and Protection Fund (IEPF) at the point when the corresponding shares are
transferred under sub-section (6). It further amends sub-section (6) to specify
that the "Investor Education and Protection Fund Authority" administers the
Fund.

36.6.2 The Committee note the suggestion received for a mechanism to
remove non-existent or untraceable shareholders from a company's register.
The Ministry clarified that Section 59 already provides an adequate route for
rectification of the register of members through the NCLT. The Committee
concur with the Ministry's clarification that Section 59 adequately addresses
the issue of rectifying registers of members, making further amendment
unnecessary.

36.6.3 The Committee note the suggestion to substitute the term "Fund" in
Section 124 with "Authority." The Committee accept the Ministry's clarification
that "Fund" refers to the Investor Education and Protection Fund itself and
requires no modification.

                                                      295
36.6.4 The Committee find that the amendment to Section 124(5) ensures
alignment between the transfer of unclaimed dividends and the transfer of
corresponding shares, thereby strengthening the framework for investor
protection. The Committee accepts Clause 36 as proposed, without
modification.
36.6.5 The Committee further recommend that the Ministry continue to
ensure effective implementation of the provisions relating to the transfer of
unclaimed dividends and shares to the IEPF, while utilising existing
mechanisms under Section 59 for the rectification of registers where required.

                                               CLAUSE - 37

37. Clause 37 of the Bill seeks to amend section 125 of the Companies Act,
2013.

37.1 Provision proposed in The Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

In section 125 of the principal Act,--

(a) in sub-section (2),-

(i) in clause (m), the word "and" occurring at the end shall be omitted;

(c) in sub-section (4), for the words, brackets and figure "may apply to the authority

(d) after sub-section (11), the following sub-section shall be inserted, namely:--

37.2 Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (The Companies Act, 2013):

125. Investor Education and Protection Fund.

(2) There shall be credited to the Fund--

* * * * *

(m) redemption amount of preference shares remaining unpaid or unclaimed for
seven or more years; and

* * * * *

(3) The Fund shall be utilised for--

(a) the refund in respect of unclaimed dividends, matured deposits, matured

* * * * *

37.3 Reasons/Justification given by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs for the

37.4 Important Views/Suggestions given by Experts/Stakeholders:

Some of the important suggestions of the stakeholders in this regard are furnished
below:

                                                      298
37.4.1 "Section 125 should provide clarity on the transfer of sale proceeds of

37.4.2 "It is suggested to insert a new entry under Rule 3(2) of the IEPF Authority

37.4.9 "Section 125 may also provide clarity on transfer of sale proceeds of fractional

                                                      299
37.4.10  "The clause may be revised to cover sale proceeds of fractional shares

37.5 Examination by the Committee:

The Ministry in their written replies to the corresponding suggestions above have
submitted as under:

37.5.1 In response to suggestions at paragraphs 37.4.1, 37.4.2, 37.4.9 and 37.4.10
above, each seeking clarity that sale proceeds of fractional shares arising from a
demerger or other corporate restructuring (in addition to bonus issues, mergers and
amalgamations) be credited to the Investor Education and Protection Fund, the
Ministry noted that clause (n) of sub-section (2) of section 125 already provides for
such other amount as may be prescribed, and that this suggestion would accordingly
be considered through the Rules.

37.5.2 Responding to a suggestion at paragraph 37.4.3 above to expand the clause
to require unpaid or unclaimed consideration payable to public shareholders of a
delisted entity to be credited to the IEPF, the Ministry, in its written submission,
stated that delisting is presently governed by the applicable SEBI regulatory
framework, and that any transfer of such amounts to the IEPF would require careful
examination of its interaction with the existing mechanisms for payment, escrow and
investor claims under the relevant delisting regulations; that the SEBI (Delisting of
Equity Shares) Regulations, 2021 only provide for unclaimed proceeds from the
delisting of Public Service Undertakings to be transferred to the IEPF, though this
mechanism could be extended to all public companies being delisted, in consultation
with SEBI; and that the current provisions of section 125(3) may accordingly be
retained without change, with further clarity on unclaimed proceeds of shares from
delisted entities to be brought in through the SEBI Delisting Regulations.

37.5.3 Addressing a suggestion at paragraph 37.4.4 above for enabling straight-
through processing among companies, depositories and the IEPF Authority, the

                                                      300
Ministry, in its written submission, stated that the suggestion, proposing straight-
through processing between companies, depositories and the IEPF Authority for
automatic transfers via the Rules to be prescribed under section 125, would be
considered at the rule-making stage so as to ensure operational ease and facilitate
claimant verification and reconciliation, and that the provision may accordingly be
retained without any change.

37.5.4 In reply to a suggestion at paragraph 37.4.5 above for insertion of a proviso to
section 125(4) mandating an online searchable discovery facility and online claim
submission, the Ministry, in its written submission, stated that the suggestion,
proposing ease of discovery of unclaimed amounts and an online portal for claim
submission, is a matter for the Rules to be prescribed under section 125, and would
be considered at the rule-making stage as falling within the procedure for settling
unclaimed amounts; and that a proviso limiting the scope of the Rules in the statute
itself may not be prudent, as the Central Government may need to draft rules
extending beyond the ambit of this suggestion.

37.5.5 With respect to a suggestion at paragraph 37.4.6 above that the reference to
the "Investor Education and Protection Fund" in section 125 be replaced with the
"Investor Education and Protection Fund Authority", the Ministry clarified that the
references to the Investor Education and Protection Fund in section 125 relate to the
Fund itself, and not to the Investor Education and Protection Fund Authority.

37.5.6 On the suggestion at paragraph 37.4.7 above that a statutory time-limit of
ninety days be provided for disposal of refund claims, with reasons to be recorded for
rejection, the Ministry, in its written submission, stated that Rule 7(6) of the IEPFA
Rules, 2016 already provides for a sixty-day timeframe, and that keeping the timeline
under Rules provides flexibility. It further noted that a proposal to reduce the
timeframe further for low-volume claims is under active consideration, and that the
provision may accordingly be retained without any change.

37.5.7 In response to a suggestion at paragraph 37.4.8 above to insert a specific
proviso to section 125(4) mandating an online searchable discovery facility, the

                                                      301
Ministry noted that the manner of administering the Investor Education and
Protection Fund, including identification of unclaimed amounts and processing of
refund claims, would appropriately be considered during the framing of subordinate
legislation.

37.5.8.  Secretary, MCA at the sitting held on 16.7.2026 explained that most

suggestions on section 125 were interrelated and already addressed: unclaimed

amounts from buy-backs stood clarified, while those from a demerger or other

restructuring fell under the residuary "any other" clause, which stakeholders simply

wanted made explicit. It was noted that fractional shares from a demerger were not

being brought within the IEPF, since demergers are governed by SEBI's own

separate fund, and for the same reason the suggestion to expand the IEPF's scope

beyond section 125(3) was not accepted. Both bodies function satisfactorily within

their own jurisdictions. It was further noted that a searchable facility for unclaimed

amounts already exists on the IEPF portal, and that a sixty-day timeline for deciding

claims is already prescribed under the Rules, with discussions ongoing to shorten

this further for small-value claims.

37.5.9.  Responding to queries on fractional shares, the Secretary, MCA,

clarified that Section 125(2)(l) already accounts for unclaimed sale proceeds of

fractional shares arising from bonus issues, mergers, and amalgamations, noting

that while a separate SEBI purchase mechanism does not exist, fractions practically

arise from merger exchange ratios.

37.5.10  Addressing concerns over cumbersome IEPF recovery processes and

fee-charging private intermediaries, the Secretary, MCA, explained the recovery

mechanism involving company verification, depositories, and PFMS. The Secretary

noted significant operational improvements, including reducing the backlog to 90

days, approving 67,000 cases last year, and developing an upcoming AI-enabled

portal for straight-through processing. It was further clarified that unclaimed

dividends cannot be used by the Authority and that modest budgetary allocations

fund financial literacy initiatives like 'Niveshak Didis'.

                                      302
37.6 Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

37.6.1 The Committee note that Clause 37 expands the categories of amounts
credited to the Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF), including
unclaimed buy-back consideration, consolidates refund provisions under sub-
section (3), empowers the IEPF Authority to delegate its powers and functions,
and confers rule-making power under section 125(4) to prescribe procedures
and required documents for claims.

37.6.2 Suggestions were received for improving the claims discovery and
processing framework under Section 125, including straight through
processing, an online searchable discovery facility, and inclusion of demerger
related fractional share proceeds. The Ministry clarified that these matters fall
within subordinate legislation under the existing rule making powers in
Section 125. The Committee concur with the Ministry's position that
suggestions relating to discovery and processing mechanisms are best
addressed through subordinate legislation, ensuring flexibility in
implementation. The Committee further note that the rule-making power under
section 125(4) is strictly procedural and remains subject to parliamentary
oversight under section 469 of the Companies Act, 2013.

37.6.3 The Committee note the suggestions concerning unclaimed
consideration payable to shareholders of delisted entities, and concur with the
Ministry's explanation that this is more appropriately addressed through the
SEBI Delisting Regulations, in consultation with SEBI, rather than through
section 125 of the Companies Act.

37.6.4 The Committee find that Clause 37 strengthens the IEPF framework by
broadening the scope of amounts credited and consolidating refund
provisions, thereby significantly enhancing investor protection.

                                                      303
37.6.5 The Committee recommend that, while framing the Rules under
section 125, the Ministry give due consideration to stakeholder suggestions
concerning ease of online discovery of unclaimed assets, straight-through
processing with depositories, and the treatment of demerger-related fractional
shares.
37.6.6 Subject to the observations and recommendations above, the
Committee accept Clause 37 as proposed, without modification.

                                                      304
                                               CLAUSE - 38

38. Clause 38 of the Bill seeks to amend section 128 of the Companies Act,
2013.

38.1 Provision proposed in The Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

In section 128 of the principal Act, in sub-section (6),--

(a) for the words "be punishable with fine which shall not be less than fifty thousand
rupees but which may extend to five lakh rupees", the words "be liable to a penalty of
five lakh rupees in case of a listed company and fifty thousand rupees in case of any
other company" shall be substituted;

(b) the following proviso shall be inserted, namely:--

"Provided that where the contravention relates to sub-section (1) or sub-section (5),
the person referred to in this sub-section shall be liable to a penalty of twenty lakh
rupees in case of a listed company and five lakh rupees in case of any other
company."

38.2 Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (The Companies Act, 2013):

128. Books of account, etc., to be kept by company.

* * * * *

(6) If the managing director, the whole-time director in charge of finance, the Chief
Financial Officer or any other person of a company charged by the Board with the
duty of complying with the provisions of this section, contravenes such provisions,
such managing director, whole-time director in charge of finance, Chief Financial
Officer or such other person of the company shall be punishable with fine which shall
not be less than fifty thousand rupees but which may extend to five lakh rupees.

38.3 Reasons/Justification given by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs for the
proposed provision:

                                                      305
"The amendment replaces the existing fine-based punishment with a penalty
framework, prescribing higher penalties for listed companies and enhanced penalties
for contraventions relating to sub-sections (1) and (5) of the provision. The
amendment is part of the broader decriminalisation exercise under the Bill."

38.4 Important Views/Suggestions given by Experts/Stakeholders:

Some of the important suggestions of the stakeholders in this regard are furnished
below:

38.4.1 "It is suggested that the word `penalty' as proposed in clause 38 may be
substituted with the word `fine', or alternatively that an appropriate appellate
mechanism be provided to reduce the fixed penalty in deserving cases, with
safeguards including a discretionary penalty framework, reasonable opportunity of
being heard, and an independent judicial appellate mechanism before bodies such
as the NCLT/NCLAT, in addition to the existing appeal to the Regional Director under
section 454."

38.4.2 "By way of the proposed amendment, the minimum penalty for private limited
companies may be reduced to `twenty-five thousand' rupees from the proposed `fifty
thousand', and the maximum penalty may be reduced to `one lakh' rupees from the
proposed `five lakhs."

38.4.3 "While shifting enforcement to penalties, the Committee must protect the
baseline statutory audit requirement; any proposed compliance exemptions for
specified classes of companies from statutory audit must be reconsidered."

38.4.4 "Strongly reject any compliance or audit exemption windows under this
accounting framework."

38.4.5 "While changing Section 128 penalties, the Committee must reject any parallel
proposals to introduce exemptions from mandatory statutory audits for specific
classes of companies."

38.4.6 "Urge the Committee to fully retain mandatory statutory audits for all classes
of companies under the Section 128/139 framework; if any turnover-based
exemption is introduced, it must be drawn narrowly, excluding companies with bank
borrowings, group companies, significant related-party transactions, or those audited
under any other law, and should substitute a lighter mechanism such as a "limited
assurance" or "compilation engagement"."

                                                      306
38.4.7 "By way of the proposed amendment, the minimum penalty for private limited
companies may be reduced to `twenty-five thousand' rupees from the proposed `fifty
thousand', and the maximum penalty may be reduced to `one lakh' rupees from the
proposed `five lakhs."

38.4.8 "Welcomes decriminalisation as a move in the right direction, but flags that
even where the NCLT reviews a matter extensively, it is unable to itself punish the
guilty party and must refer the matter to another court/forum for punishment,
resulting in parallel proceedings at two forums and considerable delay."

38.4.9 "The penalty for contravention of sub-section (1) or sub-section (5) of Section
128 may be reduced, especially for listed companies, who may also face
proceedings by SEBI in this regard."

38.4.10  "It is recommended that the proposed clauses be retained as drafted."

38.4.11  "It is suggested that Rule 3 of the Companies (Declaration and

Payment of Dividend) Rules, 2014 be harmonised with the second proviso to section

123(1) of the Companies Act, so as to clarify that the conditions in Rule 3 apply only

where dividend is declared out of accumulated profits transferred to free reserves,

and not where it is declared out of surplus in the profit and loss account that has not

been so transferred, consistent with the recommendation of the Company Law

Committee, 2016."

38.5 Examination by the Committee:

The Ministry in their written replies to the corresponding suggestions above have
submitted as under:

38.5.1 In response to a suggestion at paragraph 38.4.1 above that the word `penalty'
be substituted with `fine', or that an appellate remedy before judicial bodies such as
the NCLT/NCLAT be provided in addition to the existing appeal to the Regional
Director under section 454, the Ministry, in its written submission, stated that the
suggestion to retain the term `fine' may not be accepted, as it would be inconsistent
with the objective of replacing criminal consequences with a civil enforcement
framework; and that the current structure under section 454, confining appellate
review to the Regional Director, an administrative authority within the same
regulatory hierarchy as the Adjudicating Officer, is an appropriate administrative

                                                      307
review mechanism, such that requiring a further appeal to a body like the
NCLT/NCLAT would add another layer to the process.

38.5.2 Responding to suggestions at paragraphs 38.4.2 and 38.4.7 above that the
minimum and maximum penalty for private limited companies be reduced to twenty-
five thousand and one lakh rupees respectively, the Ministry, in its written
submission, stated that the monetary penalties under the Amendment Bill have been
proposed after considering the nature and gravity of the defaults and the aspect of
proportionality, and already incorporate a calibrated penalty framework; that the
penalties under Clause 38 relate to maintenance of books of account, a serious
compliance requirement; and that the amount prescribed has been adjusted
accordingly to deter companies from contravening the provisions of the Companies
Act, 2013.

38.5.3 Addressing suggestions at paragraphs 38.4.3 to 38.4.6 above, each objecting
to any proposed exemption of specified classes of companies from mandatory
statutory audit, the Ministry, in its written submission, stated that the proposal seeks
to enable the Central Government to exempt such class or classes of companies as
may be prescribed from the requirement of statutory audit, with a view to reducing
compliance burden for low-risk companies, without dispensing with the preparation
and filing of financial statements, annual returns or other statutory compliances, all of
which continue to remain mandatory. The Ministry further noted that the content of
these suggestions is more properly addressed under the separate provisions of the
Bill dealing with auditor-appointment exemptions, rather than under Clause 38.

38.5.4 In reply to a suggestion at paragraph 38.4.8 above flagging that, even where
the NCLT reviews a matter extensively, it must refer the punitive element to another
forum, resulting in parallel proceedings and delay, the Ministry, in its written
submission, stated that this concern is factually incorrect, as only Special Courts deal
with criminal offences under the Companies Act and there is no provision for dual
proceedings in criminal matters. Criminal offences are presently tried before Special
Courts constituted under section 435, with sections 436 to 438 providing for the
nature of offences and the procedure for trying them.

                                                      308
38.5.5 With respect to a suggestion at paragraph 38.4.9 above that the penalty for
contravention of sub-section (1) or sub-section (5) of section 128 be reduced,
especially for listed companies who may also face proceedings by SEBI, the
Ministry, in its written submission, stated that the higher penalty prescribed for
contraventions of sub-sections (1) and (5) relates to the maintenance of books of
account, a fundamental statutory obligation critical to transparency, accountability
and the integrity of financial reporting. The prescribed penalty has accordingly been
calibrated as an effective deterrent given the seriousness of such defaults; and the
possibility of parallel proceedings under other laws, including the SEBI framework,
does not warrant a reduction in the penalty under the Companies Act, 2013.

38.5.6 On the suggestion at paragraph 38.4.10 above that the proposed clauses be
retained as drafted, the Ministry noted that the stakeholders were in agreement with
the amendment.

38.5.7 In response to a suggestion at paragraph 38.4.11 above that Rule 3 of the
Companies (Declaration and Payment of Dividend) Rules, 2014 be harmonised with
the second proviso to section 123(1) of the Companies Act, the Ministry noted that
this would be considered appropriately during the framing of subordinate legislation,
since the suggestion relates to the scope and operation of the Rules and does not
require any amendment to the Act.

38.5.8 Explaining the rationale for decriminalisation of the offence under section 128,
Secretary, MCA at the sitting held on 16.7.2026, stated that the nature of such a
default is largely procedural, since keeping the books at a location other than the
designated office does not necessarily indicate an intent to defraud, which is why the
offence is being decriminalised. Two aspects were highlighted: first, that the penalty
for contraventions of sub-sections (1) and (5) has deliberately been kept somewhat
higher than for other contraventions under the section, while remaining proportionate
as between listed and other companies and second, that for small companies and
One Person Companies, the applicable penalty would in any event be capped at fifty
per cent or two lakh rupees, whichever is lower, the concept of proportionality being
already built into the Companies Act.

                                                      309
38.6 Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

38.6.1 The Committee note that Clause 38 replaces the existing fine under
section 128(6) with a calibrated civil penalty, set at 5 lakh for listed companies
and 50,000 for other companies generally, rising to 20 lakh and 5 lakh
respectively where the contravention relates to sub-sections (1) or (5) of
Section 128, as part of the Bill's broader decriminalisation exercise.

38.6.2 Suggestions were received regarding retention of the term "fine" and
provision of an additional judicial appellate remedy. The Ministry clarified that
the existing appellate structure under Section 454 provides an appropriate
administrative safeguard. The Committee concur with the Ministry's position
that the appellate mechanism under Section 454 provides adequate
safeguards, obviating the need for additional judicial remedies.

38.6.3 The Committee note the Ministry's clarification that, for companies
other than listed companies (including private companies), the quantum of
penalty under the un-amended provision is not altered by Clause 38 except
where the higher penalty for contraventions under sub-sections (1) or (5)
applies. The Committee find that the suggestion for a further reduction specific
to private companies does not warrant change.

38.6.4 The Committee also note the concerns raised regarding parallel
proceedings. The Committee accept the Ministry's clarification that concerns
about parallel proceedings are misplaced, as criminal matters remain
exclusively within the jurisdiction of Special Courts.

38.6.5 The Committee recognize that Clause 38 advances the Bill's objective
of decriminalisation by replacing criminal fines with calibrated civil penalties,
thereby reducing litigation risk while maintaining effective deterrence, and that
the penalty framework appropriately distinguishes between listed and other
companies.

                                                      310
38.6.6 The Committee recommend that the Ministry continue to ensure clarity
in the application of civil penalties under section 128(6), while properly
addressing related matters such as auditor-appointment exemptions under the
appropriate provisions of the Bill.
38.6.7 Subject to the observations and recommendations above, the
Committee accept Clause 38 as proposed, without modification.

                                               CLAUSE - 39

39. Clause 39 of the Bill seeks to amend section 131 of the Companies Act,
2013.

39.1 Provision proposed in The Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

In section 131 of the principal Act, in sub-section (1), in the long line, for the words
"three preceding financial years", the words "three immediately preceding financial
years" shall be substituted.

39.2 Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (The Companies Act, 2013):

131. Voluntary revision of financial statements or Board's report.

(1) If it appears to the directors of a company that--

(a) the financial statement of the company; or

(b) the report of the Board,

do not comply with the provisions of section 129 or section 134 they may prepare
revised financial statement or a revised report in respect of any of the three
preceding financial years after obtaining approval of the Tribunal on an application
made by the company in such form and manner as may be prescribed and a copy of
the order passed by the Tribunal shall be filed with the Registrar:

Provided that the Tribunal shall give notice to the Central Government and the
Income-tax authorities and shall take into consideration the representations, if any,
made by that Government or the authorities before passing any order under this
section:

Provided further that such revised financial statement or report shall not be prepared
or filed more than once in a financial year:

Provided also that the detailed reasons for revision of such financial statement or
report shall also be disclosed in the Board's report in the relevant financial year in
which such revision is being made.

                                                      312
39.3 Reasons/Justification given by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs for the
proposed provision:

"The word `immediately' is being inserted in the provision for clarity."

39.4 Important Views/Suggestions given by Experts/Stakeholders:

Some of the important suggestions of the stakeholders in this regard are furnished
below:

39.4.1 "Recommends that the Committee permit revision of financial statements or
the Board's report beyond the prescribed three-year period where such revision is
required pursuant to an order of a Court, Tribunal, SEBI, the RoC, RD, or any other
statutory regulator; and consider permitting such revision, at the discretion of the
competent authority, in cases involving fraud, genuine hardship, or were considered
necessary in the public interest."

39.4.2 "It is recommended that the proposed clauses be retained as drafted."

39.4.3 "It is suggested that Rule 3 of the Companies (Declaration and Payment of
Dividend) Rules, 2014 be harmonised with the second proviso to section 123(1) of
the Companies Act, so as to clarify that the conditions in Rule 3 apply only where
dividend is declared out of accumulated profits transferred to free reserves, and not
where it is declared out of surplus in the profit and loss account that has not been so
transferred, consistent with the recommendation of the Company Law Committee,
2016."

39.5 Examination by the Committee:

The Ministry in their written replies to the corresponding suggestions above have
submitted as under:

39.5.1 In response to a suggestion at paragraph 39.4.1 above that the Committee
permit revision of financial statements or the Board's report beyond the prescribed
three-year period where required pursuant to an order of a Court, Tribunal, SEBI, the
RoC, RD, or any other statutory regulator, the Ministry noted that revision of financial
statements pursuant to an order of the Court or Tribunal, on an application by the

                                                      313
Central Government, Income-tax authorities, SEBI or any other statutory authority, is
already provided for under section 130 of the Act.

39.5.2 On the suggestion at paragraph 39.4.2 above that the proposed clauses be
retained as drafted, the Ministry, reiterating its position on the identical suggestion
raised under Clause 38, noted that the stakeholders were in agreement with the
amendment.

39.5.3 Addressing a suggestion at paragraph 39.4.3 above that Rule 3 of the
Companies (Declaration and Payment of Dividend) Rules, 2014 be harmonised with
the second proviso to section 123(1) of the Companies Act, consistent with the
recommendation of the Company Law Committee, 2016, the Ministry, reiterating its
position on the identical suggestion raised under Clause 38, noted that this would be
considered appropriately during the framing of subordinate legislation, since the
suggestion relates to the scope and operation of the Rules and does not require any
amendment to the Act.

39.5.4 Secretary, MCA at the sitting held on 16.7.2026 explained that the
amendment was intended to bring clarity, since companies had in practice
undertaken voluntary revision of financial statements many years after the relevant
financial year, in some instances citing court orders even after a decade, giving rise
to litigation. The amendment accordingly confines voluntary revision under section
131 to the three immediately preceding financial years.

39.5.5 On the suggestion at paragraph 39.4.1 above, that revision be permitted
beyond this window were based on a Court, Tribunal or other regulatory order, or in
cases of fraud or genuine hardship, the Secretary clarified that section 130 already
separately provides for reopening of accounts pursuant to a Court or Tribunal order,
and that this suggestion was therefore not accepted. Sections 130 and 131 dealing
with the two situations respectively.

                                                      314
39.6 Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:
39.6.1 The Committee note that Clause 39 inserts the word "immediately"
before "preceding financial years" in section 131(1), for the purpose of
bringing clarity as to the three-year window within which a company may
voluntarily revise its financial statements or Board's report.
39.6.2 The Committee note the suggestions for widening the revision window
in cases involving Court, Tribunal, or regulatory orders, or in situations of
fraud or hardship. The Ministry clarified that revisions pursuant to Court or
Tribunal orders are already provided for under Section 130 of the Act,
independent of the voluntaryrevision window in Section 131. The Committee
concur with this clarification and observe that Clause 39, being a purely
clarificatory amendment to remove ambiguity regarding the threeyear window,
requires no modification.
39.6.3 The Committee accept Clause 39 as proposed, without modification.
39.6.4 The Committee further recommend that the Ministry continue to ensure
clarity in the application and guidance of Sections 130 and 131, so that
companies are able to seamlessly distinguish between voluntary revisions and
those mandated by judicial or regulatory directions.

40.2. Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (Companies Act, 2013):

132. Constitution of National Financial Reporting Authority.--(1) The Central
Government may, by notification, constitute a National Financial Reporting Authority
to provide for matters relating to accounting and auditing standards under this Act.

[(1A) The National Financial Reporting Authority shall perform its functions through
such divisions as may be prescribed.]

(2) Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force,
the National Financial Reporting Authority shall--

(a) make recommendations to the Central Government on the formulation and laying
down of accounting and auditing policies and standards for adoption by companies
or class of companies or their auditors, as the case may be;

(b) monitor and enforce the compliance with accounting standards and auditing
standards in such manner as may be prescribed;

(c) oversee the quality of service of the professions associated with ensuring
compliance with such standards, and suggest measures required for improvement in
quality of service and such other related matters as may be prescribed; and

(d) perform such other functions relating to clauses (a), (b) and (c) as may be
prescribed.

                                                      319
(3) The National Financial Reporting Authority shall consist of a chairperson, who
shall be a person of eminence and having expertise in accountancy, auditing, finance
or law to be appointed by the Central Government and such other members not
exceeding fifteen consisting of part-time and full-time members as may be
prescribed:

Provided that the terms and conditions and the manner of appointment of the
chairperson and members shall be such as may be prescribed:

Provided further that the chairperson and members shall make a declaration to the
Central Government in the prescribed form regarding no conflict of interest or lack of
independence in respect of his or their appointment:

Provided also that the chairperson and members, who are in full-time employment
with National Financial Reporting Authority shall not be associated with any audit firm
(including related consultancy firms) during the course of their appointment and two
years after ceasing to hold such appointment.

[(3A) Each division of the National Financial Reporting Authority shall be presided
over by the Chairperson or a full-time Member authorized by the Chairperson.

(3B) There shall be an executive body of the National Financial Reporting Authority
consisting of the Chairperson and full-time Members of such Authority for efficient
discharge of its functions under sub-section (2) [other than clause (a) and sub-
section (4).]

(4) Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force,
the National Financial Reporting Authority shall--

(a) have the power to investigate, either suo motu or on a reference made to it by the
Central Government, for such class of bodies corporate or persons, in such manners
may be prescribed into the matters of professional or other misconduct committed by
any member or firm of chartered accountants, registered under the Chartered
Accountants Act, 1949 (38 of 1949):

Provided that no other institute or body shall initiate or continue any proceedings in
such matters of misconduct where the National Financial Reporting Authority has
initiated an investigation under this section;

(b) have the same powers as are vested in a civil court under the Code of Civil

and at such time as may be specified by the National Financial Reporting Authority;

(ii) summoning and enforcing the attendance of persons and examining them on
oath;

(iii) inspection of any books, registers and other documents of any person referred to
in clause (b) at any place;

(iv) issuing commissions for examination of witnesses or documents;

(c) where professional or other misconduct is proved, have the power to make order
for--

(A) imposing penalty of--

(I) not less than one lakh rupees, but which may extend to five times of the fees

(II) not less than [five lakh rupees], but which may extend to ten times of the fees

[(B) debarring the member or the firm from--

I. being appointed as an auditor or internal auditor or undertaking any audit in

for a minimum period of six months or such higher period not exceeding ten years as
may be determined by the National Financial Reporting Authority.]

Explanation.--For the purposes of this sub-section, the expression "professional or

40.3. Reasons/Justification given by the Ministry for the proposed provisions:

"Clause No. 40(a)

The amendment seeks to rationalise the framework of the National Financial
Reporting Authority. The amendments in section 132 is part of a broader set of
changes to strengthen the NFRA, on the lines of similar regulators.

Clause No. 40(b)

This amendment is proposed to include words "bodies corporates" for clarifying the
role of NFRA.

Clause No. 40(c)

The amendment seeks to rationalise the framework of the National Financial
Reporting Authority. The amendments in section 132 is part of a broader set of
changes to strengthen the NFRA, on the lines of similar regulators.

Clause No. 40(d)

This amendment seeks to insert a new sub-section (3C) to provide for the powers of
general superintendence and direction of the affairs of the NFRA to be vested in the
Chairperson.

New sub-section (3D) seeks to enable the executive body to delegate its powers to
the Chairperson, full-time Members, officers or committees, subject to specified
conditions. The amendment in section 132 is part of a broader set of changes to
strengthen the NFRA, on the lines of similar regulators.

Clause No. 40(e)

The amendment strengthens NFRA's enforcement framework by clarifying the scope
of investigable misconduct, allowing it to issue graded remedial measures, and

                                                      323
enabling the Central Government to define the classes subject to investigation while
NFRA specifies the investigative procedure by regulations.

Clause No. 40(f)

The amendment strengthens NFRA's enforcement by penalising non-compliance
with its orders or failure to pay penalties within the prescribed period, including
through imprisonment, fines and additional debarment. The amendment in section
132 is part of a broader set of changes to strengthen the NFRA, on the lines of
similar regulators.

Clause No. 40(g)

This amendment seeks to provide powers to Authority regarding internal procedures
and transaction of its business at its meetings.

Clause No. 40(h)

This amendment seeks to provide powers to Authority regarding appointment of
secretary and other employees.

Clause No. 40(i)

The insertion of sub-section (16) clarifies that procedural or compositional defects in
the NFRA shall not invalidate its proceedings, thereby ensuring certainty and
continuity in its functioning.

The insertion of sub-section (17) enables the Authority to engage domain experts
and professionals to strengthen its technical capacity and support effective discharge
of its functions. The amendments in section 132 is part of a broader set of changes
to strengthen the NFRA, on the lines of similar regulators."
