Definition of Professional Misconduct

40.4.9  "Section 22 of the CA Act lists down various acts or omissions in the

Schedule, which, in the case of a disciplinary proceeding, enables specific and fair

process. Clear and detailed Rules should be framed to define and explain what

                                       326
constitutes "professional misconduct". Given the serious professional consequences
involved, such misconduct should be precisely articulated to distinguish wilful and
pervasive violations from errors of professional judgment or procedural lapses,
thereby ensuring certainty, consistency and adherence to principles of natural
justice."

40.4.10      "Ensure a balanced enforcement framework by avoiding excessive

layering of sanctions for a single instance professional misconduct."

Jurisdictional Overlap

40.4.11      "Section 132(1A) - "The National Financial Reporting Authority shall be

a body corporate..." NFRA was originally envisaged as an oversight authority with a

limited and clearly defined mandate in relation to accounting and auditing standards

for public interest entities, while regulation of the Chartered Accountancy profession

continued under the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949. However, when the

proposed body corporate status is read together with the expanded powers relating

to registration, investigation, disciplinary proceedings, fee collection, issuance of

directions, and delegated regulation making powers, the framework significantly

broadens the role of NFRA beyond its original oversight function. This may result in

overlap with the statutory functions of ICAI, leading to regulatory duplication,

institutional fragmentation, increased compliance burden, and uncertainty regarding

jurisdictional boundaries. Accordingly, the proposed framework may require

reconsideration to preserve regulatory clarity, institutional balance, and consistency

with the legislative scheme governing the profession. It was not recommended in the

Company Law Committee Report, 2022."

40.4.12      "Clear statutory demarcation of jurisdiction be provided between NFRA

and other investigative authorities functioning under the Companies Act, 2013 to

avoid overlapping proceedings and regulatory uncertainty."

40.4.13      "Expansion of the jurisdiction of the National Financial Reporting

Authority (NFRA) is not warranted at the present stage. Existing regulatory

mechanisms under ICAI and other statutory authorities already provide adequate

oversight. Further expansion may result in overlapping jurisdiction, regulatory

duplication, increased compliance burden. and uncertainty for professionals and

companies."

40.4.14      "The text of the Bill must explicitly clarify that NFRA's enforcement

jurisdiction strictly covers listed entities, Public Interest entities (PIEs), and massive

                        327
unlisted subsidiaries. MSMEs and their small-tier accounting firms can remain under
the oversight of the ICAI to prevent regulatory overreach. Allowing ICAI, instead of
NFRA, to regulate audits of Small Companies would significantly reduce audit costs
by not adding an additional layer of regulation in form of NFRA, while maintaining
appropriate professional oversight"

40.4.15  "In Section 132(4) (a) the removal of the words- `where the National

Financial Reporting Authority has initiated an investigation under this Section' As per

the legislative mandate, NFRA's jurisdiction extends to all entities as provided under

Rule 3 of NFRA Rules 2018. However, it has been observed that ICAI has continued

to exercise disciplinary powers in respect of the entities over which it has no

jurisdiction. The proviso takes care of the period of transition and now, to bring more

clarity in the statutory framework and avoid ambiguity, if any is being perceived, and

any future legal challenges, it is proposed to be deleted."

Penal Provisions

40.4.16  "The proposed amendment (including censure, additional professional

training, etc.) seeks to insert the expression "one or more of the following namely" at

the end of first line of 132 (4) (c). Existing provision of the law provides for a

monetary penalty in case of proved misconduct. It is suggested that the existing

principle of levy of monetary penalty in cases of proved misconduct must be

maintained, and the other actions may supplement the monetary penalty."

40.4.17  "It is recommended omission of the proposed Section 132(4A) in its

entirety. The proposed framework of imprisonment, additional penalties and further

debarment for non-payment of a penalty imposed under Section 132(4)(c) may be

reconsidered, and recovery may instead be effected through the existing statutory

recovery mechanisms available under the Act. This would ensure proportionality in

enforcement and alignment with the Bill's objective of decriminalisation."

40.4.19  "Consider adding a milder sanction option (advisory or warning) for

NFRA, while emphasizing the importance of fair and consistent application. NFRA

should develop clear sanction guidelines, and where a warning or censure is issued

under this new power, other regulators should avoid initiating duplicative proceedings

for the same underlying conduct. We also recommend two suggestions on the

expanded NFRA powers. - First, any debarment should apply only to individual

auditors responsible for misconduct and not to entire firms, so innocent partners and

clients are not unfairly impacted. - Second, the broadened definition of "professional

or other misconduct" should be refined to cover only violations related to auditors'

                  328
duties, which ensures NFRA focuses on serious audit failures without overreaching
into unrelated compliance matters."

40.4.20    "Section 132(1A) needs to define the scope of adjudicatory and

jurisdictional powers of NFRA. Quasi-judicial powers of regulators such as SEBI, RBI

need to be evaluated and a redraft to be considered and incorporated. The

functionality cannot be in totality left to rules. NFRA is envisaged with ombudsman

powers with scope for entities above ICAI and not as a tribunal."

Appeals

40.4.21    "In Section 132(5) - For the suggested Amendment relating to the

Appellate Authority - It is suggested that appeals against orders passed by NFRA

40.4.22    "Proposal that no injunction shall be granted by any court or other

settlement mechanism may be considered to be incorporated for ease of doing

40.5.3.  With regard to the concern regarding overlapping of jurisdiction

between NFRA and ICAI, the Ministry in its written response submitted as under:

"The Companies Act, 2013 and the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949 establish
distinct statutory frameworks with clearly defined roles for NFRA and ICAI. NFRA
has been constituted as an independent regulator for audit oversight in respect of
prescribed classes of companies and bodies corporate (listed companies, unlisted
public companies having paid-up capital of 500 crore or more, turnover of 1,000
crore or more, or aggregate outstanding loans, debentures and deposits of 500
crore or more, as well as banking companies, insurance companies, electricity
companies, companies governed by special Acts), while ICAI continues to exercise
its statutory functions under the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949.

NFRA was created in the aftermath of various corporate scams/frauds and audit
failures of the 1990s and early 2000s, and in consonance with the global trend of
moving away from self-regulation by the CA profession. NFRA was notified on 1

                                                      331
October 2018. NFRA's jurisdiction extends to only about 9000+ companies which
mainly are listed companies, unlisted public companies over certain financial
thresholds, all insurance, banking and electricity generating companies, as per Rule
3 of NFRA Rules 2018.

NFRA is a member of the International Forum of Independent Audit Regulators
(IFIAR) on account of its meeting two fundamental requirements: (1) NFRA is
independent of the profession; and (2) NFRA carries out recurrent audit quality
inspections. Both these conditions have to be met by audit regulators wanting to be
members of IFIAR.

The proposed amendments do not enlarge the jurisdiction of NFRA but only
strengthen its existing regulatory and enforcement framework as recommended by
the Company Law Committee Report, 2022. The respective jurisdictions of NFRA
and ICAI remain as provided under the existing statutory framework and do not result
in regulatory overlap or duplication."

40.5.4.  In response to the suggestions regarding amendment in the functions

or composition of the NFRA and its Executive Body, the Ministry in their written reply

submitted as under:

"The NFRA constituted under section 132 read with NFRA (Manner of Appointment
and other Terms and Conditions of Service of Chairperson and Members) Rules,
2018 includes members from the profession (i.e. Chartered Accountants) implying
that regulates/regulated persons (i.e. CAs) are on the regulator's governing board.

Recognizing this conflict of interest at the level of full Authority and to ensure
independence in regulation of auditors especially with regard to quality control
management, investigation and enforcement in respect of. Professional or other
misconduct, the Executive Body of NFRA was created independent of the profession
through sub-section (3B),

Executive Body is vested with statutory functions of monitoring and enforcing
compliance with auditing and accounting standards, exercising oversight over audit
quality and disciplinary proceedings in keeping with the legislative intent of setting up
of NFRA. "

                     332
40.5.5.   With regard to the concerns about the penal provisions provided to the

NFRA under the Bill, the Ministry in their written reply submitted as follows:

"The proposed provisions provide a comprehensive disciplinary framework, and an

the principles of natural justice. The nature of disciplinary action, including advisory,
censure, warning or debarment, will depend on the facts and circumstances of each
case. Further, the Act recognises both individual members and audit firms within the
regulatory jurisdiction of NFRA, accordingly, the proposed provision appropriately
enables disciplinary action against the person or entity found responsible for the
misconduct, depending on the facts of the case"

40.5.6.   With regard to the appellate mechanism under the Bill, the Ministry

Section 132(5) preserves the statutory appeal to NCLAT. A settlement mechanism is

40.6. Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

40.6.1.  The Committee note that Clause 40 seeks amendment of Section

132 of the Companies Act. Clause 40(d) seeks to insert new sub-sections (3C)

and (3D) after Section 132 (3B) of the parent act.

The Committee understand that Section 132 (3B) of the Companies Act creates
an executive body of the National Financial Reporting Authority consisting of
the Chairperson and full-time Members of such Authority for efficient
discharge of its functions under sub-section (2) [other than clause (a) and sub-
section (4). The Committee also note that sub-section (2) outlines the core
responsibilities of the NFRA regarding corporate financial reporting and sub-
section (4) equips the NFRA with the authority needed to act as a strict
regulator, granting it significant investigative and penal powers.

Thus, Section 132 (3B) distinctly identifies the function of the Executive Body
vis a vis the General Body. During examination of the suggestions, it was
highlighted that the present formulation of Section 132(3B) of the Act, has
missed out incorporating the relevant proposed sections 132A, 132C, 132D,
132I, 132J, 132K, and 454C in the functions of the Executive Body. Similarly,
suggestions were also received from stakeholders asking for the clarification
in the role and functions of Executive Body and full NFRA. The Committee
arrived at the considered opinion that the role and functions of Executive Body
and full NFRA must be clearly specified in the statute. The Ministry was in
agreement with the view of the Committee. Accordingly, after extensive
discussions with the Ministry and in view of the suggestions of the
stakeholders the Committee recommend that a new sub-clause, namely, 40(ca)
be added after Clause 40 (c) to make necessary changes in Section 132, sub-
section (3B)

                                                      335
"(ca) in sub-section (3B), for the words, brackets, figures and letter "functions
under sub-section (2) [other than clause (a)] and sub-section (4)", the following
shall be substituted, namely:--

"functions under--

(i) sub-section (2) [other than clause (a)], sub-sections (4) and (4A), sub-
section (10) in respect of meetings of the Executive Body, sub-section (11) and
sub-section (17), of section 132;

(ii) section 132A;

(iii) sub-section (2) of section 132C; and

(iv) section 132D.";

40.6.2.  The Committee note that under Clause 40, the proposed Section

132(3C) vests the Chairperson with powers of general superintendence and

permits the exercise of powers delegated by the Executive Body, while Section

132(3D) enables further delegation of powers by the Executive Body. The

Committee also note that present framework provides that substantive

decision making and regulatory functions are exercised by a limited subset of

members. The Committee feel such concentration of powers may dilute the

benefits of collective decision-making, institutional checks and balances, and

the diverse expertise intended to be represented within the Authority. The

Committee therefore recommend that the power of delegation through

`General' order may not be vested in the Executive Body. Accordingly, the

Committee desire the removal of the words `general or' from the text of the

Clause 40 (d) (3D).

40.6.3.  The Committee note that Clause No. 40(e) seeks to strengthen

NFRA's enforcement framework by clarifying the scope of investigable

misconduct, allowing it to issue graded remedial measures, and enabling the

Central Government to define the classes subject to investigation while NFRA

specifies the investigative procedure by regulations. Clause 40(e) amends

Section 132 (4) (a) of the Companies Act, 2013 which provides NFRA the power

to investigate in such manner as may be prescribed by the Central

Government. It seeks to substitute the words *"in such manner as may be

prescribed"*, with the words ", *as may be prescribed, and in such manner as

may be specified by regulations by the said Authority"*.

                      336
The Committee find that the substitution of the words as stated above
enhances the power of NFRA to determine the manner of investigation under
Section 132 (4)(a). In this regard, concerned about the expansion of NFRA's
investigative powers, the stakeholders have suggested that the words "as may
be prescribed" be restored in Section 132(4)(a) to enable the manner and
procedure of investigation to be prescribed through rules. The Committee
understand that in the context of the Companies Act, "prescribed" refers to
rules made by the Central Government, as opposed to "specified by
regulations" which refers to the Authority. The Ministry accepted the proposed
suggestion and stated that the amendment pertaining to clause (a) of sub-
section (4) may be omitted as the power of prescribing manner of investigation
is to be retained with Central Government on lines of proposed provision of
section 132D (under Clause 41) which seeks to empower Central Government
to prescribe manner of inquiry.

In view of the reply furnished by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs and after due
consideration of the suggestions received the Committee recommend that in
the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026, in clause 40, in sub clause (e),
item (i) may be omitted.

40.6.4.  With regard to the investigative powers of the NFRA In Section

132(4) (a), the Committee further note the suggestion regarding Section

132(4)(a) to omit the words `where the National Financial Reporting Authority

has initiated an investigation under this Section' from the proviso to the said

clause. The Committee understand that this proviso was originally intended to

address the period of transition when the National Financial Reporting

Authority (NFRA) was first established.

The Committee observe that the Ministry has stated that jurisdiction of the
NFRA over specific classes of companies is clearly defined under the
legislative mandate and the NFRA Rules. However, the Committee are apprised
that despite this demarcation, there are instances where the Institute of
Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI) has continued to exercise disciplinary
powers and initiate actions against entities that squarely fall under the NFRA's
jurisdiction, leading to regulatory duplication and jurisdictional conflict. The
Committee are of the firm view that the statutory framework must provide
absolute clarity regarding the powers to be exercised by respective regulators,
leaving no ambiguity as to whether a matter falls under the purview of the ICAI
or the NFRA. The Ministry on its part have accepted that the omission of the
relevant words would bring clarity in the respective roles of NFRA and other
bodies. Therefore, to prevent parallel proceedings and in view of the Ministry's

                                                      337
agreement on the issue, the Committee agrees with the proposed modification.
Thus, the Committee recommend that in clause 40, in sub clause (e), item (i) to
be omitted may be replaced by

"(i) in clause (a), in the proviso, the words "where the National Financial
Reporting Authority has initiated an investigation under this section" shall be
omitted;"

40.6.5.  The Committee further note that Clause 40(e) (iii) seeks to

substitute the Explanation under Section 132 Sub-section (4). The proposed

amendment seeks to define the expression "professional or other misconduct"

and state that it shall include the meaning assigned to it under section 22 of

the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949, and shall further include `such acts or

omissions which constitute a contravention of the provisions of this Act, or the

rules or regulations made thereunder, in so far as such provisions relate to

matters within the jurisdiction, functions, or regulatory remit of the National

Financial Reporting Authority'. The Committee note the suggestion that the

broadened definition of "professional or other misconduct" should be refined

to cover only violations related to auditor duties.

The Committee also observe that the Ministry has accepted the need to limit
the definition of professional or other misconduct to audit matters.

The Committee therefore recommend that the Explanation be suitably modified
and be read as under:

"Explanation.--For the purposes of this sub-section, the expression
"professional or other misconduct" shall include the meaning assigned to it
under section 22 of the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949, and shall further
include such acts or omissions which constitute a contravention of the
provisions of this Act, or the rules or regulations made thereunder, in so far as
such provisions relate to audit matters within the jurisdiction, functions, or
regulatory remit of the National Financial Reporting Authority."

40.6.6.  The Committee note that Clause 40(f) seeks to strengthen NFRA's

enforcement by penalising non-compliance with its orders or failure to pay

penalties within the prescribed period, including through imprisonment, fines

and additional debarment. The Committee note that the provision allowing

imprisonment for failure to comply with orders of NFRA is not in consonance

with the larger objective of decriminalisation of the present legislation. The

Committee therefore recommend that the provision for imprisonment for non-

         338
compliance with the orders of the NFRA or failure to pay penalties be deleted
and the punishment restricted to a fine. This would ensure that the
enforcement mechanism retains adequate deterrence while aligning the clause
with the broader legislative intent of decriminalisation. Thus, the Committee
desire that under Clause 40 (f) the Sub-section 4A(a)(i) the words `with
imprisonment which may extend to six months or' may be removed so that the
amended 4A(a)(i) reads as under:

"(i) with fine which shall not be less than one lakh rupees but which may
extend to five lakh rupees, if such person is an individual; or"

40.6.7.  The Committee note that Clause 40(g) of the Bill seeks to amend

sub-section (10) of Section 132 of the Principal Act, inter-alia substituting the

word "prescribed" with "specified by regulations by the said Authority." The

Committee observe that this amendment is intended to transfer the power to

determine the time, place, and rules of procedure for the meetings of the

National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA) from the Central Government to

the Authority itself.

The Committee note the apprehensions expressed by various stakeholders
regarding the excessive delegation of powers to the Authority, with concerns
being raised about potential regulatory overreach. While the Committee
recognise the need to restrict the delegation of broad substantive powers, they
are of the considered view that the transaction of business at internal
meetings is strictly a procedural and administrative matter. The Committee feel
that such internal procedures do not impact the substantive rights, liabilities,
or compliance requirements of the regulated entities. The Committee,
therefore, agrees that granting the Authority the requisite flexibility to govern
its own day-to-day internal workings through regulations is administratively
beneficial. Similar operational autonomy is granted to independent regulators,
and is not equivalent to an excessive delegation of legislative power. The
Committee therefore desire that Clause 40(g) seeking amendment to sub-
section (10) of Section 132 of the Principal Act be read as under:

"(g) in sub-section (10),--

(i) after the words "National Financial Reporting Authority", the words "and
Executive Body" shall be inserted;

                             339
(ii) for the word "prescribed", the words "specified by regulations by the said
Authority" shall be substituted;"

40.6.8.    The Committee observe that Clause 40 (h) seeks to provide

powers to Authority regarding appointment of secretary and other employees

by making changes in sub-section 11 of Section 132. During examination the

Committee received suggestions that the power under Section 132(11) should

to be retained with the Central Government and should not be delegated.

Multiple stakeholders also expressed their apprehensions regarding the

excessive delegation of powers to the NFRA by the Central Government. The

Committee after careful consideration of the views of the stakeholders with

particular regard to the issue of excessive delegation feel that the Central

Government should consider keeping the power to appoint the Secretary and

other employees of the Authority under Section 132(11) vested with itself,

rather than delegating it to the NFRA. This will address the concerns that

allowing a regulatory body completely unchecked administrative hiring power

can negatively impact accountability checks and general oversight. The

Committee accordingly recommend that Clause 40(h) may be omitted in

entirety.

40.6.9.    The Committee also note that Section 132(3) of the Companies

Act, 2013 deals with the composition of the National Financial Reporting

Authority (NFRA). Section 132(3) provides that the NFRA shall consist of a

Chairperson, appointed by the Central Government, who must be a person of

eminence with expertise in accountancy, auditing, finance, or law. However,

the act does not specify the qualifications of the Members. The Ministry, under

Clause 40 (i) seeks to insert sub-section 16 and 17 after sub-section 15 of

section 132 of Companies Act, 2013. The proposed section (17) provides that

the National Financial Reporting Authority may, in such manner as may be

`specified by regulations', engage such number of experts and professionals

who have special knowledge of, and experience in, accounting standards,

auditing standards, economics, law, business or such other disciplines related

to its functions.

The Committee observe that the Bill does not prescribe any qualifications for
the Members of the Executive Body. The Committee are of the considered view
that the Members of NFRA particularly the Executive Body should be drawn
from a diverse mix of backgrounds across administration, business, finance,
and corporate law.

                   340
In this regard the Committee recommend that in Clause 40 (i) (f) the words
`specified by regulations' may be replaced with the words `prescribed' so that
the power to determine the qualifications of NFRA members remains with the
Central Government. Thus, Clause 40 (i) (17) of the Bill may be reframed as
under:

"(17) The National Financial Reporting Authority may, in such manner as may
be prescribed, engage such number of experts and professionals who have
special knowledge of, and experience in, accounting standards, auditing
standards, economics, law, business or such other disciplines related to its
functions, as it deems necessary to assist the said Authority in the discharge
of its functions under this Act.".
40.6.10. The Committee further recognise the need for amending the
Companies Act to explicitly prescribe the professional composition of the
Executive Body directly within the principal statute. This would ensure that
authority possesses the technical, legal, and financial expertise necessary to
govern specialized sectors and prevent it from becoming a generalist
administrative body. The Committee therefore recommend that Section 132,
sub-section 3 of the Companies Act may be amended to include the following
words:

"who have special knowledge of, and experience in, accounting standards,
auditing standards, economics, law and business".

                                               CLAUSE - 41

41.1. Provision proposed in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

After section 132 of the principal Act, the following sections shall be inserted,
namely:--

132 A. (1) With effect from such date as the Central Government may, by notification,
specify in this behalf, no individual or firm shall be appointed as auditor under section
139 in respect of companies or class of companies or bodies corporate referred to in
clause (a) of sub-section (4) of section 132, unless the individual or firm intimates the
details of his or its registration with the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India to
the National Financial Reporting Authority within such time, in such manner and
alongwith such fees, as may be prescribed.

(2) The auditors of companies or class of companies or bodies corporate referred to
in sub-section (1) shall file such documents or returns or information with the
National Financial Reporting Authority, in such form and manner, within such period,
and on payment of such fees, as may be specified by regulations by the said
Authority.

(3) A person required to furnish any document or return or any other information
under sub-section (2), who fails to furnish any document or return or any other
information, shall be liable to penalty of not less than twenty-five thousand rupees,
but which may extend to five hundred rupees for each day during which such default
continues, subject to a maximum of twenty-five lakh rupees, if such person is an
auditor or an audit firm.

(4) If any person, while fulfilling his obligations under this section,-

(a) makes a statement or furnishes any document or return or any other information
which he knows or has reason to believe to be false in any material particular; or

(b) omits to state any material facts or particulars knowing them to be material; or

(c) wilfully alters, suppresses or destroys any document, return or information, which
is required to be furnished,

                                                      342
then, without prejudice to any other action which may be taken under any law for the
time being in force, such person shall be liable to a penalty of not less than fifty
thousand rupees, but which may extend to one thousand rupees for each day during
which such default continues, subject to a maximum of fifty lakh rupees, if such
person is an auditor or an audit firm.

132B. (1) The Central Government may, after due appropriation made by Parliament
by law in this behalf, make to the National Financial Reporting Authority, grants of
such sums of money as the Central Government may think fit for being utilised for
the purposes of this Act.

(2) There shall be constituted a Fund to be called the National Financial Reporting
Authority Fund wherein the following shall be credited, namely:--

(a) grants made by the Central Government for the purposes of the National
Financial Reporting Authority Fund;

(b) all fees received by the said Authority under this Act;

(c) all sums received by the said Authority from such other sources as may be
decided by the Central Government;

(d) interest or other income received out of the investments made from the National
Financial Reporting Authority Fund.

(3) The Fund shall be applied for meeting the expenses of the National Financial
Reporting Authority for the discharge of its functions and for the purposes of this Act
and for such other purposes, as may be prescribed.

132C. (1) In exercise of its functions under this Act, where the National Financial
Reporting Authority is satisfied that it is necessary in public interest or the interest of
investors or creditors or other persons concerned, it may give such directions to
auditors of companies, class of companies or bodies corporate referred to in clause
(a) of sub-section (4) of section 132, as it may consider appropriate.

(2) Whoever fails to comply with any direction given under sub-section (1), shall be
liable to a penalty of not less than fifty thousand rupees but which may extend to one
thousand rupees for each day during which such default continues, subject to a
maximum of fifty lakh rupees in case of an auditor or one crore in case of an audit
firm.

                                                      343
132D. (1) The National Financial Reporting Authority may, after holding inquiry, in
such manner as may be prescribed and after giving a reasonable opportunity of
being heard, impose such penalty under sub-section (4) of section 132A or sub-
section (2) of section 132C, as it may consider appropriate.

(2) While holding an inquiry, the National Financial Reporting Authority shall have
power to summon and enforce the attendance of any person acquainted with the
facts and circumstances of the case to give evidence or to produce any document,
which in the opinion of the said Authority, may be useful for or relevant to the subject
matter of the inquiry and if, on such inquiry, it is satisfied that the person has failed to
comply with the provisions of any of the sections specified in sub-section (1), it may
impose such penalty as it considers appropriate in accordance with the provisions of
any of those sections.

(3) The amount of any penalty imposed under this section, if not paid, may be
recovered by the National Financial Reporting Authority, in such manner as may be
prescribed, as if it were an arrear of land revenue.

(4) All sums realised by way of penalties under this section shall be credited to the
Consolidated Fund of India.

(5) Any person aggrieved by an order of the National Financial Reporting Authority
under this section may prefer an appeal before the Appellate Tribunal within a period
of forty-five days from the date on which a copy of the order of said Authority is made
available, in such manner and on payment of such fee, as may be prescribed.

132E. No civil court shall have jurisdiction to entertain any suit or proceeding in
respect of any matter which the National Financial Reporting Authority is empowered
to determine by or under this Act and no injunction shall be granted by any court or
other authority in respect of any action taken or to be taken by the said Authority in
pursuance of any power conferred by or under this Act.

132F. No suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding shall lie against the Central
Government or the National Financial Reporting Authority or the chairperson or any
Member or any officer, or other employees of Authority for anything which is in good
faith done or intended to be done under this Act or the rules or regulations made
thereunder.

132G. Without prejudice to the provisions of this Act, the National Financial
Reporting Authority shall, in exercise of its powers or the performance of its functions
under this Act, be bound by such directions on questions of policy, as the Central
Government may give in writing to it from time to time:

                                                      344
Provided that the Authority shall, as far as practicable, be given an opportunity to
express its views before any direction is given under this section:

Provided further that the decision of the Central Government, on whether a question
is one of policy or not, shall be final.

132H. Power of Central Government to supersede Authority.-

(1) If at any time, the Central Government is of the opinion--

(a) that on account of grave emergency, the National Financial Reporting Authority is
unable to discharge the functions and duties imposed on it by or under the provisions
of this Act; or

(b) that the National Financial Reporting Authority has persistently not complied with
any direction given by the Central Government under this Act or in the discharge of
the functions and duties imposed on it by or under the provisions of this Act, and as a
result of such non-compliance, the financial position or the administration of such
Authority has deteriorated; or

(c) that circumstances exist which render it necessary in the public interest so to do,
the Central Government may, by notification, supersede the National Financial
Reporting Authority for such period, not exceeding six months, as may be specified
in the notification.

(2) Upon the publication of a notification under sub-section (1) superseding the
National Financial Reporting Authority,--

(a) the Chairperson and all the members shall, as from the date of supersession,
vacate their offices as such;

(b) all the powers, functions and duties which may, by or under the provisions of this
Act, be exercised or discharged by or on behalf of the National Financial Reporting
Authority shall, until the said Authority is reconstituted under sub-section (3), be
exercised and discharged by such person or persons as the Central Government
may direct; and

(c) all properties owned or controlled by the National Financial Reporting Authority
shall, until the said Authority is reconstituted under sub-section (3), vest in the
Central Government.

                                                      345
(3) On the expiration of the period of supersession specified in the notification issued
under sub-section (1), the Central Government may reconstitute the National
Financial Reporting Authority by a fresh appointment, and in such case, any person
or persons who vacated their offices under clause (a) of the said sub-section, shall
not be deemed disqualified for appointment:

Provided that the Central Government may, at any time, before the expiration of the
period of supersession, take action under this sub-section.

(4) The Central Government shall cause a notification issued under sub-section (1)
and a full report of any action taken under this section and the circumstances leading
to such action to be laid before each House of Parliament at the earliest.

132I. (1) For the purposes of carrying out its functions under this Act, the National
Financial Reporting Authority may levy such fees or other charges as may be
specified by it by regulations, on the auditors of companies or class of companies or
bodies corporate referred to in clause (a) of sub-section (4) of section 132.

(2) The payment of such fees or other charges shall be in such manner as may be
specified by regulations by the National Financial Reporting Authority.

132J. (1) The National Financial Reporting Authority may, by notification, make
regulations consistent with this Act and the rules made thereunder, for carrying out its
functions under this Act.

(2) In particular, and without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing powers, such
regulations may provide for all or any of the following matters, namely:--

(a) the manner of investigation under clause (a) of sub-section (4) of section 132;

(b) the place and time of meetings of the Authority and the procedure to be followed
at such meetings under sub-section (10) of section 132;

(c) the manner of appointment, salary, allowances and other terms and conditions of
service of the Secretary and employees of the Authority under sub-section (11) of
section 132;

(d) the manner of engagement of experts and professionals under sub-section (17)
of section 132;

                                                      346
(e) the documents, returns, or information, and the form, manner, period, and fees for
filing the same under sub-section (2) of section 132A;

(f) the manner of recovery of the amount of penalty under sub-section (3) of section
132D; and

(g) the fees or other charges and the manner of payment thereof under section 132-I.

(3) Every regulation made under this section shall be laid, as soon as may be after it
is made, before each House of Parliament, while it is in session, for a total period of
thirty days which may be comprised in one session or in two or more successive
sessions, and if, before the expiry of the session immediately following the session or
the successive sessions aforesaid, both Houses agree in making any modification in
the regulation, or both Houses agree that the regulation should not be made, the
regulation shall thereafter have effect only in such modified form or be of no effect,
as the case may be; so however, that any such modification or annulment shall be
without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under that regulation.".

132K. The Authority shall, prior to issuing regulations under section 132J, ensure
transparency by--

(a) publishing the draft regulations along with all relevant details on its website and
inviting public comments for a such period as may be specified therein; and

(b) reviewing such regulations at least once in three years:

Provided that if the Authority is of the opinion that it is necessary or expedient to
make, or amend, any regulations urgently in public interest or where the subject
matter of the regulations relates solely to the internal functioning of the Authority, it
may, for reasons to be recorded in writing for doing so, make or amend such
regulations without following the procedure specified in clause (a).".

41.2. Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (The Companies Act, 2013):

New sub-sections being inserted after section132

41.3. Reasons/Justification given by the Ministry for the proposed provisions:

                                                      347
"132 A

The amendment seeks to insert a new section 132A to require auditors of specified
companies and bodies corporate to intimate details of his/ its registration with ICAI to
the NFRA. The requirement in respect of filing with NFRA and penalty framework for
non-compliance and misreporting have also been provided.

132B

The amendment seeks to insert a new section 132B to provide for grants by the
Central Government and the establishment of a dedicated fund for the NFRA to meet
its expenses and discharge its functions. The amendment is part of the broader set
of insertions to strengthen the NFRA, on the lines of other regulators.

132C

The amendment seeks to insert a new section 132C to empower the NFRA to issue
directions to auditors in public interest or in the interest of investors, creditors or
other stakeholders, along with a penalty framework for non-compliance. It is part of
the broader set of insertions to strengthen the NFRA, on the lines of other regulators.

132D

The clause inserts a new section 132D to provide a framework for inquiry,
adjudication and imposition of penalties by the NFRA, including powers to summon
persons, enforce attendance, and recover penalties, along with a provision for
appeal to the Appellate Tribunal. The amendment is part of the broader set of
insertions to strengthen the NFRA, on the lines of other regulators.

132E

The amendment seeks to insert a new section 132E to bar the jurisdiction of civil
courts in matters within the domain of the NFRA and to prevent grant of injunctions
against actions taken by it under the Act,

132F

The amendment seeks to insert new section 132F to provide protection to the
Central Government, NFRA and its officials against legal proceedings for actions
taken in good faith under the Act. The amendment is part of the broader set of
insertions to strengthen the NFRA, on the lines of other regulators.

                                                      348
132G

The amendment seeks to insert a new section 132G to provide that the NFRA shall
be bound by directions of the Central Government on questions of policy, subject to
being given an opportunity to express its views, and with the decision of the Central
Government on such questions being final. The amendment is part of the broader set
of insertions to strengthen the NFRA, on the lines of other regulators.

132H

The amendment seeks to insert a new section 132H to empower the Central
Government to supersede the NFRA in specified circumstances, including grave
emergency, persistent default, or public interest, and to provide for interim
administration and reconstitution of the Authority.

132I

The amendment seeks to insert a new section 132I to empower the NFRA to levy
fees or other charges on auditors of specified companies and bodies corporate, in
such manner as may be specified by regulations.

132J

The amendment seeks to insert a new section 132J to enable NFRA to make
regulations for carrying out its functions under the Act, subject to parliamentary
oversight. The amendment is part of the broader set of insertions to strengthen the
NFRA, on the lines of other regulators.

132K

The amendment seeks to insert a new section 132K to provide for transparency and
periodic review in the regulation-making process of the NFRA, including prior public
consultation and review of regulations at regular intervals, with an exception for
urgent or internal matters. The amendment is part of the broader set of insertions to
strengthen the NFRA, on the lines of other regulators."

41.4. Important Views/Suggestions given by Experts/Stakeholders:

Some of the significant changes proposed by the Stakeholders are as under:

Intimation of Registration details of auditors and filing of returns - 132A
                                                      349
41.4.1       "Introduce a single-window online registration and annual return-filing

portal for auditor intimation to NFRA (s.132A) that is interoperable with existing ICAI

and MCA21/V3 portals, so auditors are not required to separately re-file substantially

the same registration particulars with multiple authorities.Singapore's ACRA model (a

single integrated registrar for company filings and accountancy-profession oversight)

and the US PCAOB's centralised firm-registration system both minimise duplicative

filing for audit firms. Reducing duplicate compliance filings for audit firms lowers the

cost of audit services economy-wide, particularly for small and mid-sized practices

serving small companies, supporting the Bill's own objective of easing compliance for

smaller entities."

41.4.2       The following change is suggested to Section 132A (1) - The words `as

may be prescribed' should be replaced by `as may be specified by regulations by the

said Authority'

"Consequently, Section 132J (2), which provides for the specific matters of making of
regulations by NFRA should also be amended to include 132A(1)."

41.4.3       "Exempt small companies as auditors from filing documents, returns or

information with NFRA as it will increase cost of audit; simplify NFRA filings. Since

Multiple filings increase audit cost; may cause shortage of auditors also"

41.4.4       "132A: Not Recommended It is recommended that the proposed

requirement for separate registration and periodic return filing with NFRA be omitted.

The framework may instead leverage existing information available with MCA

through appropriate data-sharing and system integration mechanisms, thereby

avoiding duplicative filings, compliance costs and regulatory overlap."

41.4.5       "In 132A (3) and 132C(2). - The penalty for contravention of this

provision should be a fixed amount. Intention should not matter for non-compliance

and hence, any auditor, who fails to comply with this mandatory requirement must be

liable to pay a fixed amount as penalty. It is suggested that it should not be

discretionary in nature."

41.4.6           "It is submitted, as a two-fold suggestion, that: (a) first, the duplicative

regulatory burden may kindly be rationalised: for auditors of listed companies/MIIs

already within SEBI's oversight, the new NFRA registration, periodic-filing and

direction-compliance obligations should be calibrated to avoid a parallel compliance

layer over SEBI's framework, consistent with the Bill's ease-of-doing-business

objective".

41.4.7       "The newly inserted section 132A (3) of the draft Corporate Laws

(Amendment) Bill 2026 may consider different penalty amounts for individual auditors

                           350
and audit firms. In case of Audit Firms, Individual as well as Audit Firm should be
held liable".

FUND OF AUTHORITY - 132B

41.4.8   "132B: Not Recommended. It is recommended omission of the

proposed Section 132B. Alternatively, NFRA may continue to be funded through

budgetary support from the Consolidated Fund of India, and any provision relating to

fees or charges may be accompanied by appropriate safeguards regarding the

source, utilisation and oversight of such funds."

41.4.9   "Proposed redraft of Section 132 B (3) proposed to be inserted - (3)

The Fund shall be applied for meeting the expenses of the National Financial

Reporting Authority for the discharge of its functions and for the purposes of this Act

and for such other allied purposes, as may be specified by Authority by regulations."

POWER OF AUTHORITY TO ISSUE DIRECTIONS - 132 C

41.4.10  "132C and 132D: Not Recommended It is recommended

reconsideration of the proposed Sections 132C and 132D. The provisions may

incorporate clear statutory safeguards, including definition of key terms such as

"public interest", functional separation between investigation and adjudication,

objective criteria for exercise of powers and imposition of penalties, adequate

procedural safeguards, and a clear coordination framework with ICAI to avoid

overlapping jurisdiction and parallel proceedings. Further, recovery of penalties as

arrears of land revenue may be omitted".

41.4.11  "The language in this sub-section is proposed to be in line with the

other provisions of the Companies Act viz. Section 90, Section 172.

".....shall be liable to penalty of not less than fifty thousand rupees, and in case of
continuing failure, with a further penalty of one thousand rupees for each day during
which such default continues, subject to a maximum of fifty lakh rupees, if such
person is an auditor or one crore rupees if such person is an audit firm".

POWER OF AUTHORITY TO IMPOSE PENALTY - 123D

41.4.12  "Imposition and Utilisation of Penalties under the NFRA Framework

[132D] It is submitted that all penalties imposed under the regulatory framework of

the National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA) should be levied exclusively by

the Authority itself and should not be delegated to, or exercised by, any subordinate

body, including the Executive Body. Given the quasi-judicial nature of such decisions,

this would ensure that penalty decisions benefit from the collective expertise,

                                          351
experience and judgment of all members of the Authority, including both full-time and
part-time members, thereby enhancing the quality, credibility and institutional
robustness of the decision- making process. In order to ensure consistency with this
principle, Sections 132(4), 132(4A) and 132A(3) should also be expressly brought
within the scope of Section 132D(1), similar to Sections 132A(4) and 132C(2). This is
also necessary to preserve the independence and perceived impartiality of NFRA's
enforcement functions"

41.4.13     "Proposed Amendment: "132D (2) While holding an inquiry, the

National Financial Reporting Authority shall have power to summon and enforce the

attendance of any person acquainted with the facts and circumstances of the case to

give evidence and examine them on oath or to produce any document, which in the

opinion of the said Authority, may be useful for or relevant to the subject matter of the

inquiry and if, on such inquiry, it is satisfied that the person has failed to comply with

the provisions of any of the sections specified in sub-section (1), it may impose such

penalty as it considers appropriate in accordance with the provisions of any of those

sections."

The power to examine a person on oath constitutes a standard enabling provision
conferred upon independent regulators within the domestic legislative framework.
This is also in line with its power as prescribed u/s. 132(4)(b)(ii), for the Authority's
disciplinary functions. Therefore, the same deserves to be incorporated in section
132D (2)."

41.4.14     "Proposed Amendment: 132D (3) The amount of any penalty imposed

under this section and section 132 of this Act if not paid, may be recovered by the

National Financial Reporting Authority, in such manner as may be prescribed, as if it

were an arrear of land revenue."

41.4.15     "The proposed formulation does not include all penalties levied by

NFRA. It is, therefore, suggested that all penalties imposed by NFRA be included in

the proposed section 132D (3)".

41.4.16     "Powers of NFRA to issue penalties, types of offences, directions to be

issues should be categorically specified. Orders of NFRA must have specific

structure as is the case with the adjudicating authority under Section 31 of the

Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016. Penalties proposed for noncompliance

should have specific grounds and corresponding quantum. In the proposed section

132D, it is suggested that while imposing penalty NFRA may take into consideration

the following: the nature, gravity and duration of the default; the repetitive nature of

the default; the disproportionate gain or unfair advantage, wherever quantifiable,

made as a result of the default; the action taken by the person to mitigate the effects

and consequences of the default, and the timeliness and effectiveness of such

action; whether the penalty to be imposed is proportionate, having regard to the need

to secure observance of and deter breach of the provisions of the Act; and such

                                  352
other factors as may be deemed appropriate by the National Financial Reporting
Authority."

41.4.17        "132D (1) The National Financial Reporting Authority may, after holding

inquiry, in such manner as may be specified by the regulations and after giving a

reasonable opportunity of being heard, impose such penalty under sub-section (3) or

sub-section (4) of section 132A or sub-section (2) of section 132C, as it may consider

appropriate."

"a. The manner of inquiry deserves to be specified by regulations. Most independent
regulators have powers to make regulations to govern their own procedure.
Moreover, the proposed amendments already provide for NFRA to make regulations
for investigations undertaken by it under Section 132 (4).

b. It is, therefore, suggested to include sub-section 3 of Section 132A also under the
scope of inquiry, in the interest of fair procedure."

CIVIL COURTS NOT TO HAVE JURISDICTION - 132E

41.4.18        "132E: Not Recommended (i) The proposed provision bars the

jurisdiction of civil courts in matters falling within the powers of the National Financial

Reporting Authority (NFRA) and prohibits grant of injunctions. While such exclusions

are common in regulatory frameworks, the absence of a clearly defined and robust

appellate mechanism may unduly restrict access to justice for aggrieved auditors and

firms. (ii) The blanket prohibition on injunctions may also prevent timely judicial

intervention in cases involving jurisdictional error, violation of principles of natural

justice, or manifest arbitrariness. Given NFRA's extensive investigative and quasi-

judicial powers, complete insulation from immediate judicial scrutiny may increase

the risk of regulatory overreach. (iii)Further, the expression "any matter which NFRA

is empowered to determine" is broad and ambiguous, and may be interpreted

expansively to exclude legitimate civil disputes from judicial consideration. In the

absence of adequate safeguards such as a clear appellate framework, defined scope

of exclusion, and preservation of judicial review, the provision may create an

imbalance between regulatory authority and the rights of professionals, including

members of Institute of Chartered Accountants of India".

41.4.19        "132 E- Suggested that this sub-section should not be introduced as

there is a redressal mechanism already existing in the Act. However, if this

subsection is to be retained, we suggest the following amendment to the same: No

civil court shall have jurisdiction to entertain any suit or proceeding in respect of any

matter which the National Financial Reporting Authority is empowered to determine

by or under this Act and no injunction shall be granted by any court or other authority

in respect of any action to be taken by the said Authority in pursuance of any power

conferred by or under this Act.

                                 353
41.4.20     "Recommend omitting the proposed Section 132E, as it is unnecessary

given that the Companies Act already provides a specific redress mechanism

(appeals to NCLAT) for NFRA's decisions. A broad ouster of civil court jurisdiction

could create confusion without adding value. If Section 132E is nonetheless retained,

it should be carefully worded to ensure it does not inadvertently curtail the existing

right of appeal to NCLAT. For instance, the phrasing should be clarified so that it

does not preclude NCLAT's oversight (e.g., by removing or modifying the broad

reference to "any action to be taken" by NFRA). It is essential that auditors and firms

retain a clear and effective avenue for appeals or judicial review of NFRA's significant

decisions.

41.4.21     "132E - The provision needs reconsideration restricting jurisdiction of

civil courts and grant of injunctions in matters involving jurisdictional issues or

principles of natural justice.  It may be advisable to align the NFRA framework with

global regulatory practices, including provision for multi layered oversight and review

of regulatory decisions to ensure principles of natural justice.  The Companies Act

already provides a specific redressal mechanism (appeal to NCLAT) for NFRA's

decisions, making a blanket ouster of civil court jurisdiction unnecessary. If, however,

Section 132E is retained, it must be clarified that it does not override the existing

right of appeal to NCLAT - for example, by removing or modifying the broad phrase

"any action to be taken by the Authority" which may be interpreted to remove

NCLAT's oversight. We recommend ensuring that auditors and firms preserve an

effective avenue for appeal or judicial review of NFRA's actions.

PROTECTION OF ACTION TAKEN IN GOOD FAITH - 132F

41.4.22     "132F: Not Recommended The provision is not supported by

corresponding accountability or review mechanisms, which will lead to imbalance in

the regulatory framework and weaken institutional responsibility."

41.4.23     "132F- It is suggested that the following amendment to the section: No

suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding shall lie against the Central Government

or the National Financial Reporting Authority or chairperson or any member or any

officer or other employee of Authority for anything which is in good faith done or

intended to be done under this Act or the rules or regulations made thereunder. .

41.4.24     "132 F - It may be recommended to reconsider the immunity for the

Central Government and for NFRA as institutions, while retaining protection for

individual officers or members acting in good faith. This may allow the authorities

themselves (as bodies) take actions that adversely affect firms or professionals,

aggrieved parties are not barred from seeking judicial remedy. Individual

functionaries may still be safeguarded for good-faith conduct.

LEVY OF FEES OR OTHER CHARGES BY AUTHORITY - 132I
                                                      354
41.4.25. "132I: Not Recommended: The proposed provision enabling the
National Financial Reporting Authority to levy "such fees or other charges as may be
specified" on auditors should not be retained. The Authority is a regulatory body and
auditors are not its members; accordingly, there is no statutory or functional basis for
imposing any fee or charge. The provision, in its current form, also grants wide and
unguided discretion to prescribe fees and "other charges" through regulations,
without any principles, limits, or legislative safeguards, which may lead to arbitrary
imposition and regulatory overreach. In view of the above, it is recommended that
Section 132-I be omitted in entirety and no fees or other charges be levied by NFRA
on auditors.

41.4.26. "It appears that there is a drafting error in proposed sub-section 3. It
refers to persons mentioned in proposed sub-section 2 i.e. who are auditors. Then
the last phrase "if such person is an auditor or an audit firm" doesn't have any
relevance since by reference, the persons mentioned are already auditors, unless
the drafter intended to provide a separate penalty for an auditor or an audit firm but
unintentionally omitted".

41.4.27. "In Section 132-I - Maximum fee that could be levied may be specified.
Excessive levying power might be against the fundamental right of business and
profession. Some guidance or criteria shall be provided".

POWER OF AUTHORITY TO MAKE REGULATIONS - 132J

41.4.28  "Section 132J (2), which provides for the specific matters of making of

regulations by NFRA should also be amended to include 132A(1). Thus, following

amendment is suggested "132J(2)(e) the documents, returns, or information, and the

form, manner, period, and fees for filing the same under section 132A"

41.4.29  "132J and 132K: Not Recommended The NFRA does not presently

have explicit powers akin to Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) under

Section 469 of the Companies Act, 2013 to frame and lay regulations before

Parliament. In the absence of such enabling provision, the validity of NFRA issuing

regulations, particularly those intended to have statutory effect may be open to legal

challenge. Further, even assuming such powers are implied, the question arises as

to why a separate authority should be vested with regulation-making functions when

the Central Government (through the Ministry of Corporate Affairs) already has

comprehensive rule- making powers under the Act. Creating parallel regulatory

powers not only leads to duplication but also blurs accountability and legislative

hierarchy. The provision grants wide and residuary powers to the National Financial

Reporting Authority to frame regulations "for carrying out its functions," including

matters relating to investigation, reporting, fees, and enforcement. Such broad and

open- ended delegation, particularly when read with the phrase "without prejudice to

the generality," may result in excessive delegation of legislative powers and enable

creation of a parallel regulatory framework without adequate legislative oversight.

The absence of clearly defined boundaries may also permit expansion of regulatory

         355
scope and introduction of new compliance requirements beyond what is
contemplated under the Act, leading to regulatory uncertainty and frequent changes.
Further, the power to frame regulations in areas such as investigations, professional
conduct, and reporting requirements may overlap with the statutory mandate of the
Institute of Chartered Accountants of India, potentially resulting in dual regulation,
conflicting requirements, and uncertainty for the profession. In view of the above, it is
recommended the scope of regulation-making powers be clearly defined and limited
primarily to procedural and operational aspects, with substantive matters affecting
rights and obligations governed under the Act or Rules. A limiting provision should
clarify that regulations cannot expand the scope of powers beyond the Act, and core
principles relating to investigation, including procedural safeguards, rights of
representation, timelines, and transparency, should be codified."

41.4.30         "reviewing such regulations, at such regular intervals, as the Authority

considers necessary and at least once in three years. Minimum period open for

public comments may be specified for more effectiveness and transparency."

TRANSPARENCY IN MAKING REGULATIONS -132K

41.4.31         "Need to have a clear consultation process for the National Financial

Reporting Authority's regulation making. Clause 41 inserts a new section 132 K into

the Companies Act and proposes public consultation on draft regulations. However,

experiences from other regulators, international best practices as well as the Pre-

Legislative Consultation Policy 2014 suggest that the objectives, rationale of the

proposed regulations and relevant international best practices should be included in

the draft released for consultations. Stakeholders and the public at large should be

provided a minimum of thirty days to respond to these drafts. These features should

be expressly mentioned in the Act while leaving the detailed process to be prescribed

by the rules."

ADDITIONAL SUGGESTIONS

41.4.32         "It is crucial to pair these expanded powers with clear procedural

safeguards. The law or subsequent rules should explicitly outline due process for

NFRA's investigations and disciplinary proceedings, including transparent notice and

hearing requirements, reasonable timelines for completing inquiries, and a well-

defined mechanism for appeals or reviews of NFRA's orders. Providing these

procedural details will ensure that NFRA's increased authority is exercised in a fair

and predictable manner. Auditors and firms will then understand their rights and

obligations under the new regime, and NFRA's enforcement will align with principles

of natural justice. In sum, combining robust oversight with clear rules of procedure

and reasonable timelines will strengthen NFRA's credibility and maintain trust in the

audit regulatory framework. The Auditors should be mandated to confirm to the

concerned company (as part of their eligibility certificate) that they have duly

registered with the NFRA.

                           356
41.4.33       "A formal NFRA-SEBI coordination protocol may kindly be established

(through the rules under Section 132 / Note on Clauses): NFRA to notify SEBI on

initiating investigation, imposing penalty or debarring an auditor of a listed

company/MII; clarify whether NFRA's jurisdiction over MII-auditors is concurrent with

or supersedes SEBI's audit-related oversight; and ensure orders with market-wide

implications are communicated to exchanges/ depositories promptly. In addition, it is

suggested that appropriate safeguards be prescribed for the handling and

dissemination of UPSI, particularly where auditors are required to report directly to

NFRA or where NFRA's directions may have market-sensitive implications, so that

confidentiality is preserved consistent with the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading)

Regulations, 2015.

41.4.34       "With regard to 132 A to 132 K - It is recommended that the clauses be

retained, subject to the following modifications: (i) in section 132C, insert a proviso

that no direction shall be issued without recording reasons, and, save in urgent

cases, without affording an opportunity to be heard; (ii) in section 132A(3) and (4)

and section 132C(2), provide that penalties shall be imposed only after inquiry under

section 132D (a cross-reference exists in 132D(1) but the converse linkage should

be textual); and (iii) in section 132K, provide a minimum public-comment period of

thirty days.

41.5.3 On the suggestion of removal of penalties as arrears of land revenue, the

It is also proposed to replace section 132D(2) as under:-

"132D (3) The amount of any penalty imposed under this section and section 132 of

It is also proposed to insert words "or an officer of the NFRA" in section 454B to

41.5.4.  In response to the suggestion at 41.4.13 above regarding the power of

NFRA to summon and enforce the attendance of any person acquainted with the

facts and circumstances of the case to give evidence during enquiry, the Ministry

submitted as follows:

"The power to examine a person on oath is a necessary corollary to the power to
summon and enforce attendance for the purpose of conducting an effective inquiry.
Similar powers are already available under the Companies Act, 2013, including
under section 207(3)(b), and are also vested in other statutory authorities such as
the Income Tax Authorities under section 131 of the Income-tax Act, 1961, SEBI Act,
1992 and Competition Act, 2002. The proposed provision is, therefore, consistent
with the legislative framework governing statutory regulators and is necessary to
enable NFRA to effectively discharge its inquiry and enforcement functions in the
larger public interest."

41.5.5.  On the question of overlapping of jurisdiction between NFRA and ICAI

the representatives of NFRA deposed before the Committee as under:

"the jurisdiction has been clearly defined by the Government under Rule 3 of the
NFRA Rules, 2018. At the beginning of the presentation, I highlighted the categories
of companies that fall under the jurisdiction of the NFRA. Therefore, there is no
ambiguity regarding NFRA's jurisdiction. What causes concern is that despite this

                                                      358
clear demarcation, the ICAI continues to initiate actions against these companies,
which, as an hon. Member rightly pointed out, leads to duplication. This can cause
jurisdictional conflicts. Consequently, we have suggested amending the proviso so
that wherever NFRA exercises its jurisdiction, there is absolute clarity regarding the
powers to be exercised, leaving no ambiguity as to whether a matter falls under the
purview of the ICAI or the NFRA. This clarifies the position concerning the powers of
the ICAI and the NFRA regarding auditors."

41.5.10. As regard the suggestions concerning the provision of the Fund of the

41.5.11. On the suggestion at 41.4.33 regarding separation of regulatory powers

any proceedings in such cases of misconduct where National Financial Reporting
Authority has jurisdiction."

Further, the mandate of NFRA under Section 132 of the Companies Act, 2013 is
distinct from the regulatory functions exercised by sectoral regulators such as SEBI.
While SEBI regulates listed entities, market intermediaries and market-related
activities, NFRA is entrusted with oversight of auditors and audit firms in respect of
specified entities. The exercise of such functions does not result in duplication, as
the respective regulators operate within their defined statutory domains".

                                                      360
41.5.12. On the issue of exempting auditors of Small Companies from filing

"NFRA has been constituted as an independent regulator for audit oversight in

listed companies; unlisted public companies having a paid-up share capital of 500
crore or more, or an annual turnover of 1,000 crore or more, or aggregate
outstanding loans, debentures and deposits of 500 crore or more as on 31 March of
the immediately preceding financial year; banking companies, insurance companies,
companies engaged in the generation or supply of electricity, and companies

The proposed amendments do not enlarge the jurisdiction of NFRA but only
strengthen its existing regulatory and enforcement framework as recommended by
the Company Law Committee Report, 2022"

41.5.13. On the suggestion for different penalty amounts for individual auditors
