                                               CLAUSE - 62

62. Clause 62 of the Bill seeks to amend Section 189 of the Companies Act
2013 regarding Register of contracts or arrangements in which directors are
interested.

62.1 Provision proposed in The Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

                  In section 189 of the principal Act, after sub-section (5), the following
sub-section shall be inserted, namely:-- "(5A) Every company which fails to comply
with the provisions of this section and the rules made thereunder shall be liable to a
penalty of two lakh rupees.".

62.2 Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (The Companies Act, 2013):

189. Register of contracts or arrangements in which directors are interested.--(1)
Every company shall keep one or more registers giving separately the particulars of
all contracts or arrangements to which sub-section (2) of section 184 or section 188
applies, in such manner and containing such particulars as may be prescribed and
after entering the particulars, such register or registers shall be placed before the
next meeting of the Board and signed by all the directors present at the meeting.

(2) Every director or key managerial personnel shall, within a period of thirty days of
his appointment, or relinquishment of his office, as the case may be, disclose to the
company the particulars specified in subsection (1) of section 184 relating to his
concern or interest in the other associations which are required to be included in the
register under that sub-section or such other information relating to himself as may
be prescribed.

(3) The register referred to in sub-section (1) shall be kept at the registered office of
the company and it shall be open for inspection at such office during business hours
and extracts may be taken therefrom, and copies thereof as may be required by any
member of the company shall be furnished by the company to such extent, in such
manner, and on payment of such fees as may be prescribed.

(4) The register to be kept under this section shall also be produced at the
commencement of every annual general meeting of the company and shall remain
open and accessible during the continuance of the meeting to any person having the
right to attend the meeting.

(5) Nothing contained in sub-section (1) shall apply to any contract or arrangement--
                                                      504
         (a) for the sale, purchase or supply of any goods, materials or services if the
value of such goods and materials or the cost of such services does not exceed five
lakh rupees in the aggregate in any year; or

         (b) by a banking company for the collection of bills in the ordinary course of
its business.

(6) Every director who fails to comply with the provisions of this section and the rules
made thereunder shall be liable to a penalty of twenty-five thousand rupees.

62.3 Reasons / Justification given by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs for the
         proposed provision:

"The new sub-section (5A) is being inserted to provide that every company which
fails to comply with the provisions of this section and the rules made thereunder shall
be liable to a penalty of two lakh rupees, to cover penalties for defaulting companies
which is currently missing."

62.4 Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

62.4.1       The Committee note that Section 189 of the Companies Act 2013

requires companies to maintain a register recording particulars of

contracts/arrangements in which directors have an interest under section 184.

The Committee further note that the unamended section did not contain a self-

contained penalty provision for non-compliance with section 189 specifically.

Clause 62 seeks to insert a dedicated penalty thereby creating explicit and

standalone enforceability for the register-maintenance obligation under

Section 189. The Committee find merit in the insertion of a dedicated penalty

provision, as it removes ambiguity about which penalty applies to defaults

under Section 189 and strengthens enforceability of the register-maintenance

obligation.

62.4.2       The Committee further note that the penalty structure imposes a

flat 2 lakh penalty on the company, without a per-day continuing default

formula or officer-level liability, thereby treating non-maintenance as a

one-time compliance lapse rather than an ongoing default. The Committee

             505
recognize that this approach reflects the nature of the lapse while avoiding
disproportionate exposure for companies and officers. The Committee,
therefore, after examining the Clause and considering the justification given by
the Ministry, accept the amendment to Clause 62 without any modification.

                                                      506
        CLAUSE - 62A

62A New insertion of provisions in the Bill with regard to appointment of
         managing director, whole-time director or manager.

62A.1 Examination by the Committee:

62A.1.1 During the deliberation by the committee one of the stakeholders raised
the point on managerial appointments (managing directors and whole-time directors)
under Section 196. It was explained that under the current law the minimum age for
eligibility to be appointed as a Director is 21 years and the maximum age is 70 years.
The provision regarding appointment beyond 70 years of age requires a special
resolution and, failing that, Central Government approval. The stakeholder proposed
to retain the minimum age at 21 but raise the maximum age from 70 to 75 years, and
exclude the mandate of a special resolution or Central Government approval. In
support of this proposal, an international comparison was made with the
corresponding laws in United Kingdom which has a minimum age of 16 years; the
US, Singapore, Germany, and Australia which has the minimum age as 18 years.

62A1.2  During the deliberations, a general consensus withing the Committee

arose as to lowering of the minimum age from 21 to 18 years.

62A.1.3 The Ministry have informed that similar suggestions were received from
HLC-NITI Aayog in order to encourage and increase the representation of young
people in Boards and to allow persons above 70 years to get appointed and continue
as Managing Director, Whole-time Director without requirement of special resolution.

62A.2 Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

62A.2.1 The Committee note that the proposal to revise the age criteria for
appointment as Managing Director, Whole-time Director or Manager originates
from a suggestion of the High-Level Committee constituted by NITI Aayog, with

                                                      507
the stated objective of encouraging greater representation of younger persons
on company boards, while simultaneously easing the appointment process for
persons above the age of seventy by removing the mandatory requirement of a
special resolution or Central Government approval in respect of the revised
upper age limit of seventy-five years.

62A.2.2 The Committee heard evidence on this proposal and thereby
recommend that the proposed amendment to Section 196(3)(a) -- reducing the
minimum age for appointment as Managing Director, Whole-time Director or
Manager from twenty-one to eighteen years, and raising the maximum age
from seventy to seventy-five years, may be incorporated in the Bill as follows:

          In section 196 of the principal Act, -

              (a) in sub-section (3), in clause (a), for the words "twenty-one years
           or has attained the age of seventy", the words "eighteen years or has
           attained the age of seventy-five" shall be substituted;

              (b) in first proviso to clause (a) in sub-section (3), for the word
           "seventy", the word "seventy-five" shall be substituted;

              (c) in second proviso to clause (a) in sub-section (3), for the word
           "seventy", the word "seventy-five" shall be substituted;

62A.2.3 Keeping in view the importance of having an enabling statutory
provision for the appointment of managing director, whole-time director or
manager, the Committee desire that the Bill be modified and the
aforementioned provisions be suitably inserted therein.

                                                      508
                                               CLAUSE - 63

63. Clause 63 of the Bill seeks insertion of a new section 203A regarding
Resignation of a whole-time key managerial personnel, who is not a director.

63.1 Provision proposed in The Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

         After section 203 of the principal Act, the following section shall be inserted,
namely:--

"203A. (1) A whole-time key managerial personnel of a company, who is not a
director, may resign from his office by giving a notice in writing to the company, and
the Board shall, on receipt of such notice, take note of the same and shall intimate
the Registrar of such resignation in such form and manner and within such time, as
may be prescribed:

Provided that where the company fails to intimate the Registrar under this sub-
section within such time the said key managerial personnel may forward a copy of
his resignation along with detailed reasons for his resignation to the Registrar in such
manner, as may be prescribed.

(2) The resignation of a key managerial personnel under sub-section (1) shall take
effect from the date on which the notice is received by the company or the date, if
any, specified by such key managerial personnel in the notice, whichever is later:

Provided that such key managerial personnel who has resigned shall be liable even
after his resignation for the default for which he was liable during his tenure.".

63.2 Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (The Companies Act, 2013):

This is insertion of new section 203A regarding resignation of a whole-time key
managerial personnel, who is not a director.

63.3 Reasons / Justification given by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs for the
proposed provision:

"The amendment seeks to insert a new section 203A to provide a framework for
resignation of whole-time key managerial personnel, including intimation to the

                                                      509
Registrar and clarification of the effective date and continuing liability for past
defaults."

63.4 Important Views/Suggestions given by Experts/Stakeholders:

Few of the suggestions given by stakeholders, while seeking to bring in amendments
to the provisions of the Act dealing with Mergers and Amalgamations are as follows:

63.4.1     One of the stakeholders recommended that the resignation / cessation

process and reporting under Section 203A be aligned, for MIIs, with SEBI's

requirements relating to Compliance Officer/KMP appointment, cessation and

reporting, to avoid conflicting timelines or duplicative intimations. The proposed

Section 203A does not expressly prescribe a notice period for resignation by whole-

time KMP.

63.4.2     Another stakeholder was of the view that a clarification be provided to

the effect that Section 203A applies only to companies required to appoint KMPs,

and not those who appoint KMPs voluntarily.

63.4.3     Few stakeholders suggested that the provision should expressly state

that the notice period under Section 203A shall be subject to and shall not override

any longer notice period stipulated in the KMP's employment or service contract. The

words "whichever is later" in the effective date proviso should be amended to read

"subject to such period as may be agreed upon in the employment contract of such

key managerial personnel.

63.4.4     One of the suggestions received was that the proviso may be suitably

modified to limit post-resignation liability to a reasonable and specified period,

considering age and health issues beyond a reasonable period, thereby ensuring a

balanced approach between accountability and professional certainty.

63.4.5     The provisions of resignation of KMP who is a director may also be
covered.                                       510
63.4.6         The new Section 203A should be deleted because the existing

contractual and statutory framework already governs KMP resignation adequately.

Also, Section 203A(2) implies a KMP could leave on just one day's notice -- this

cannot be the legislative intent probably the intention here would be that of

disclosure of KMP's resignation and not of notice. A statutory prescription would

override or conflict with contractual notice-period obligations. Employment terms,

internal policies and contractual arrangements should continue to govern

resignations.

63.5 Examination by the Committee:

63.5.1 In response to the suggestion given by the stakeholder, the Ministry of
Corporate Affairs, in their written replies, have submitted as under:

"Regarding issue regarding the notice period required for a resigning KMP as stated
at 63.4.1, 63.4.3 and 63.4.6, the Ministry acknowledged the underlying issue that the
current drafting/wording of the Section needs to be more specific and agreed to bring
about an update in the proposed new section".

63.5.2         As regards the suggestion made at para 63.4.4, the Ministry stated that

the proposed Section 203A merely preserves liability for defaults committed during

the individual's tenure. Prescribing a fixed post resignation period may inadvertently

limit accountability for defaults committed during the tenure of the individual.

63.5.3         In response to the suggestion mentioned at 63.4.5 which seeks

extension of the proposed provisions relating to resignation of whole time KMPs to

cover KMPs who are directors, the Ministry submitted that the proposed Section

203A is intended to provide a statutory mechanism for resignation of whole-time

KMPs who are not directors. The resignation of KMPs who are directors is already

governed by the provisions of Section 168 of the Companies Act, 2013.

                                    511
63.6 Observations/Recommendations of the Committee

63.6.1 The Committee note that while the Companies Act, 2013 provides a
structured mechanism for resignation of directors under section 168, there is
presently no corresponding statutory framework governing the resignation of
whole-time key managerial personnel (KMP) who are not directors. The
proposed insertion of section 203A, therefore, seeks to address this legislative
gap and enhance regulatory transparency by mandating formal intimation of
such resignations to the Registrar.

63.6.2 The Committee further note that the proposed provision lays down a
clear procedural framework, inter alia, providing that: (i) resignation shall be
tendered by way of a written notice; (ii) the Board shall take note of such
resignation and intimate the Registrar within the prescribed time; (iii) in case
of failure by the company, the KMP may independently file such resignation
with reasons; (iv) the effective date of resignation is linked to receipt of notice
or a specified later date; and (v) liability for acts during the tenure continues
even after resignation.

63.6.3  The Committee note the concerns that the current drafting

of Section 203A could be misread as permitting resignation of a whole-time

key managerial personnel on a bare one day's notice, which would undermine

governance stability. The Committee observe that the legislative intent of

Section 203A is to provide a statutory mechanism for disclosure and

regulatory visibility of KMP resignations, not to override or shorten contractual

or policy-based notice periods. The Committee find merit in clarifying that the

provision should expressly state that the notice period for resignation of a

whole-time KMP shall be such period as may be agreed upon in the

employment contract or be mutually agreed upon between the KMP and the

company. Such clarification will prevent misuse of the provision, ensure

accountability remains tied to the individual's tenure, and preserve

professional certainty without creating conflict with contractual arrangements.

Accordingly, the Committee recommend that the clause be suitably amended
                                                      512
to make clear that Section 203A governs disclosure and intimation to the
Registrar, while the length of notice period continues to be determined by
employment contract, thereby safeguarding governance stability and avoiding
unintended interpretation of one day resignations.

63.6.4 The Committee also recommend that it may be specified, by way of an
explanatory clarification accompanying Section 203A or in the Rules to be
prescribed thereunder, that Section 203A is intended to govern the disclosure
and intimation of such resignation to the Registrar, and not to override or
shorten any contractually or internally prescribed notice period.

63.6.5 The Committee note the suggestion that the proviso to Section 203A
may be suitably modified to limit post-resignation liability of whole-time KMPs
to a reasonable and specified period, with the objective of balancing
accountability and professional certainty. The Committee observe that while
this proposal seeks to provide clarity and fairness, they concur with the
Ministry's clarification that prescribing such a limitation could undermine
accountability for defaults committed during the individual's tenure.
Accordingly, the Committee recommend that Section 203A be retained in its
present form on this point, with liability firmly anchored to acts committed
while in office, thereby ensuring accountability without introducing arbitrary
post-resignation periods.

63.6.6  Concerns have been raised about aligning of timelines relating to

resignation and reporting under Section203A with that of SEBI's requirements

relating to KMP appointment and resignation. The Committee, feel that the

official filing window under the Companies Act should align with broader

market disclosure structures to eliminate discrepancies between stock

exchange notifications and public registry records. The committee therefore

recommend that the Ministry, either in the provisions or the rules formulated

thereunder, should specify the timelines to be followed by the Company and

the Key Managerial Personnel regarding intimation to the Registrar thus

eliminating any confliction with the SEBI guidelines.
                                                      513
63.6.7  Accordingly, after considering the suggestions received and the

submissions of the Ministry as well as detailed deliberation in the matter, the

Committee recommend that the clause be amended as under :-

"After section 203 of the principal Act, the following section shall be
inserted, namely:--

    "203A. (1) A whole-time key managerial personnel of a company, who is
not a director, may resign from his office by giving a notice in writing to the
company, and the Board shall, on receipt of such notice, take note of the
same and shall intimate the Registrar of such resignation in such form and
manner and within such time, as may be prescribed:

    Provided that where the company fails to intimate the Registrar under
this sub-section within such time the said key managerial personnel may
forward a copy of his resignation along with detailed reasons for his
resignation to the Registrar in such manner, as may be prescribed.

    (2) The resignation of a key managerial personnel under sub-section (1)
shall take effect from the date as mutually agreed by such key managerial
personnel and the company or the date arrived at based on the contract of
employment between such key managerial personnel and the company
whichever is earlier.

     Provided that such key managerial personnel who has resigned shall be
liable even after his resignation for the default for which he was liable
during his tenure.".

                                               CLAUSE - 64

64. Clause 64 of the Bill seeks to amend Section 204 of the Companies Act
2013 regarding Secretarial audit.

64.1 Provision proposed in The Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

         In section 204 of the principal Act,-- (a) in sub-section (1), for the words
"company secretary in practice", the words "secretarial auditor" shall be substituted;

(b) after sub-section (1), the following sub-section shall be inserted, namely:--

         "(1A) A person shall be eligible for appointment as a secretarial auditor of a
company only if he is a company secretary in practice: Provided that a firm, whereof
majority of partners practising in India who are qualified for appointment, may be
appointed by its firm name to be the secretarial auditor of a company:

Provided further that every partner of the firm shall be a person who has been
registered with a statutory institute or body established under a law in India having
powers of such registration.";

(c) in sub-sections (2) to (4), for the words "company secretary in practice",
wherever they occur, the words "secretarial auditor" shall be substituted.

64.2 Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (The Companies Act, 2013):

204. (1) Every listed company and a company belonging to other class of
companies as may be prescribed shall annex with its Board's report made in terms of
sub-section (3) of section 134, a secretarial audit report, given by a company
secretary in practice, in such form as may be prescribed.

         (2) It shall be the duty of the company to give all assistance and facilities to
the company secretary in practice, for auditing the secretarial and related records of
the company.

         (3) The Board of Directors, in their report made in terms of sub-section (3) of
section 134, shall explain in full any qualification or observation or other remarks
made by the company secretary in practice in his report under sub-section (1).

                                                      515
         (4) If a company or any officer of the company or the company secretary in
practice, contravenes the provisions of this section, the company, every officer of the
company or the company secretary in practice, who is in default, shall be liable to a
penalty of two lakh rupees.

64.3 Reasons / Justification given by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs for the
proposed provision:

"Proposed amendments in section 204 to allow Multi-Disciplinary Partnerships
(MDPs) for Secretarial Auditors in a similar manner as provided under section 141 for
auditors (also similar amendment is proposed in section 148). It is also proposed that
every partner in such MDPs must be a member of an institute or body registered in
India, while replacing the term "company secretary in practice" with "secretarial
auditor" and prescribing eligibility conditions accordingly."

64.4 Important Views/Suggestions given by Experts/Stakeholders:

         Few of the suggestions given by stakeholders, while seeking to bring in
amendments to the provisions are as follows:

64.4.1  One of the stakeholders welcomed the amendment and further

proposed to align the provisions w.r.t appointment of Secretarial Auditor with the

provisions provided under SEBI (LODR) Reg 24A(b) which read as follows:

(b) On the basis of recommendation of board of directors, a listed entity shall appoint
or re-appoint: (i) an individual as Secretarial Auditor for not more than one term of
five consecutive years; or (ii) a Secretarial Audit firm as Secretarial Auditor for not
more than two terms of five consecutive years, with the approval of its shareholders
in its Annual General Meeting.

64.4.2  Another stakeholder proposed that appointment and removal of

Secretarial Auditor of Government Companies also be made by CAG in the same

manner as statutory auditor is appointed.

64.4.3  Another stakeholder suggested addition of additional proviso to section

204: "Provided that in case of a listed company, the secretarial auditor may be

appointed or re-appointed in such manner as may be prescribed by the Securities

and Exchange Board of India." In Rule 8, sub-rule (4) may be substituted to provide
"to appoint internal auditor." After sub-rule (4), a provision may be added to provide

        516
for appointment of secretarial auditor, except in case of listed companies. For listed
companies, the SEBI LODR Regulations already includes elaborate provisions on
the term and manner of appointment.

64.4.4  Mandatory registration with a statutory institute/ body may constrain the

development of multi-disciplinary partnership (MDP), as many specialised

professions and subject matter experts operate in unregulated fields e.g. Consultants

(e.g. MBAs), IT experts (e.g. AI, data security), ESG specialist, Forensic, etc.

Framework should be based on recognised qualifications, and relevant professional

experience, rather than registration alone. Making statutory registration a

precondition is not aligned with the objective of tapping global consulting and

auditing industry.

64.5 Examination by the Committee:

         In response to suggestion given by the stakeholder, the Ministry of Corporate
Affairs, in their written replies, have submitted as under:

64.5.1  While expressing their disagreement with the suggestion stated at

64.4.1 the Ministry stated that applying the SEBI (LODR) framework to Secretarial

Auditors under the Companies Act would unnecessarily increase compliance

burdens for unlisted companies; therefore, the provision should remain unchanged.

64.5.2  In response to the suggestion listed at 64.4.2. the Ministry stated that

extending the CAG appointment and removal mechanism to Secretarial Auditors is

not warranted, as their appointment under Section 204 is governed by the Board.

64.5.3  As regards suggestions given at 64.4.3, the Ministry replied the

Companies Act should continue to provide a uniform statutory framework for

Secretarial Auditors, with SEBI (LODR) requirements operating in addition for listed

companies. Proposed Second proviso is also proposed to be deleted to promote

MDPs. This is in line with the proposal for CAs and Cost Accountants."

64.5.4  Elaborating on the suggestion, the representative from the Ministry of

Corporate Affairs, during the Clause-by-Clause consideration of the Bill explained
                                                      517
that Clause 64 addresses a structural gap: while Section 144 (audit firms) and
Section 148 (cost audit firms) allow firm-level constitution, there was no provision for
a "Secretarial Audit Firm" under Section 201/204. The Bill now introduces this.

64.6 Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

64.6.1 The Committee note that the proposed amendment seeks to formally
align the terminology under section 204 by substituting the expression
"company secretary in practice" with "secretarial auditor", while retaining the
substantive requirement that such auditor shall be a company secretary in
practice. The Committee note that this brings the framework for secretarial
audit in line with the provisions relating to statutory auditors and cost auditors
under sections 141 and 148 of the Act, thereby ensuring consistency across
audit functions.

64.6.2 The Committee further note that the proposed insertion of sub-section
(1A) enables appointment of secretarial auditors in the name of a firm, subject
to the condition that a majority of partners are practicing in India and are
eligible for such appointment. This provides statutory recognition to multi-
disciplinary partnership structures.

64.6.3 The Committee note the suggestion that the appointment and tenure of
Secretarial Auditors be aligned with the framework prescribed under SEBI
(LODR) Regulation 24A(b), including fixed terms and shareholder approval at
the Annual General Meeting. The Committee note the Ministry's response that
applying the SEBI (LODR) framework to Secretarial Auditors under the
Companies Act would unnecessarily increase compliance burden, particularly
for unlisted companies, and that the provision should accordingly remain
unchanged. The Committee concur with the Ministry's view and do not
recommend any modification on this count.

                                                      518
64.6.4 As regards the suggestion that appointment and removal of Secretarial
Auditors of Government companies be entrusted to the Comptroller and
Auditor General, in the same manner as statutory auditors, the Committee find
that appointment of Secretarial Auditors under section 204 is, and ought to
remain, a matter governed by the Board of Directors of the company. The
Committee accept this position and do not recommend any change.

64.6.5 The Committee also examined the suggestion that the manner of
appointment of Secretarial Auditors of listed companies be separately
prescribed by the Securities and Exchange Board of India, with corresponding
changes to Rule 8. The Committee recognize the merit in the Companies Act
continuing to provide a uniform statutory framework for Secretarial Auditors
across all companies, with SEBI (LODR) requirements operating in addition for
listed companies. The Committee accordingly do not recommend separately
empowering SEBI to prescribe the manner of appointment under section 204.

64.6.6 The Committee note that the Ministry, in its response, has itself
proposed deletion of the second proviso to sub-section (1A) so as to promote
multi-disciplinary partnerships, consistent with the corresponding approach
adopted for Chartered Accountants and Cost Accountants under similar
provisions. The Committee find merit in this approach, particularly given the
concern that mandating registration of every partner of a Secretarial Audit firm
with a statutory institute or body may constrain the development and
functioning of multi-disciplinary partnership firms, especially where several
emerging professional domains operate without a corresponding statutory
regulator. The Committee, therefore, concur with the Ministry's proposal and
recommend that the said second proviso be omitted.

64.6.7 In view of the above, the Committee recommend that Clause 64 of the
Bill may be modified as follows:

         "In section 204 of the principal Act,--

                                                      519
(a) in sub-section (1), for the words "company secretary in practice", the
words "secretarial auditor" shall be substituted;
(b) after sub-section (1), the following sub-section shall be inserted,
namely:--
"(1A) A person shall be eligible for appointment as a secretarial auditor
of a company only if he is a company secretary in practice:
Provided that a firm, whereof majority of partners practising in India who
are qualified for appointment, may be appointed by its firm name to be
the secretarial auditor of a company.";
(c) in sub-sections (2) to (4), for the words "company secretary in
practice", wherever they occur, the words "secretarial auditor" shall be
substituted."

                                               CLAUSE - 65

65. Clause 65 of the Bill seeks to amend Section 206 of the Companies Act
2013 regarding Power to call for information, inspect books and conduct
inquiries.

65.1 Provision proposed in The Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

         In section 206 of the principal Act, for sub-section (7), the following sub-
section shall be substituted, namely:--

                  "(7) If a company fails to furnish any information or explanation or
produce any document required under this section, the company shall be liable to a
penalty of one lakh rupees and in case of continuing failure, with a further penalty of
five hundred rupees for each day, after the first during which such failure continues,
subject to a maximum of five lakh rupees and every officer of the company who is in
default shall be liable to a penalty of twenty-five thousand rupees and in case of
continuing failure, with a further penalty of two hundred rupees for each day, after the
first during which such failure continues, subject to a maximum of one lakh rupees."

65.2 Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (The Companies Act, 2013):

206. (1) * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

(7) If a company fails to furnish any information or explanation or produce any
document required under this section, the company and every officer of the
company, who is in default shall be punishable with a fine which may extend to one
lakh rupees and in the case of a continuing failure, with an additional fine which may
extend to five hundred rupees for everyday after the first during which the failure
continue.

* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

65.3 Reasons / Justification given by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs for the
proposed provision:

"The amendment replaces the existing fine-based punishment with a structured
penalty framework, including fixed and continuing penalties for non-compliance. The
amendment is part of the broader decriminalisation exercise under the Bill"

                                                      521
65.4 Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

65.4.1  The Committee note that the proposed amendment seeks to

substitute sub-section (7) of section 206 with a revised penalty framework for

failure to furnish any information or explanation, or to produce any document,

required under the said section. The Committee observe that the existing

provision prescribes a fine which may extend to one lakh rupees on the

company and every officer in default, with an additional fine of up to five

hundred rupees for each day of continuing failure, without any prescribed cap.

65.4.2  The Committee further note that the proposed sub-section (7)

replaces this fine-based punishment with a structured, capped penalty. The

company shall be liable to a penalty of one lakh rupees, with a further penalty

of five hundred rupees per day of continuing failure, subject to a maximum of

five lakh rupees; and every officer in default shall be liable to a penalty of

twenty-five thousand rupees, with a further penalty of two hundred rupees per

day of continuing failure, subject to a maximum of one lakh rupees. The

Committee note that, as stated by the Ministry, this amendment is part of the

broader decriminalisation exercise under the Bill.

65.4.3  The Committee recognize that the proposed amendment provides

certainty on maximum exposure through express caps, while preserving a

meaningful daily deterrent for continuing non-compliance with Registrar

inquiries. The Committee further note that this also strengthens the Registrar's

practical enforcement leverage in information-gathering and inspection

proceedings, by making non-cooperation a quantifiable, swiftly ad judicable

civil wrong rather than a criminal offence requiring prosecution.

65.4.4  The Committee find that the proposed framework brings certainty

and proportionality to the penalty structure under section 206 by prescribing

distinct, capped penalties for the company and its officers in place of the

earlier open-ended fine. The Committee, having examined the provisions of the

Clause, accept Clause 65 as proposed, without any modification.

67 Clause 67 of the Bill seeks to amend Section 230 of the Companies Act
2013 regarding Power to compromise or make arrangements with creditors
and members.

67.1 Provision proposed in The Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

          In section 230 of the principal Act,--

(a) in sub-section (1),--

                  (i) the words and figures "or under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy
Code, 2016, as the case may be," shall be omitted;

          (ii) before the Explanation, the following provisos shall be inserted,

namely:-

                  "Provided that on and from the commencement of the Corporate Laws
(Amendment) Act, 2026, every application to be made under this section or sections
231 to 233 to the Tribunal, shall be made to the Tribunal having jurisdiction over the
transferee company or the resultant company, as the case may be, and such
Tribunal shall exercise all the powers of the Tribunal referred to in such sections for
all the companies involved in the schemes of compromise or arrangement or
amalgamations:

                  Provided further that any application pending before the Tribunal as on
the date of commencement of the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Act, 2026, shall
continue to be dealt with by the Tribunal in accordance with the provisions applicable
before such commencement.";

         (b) in sub-section (6), the words and figures "or under the Insolvency and
Bankruptcy Code, 2016, as the case may be" shall be omitted.

67.2 Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (The Companies Act, 2013):

230. (1) Where a compromise or arrangement is proposed--

(a) between a company and its creditors or any class of them; or

                           526
         (b) between a company and its members or any class of them,

the Tribunal may, on the application of the company or of any creditor or member of
the company, or in the case of a company which is being wound up, of the liquidator,
appointed under this Act or under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, as the
case may be, order a meeting of the creditors or class of creditors, or of the
members or class of members, as the case may be, to be called, held and conducted
in such manner as the Tribunal directs.

         Explanation.--For the purposes of this sub-section, arrangement includes a
reorganisation of the company's share capital by the consolidation of shares of
different classes or by the division of shares into shares of different classes, or by
both of those methods.

                                                    * * * * *

         (6) Where, at a meeting held in pursuance of sub-section (1), majority of
persons representing three-fourths in value of the creditors, or class of creditors or
members or class of members, as the case may be, voting in person or by proxy or
by postal ballot, agree to any compromise or arrangement and if such compromise or
arrangement is sanctioned by the Tribunal by an order, the same shall be binding on
the company, all the creditors, or class of creditors or members or class of members,
as the case may be, or, in case of a company being wound up, on the liquidator
appointed under this act or under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, as the
case may be, and the contributories of the company.

                                                    * * * * *

67.3 Reasons / Justification given by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs for the
         proposed provision:

         "This amendment is to facilitate speedier disposal of merger cases before
NCLT. It is proposed that instead of both/all benches hearing petitions separately, a
single bench of NCLT having jurisdiction over transferee company shall hear
petitions on behalf of all companies involved.

The words "or under the IBC-2016" are proposed to be omitted in sub-section (1) and
(6)."

                                                      527
67.4 Important Views/Suggestions given by Experts/Stakeholders:

         Few of the suggestions given by stakeholders, while seeking to bring in
amendments to the provisions are as follows:

67.4.1  One of the suggestions received proposed an insertion before the

Explanation, as follows "No application under this section shall be maintainable

during the corporate insolvency resolution process under the Insolvency and

Bankruptcy Code, 2016, but the Tribunal may permit such application after

commencement of liquidation where it is satisfied that the proposed compromise or

arrangement is likely to maximise value for stakeholders.

67.4.2  A stakeholder further proposed insertion of the following paragraph

after the proviso--"Provided that the President of the Tribunal may, on an application

by any party or on administrative grounds, transfer the proceedings to another Bench

or constitute a Special Bench where such transfer is necessary in the interests of

justice, convenience of stakeholders, efficient disposal, or balanced distribution of

cases. The modification ensures that creditors, shareholders and regulators

connected with the transferor company can effectively participate.

67.4.3  Another stakeholder suggested that Sections 230 to 232 be amended

to permit creditor consent to be submitted by way of simple consent letters in lieu of

affidavits, aligning the procedural requirements with the comparatively streamlined

framework already available under Section 233. The justification given was that

requiring separate affidavits from each consenting creditor imposes unnecessary

procedural burden and cost, particularly since the application itself is already

supported by a sworn affidavit executed by the parties to the scheme.

67.4.4  One more suggestion received was regarding extending this "single-

window" principle to include all post-merger compliance, including unified processing

for RoC and RD approvals across all involved entities. While single-bench jurisdiction

reduces NCLT timelines by 3-6 months, advisers still face fragmented post-order

filings with different RoCs. A unified digital workflow is needed to prevent

administrative bottlenecks.

67.4.5  The proposed amendment is welcome. It may also be considered

whether similar provisions could be extended to LLP-to-LLP mergers in due course,

given that AIFs are increasingly expected to adopt the LLP structure. Lower approval

thresholds remove practical obstacles that had rendered the fast-track route difficult

to use in practice, particularly for companies with dispersed shareholding.

                             528
67.5 Examination by the Committee:

         In response to suggestion given by the stakeholder, the Ministry of Corporate
Affairs, in their written replies, have submitted as under:

67.5.1       As regards the proposal listed at 67.4.1 the Ministry clarified that the

amendment to Section 230 removes references to the liquidation process under the

Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016. A major delay in the present mechanism for

liquidation is due to considerations by companies to enter into schemes of

arrangement under the Companies Act, 2013. In an effort to separate the liquidation

process under the Companies Act, 2013 from that under the Insolvency and

Bankruptcy Code, 2016, the amendment to Section 230 iterates that there may be no

schemes of arrangement or compromises under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy

Code, 2016.

67.5.2       With respect to the suggestion at 67.4.2, the Ministry replied that since

the suggestion proposes that upon application the Tribunal may be switched to a

more convenient location for creditors, shareholders of the transferor company (as

the case may be). The present amendment has been expressly brought about to

ensure operational efficiency and facilitate speedier disposal of merger schemes by

the NCLT. A single bench having jurisdiction of the resultant company or the

transferee company may be the avenue for hearing of merger schemes, so that

parallel proceedings are not initiated for the same scheme. In exceptional cases an

application may be made to the NCLT with original territorial jurisdiction, and

subsequent orders may be passed by such bench on an ad-hoc basis if deemed

necessary in the interest of justice. An exception for such extraordinary

circumstances may be required.

67.5.3.      In response to the suggestion regarding obtaining creditor consent in

writing the Ministry reasoned that Sections 230-232 of the Companies Act, 2013

provide for compromises, arrangements and amalgamations that are sanctioned by

the NCLT. The requirement of furnishing creditor consent by way of affidavits forms

part of the procedural framework governing these proceedings. The comparison with
                                                      529
the framework under Section 233 may not be appropriate. Section 233 provides a
fast merger mechanism for specified classes of companies, whereas as mentioned
above the schemes under 230-232 are sanctioned by the NCLT. Accordingly, the
procedural requirements governing the two frameworks are distinct. Further,
pursuant to the recommendations of the Company Law Committee, 2022, affidavits
were proposed to be replaced with self-declarations, only in case of provisions not
requiring filing of affidavits before judicial or quasi-judicial bodies. The Committee
explicitly excluded proceedings before the NCLT, NCLAT and the Regional Director,
recognising evidentiary value of affidavits in such proceedings.

67.5.4  As regards the suggestion listed at 67.4.4, the response received from

the Ministry stated that the suggestion proposes including port-merger compliances

within the ambit of the proposed amendment to Companies Act, 2013. Presently, the

Companies Act, 2013 does not prescribe any specific post-merger compliance

requirements with the NCLT. Forms to be filed are mandated to be filed with the

Registrar, while the NCLT is involved in a more supervisory role. As such, the

present compliances are streamlined to the extent possible as they mainly involve

filing requirements to be completed with the Registrar, under any supervision that the

NCLT may provide. However, this suggestion would be dealt appropriately through

Rules.

67.5.5  In response to para 67.4.5 suggesting application of similar provisions

to LLP to LLP mergers etc, the Ministry explicitly informed that LLP merger schemes

are few. LLPs are structurally a different where the LLP Agreement itself already

provides flexible mechanisms -- partner admission, retirement, capital restructuring,

conversion to company -- to achieve most of what a "merger" would achieve.

67.5.6  While deposing before the Committee the Joint Secretary, Ministry of

Corporate Affairs justified the amendment proposed in this Clause saying that

mergers currently require applications in both companies' respective NCLTs, causing

delay; under the amendment, only the NCLT where the surviving (transferee)

company is located needs to be approached, with details of the merging company

submitted there -- intended to expedite the process.
                                                      530
67.5.7  A concern was also raised regarding the need for a separate,

specialised tribunal for mergers and acquisitions, given that the NCLT is over-

burdened and clogged with cases, including matters under the Insolvency and

Bankruptcy Code. Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs while addressing the

concerns clarified that provision for special benches already exists via Clause

96/Section 419 (President of NCLT may constitute special benches, including for

group insolvency, etc.), so a fresh provision under Section 230 was not called for. On

transfer of cases between NCLT benches, she said this was not added in the

provision because the President's rule-making power to transfer cases is currently

sub judice before the Supreme Court, so the Ministry deliberately avoided interfering

with rules pending that outcome.

67.5.8 The Committee further enquired as to whether the relaxed merger/demerger
framework, including dispensation of filing before the Official Liquidator, has been
harmonized with the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code. Additionally, it was sought to
be clarified as to the fate of parallel IBC proceedings in respect of a holding or
subsidiary company already undergoing corporate insolvency resolution. In response
the Ministry informed that matters relating to schemes during liquidation are
governed by the provisions of the IBC and the regulations made thereunder.

67.6 Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

67.6.1  The Committee note that Clause 67 seeks to amend Section 230 of

the Companies Act, 2013 to provide for a single jurisdictional bench of the

National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) for schemes of compromise,

arrangement and amalgamation, and to omit references to the Insolvency and

Bankruptcy Code, 2016. The Committee further note that, with effect from

commencement of the Amendment Act, every application under section 230 or

sections 231 to 233 must be filed before the NCLT bench having jurisdiction

over the transferee or resultant company, with such bench exercising all

powers of the Tribunal for all companies involved in the scheme, while

applications already pending as on the date of commencement will continue

under the pre-amendment regime. The Committee are of the view that this
                                                      531
measure will reduce multiplicity of proceedings, compress timelines, and
lower cost and procedural duplication in multi-state mergers, demergers and
amalgamations, while the savings clause preserves certainty for schemes
already in process. The Committee also note that the amendment aligns this
framework with the existing fast-track approach under Rule 25(4)(a) of the
Companies (Compromises, Arrangements and Amalgamations) Rules, 2016.

67.6.2  The Committee considered the suggestions received for a

mechanism to transfer proceedings between Benches, or to constitute a

Special Bench, having regard also to concerns raised during deliberations

regarding NCLT pendency and a further suggestion for a separate, specialised

tribunal for mergers and acquisitions. The Committee note the Ministry's

response that a single bench hearing merger schemes ensures efficiency and

avoids parallel proceedings, that provision for Special Benches already exists

under section 419 read with Clause 96 of the Bill, and that the question of inter-

Bench transfer of proceedings is presently sub judice before the Hon'ble

Supreme Court, for which reason the Ministry has refrained from legislating on

the point. The Committee accept this position, while recommending that NCLT

capacity be augmented, including through additional Benches and members,

given that capacity constraints remain a root cause of delay. The Committee

urge the Ministry to revisit the question of inter-Bench transfer once the

pending matter before the Supreme Court is decided.

67.6.3  The Committee note that the deletion of the Insolvency and

Bankruptcy Code cross-reference in sub-sections (1) and (6) confines

schemes under Section 230 to the Companies Act framework and sharpens the

jurisdictional boundary between the two statutes. In this connection, the

Committee considered the suggestion that applications under section 230 be

barred during the corporate insolvency resolution process, subject to the

Tribunal's discretion post-liquidation, and a query raised during deliberations

on reconciling the relaxed merger/demerger process with parallel IBC

proceedings involving a holding or subsidiary company. The Committee note

the Ministry's clarification that the amendment is intended to keep the

        532
Companies Act and IBC liquidation frameworks distinct to avoid delay, and
that schemes during liquidation continue to be governed by the Insolvency
and Bankruptcy Code and regulations made thereunder. The Committee
accept this position, while desiring that the Ministry ensure a balanced and
clear approach to this Code/Companies Act boundary while framing the Rules.

67.6.4  The Committee considered the suggestions received on

procedural aspects, namely, permitting creditor consent under sections 230 to

232 through simple consent letters instead of affidavits, and dispensing with

members' meetings on the basis of 100% written consent. The Committee note

the Ministry's response that affidavits retain evidentiary value in Tribunal-

sanctioned schemes and that the fast-track framework under section 233 is not

comparable, and that members' meetings safeguard the interests of minority

shareholders. The Committee accept the Ministry's position on both counts

and do not recommend any modification.

67.6.5  The Committee further considered the suggestions to extend the

single-window mechanism to post-merger compliance, to enable end-to-end

digital processing of schemes, and to clarify that SEBI compliance for listed

entities remains unaffected by Tribunal approval, as also the suggestion to

extend similar merger provisions to LLP-to-LLP mergers. The Committee note

the Ministry's response that post-merger compliance and digital-processing

measures will be examined at the rule-making stage, that SEBI compliance

applies to listed entities independently in any event, and that LLP mergers

remain few given the flexibility already available under the LLP Agreement. The

Committee accept this position, while recommending that due consideration

be given to the post-merger compliance and digitisation suggestions while

framing the Rules.

67.6.6  During deliberation by the Committee, there appeared to be

ambiguity regarding the applicability of this amendment to cases/schemes

involving foreign companies and cross border mergers. The Committee note

that such cross- border mergers involving foreign companies are governed by
                                                      533
Section 234 of the Indian Companies Act. Therefore, with a view to bring clarity
and avoid misconstruction of the provision, the following may be added to
subsection (1) of Section 230:-

         "In section 230 of the principal Act,--
         (a) in sub-section (1),--

               Provided further that nothing contained in the first proviso shall
           apply to the application made under section 234.";

                                                CLAUSE- 68

68. Clause 68 of the Bill seeks to amend Section 232 of the Companies Act

68.1 Provision proposed in The Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

the proviso, after the words "or extinguished" occurring at the end, the words "on the

68.2 Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (The Companies Act, 2013):

232. (1) * * * * *

(3) The Tribunal, after satisfying itself that the procedure specified in sub-sections
(1) and (2) has been complied with, may, by order, sanction the compromise or
arrangement or by a subsequent order, make provision for the following matters,
namely:--

* * * * * * * * * *

(b) the allotment or appropriation by the transferee company of any shares,
debentures, policies or other like instruments in the company which, under the
compromise or arrangement, are to be allotted or appropriated by that company to or
for any person: Provided that a transferee company shall not, as a result of the

                                                    * * * * *

68.3 Reasons / Justification given by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs for the
         proposed provision:

"The amendment seeks to clarify that shares held by the transferee company in its
own name or through a trust shall be cancelled or extinguished at the stage of
merger or amalgamation."

                                                      535
68.4 Important Views/Suggestions given by Experts/Stakeholders:

Few of the suggestions given by stakeholders, while seeking to bring in amendments
to the provisions are as follows:

68.4.1  A suggestion received proposed to insert the word "automatically" after

the words "or extinguished" and before the proposed wordings "on the merger or

amalgamation". The justification given was that the insertion shall enable and ensure

that such shares will stand cancelled pursuant to the scheme becoming effective in

situations where the scheme/NCLT order may not have such wordings or in case

they have been accidentally missed. This will also avoid unnecessary amendments

to scheme post NCLT order at subsequent and will also avoid additional compliance

efforts for cancellation of shares i.e. additional filings and explanations at the ROC.

68.5 Examination by the Committee:

         In response to suggestion given by the stakeholder, the Ministry of Corporate
Affairs, in their written replies, consented to the suggestion proposing the addition of
the word automatically' before the phrase `or extinguished' in the proviso to sub-
section 232(3) of the Companies Act, 2013.

68.5.1  The Joint Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs while justifying the

Ministry's stand on the said suggestion stated that when a merger/amalgamation

involves absorbing a company's own subsidiary, the resulting shares can't be held by

the company (as it would amount to holding its own shares) and must be cancelled

-- but the existing provision lacked the words "on merger and amalgamation,"

leaving this ambiguous. The clause adds that language to remove the ambiguity. He

noted that the suggestion received to make this cancellation automatic, is considered

as a good suggestion and will be incorporated.

68.5.2  Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs added to the deliberation stating

that the Ministry's own officers had flagged a related clarification point on the merger-

                                    536
position language, which the Ministry will incorporate on its own initiative and
committed to providing the underlying rationale/logic when that clarification is added,
rather than leaving it unexplained."

68.6 Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

68.6.1  The Committee note that Section 232(3)(b) permits a Tribunal-

sanctioned scheme to provide that share held by a transferee company (or its

nominee) in a transferor company be cancelled or extinguished, without this

being treated as a reduction of capital of the transferee company. The

Committee further note that Clause 68 inserts a qualifying phrase clarifying

that this cancellation/extinguishment is specifically tied to, and occurs in the

context of, the merger or amalgamation itself.

68.6.2  The Committee find that this is a clarificatory, draft-tightening

amendment that anchors the cancellation/extinguishment mechanism

explicitly to the merger/amalgamation event, reducing scope for interpretive

ambiguity about when this special treatment applies.

68.6.3  The Committee note the suggestion that shares held by a

transferee company stand automatically cancelled or extinguished on the

merger or amalgamation becoming effective, so as to avoid the need for

separate scheme amendments or additional regulatory filings, and the

Ministry's acceptance of this suggestion, with the word "automatically" to be

inserted before the phrase "or extinguished" in the proviso to sub-section

232(3). The Committee further note that the Ministry has identified a related

clarification concerning the merger-position language in this proviso, and has

undertaken to incorporate the same along with the underlying rationale

therefor. The Committee welcome this proactive approach and recommend

that the Clause may be amended as follows:-

        537
"In section 232 of the principal Act, in sub-section (3), in clause (b), in
the proviso, for the words "or extinguished" occurring at the end, the
words "or automatically extinguished on the merger or amalgamation"
shall be substituted"

                                               CLAUSE - 69

69. Clause 69 of the Bill seeks to amend Section 233 of the Companies Act

69.1 Provision proposed in The Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

2016. 31 of 2016. 29 18 of 2013. 5 10 15 20 25 30 35 40 45 "(b) the objections and
suggestions received are considered by the companies in their respective general

such members present and voting;"; (ii) in clause (d), for the word "nine-tenths", the
