69.2 Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (The Companies Act, 2013):

233. (1) Notwithstanding the provisions of section 230 and section 232, a scheme of
merger or amalgamation may be entered into between two or more small companies
or between a holding company and its wholly-owned subsidiary company or such
other class or classes of companies as may be prescribed, subject to the following,
namely:--

* * * * *

         (b) the objections and suggestions received are considered by the companies
in their respective general meetings and the scheme is approved by the respective
members or class of members at a general meeting holding at least ninety per cent.
of the total number of shares;

* * * * *

                                                      539
         (d) the scheme is approved by majority representing nine-tenths in value of
the creditors or class of creditors of respective companies indicated in a meeting
convened by the company by giving a notice of twenty-one days along with the
scheme to its creditors for the purpose or otherwise approved in writing.

(2) The transferee company shall file a copy of the scheme so approved in the
manner as may be prescribed, with the Central Government, Registrar and the
Official Liquidator where the registered office of the company is situated.

* * * * *

(13) The Central Government may provide for the merger or amalgamation of
companies in such manner as may be prescribed.

69.3 Reasons / Justification given by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs for the
         proposed provision:

"This clause proposes amendment in section 233 of the Companies Act, 2013 to
expedite mergers and amalgamations. It is proposed that for fast-track mergers, the
present stipulated approval of the scheme by members/creditors holding 90% of total
voting power/value will be reduced to majority of members/creditors who are present
and who hold at least 75% of total voting power/value of the members/creditors who
are present. This is similar to the condition laid down for cases which are submitted
for sanction before National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT)"

69.4 Important Views/Suggestions given by Experts/Stakeholders:

Few of the suggestions given by stakeholders, while seeking to bring in amendments
to the provisions are as follows:

69.4.1     "Expand fast-track eligibility to include demergers and hive-offs for

solvent, low-risk private company groups. Currently, even simple internal demergers

are often forced through the lengthy NCLT route. Expanding the fast-track scope

supports agile restructuring for PE-backed and scaling startups."

69.4.2     "Section 233 may be amended to introduce a provision permitting

dispensation from convening a meeting of members where members representing

100% in value provide their consent in writing."

           540
69.4.3      "Extend the applicability of Section 233 to mergers involving Section 8

companies which do not receive or hold public funds, grants, donations or other

public charitable contributions, subject to such safeguards and conditions as may be

prescribed. Omit the words `not being a company incorporated under Section 8 of CA

2013 which fulfils the criteria as may be prescribed' from the eligible unlisted

companies"

69.4.4      "A proviso may be added after the insertion of the revised clause (b):

"Provided that any member holding not less than ten per cent of the total voting

power, who dissented from or was absent at the meeting approving the scheme

under clause (b), may within thirty days apply to the Regional Director objecting to

the fairness of the valuation or exchange ratio; the Regional Director shall refer such

objection to the Tribunal, and the scheme shall not bind the objecting member until

the Tribunal disposes of the reference."

69.4.5      "Permit written consent as an alternative to physical or virtual meetings,

Allow written consent for approvals of wholly-owned subsidiaries and substitute

'merger and amalgamation' with the words 'compromise and arrangement'"

69.4.6      "Sec 233(a) in sub-section (1),(i) for clause (b), the following clause

shall be substituted, namely:--

"(b) the objections and suggestions received are considered by the companies in
their respective general meetings and the scheme is approved by a majority of
members or class of members present and voting at the meeting held in such
manner, as may be prescribed, who hold at least ninety per cent. of the value in
shares held by such members present and voting;";

69.4.7      "In section 233(1)(d), after the words "creditors or class of creditors of

respective companies", the words "present and voting" may be inserted".

69.4.8      "To include the words "present and voting" after the words "in value of

creditors or class of creditors" to align it with the shareholders meeting. Revised

clause including proposed amendment (d) the scheme is approved by majority

representing "atleast three-fourths" in value of the creditors or class of creditors

"present and voting" of respective companies indicated in a meeting convened by the

company by giving a notice of twenty-one days along with the scheme to its creditors

for the purpose or otherwise approved in writing."

                                          541
69.4.9   "While Section 233(1)(d) clearly permits creditors to approve the

scheme through written consent, a similar enabling provision is not expressly stated

for shareholders under Section 233(1)(b), even though such approval is accepted in

practice. It is suggested that shareholders should also be expressly permitted to

approve schemes through written consent, to avoid unnecessary meetings".

"Section 233(2) requires the transferee company to file the scheme, which may lead
to confusion in cross-jurisdiction or cross-border situations. It is recommended that
clear guidance be provided on filing responsibilities and on whether the involvement
of the Official Liquidator is required in all cases."

"It is also recommended that the section explicitly state that demergers are included
within its scope, to avoid interpretational issues. These clarifications would enhance
certainty, ease of implementation, and consistency in the application of the fast-track
merger and demerger framework."

69.4.10  Another stakeholder stated that the fast track merger route in India is

available for a restricted set of companies: startups, small companies and a merger

with a wholly-owned subsidiary. If such mergers involve a public listed company,

SEBI's regulations on schemes of control would apply which require at least a

majority of minority vote of shareholders of the listed company involved. We agree

with the amendment on fast-track mergers in the Companies Act, 2013 given that

any such merger involving listed companies will continue to require majority of

minority approval.

69.4.11  Rationalization of Section 233(11) relating to set-off of authorized share

capital fees in mergers. The Act or the Rules may expressly provide that: "For the

purpose of granting set-off under Section 233(11), the Registrar shall determine the

amount of fees already paid by the transferor company on the basis of records

available with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs. The transferee company shall not be

required to produce historical payment receipts or challans where such information is

available in Government records." The section may also state that where historical

records are unavailable with MCA, A declaration by the company, certified by a

practicing Company Secretary or Chartered Accountant, together with the records

available on the MCA portal, shall be sufficient evidence of payment.

69.4.12  Welcome the reduction of the approval threshold to 75% and consider

allowing written shareholder/creditor consent as an alternative to convening a formal

meeting. Strike-off process: Introduce a 30-day objection-free timeline for strike-off

                    542
and permit distribution of surplus to shareholders. Summary liquidation: Introduce a
digital interface and prescribe a time-bound closure of 3-6 months.

69.4.13    Voting threshold in sub clause (1)(i) to be increased to ninety per cent

because a uniform approval threshold may not be appropriate for all categories of

fast-track mergers. It is therefore recommended that the approval thresholds or

additional procedural safeguards be calibrated depending on the nature of the

merger.

69.4.14    It is recommended that the clauses be retained, subject to the

clarification that the three-fourths creditor threshold in section 233(1)(d) refers to

creditors in value, and that the rules preserve the right of any creditor to object

before the Regional Director within the existing thirty-day window.

69.4.15    It is suggested to provide dissenting shareholders an exit via a Section

247 registered valuer. Further, to base the 75% on total voting capital or set a

minimum quorum. Allow a 10-15% minority to escalate the scheme into the full

Section 230/232 Tribunal process. Make class-wise voting mandatory where classes

are affected and reconsider the mismatch between the new 75% member threshold

and the unchanged 90% creditor threshold. Thus, providing a fair-value exit or a right

to refer the scheme to the Tribunal would align the provision with international

practice.

69.5 Examination by the Committee:

In response to suggestion given by the stakeholder, the Ministry of Corporate Affairs,
in their written replies, have submitted as under :

69.5.1     As regards the suggestions relating to obtaining written consents

instead of holding the mandatory meeting with shareholders and creditors, the

Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs deposed as follows,

        "             ,     
                 That is not being accepted. 
           ,  - ,   ,      "

                                    543
69.5.2  In response to the suggestions proposing that the stipulated voting

majority be confined to those creditors present and voting in the meeting to approve

a scheme of arrangement and insertion of the words "present and voting" in section

233(1)(d), after the words "creditors or class of creditors of respective companies",

the Ministry stated that a similar provision is provided for members of such

companies wishing to enter into a scheme of arrangement therefore the suggestion

will be incorporated. The addition of the phrase `present and voting' may provide

operational clarity regarding the nature of majority required for creditors' approval

under Section 233.

69.5.3  As regards extending the applicability of Section 233 to mergers

involving Section 8 companies which do not receive or hold public funds, grants,

donations or other public charitable contributions the Ministry replied that the

suggestions are noted and if required, the same will be taken for consideration

through Rules.

69.5.4  One of the major concerns arising in the suggestions was about

ensuring protection of interest of minority shareholders. In many sittings, concerns

were raised stating that lowering the approval threshold from 90% to 75% could

disadvantage minority shareholders, especially where foreign institutional investors

hold majority stakes with different investment horizons than small/promoter

shareholders, It was also pointed out that shifting the calculation denominator to

"present and voting" lets dominant shareholder groups pass major merger

restructurings while minority owners are absent.

69.5.5  In response the Ministry replied that the proposed amendment

stipulates that the scheme shall be approved by a majority of members or class of

members present and voting at the meeting held in such manner as may be

prescribed who hold at least seventy-five per cent of the value in shares held by such

members present and voting. The revised voting requirement seeks to broaden

shareholder participation while continuing to require substantial shareholder approval

for the scheme.

         Thus, it ensures protection of interest of minority shareholders and
democratization of the process of voting amongst shareholders and further ensures
that holding of 75 % of shares alone is not enough, it must also gather the support of
the majority of members present and voting. Further, the Act already contains
provision for referring the scheme to NCLT in case the Regional Director after
receiving the objections or suggestions is of the opinion that such scheme is not in
public interest or in the interest of creditors.

                                                      544
69.5.6   In response to the suggestions regarding retaining the current

requirement of 90% of shareholders/creditors consent, the Ministry reiterated that

this clause has been proposed to expedite mergers and amalgamations and for fast-

track mergers, it is proposed to bring the approval requirement in line with condition

laid down for cases before NCLT.

69.5.7   Elaborating on the issue, the representative of the Ministry of Corporate

Affairs deposed as under:

        "You had also asked why the 90 per cent requirement is being brought down
        to 75 per cent. We have seen internationally that no jurisdiction has a 90 per
        cent requirement. Again, already in NCLT approved mergers and acquisitions,
        the requirement is only 75 per cent. We are aligning the 75 per cent provision
        in NCLT with the Fast Track Merger route as well. There are inbuilt safeguards
        available for minority stakeholders because, before approving the merger
        application, the company publishes it and all the stakeholders are asked to
        give their comments. So, there are inbuilt mechanisms. As I already
        mentioned, it takes only 60 days when compared with NCLT, where it takes
        almost one year."

69.5.9   In relation to the suggestion regarding the filing obligations, the Ministry

has pointed out that these have been explicitly provided for in the provision itself, and

may not require a change. Also, with respect to the suggestion regarding demerger, it

was informed that Section 233(12) already provides for demerger of companies by

the Regional Director.

69.5.10  As regards the suggestion regarding inclusion of listed companies and

provision of majority of minority shareholders' consent, the Ministry clarified that

Listed companies are also governed by SEBI regulations, wherein such companies

are required to obtain a NOC from SEBI/stock exchange before-hand. The

requirements pertaining to SEBI regulations may be referred to/raised with SEBI.

69.5.11  With regards to the suggestions relating to set-off of authorized share

capital fees in mergers, the Ministry stated that Section 233(11) corresponds to

section 232(3)(i) which is applicable in case of NCLT mergers. Both these provisions

are based on the principle that when companies merge, their authorised capital is

combined into the resultant entity. Thus, instead of asking the resultant company to

pay registration fees on the entire increased amount of authorised capital, section

233(11) allows a fee set-off. This means that the registration fees already paid by the

transferor companies in the past are subtracted from the fees payable by the

                                  545
resultant entity on the increase in authorised capital on account of merger. Therefore,
actual receipts of payment are required to be furnished to claim this set-off and a
declaration from a professional may not suffice for this purpose, as it may lead to a
loss to the exchequer.

69.5.12  As regards the strike-off process under section 248, the Ministry was in

agreement of the suggestion stating that RoC, C-PACE to decide the application

within 60 days, with reasons to be mentioned in case of delay, failing which the

application is Suo-moto approved.

69.5.13  However, regarding the part envisaging surplus funds to be distributed

amongst shareholders under the strike off process, the Ministry expressed their

disagreement stating that the same cannot be considered as any liquidation of

assets and subsequent distribution to creditors and shareholders involves process of

sale, invitation of claims, their adjudication and then distribution. All these require a

due process to be followed and oversight of quasi-judicial authority to ensure the

integrity of the process. The time lines are already prescribed in provisions of section

361 to 365 of the Act.

69.5.14  As regards digitization the Ministry assured that the same may be dealt

with while formulation of Rules. Streamlining the process of summary liquidation on a

digital interface may be considered at the stage of MCA21.

69.5.15  Another major concern raised was regarding minority shareholder exit

problem. It was pointed out that if the approval threshold drops to 75%, a minority

shareholder opposed to a merger can be forced into it with no recourse. It was also

proposed a buy-out/exit-at-market-valuation option for dissenting minority

shareholders as a structural fix.

69.6 Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

69.6.1   The Committee note that the Section 233 of the Companies Act

2013 provides a simplified, Regional-Director-sanctioned fast-track merger

route for prescribed categories of companies (e.g., small companies, holding-

wholly owned subsidiary mergers, and other prescribed classes), as an

alternative to the full NCLT process under sections 230-232.

69.6.2   The Committee also note that as per the current amendment the

scheme must now be approved by a majority of members or class of members

                                   546
present and voting at the meeting (in the prescribed manner) who hold at least
75% of the value in shares held by such members present and voting. This is a
marked relaxation from the requirement of a 90% (nine-tenths) shareholder
approval threshold under the unamended provision and is expected to
materially increase the practical usability of section 233. The Committee
accept that the safeguard of a members' meeting, whether physical, hybrid, or
through e-voting, may continue to be mandatory in order to preserve
transparency and stakeholder participation in the merger process.

         However, the Committee are of the considered view that the reduction of
the approval threshold from 90% to 75%, taken together with the built-in
safeguard of publication of the scheme for stakeholder comment, is not, by
itself, a sufficient answer to the concerns raised regarding minority
shareholder protection. Therefore, the Committee recommend that a statutory
exit right for dissenting/non-voting shareholders may be provided explicitly
safeguarding minority shareholders' ability to object, particularly where
foreign institutional investors and promoters may have a different investment
horizon than small shareholders.

         Accordingly, the Committee recommend that the Ministry, within the Act
itself may provide a clear and enforceable mechanism such as a fair-value exit
or buyout option for shareholders who dissent from a fast-track merger or
amalgamation, so that the interests of minority shareholders, including retail
and non-institutional shareholders, are not subordinated to the interests of
majority or institutional shareholders. The Committee therefore, recommend
that under Section 233(1) after (b) the following provision may be inserted:

                 "Provided that a fair-value exit or buyout option for shareholders
        who dissent from a fast-track merger or amalgamation may be provided
        in such manner as may be prescribed:"

69.6.3  As regards, the Creditor approval threshold change wherein the

existing "nine-tenths" (90%) threshold for creditor approval is reduced to "at
least three-fourths" (75%), The Committee are of the view that the amendment
be suitably worded to require approval by creditors representing the stipulated

majority in value who are present and voting at the meeting, in the same

manner as is already provided for members under clause (b) of the amended

sub-section. This will remove ambiguity as to whether the prescribed majority

is to be computed with reference to the entire body of creditors or only those

actually present and voting, and will bring parity of drafting between the

shareholder-approval and creditor-approval limbs of Section 233.

        547
The Committee endorse the alignment of the method of computing creditor
approval under Section 233 with that under Section 230, as already accepted
by the Ministry, and recommend that this be explicitly reflected in the final text
of the Bill. The Committee recommend that Section 233(1)(d), as proposed to
be amended as follows:-

        "(ii) for clause (d), the following clause shall be substituted, namely:--

        "(d) the scheme is approved by majority of persons representing three-
        fourths in value of the creditors, or class of creditors, as the case may
        be, voting in person or by proxy or by postal ballot in a meeting
        convened by respective companies by giving a notice of twenty-one
        days along with the scheme to its creditors for the purpose.;"

69.6.4      The Committee are in agreement with the underlying objective of

reducing procedural delay in mergers, particularly given the evidence placed

before them that mergers routed through NCLT presently take up to a year,

against 60 days under the fast-track route. The Committee, therefore,

recommend that a definite timeline be prescribed for disposal of applications

under Section 233, either by amendment to Section 233 or the Rules made

thereunder, to explicitly provide that the Registrar of Companies / Centre for

Processing Accelerated Corporate Exit C-PACE shall decide an application

under this section within sixty (60) days of its filing, and also that the reasons

be recorded in writing where the application is not disposed of within this

period, failing which, the application shall be deemed to have been approved.

This will bring certainty and time-bound processing to the fast-track merger

route, consistent with the Bill's broader objective of ease of doing business,

while preserving accountability through the requirement to record reasons for

any delay.

            548
                                               CLAUSE - 70

70 Clause 70 of the Bill seeks to insert a new Section 233A in the
Companies Act 2013 regarding Treatment of certain shares held in the name of
a company or trust.

70.1 Provision proposed in The Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

         After section 233 of the principal Act, the following section shall be inserted,
namely:-- "233A.

         (1) Where a transferee company, as a result of a compromise or an
arrangement which has taken place prior to the commencement of the Companies
Act, 2013, has held any shares in its own name or in the name of any trust (whether
on its behalf or on behalf of any of its subsidiary or associate companies), such
shares shall, within a period not exceeding three years from the date of
commencement of the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Act, 2026, be dealt with or
disposed of in such manner, as may be prescribed.

         (2) Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, if a company fails to deal
with or dispose of the shares referred to in sub-section (1), such shares shall be
cancelled and extinguished by the company in such manner, as may be prescribed,
and such cancellation and extinguishment shall be deemed to be a reduction of the
share capital of the company.

         (3) If the company fails to comply with the provisions of sub-section (2), the
company and every officer of the company who is in default, shall be liable to a
penalty of ten thousand rupees for every day during which the default continues.".

70.2 Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (The Companies Act, 2013):

         This is a new Section proposed to be inserted in the Act.

70.3 Reasons / Justification given by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs for the
proposed provision:

         "The amendment seeks to insert a new section 233A to provide a framework
for treatment of treasury shares arising from past compromises or arrangements,

                                                      549
including their disposal within a prescribed period or cancellation and
extinguishment, along with a penalty for non-compliance."

70.4 Important Views/Suggestions given by Experts/Stakeholders:

         Few of the suggestions given by stakeholders, while seeking to bring in
amendments to the provisions of the Act are as follows:

70.4.1  A request was made that a proportionate remedy be adopted, e.g.,

shares cease to carry voting/dividend rights until divested, instead of cancellation. It

was further suggested that the requirement be limited to listed and large public

companies, and that the appropriate authority be given the power to extend the

three-year period, not exceeding such further period as the Committee thinks fit.

70.4.2  A suggestion was received to consider alternatives to mandatory

cancellation, such as suspension of voting and dividend rights until compliance, to

provide a longer transition period beyond three years, and to limit the requirement to

listed companies and large public companies.

70.4.3  One stakeholder, in support of the provision, recommended (i) an

express provision that no voting rights shall be exercised, and no dividend received,

in respect of such shares during the disposal window; and (ii) that the prescribed

manner of disposal for listed companies require sale through the stock-exchange

mechanism in tranches, so as to minimise price impact. It was submitted that the

voting/dividend freeze prevents the three-year window from becoming a period of

entrenched management voting through trust-held shares, and that a market-

mechanism disposal rule protects public shareholders.

70.4.4  One of the suggestions received stated that the proposed Section 233A

expressly clarify whether shares held by a trust prior to the commencement of the

Companies Act, 2013 are intended to be covered within the scope of the provision.

Further, detailed rules may be prescribed specifying the procedure, timelines,

documentation requirements, and consequential regulatory approvals for disposal,

        550
cancellation or extinguishment of such shares, particularly in the case of listed
companies.

70.4.5   Another stakeholder suggested that the provision directly affects share

capital structure, public shareholding and depository records of listed companies,

and that system-driven processing would ensure transparent, uniform and auditable

compliance. It was suggested that the onus be expressly placed on the company to

notify the depository, within prescribed timelines, of any cancellation or

extinguishment of shares under section 233A, so that the depository may update

ISIN-level records, capital balances and beneficial-ownership records in a timely

manner.

70.4.6   A further suggestion was received to provide a three-year disposal

period for legacy cross-held shares, with exemptions for court-sanctioned or

regulator-approved cases.

70.5 Examination by the Committee:

70.5.1   While deposing before the Committee, the Ministry officials explained

that, under the Companies Act, it is prohibited for a company to be the legal owner of

its own shares. However, a gap existed from the 1956 Act (never carried into the

2013 Act), whereby, when companies merge, the resulting entity could end up

holding "own shares," either in its own name or through a trust. It was explained that

Clause 70 closes this lacuna by mandating that any such self-held shares be

cancelled, with a three-year transition period given to companies to extinguish or

regularise their position. The Ministry officials further justified the provision, stating

that this is "not a good corporate governance principle," and that such trust-held

shares can generate extra voting rights for the company itself. It was further informed

that SEBI had already moved to stop this practice for listed companies from 2021.

70.5.2   As regards the suggestions relating to alternatives to mandatory

cancellation, the Ministry replied that these shares are viewed as undesirable from

                                    551
the perspective of corporate governance, since voting rights in such shares may be
used by the directors or promoters of a company to exercise control over the
company indirectly, thereby potentially thwarting the interests of minority
shareholders. It was further submitted that long-term holding of treasury stock is
opposed to the principles of shareholder democracy, and that restricting the provision
to listed and large public companies only would not be feasible.

70.5.3    In response to the suggestion regarding curtailment of voting rights

and dividends in respect of such shares during the disposal window, the Ministry

stated that the same will be considered appropriately during the framing of

subordinate legislation.

70.5.4    As regards the suggestion at paragraph 70.4.4, the Ministry stated that

the scope of coverage of trust-held shares, as well as the procedure, timelines,

documentation requirements and consequential regulatory approvals for disposal,

cancellation or extinguishment of such shares, would be appropriately addressed at

the stage of framing the Rules under the provision.

70.5.5    With regard to the suggestion regarding the requirement of further

Rules relating to prescribed timelines for notifying the depository of cancellation or

extinguishment of shares, in respect of listed companies, the Ministry stated as

follows:

         "Suggestion will be considered appropriately during framing of subordinate
         legislation. The suggestion is noted and the procedural aspects relating to
         disclosures, timelines and implementation would be appropriately considered
         at the time of framing the relevant rules."

70.6 Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

70.6.1    The Committee note that, historically, under schemes of

compromise/arrangement sanctioned prior to the commencement of the

Companies Act, 2013, some transferee companies ended up holding shares in

their own name, directly or via trusts, as part of the restructuring -- a practice
                                                      552
that effectively created a form of treasury stock, which is prohibited under
Indian company law, as shares cannot generally be held by a company in
itself. The Committee observe that this new insertion of section 233A creates a
mandatory, time-bound mechanism to deal with this legacy position.

70.6.2  The Committee find that this amendment closes a long-standing

structural anomaly in Indian company law by giving companies a definite

three-year window to regularize legacy treasury-shareholdings arising from

pre-2013-Act schemes. The Committee are of the view that the automatic,

deemed-capital-reduction consequence for non-disposal provides a self-

executing backstop, reducing reliance on case-by-case Tribunal intervention

to address non-compliant treasury holdings.

70.6.3  The Committee further observe that the uncapped, per-day

penalty for continuing non-compliance with the cancellation obligation, unlike

many other penalties in the Bill, which are capped, signals that continued

retention of treasury shares beyond the cancellation trigger is treated as a

serious, ongoing governance failure.

70.6.4  The Committee are of the view that companies, particularly older

listed and unlisted entities that underwent pre-2013 mergers or restructurings,

would benefit from conducting a shareholding audit to identify any legacy self-

held or trust-held shares, and recommend that the Rules require such

identification and planning for disposal well within the three-year window once

the provision is notified. The Committee also recognize the merit in the

suggestion that the Rules provide for restrictions on voting and dividend

rights during the disposal window, and for exchange-based sale in the case of

listed companies, an approach consistent with the Ministry's own submission

that SEBI had already acted to curb this practice for listed companies from

2021, and recommend that the Ministry give due consideration to this

suggestion while framing the Rules.

                                      553
70.6.5  During their deliberation, a concern was raised regarding the

shares bought back and extinguished, remaining unpaid/unclaimed for over 7

years, go to the Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF), but there's

currently no equivalent provision for unclaimed consideration in delisted

companies. The representatives of the Ministry confirmed that an amendment

is being brought to address the "amount in respect of shares bought back and

extinguished remaining unpaid or unclaimed" while expressly stating that this

is a distinct issue (buyback/IEPF) rather than the self-held/treasury-share

extinguishment provision. The Committee therefore recommend that the

provision in itself must remove this ambiguity which connects the

extinguishment of treasury shares to the provisions under section 66 of the

Companies Act.

70.6.6  In view of the above, the Committee recommend that Clause 70

may be amended as follows:-

        "After section 233 of the principal Act, the following section shall be
        inserted, namely:--

        "233A. (1) Where a transferee company, as a result of a compromise or
        an arrangement which has taken place prior to the commencement of
        the Companies Act, 2013, has held any shares in its own name or in the
        name of any trust (whether on its behalf or on behalf of any of its
        subsidiary or associate companies), such shares shall, within a period
        not exceeding three years from the date of commencement of the
        Corporate Laws (Amendment) Act, 2026, be dealt with or disposed of in
        such manner, as may be prescribed.

        (2) Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, if a company fails to
        deal with or dispose of the shares referred to in sub-section (1), such
        shares shall be cancelled and extinguished by the company in such
        manner, as may be prescribed, and such cancellation and
        extinguishment shall be deemed to be a reduction of the share capital of
        the company, for which the provisions of section 66 of this Act shall not
        apply.

        (3) If the company fails to comply with the provisions of sub-section (2),
        the company and every officer of the company who is in default, shall be

                                                     554
liable to a penalty of ten thousand rupees for every day during which the
default continues."

                                             555
                                              CLAUSE - 70A

70A New insertion of provisions in the Bill with regard to Section 240 of the
         Companies Act regarding Liability of officers in respect of offences
         committed prior to merger, amalgamation, etc

70A.1 Examination by the Committee:

70A.1.1 While deliberating on the issues related to decriminalization of
offences, the Committee note that no amendments or clarity was provided in the Bill
regarding the treatment of existing criminal proceedings pending against the officers
in default of the transferor company.

70A.2 Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

70A.2.1 The Committee note that the current provisions of the Section 240
ensures that an officer-in-default of a transferor company cannot escape
liability for offences committed before a merger/amalgamation/acquisition
simply because the merger took place -- the officer's personal liability
survives the corporate restructuring.

70A.2.2 The Committee further note that the existing provision is silent on
what happens to the transferor company's own pending legal proceedings.
Since the transferor company ceases to exist upon merger, it's ambiguous
whether ongoing prosecutions/proceedings that were initiated against the
company itself (as opposed to against individual officers) can continue -- and
if so, against whom.

70A.2.3 The Committee feel that addressing the treatment of ongoing
prosecutions/proceedings initiated against the company itself, is of vital
importance. Therefore, the Committee recommend that the following provision
may be suitably incorporated in the Bill:

                                                      556
"In section 240 of the principal Act,-
     (a) in the marginal heading, -
     (i) the word "of officers" shall be omitted;
     (ii) after the word "offences", the word "default" shall be inserted;
     (b) for the words "the liability in respect of offences committed

  under this Act by the officers in default, of the transferor company
  prior to its merger, amalgamation or acquisition shall continue", the
  following words, brackets, letters and figures

     "(i) the liability of the officers in default of the transferor company in
  respect of offences and default committed under this Act prior to its
  merger, amalgamation or acquisition shall continue; and

     (ii) the proceedings in respect of offences and default committed
  under this Act prior to its merger, amalgamation or acquisition against
  the transferor company, shall be continued against the transferee
  company," shall be substituted"

                                             557
                                                  CLAUSE - 71

71. Clause 71 of the Bill seeks to amend Section 242 of the Companies Act
2013 regarding Powers of Tribunal.

71.1 Provision proposed in The Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

                  In section 242 of the principal Act, sub-section (8) shall be omitted.

71.2 Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (The Companies Act, 2013):

242. (1) * * * * * * * * * *.* * * * * *.* * * * * * * * * * *.* * * * * *.* * * * * * *

         (8) If a company contravenes the provisions of sub-section (5), the company
shall be punishable with fine which shall not be less than one lakh rupees but which
may extend to twenty-five lakh rupees and every officer of the company who is in
default shall be punishable with fine which shall not be less than twenty-five
thousand rupees but which may extend to one lakh rupees.

         * * * * *.* * * * * *.* * * * * *.* * * * * *.* * * * * *.* * * * * *.* * * * * *.*

71.3 Reasons / Justification given by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs for the
proposed provision:

"The amendment omits sub-section (8) of section 242, thereby removing the existing
offence and penalty provision for contravention. The amendment is part of the
broader decriminalisation exercise under the Bill."

71.4 Important Views/Suggestions given by Experts/Stakeholders:

         Few of the suggestions given by stakeholders, while seeking to bring in
amendments to the provision are as follows:

71.4.1  One of the stakeholders suggested insertion of the following in Section

242 "(8) Any wilful non-compliance with an order made under sub-section (5) shall

        558
be liable to such civil penalties and enforcement proceedings as may be prescribed,
and the Tribunal shall have power to issue consequential directions, including
attachment of assets, appointment of an administrator, or any other order necessary
for securing compliance." The justification given for the same was that this
Approach preserves the effectiveness and authority of the adjudicatory process while
remaining consistent with contemporary corporate law reforms favouring civil over
criminal sanctions."

71.4.2  Another suggestion received stated that the original Section 242(8)

should be retained as the Tribunals should continue to retain the authority to

penalize the companies in cases of noncompliance.

71.5 Examination by the Committee:

         In response to suggestion given by the stakeholder, the Ministry of Corporate
Affairs, in their written replies, have submitted as under :

71.5.1  The amendment to Section 242 proposes the omission of sub section

(8) which relates to initiating criminal proceedings against officers of companies

which are in contravention of orders passed by the NCLT under Section 242(5). The

omission of section 242(8) is intended to decriminalize non-compliance with Tribunal

orders. Existing mechanisms for execution and enforcement of Tribunal orders are

available under the Companies Act and the applicable procedural law. It is therefore

not considered necessary to introduce a new civil penalty regime or confer additional

enforcement powers under section 242.

71.5.2  Further, the Ministry reiterated its stand stating that the Tribunals

already have powers under section 425(Contempt power) of the Companies Act,

2013. It is omitted to enable NCLT to use contempt powers to deal with non-

compliance. Hence, the provision in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026

may be retained without any change."

                                       559
71.6 Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

71.6.1 The Committee note that Clause 71 omits sub-section (8) of section 242,
thereby removing the existing criminal fine provision for contravention of
Tribunal orders passed under sub-section (5), as part of the Bill's broader
decriminalisation exercise.

71.6.2 The Committee note the suggestion that a new civil penalty and
enforcement framework be introduced in place of the omitted provision, and
the countervailing suggestion that section 242(8) be retained so that Tribunals
continue to have the power to penalise non-compliant companies. The
Committee observe that neither suggestion has been accepted by the Ministry,
since existing mechanisms for execution and enforcement of Tribunal orders,
including the Tribunal's contempt powers under section 425 of the Companies
Act, 2013, are considered adequate, obviating the need either for a new civil
penalty regime or for retention of the criminal provision being omitted.

71.6.3 The Committee find that the Ministry's reliance on the Tribunal's existing
contempt powers under section 425 is a reasonable basis for the omission,
and are satisfied that the decriminalisation of section 242(8) does not leave a
gap in the enforcement of Tribunal orders.

71.6.4 The Committee, therefore, accept Clause 71 as proposed, without any
modification.

                                               CLAUSE - 72

72. Clause 72 of the Bill seeks to amend Section 245 of the Companies Act
2013 regarding Class Action.

72.1 Provision proposed in The Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

                  In section 245 of the principal Act, in sub-section (1), for the word,
brackets and figure "sub-section (2)", the word, brackets and figure "sub-section (3)"
shall be substituted.

72.2 Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (The Companies Act, 2013):

245. (1) Such number of member or members, depositor or depositors or any class
of them, as the case may be, as are indicated in sub-section (2) may, if they are of
the opinion that the management or conduct of the affairs of the company are being
conducted in a manner prejudicial to the interests of the company or its members or
depositors, file an application before the Tribunal on behalf of the members or
depositors for seeking all or any of the following orders, namely:--

         (a) to restrain the company from committing an act which is ultra vires the
articles or memorandum of the company;

         (b) to restrain the company from committing breach of any provision of the
company's memorandum or articles;

         (c) to declare a resolution altering the memorandum or articles of the
company as void if the resolution was passed by suppression of material facts or
obtained by mis-statement to the members or depositors;

         (d) to restrain the company and its directors from acting on such resolution;

         (e) to restrain the company from doing an act which is contrary to the
provisions of this Act or any other law for the time being in force;

         (f) to restrain the company from taking action contrary to any resolution
passed by the members;

         (g) to claim damages or compensation or demand any other suitable action
from or against--

                                                      561
                  (i) the company or its directors for any fraudulent, unlawful or wrongful
          act or omission or conduct or any likely act or omission or conduct on its or
          their part;

                  (ii) the auditor including audit firm of the company for any improper or
          misleading statement of particulars made in his audit report or for any
          fraudulent, unlawful or wrongful act or conduct; or

                  (iii) any expert or advisor or consultant or any other person for any
          incorrect or misleading statement made to the company or for any fraudulent,
          unlawful or wrongful act or conduct or any likely act or conduct on his part;

         (h) to seek any other remedy as the Tribunal may deem fit.

72.3 Reasons / Justification given by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs for the
         proposed provision:

"Drafting change in section 245(1) is being made to make cross-reference to "sub-
section (3)" instead of "sub-section (2)" presently appearing."

72.4 Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

72.4.1 The Committee note that Clause 72 makes a cross-reference correction
to section 245(1), substituting the reference to "sub-section (2)" with "sub-
section (3)". The Committee observe that the requisite number of members or
depositors entitled to file a class action application under sub-section (1) is, in
fact, prescribed in sub-section (3) of section 245, whereas sub-section (2)
deals with the liability of an audit firm and its partners in respect of damages
or compensation claimed against them. The Committee find that the existing
cross-reference in sub-section (1) is, therefore, misdirected, and that Clause 72
corrects this error so as to ensure that sub-section (1) accurately refers to the
sub-section actually prescribing the threshold numbers.

72.4.2 The Committee find that this is a purely technical, drafting-correction
amendment with no independent substantive policy effect.

                                                      562
72.4.3 The Committee, therefore, accept Clause 72 as proposed, without any
modification.

73.3. Reasons/Justification given by the Ministry for the proposed provisions:

The proposed amendments to Section 247 seek to strengthen the statutory
framework governing valuation and enhance the powers of the Valuation Authority
through the following measures:

73.3.1.  Formally recognising the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India

(IBBI) as the Valuation Authority, and clarifying its powers regarding the registration

of valuers and recognition of valuers' organisations.

73.3.2.  Introducing a comprehensive enforcement and regulatory framework

governing valuers and valuers' organisations, including powers for suspension,

cancellation, imposition of penalties, penal provisions, and mechanisms for appeal.

73.3.3.  Aligning contravention consequences with the newly introduced penalty

framework, while conferring additional powers on the Valuation Authority--including

recommending valuation standards, adhering to policy directions of the Central

Government, and delegating its functions.

73.3.4.  Empowering the Valuation Authority to frame regulations for effectively

discharging its functions, subject to parliamentary oversight.

73.4. Important Views/Suggestions given by Experts/Stakeholders:

Following are some of the important suggestions received from various stakeholders:

Institutional Framework & Governance

73.4.1.  Establish the Valuation Authority as an independent, distinct statutory

body (or a self-regulatory framework) rather than bolting it onto IBBI, to prevent

potential conflicts of interest with insolvency professionals.

                     570
73.4.2.     Mandate that all valuations of corporate entities (Companies, LLPs)

across all laws be conducted exclusively by IBBI-registered valuers to ensure a

uniform regulatory framework.

73.4.3.     Expressly empower IBBI, as the Valuation Authority, with exclusive

regulation-making powers to regulate Registered Valuer Organisations (RVOs),

enforce governance/board independence norms, notify valuation standards, and levy

registration/inspection fees.

Scope, Definitions & Asset Class Jurisdictions

73.4.4.     Explicitly exclude agricultural land, immovable property, and assets

governed under the Wealth Tax Act, 1957, Income Tax Act, and SARFAESI Act from

the scope of Section 247, preserving the jurisdiction of Wealth Tax Act registered

valuers.

73.4.5.     Exclude "net worth" certification from Section 247, as Chartered

Accountants are specifically qualified to certify net worth under the Act.

73.4.6.     Restrict valuer registration under Section 247 and membership of

RVOs strictly to natural persons.

Inter-Regulatory Harmonization & Valuation Standards

73.4.7.     Recognize SEBI-empanelled valuers/merchant bankers for actions

under SEBI regulations (including Mutual Funds and AIFs) to avoid duplicative

registration, calibrate liability for early-stage startup equity, and mandate distinct

valuation standards for financial instruments developed in consultation with SEBI and

RBI. (Consolidates 73.4.20, 73.4.21, 73.4.22, 73.4.28, 73.4.30(ii))

73.4.8.     Retain and formally recognize well-established ICAI Valuation

Standards.

Disciplinary, Appeals & Enforcement Framework

73.4.9.     Define clear and practical limits for what constitutes "direct or indirect

interest" (under the 3-year pre- and post-valuation restriction) to prevent

unnecessary disqualification of valuers.

                                          571
73.4.10. Empower the Valuation Authority to recommend, monitor, and enforce
compliance with valuation standards for the IBC, 2016 and Companies Act, 2013.

73.4.11. Calibrate penalty provisions under Section 247(3A) and provide
flexibility to reduce or waive the minimum six-month suspension period for minor
contraventions; and delete Section 247(3E).

73.4.12. Establish an independent Appellate Tribunal (headed by MCA Joint
Secretary-level officers) to hear appeals within 45 days against orders of the
Valuation Authority or RVOs, ensuring strict due process (21-day notice period and
30-day decision timeline).

73.4.13. Provide a statutory mechanism allowing any person to file complaints
regarding contraventions with the Valuation Authority, subject to a mandatory 90-day
disposal timeline.

73.4.14. Mandate an electronic system for the compulsory generation and
verification of a unique Valuation Report Identification Number (VRIN) for every
valuation report.

Transitional & Grandfathering Framework

73.4.15. Introduce a comprehensive transitional/grandfathering framework
deeming existing valuers registered under the Wealth Tax Act, 1957 (Section 34AB)
and valuers/RVOs recognized under the Companies (Registered Valuers and
Valuation) Rules, 2017 to be registered under the new regime for a period of not less
than two years without requiring fresh qualifications or unconscionable fees.

73.5. Examination by the Committee:

The replies and clarifications provided by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs in
response to the stakeholder suggestions (detailed in paragraph 73.4) are set out
below, with explicit references to the corresponding stakeholder suggestions:

Institutional Framework & Governance

73.5.1. Distinct Statutory Body & Self-Regulatory Framework (Refer para 73.4.1)

                                                      572
In response to the suggestion advocating for a separate, independent Valuation
Authority or a self-regulatory structure rather than designating IBBI mentioned, the
Ministry submitted:

"The proposed amendment provides a comprehensive statutory framework by
designating the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India as the Valuation Authority
and specifying its powers, functions, appellate mechanism, regulatory framework,
policy oversight by the Central Government and parliamentary scrutiny of
regulations. In view of this, constitution of a separate statutory body is not considered
necessary. Hence, the provision in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 may
be retained without any change."

"The new regulatory framework has been designed to strengthen and recognise the
powers of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India as the Valuation Authority
and clarifying its powers with respect to recognition of valuers organization and
registration of valuers. Hence, the provision in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill,
2026 may be retained without any change."

73.5.2. Exclusive Mandate for Corporate Valuations (Refer para 73.4.2)

Regarding the suggestion to mandate that all corporate valuations across statutes be
conducted exclusively by IBBI-registered valuers, the Ministry stated:

"Section 247 per se is meant for valuation under the Companies Act, 2013. Other
regulators may use such provision by making amendments in their respective
Laws/Regulations."

73.5.3. Regulation-Making Powers over RVOs and Fee Levying (Refer para
73.4.3)

Addressing the suggestion regarding IBBI's powers over Registered Valuer
Organisations (RVOs) and the levying of fees, the Ministry submitted:

"The proposed amendment has also authorised IBBI in respect of RVOs, as IBBI will
make regulations to grant them certificate of recognition. IBBI is also empowered to
take disciplinary action as well as take criminal action against RVOs."

"The IBBI has incidental regulation making power, which is used for carrying out the
provisions of section 247. This provision may be used for levying appropriate fees."

                                                      573
Scope, Definitions & Asset Class Jurisdictions

73.5.4.  Exclusion of Property Types & Exclusive Jurisdiction (Wealth Tax /

Income Tax Acts) (Refer para 73.4.4)

Responding to proposals to exclude specific property types (e.g., agricultural land) or
grant exclusive jurisdiction to the Wealth Tax/Income Tax regimes, the Ministry
stated:

"Exclusion of any property from term "property" will would fragment this framework
and create uncertainty."

"Suggestions pertain the valuation of assets defined under statutes other than the
Companies Act, 2013 which are governed by respective statutes. Declaring or
clarifying exclusive jurisdiction for valuation under other statutes is beyond purview of
the Companies Act, 2013."

73.5.5.  Exclusion of 'Net Worth' from Section 247 (Refer para 73.4.5)

Regarding the suggestion to exclude net worth calculations from Section 247 and
reserve them for CAs, the Ministry clarified:

"The legislation keeps the pool of eligible professionals wide and to bring all
valuation related determinations under a single regulated framework. Carving out net
worth would fragment this framework and create uncertainty where multiple
provisions of the Act are engaged in the same transaction. A Chartered Accountant
who is also a registered valuer remains fully eligible to perform net worth valuations.
Hence, the provision in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 may be retained
without any change."

73.5.6.  Natural Persons vs. Entities (Refer para 73.4.6)

On restricting valuer registrations solely to natural persons, the Ministry clarified:

"As entities are also registered as Valuers. IBBI allows entities to be registered as
Valuers."

Inter-Regulatory Harmonization & Valuation Standards
                                                      574
73.5.7.  Recognition of SEBI Registered Valuers & Subordinate Legislation

Alignment (Refer para 73.4.7)

In response to calls for aligning with SEBI, RBI, FEMA, and tax statutes, the Ministry
submitted:

"The provisions of section 247 are applicable in respect of valuation required under
the Companies Act, 2013 only. The other Sectoral Regulators have mandated
valuation by a person registered under section 247 by way of regulations and any
modification may be made in relevant Regulations by such regulators, if required
after enactment of Corporate Laws Amendment Act."

"Suggestion will be considered appropriately during framing of subordinate
legislation. The suggestion regarding alignment with other regulators and statutes
may be considered at the rule/regulation making stage."

73.5.8.  Recognition of ICAI Valuation Standards (Refer para 73.4.8)

Regarding the explicit recognition of ICAI Valuation Standards, the Ministry stated:

"The suggestion recommends that ICAI Valuation Standards be explicitly recognised
as the applicable standards for valuation. This will have to be considered by the
Valuation Authority while making recommendations on valuation standards and
policies"

Disciplinary, Appeals & Enforcement Framework

73.5.9.  Defining 'Direct or Indirect Interest' (Refer para 73.4.9)

Addressing concerns regarding the ambiguity of "direct or indirect interest," the
Ministry clarified:

"The expression "directly or indirectly" is not stemming from the Amendment Bill. It is
mentioned in Section 247(2)(d) of the Companies Act, 2013. The term is well
established in the Companies Act and has a settled meaning in Indian company law.
It appears across multiple provisions of the Act, including Section 89 (beneficial
interest in shares), Section 90 (significant beneficial ownership), Section 149
(independent director eligibility), Section 184 (disclosure of director interest), and
Section 185 (loans to directors). "Directly or indirectly" is used in the Companies Act,

                                                      575
2013 to ensure that legal obligations and prohibitions cannot be circumvented by
routing actions, ownership, or control through an alternative connection."

73.5.10. Defining Scope & Jurisdiction of IBBI (Refer para 73.4.10)

On defining and restricting IBBI's valuation jurisdiction:

"The provisions of section 247 are applicable in respect of valuation required under
the Companies Act, 2013 only. The present provisions are adequate and may be
retained without any change on this aspect."

73.5.11. Suspension and Penalty Severity & Deletion of Section 247(3E)
(Refer para 73.4.11)

Regarding concerns over the mandatory minimum six-month suspension, penalty
caps, and the proposed Section 247(3E), the Ministry noted:

"The proposed section provides for suspension of certificate for minimum period of
six months or such higher period not exceeding ten years in such manner to be
specified by regulations made by Valuation Authority. Further, INR 10 lakhs is the
upper limit up to which penalty can be imposed. The nature of action, will depend on
the facts and circumstances of each case."

"Section 439(2) of the Companies Act, 2013 already restricts cognizance of offences
under the Act generally to complaints by the Registrar, a shareholder/member, or a
person authorised by the Central Government. This proposed provision simply
extends the same architecture to the new Valuation Authority regime being created. It
only ensures the trigger for prosecution is a considered regulatory/governmental
decision rather than a private party's unilateral complaint."

73.5.12. Dedicated Appellate Tribunal (Refer para 73.4.12)

Responding to suggestions for a dedicated Appellate Tribunal headed by Ministry
officials, the Ministry stated:

"The provisions of section 247 are applicable in respect of valuation required under
the Companies Act, 2013 only. Thus, it is appropriate to designate NCLAT as an
Appellate authority against orders of IBBI as Valuation Authority."

                                                      576
73.5.13.  Complaint Mechanism & Disciplinary Governance (Refer para
73.4.13)

Addressing suggestions regarding statutory complaint mechanisms, conflict
disclosures, and governance of RVOs, the Ministry noted:

"IBBI is established under section 188 of the IBC, 2016 and shall be the Valuation
Authority for the purpose of Section 247 of the Companies Act, 2013 and Section
33A of the LLP Act... a statutory regulator must function as an objective, independent
supervisor and the provisions related to disclosure of conflict, review, etc. would be
regulated by the parent statute."

73.5.14. Valuation Report Identification Number (VRIN) (Refer para 73.4.14)

While accommodating the suggestion to mandate a VRIN for every valuation report,
the Ministry submitted that:

"...the suggestion would be considered while framing of regulations by Valuation
Authority."

Transitional & Grandfathering Framework

73.5.15.  Automatic Recognition & Transitional Framework (Refer para
73.4.15)

Regarding automatic recognition of Wealth Tax valuers and grandfathering provisions
for existing valuers/RVOs, the Ministry submitted:

"Section 247 per se is meant for valuation under the Companies Act, 2013. Other
regulators may use such provision by making amendments in their respective
Laws/Regulations."

"(i) Transitional provisions are not considered necessary as existing valuers and
RVOs are already recognised.

(ii) Recognition under different regulatory regime is not under the ambit of
Companies Act,13.

                                                      577
(iii) Minimum 6 months suspension is considered reasonable."

As regards transitional provisions, the Ministry maintained that "the same will be
considered through Rules as the actions taken by valuers under extant Rules are
legally valid."

73.6. Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

73.6.1.  The Committee note that Clause 73 of the Bill seeks to amend

Section 247 of the Companies Act, 2013 to strengthen the statutory framework

governing valuation and enhance the powers of the Valuation Authority.

In this context, the Committee note the reply provided by the Ministry of
Corporate Affairs regarding the suggestion to explicitly empower the
Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) to levy, collect, and revise
fees or charges from Registered Valuers for registration, inspection, and
administrative processes.

The Committee observe that as the IBBI possesses incidental regulation-
making powers under the proposed provisions of Section 247, the same may
be effectively utilized for levying appropriate fees and charges.

The Committee are, therefore, of the view that the proposed amendment
contains sufficient administrative provisions for IBBI and accordingly accept
the justification provided by the Ministry.

73.6.2.  Regarding stakeholder suggestions on the central tracking of

valuation reports, the Committee observe that the mandatory generation of a

Valuation Report Identification Number (VRIN) is essential to enhance

authenticity, traceability, and prevent misuse.

         578
In pursuance of the Committee's observation, the Ministry of Corporate Affairs
has agreed to explicitly mandate the provision for VRIN generation at the time
of framing regulations by the Valuation Authority.

The Committee further stress that this subordinate legislative framework
should be formulated in a timely, transparent, and consultative manner with
relevant stakeholders to ensure policy coherence and seamless
implementation.

73.6.3.  The Committee also note and accept the detailed justification

provided by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs on various structural and policy

suggestions raised by stakeholders regarding the governance of valuers:

(i) Designation of IBBI as the Valuation Authority: The Committee note that
designating the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) leverages an
established statutory regulator with existing administrative infrastructure,
thereby preventing institutional duplication and avoiding the need to
constitute a separate statutory body.

(ii) Designation of NCLAT as Appellate Forum: The Committee accept that
since Section 247 specifically governs valuations required under the
Companies Act, 2013, the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) is
the appropriate specialized judicial body to hear appeals against orders of the
Valuation Authority, making a separate appellate tribunal unnecessary.

(iii) Adoption of Valuation Standards: The Committee note that framing
valuation standards and policies (including consideration of ICAI standards) is
properly within the purview of the Valuation Authority to recommend to the
Central Government via Rules/Regulations, rather than embedding specific
institutional standards rigidly into primary legislation.

         579
(iv) Recognition of Valuers under Other Enactments (SEBI Act, Wealth Tax
Act, etc.): The Committee accept that Section 247 is meant strictly for
valuations under the Companies Act, 2013, and that other sectoral regulators
(such as SEBI or RBI) or revenue authorities may align their respective rules or
regulations to recognize IBBI-registered valuers as deemed fit by them.

The Committee observe that the regulatory and institutional architecture
proposed under Clause 73 is balanced, cohesive, and adequate. The
Committee, therefore, recommend that the provisions as proposed in the Bill
as introduced regarding these matters suffice and do not necessitate further
change.

73.6.4.    Furthermore, the Committee observe that prior consultation with

stakeholders is critical to ensuring objectivity, predictability, and transparency

in the valuation regulatory process. The Committee, therefore, recommend that

after sub-section 9 of Section 247, the following new sub-section 9A shall be

inserted:

"(9A) The Valuation Authority shall, prior to making regulations under
sub-section (9),--

         (a) ensure transparency by publishing the draft regulations along
with all relevant details on its website and inviting public comments for
such period as may be specified therein; and

         (b) review such regulations at least once in three years:

         Provided that if the Valuation Authority is of the opinion that it is
necessary or expedient to make, or amend, any regulations urgently in
public interest, or where the subject matter of the regulations relates
solely to the internal functioning of the Valuation Authority, it may, for
reasons to be recorded in writing, make or amend such regulations
without following the procedure specified in clause (a)."

           580
73.6.5.  Subject to incorporation of the above amendments, the

Committee accept Clause 73 of the Bill.

                                               CLAUSE - 74

74. Clause 74 of the Bill proposes to amend Section 248 of the Companies
Act, 2013

74.1. Provision proposed in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

In section 248 of the principal Act,--

         (a) in sub-section (1),--

                  (i) in clause (c),--

                           (A) after the words "preceding financial years", the words
                           "and in the current financial year, or has not made any significant
                           accounting transaction during the preceding two financial years
                           and in the current financial year, or has not filed financial
                           statements or annual returns that were due to be filed for two
                           consecutive financial years preceding the previous financial
                           year" shall be inserted;

                           (B) after the words and figures "section 455; or", the following
                           shall be inserted, namely:--

                           `Illustration. Where, during examination in the month of June,
                           2025, it was found that a company had not filed the financial
                           statements, or had not filed the annual returns, for the financial
                           years 2022-23 and 2023-24, then a company would be covered
                           under this clause. Explanation.--For the purposes of this
                           clause, the expression "significant accounting transaction" shall
                           have the meaning assigned to it in clause (ii) of the Explanation
                           to sub-section (1) of section 455.';

         (b) in sub-section (2),--

                  (i) after the words "extinguishing all its liabilities", the words "in
                  such manner as may be prescribed," shall be inserted;

                                                      582
      (ii) the words, brackets and figure "on all or any of the grounds
      specified in sub-section (1)" shall be omitted;

   (c) in sub-section (5),--

         (i) after the words "mentioned in the notice", the words,
         brackets and figure "published under sub-section (4)" shall be
         inserted;

         (ii) after the words "is shown by the company", the words "or
         by any other person" shall be inserted;

   (d) in sub-section (6),--

      (i) for the words "before passing an order", the words "before
      striking off the name of the company" shall be substituted;

      (ii) in the proviso, for the words "date of the order removing the
      name", the words "date of striking off the name" shall be substituted.

74.2. Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (Companies Act, 2013):

248. (1) Where the Registrar has reasonable cause to believe that--

*  *  *  *  *                 *  *  *  *  *  *                        *  *

   (c) a company is not carrying on any business or operation for a period of two
   immediately preceding financial years and has not made any application
   within such period for obtaining the status of a dormant company under
   section 455; or

*  *  *  *  *                 *  *  *  *  *  *                        *  *

(2) Without prejudice to the provisions of sub-section (1), a company may, after
extinguishing all its liabilities, by a special resolution or consent of seventy-five per
cent. members in terms of paid-up share capital, file an application in the prescribed
manner to the Registrar for removing the name of the company from the register of

                                                      583
companies on all or any of the grounds specified in sub-section (1) and the Registrar
shall, on receipt of such application, cause a public notice to be issued in the
prescribed manner: Provided that in the case of a company regulated under a
special Act, approval of the regulatory body constituted or established under that Act
shall also be obtained and enclosed with the application.

*  *  *  *  *  *  *    *  *  *  *  *  *

(5) At the expiry of the time mentioned in the notice, the Registrar may, unless
cause to the contrary is shown by the company, strike off its name from the register
of companies, and shall publish notice thereof in the Official Gazette, and on the

(6) The Registrar, before passing an order under sub-section (5), shall satisfy
himself that sufficient provision has been made for the realisation of all amount due
