management of the company:

Provided that notwithstanding the undertakings referred to in this sub-section, the
assets of the company shall be made available for the payment or discharge of all its
liabilities and obligations even after the date of the order removing the name of the
company from the register of companies.

*  *  *  *  *  *  *    *  *  *  *  *  *

74.3. Reasons/Justification given by the Ministry for the proposed provisions:

"The amendment has been proposed to expand and clarify the conditions under
which a company may be considered inactive, including non-filing of financial
statements or annual returns and absence of significant accounting transactions in
the relevant period, along with insertion of an illustration and explanation for clarity. It
is also proposed to rationalise the framework for exit by modifying the existing pre-
conditions, thereby enabling faster and easier exit of companies."

                  584
74.4. Important Views/Suggestions given by Experts/Stakeholders:

Following are some of the important suggestions received from various stakeholders
during the deliberations of the Committee:

74.4.1.  "It is suggested that following proviso may be added: Provided that a

company shall not be deemed to be not carrying on any business or operation solely

for the reason that it has not made any significant accounting transaction during the

preceding two financial years and in the current financial year, where such non-

occurrence of transactions is attributable to the nature of its business, project

gestation period, or other bona fide commercial reasons, as specified by its Board of

Directors in the manner as may be prescribed."

74.4.2.  "The strike-off and restoration mechanism requires simplification."

74.4.3.  "Restoration applications should be processed through a streamlined

MCA portal-based mechanism with minimal tribunal or manual intervention."

74.4.4.  "We recommend further improvements to the strike-off process to make

it more time bound and practical. We propose that the law should establish a clear

maximum timeframe for completing a voluntary strike-off. For instance, if no

objections are received after the RoC's notice, the company's name could be struck

off within 30 days of the application. This would allow defunct companies to exit the

registry swiftly when no stakeholders or authorities have any objections."

74.4.5.  "Likewise, currently an otherwise solvent company with residual cash is

effectively forced into a costlier court-supervised liquidation simply to distribute that

surplus, since a strike-off applicant cannot have any assets on its books. This

undermines the "easy exit" objective of Section 248. By allowing a controlled return

of surplus funds to shareholders during the strike-off process, many companies could

avoid the need for an IBC liquidation and its associated time and expense. This

proposal would reduce the burden on NCLT resources, encourage more companies

to formally wind up defunct entities through the administrative strike off route, and

ultimately contribute to a more efficient regulatory environment by removing dormant

companies from the registry in a timely manner."

74.4.6.  "To facilitate the orderly exit of inactive small companies and reduce

compliance costs, a simplified and fast track strike-off mechanism may be introduced

under the Companies Act, 2013 for small companies. The framework may provide for

simplified application forms, reduced documentation requirements, and time-bound

         585
processing of applications by the Registrar of Companies. Further, notarised
affidavits and physical indemnity bonds may be replaced with digitally signed self-
declarations to enable a fully electronic filing process and reduce procedural
burdens. Additionally, concessional filing fees may be prescribed for voluntary strike-
off applications filed by small companies and eligible start-ups."

74.4.7.  "Amend Section 248 to permit strike-off of Section 8 companies that

have ceased operations and do not possess any assets, liabilities, public donations,

grants or other public charitable funds, subject to prior approval of the Regional

Director and such safeguards as prescribed."

74.4.8.  "It is recommended that the clauses be retained, subject to the

clarification that no company shall be struck off on the new non-filing ground without

the notice under section 248(1) expressly recording that ground, and that pending

investigations, prosecutions or proceedings shall bar strike-off, as presently provided

in the rules, elevated into the section."

74.5. Examination by the Committee:

Response of the Ministry of Corporate Affairs to the corresponding suggestions in
para 74.4 are as follows:

74.5.1.  Regarding the suggestion at para no. 74.4.1 to insert a proviso

protecting genuine companies in the project development, incubation, or gestation

phase from inadvertent strike-off, the Ministry, while declining to accept the

suggestion, stated:

"The existing framework already provides adequate safeguards for genuine
companies that are inactive due to project development, incubation, or business
gestation. Such companies shall obtain dormant status under Section 455, which
protects them from strike-off proceedings. Further, before striking off a company, the
Registrar must issue a notice and provide an opportunity to submit representations
and supporting documents. Hence, the provision in the Corporate Laws
(Amendment) Bill, 2026 may be retained without any change."

74.5.2.  Regarding the suggestions at para nos. 74.4.2 and 74.4.3 to simplify

the strike-off and restoration mechanism through a portal-based application system,

the Ministry submitted:

                                           586
"The suggestion to include Restoration applications through a streamlined portal has
been noted, and will be considered while designing the next version of MCA21.
Hence, the provision in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 may be retained
without any change."

74.5.3.  Regarding the suggestion at para nos. 74.4.4 and 74.4.6 requesting a

time-bound and simplified framework for processing voluntary strike-off applications

for small companies, the Ministry accepted the suggestion and stated:

"Timeline for taking decision will be incorporated in the amendment. RoC, CPACE to
decide the application within 60 days, and if this time is exceeded reasons thereof
would need to be mentioned in the final order."

74.5.4.  Regarding the suggestion at para no. 74.4.5 to permit the return of

surplus cash or funds to shareholders during the strike-off process to avoid court-

supervised liquidation, the Ministry expressed its inability to accept the suggestion

and submitted:

"The suggestion proposes the inclusion of a scenario wherein companies with
surplus assets or liabilities on their books can approach the Registrar for strike-off
under Section 248 of the Companies Act, 2013. This is not accepted as any
liquidation of assets and subsequent distribution to creditors and shareholders
involves process of sale, invitation of claims, their adjudication and then distribution.
All these require separate independent office of liquidator and oversight of quasi-
judicial authority to ensure the integrity of the process. For easier liquidation and
dissolution of companies, the Act provides for summary procedure of liquidation
under Section 361. Given the two mechanisms provide for different scenarios,
intermingling the conditions to dissolve companies between the IBC and Companies
Act, 2013 may not be prudent. Hence the suggestion to include a scenario for
approaching the Registrar with surplus assets or liabilities on the books of accounts
cannot be considered."

74.5.5.  Regarding the suggestion at para no. 74.4.7 to permit the strike-off of

Section 8 companies that have ceased operations and do not possess assets,

liabilities, or public funds, the Ministry accepted the suggestion and stated:

"This amendment has also been recommended by HLC-NFRR (Report VI). It was
recommended to amend Companies Act, 2013 to omit Section 248(3) and omit Rule
3(1)(x) of the Companies (Removal of Names of Companies from the Register of

                                                      587
Companies) Rules, 2016 thereby removing prohibition on use of strike-off for Section
8 Companies. Accordingly, the amendment will be made."

74.5.6.  Regarding the suggestion at para no. 74.4.8 to elevate the existing rule

barring strike-off during pending investigations or prosecutions directly into the

section, the Ministry declined the proposal and submitted:

"Rule 3 of the Companies (Removal of Names of Companies from the Register of
Companies) Rules, 2016 provides for prohibition of companies from striking off in
case of pending investigations, prosecutions etc. This rule sufficiently provides for
the scenario envisaged in the suggestion. The same need not be elevated to the
section under the Amendment Bill. Proviso to sub-Section (6) of the Section 248 as
well as section 250 provides for availability of assets of the company for discharging
the liabilities even the company is struck off."

74.6. Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

74.6.1.  The Committee note that Clause 74 of the Bill seeks to amend

Section 248 of the Companies Act, 2013 by expanding the grounds for treating

a company as inactive--such as non-filing of financial statements and absence

of significant accounting transactions--and rationalizing exit preconditions to

facilitate faster corporate exit.

In examining stakeholder suggestions alongside the Ministry's responses, the
Committee observe the following:

i. Safeguards for Inactive Companies: The Committee accept the
     Ministry's explanation that genuine gestation-phase companies do not
     require an additional proviso under Section 248, as Section 455
     (dormant status) and mandatory pre-strike-off notices provide adequate
     protection.

ii. Distribution of Surplus Assets: The Committee concur with the Ministry
      that administrative strike-off under Section 248 cannot be extended to
      companies with surplus assets or liabilities, as liquidating assets and

                                                    588
settling claims require independent oversight under Section 361 or the
IBC.

iii. Mandatory Decision Timeline: The Committee stress that an unguided
       processing period dilutes the ease of corporate exit. In pursuance of the
       Committee's observation, the Ministry of Corporate Affairs has agreed to
       amend the proposed provision to incorporate an explicit timeline
       requiring the Registrar of Companies (RoC) and C-PACE to decide
       voluntary strike-off applications within 60 days, with recorded reasons
       in writing for any delay.

iv. Inclusion of Section 8 Companies: The Committee observe that inactive
       Section 8 entities with no public exposure should be provided an
       efficient exit mechanism. In deference to the Committee's view, the
       Ministry of Corporate Affairs has agreed to amend the clause to extend
       voluntary strike-off facility to inactive Section 8 companies having no
       assets, liabilities, or public funds, in accordance with HLC-NFRR
       recommendations.

v. Portal Integration: The Committee note the Ministry's statement that a
      streamlined, portal-based application process "will be considered while
      designing the next version of MCA21."

Accordingly, the Committee accept Clause 74 of the         Bill, subject to
incorporating the following amendments regarding the       60-day decision
timeline and the exit framework for Section 8 companies:-

"(ba) after sub-section (2), the following sub-section shall be inserted,
namely:-

         "(2A) The Registrar shall decide the application referred to in sub-
section (2) within a period of sixty days from the date of receipt of the
application complete in all respects:

                                             589
         Provided that in case the application is decided after the said
period, the reasons for such delay shall be recorded by the Registrar";

(bb) sub-section (3) shall be omitted;"

74.6.2.  The Committee further urge the Ministry to expedite the rollout of

the streamlined, portal-based application mechanism, in consultation with

stakeholders, under the next version of MCA21.

                      CLAUSE - 75

75. Clause 75 of the Bill, 2026, proposes to amend Section 249 of the
         Companies Act, 2013

75.1. Provision proposed in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

In section 249 of the principal Act, in sub-section (2), for the words "punishable with
fine which may extend to one lakh rupees", the words "liable to a penalty of fifty
thousand rupees" shall be substituted.

75.2. Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (Companies Act, 2013):

249. (1)

*  *      *  *  *  *  *    *       *  *  *                            *  *

         (2) If a company files an application under sub-section (2) of section 248 in
violation of sub-section (1), it shall be punishable with fine which may extend to one
lakh rupees.

*  *      *  *  *  *  *    *       *  *  *                            *  *

75.3. Reasons/Justification given by the Ministry for the proposed provisions:

"The amendment replaces the existing fine with a fixed penalty of fifty thousand
rupees. It is part of the broader decriminalisation exercise under the Bill."

75.4. Important Views/Suggestions given by Experts/Stakeholders:

Stakeholders submitted that procedural defaults should attract additional or late filing
fees rather than penal consequences. They emphasized that regulatory objectives
can be effectively achieved through compliance-oriented mechanisms without
imposing punitive measures on companies.

                      591
75.5. Examination by the Committee:

Regarding the suggestion that procedural defaults should attract civil penalties or
additional fees rather than penal consequences, the Ministry, while declining to
accept the suggestion, stated the following:

"The proposed amendment to Section 249(2) of the Companies Act, 2013 states that
a company filing for removal of its name from the registry, when in contravention of
the provisions of Section 249(1) of the Companies Act, 2013 is liable for penalty of
INR 50,000 (Indian Rupees Fifty Thousand). The conditions prescribed in sub
section (1) of the Section 249 of the Act are not procedural but substantial having
bearing on striking off the company and provision of penalty is required to deter the
companies from filing an application for strike of in non-compliance of such
conditions. Hence, the provision in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 may
be retained without any change."

75.6. Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

The Committee note that Clause 75 of the Bill seeks to amend Section 249(2) of
the Companies Act, 2013 by replacing the existing criminal fine of up to one
lakh rupees with a fixed civil penalty of fifty thousand rupees, in line with the
overall objective of decriminalizing minor corporate offenses.

Addressing the stakeholder suggestion to replace penalties with simple late
filing fees, the Committee accept the Ministry's explanation that the conditions
governing the removal of a company's name under Section 249(1) are
substantive rather than purely procedural. The Committee agree that
maintaining a statutory penalty is necessary to deter companies from
improperly applying for strike-off while in violation of these conditions.

Accordingly, the Committee accept Clause 75 as proposed in the Bill.

                                                      592
                                               CLAUSE - 76

76. Clause 76 of the Bill, 2026, proposes to amend Section 252 of the
Companies Act, 2013

76.1. Provision proposed in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

In section 252 of the principal Act,--

(a) in the marginal heading, for the word "Tribunal", the words "Regional Director
or Tribunal" shall be substituted;

(b) in sub-section (1),--

         (i) for the word "Tribunal" wherever it occurs, the words "Regional
         Director" shall be substituted;

         (ii) for the words "it may order", the words "the Regional Director may
         order" shall be substituted;

(c) in sub-section (2), for the word "Tribunal", the words, brackets and figures
"Regional Director under sub-section (1) or the Tribunal under sub-section (3), as the
case may be," shall be substituted.

76.2. Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (Companies Act, 2013):

252. (1) Any person aggrieved by an order of the Registrar, notifying a company
as dissolved under section 248, may file an appeal to the Tribunal within a period of
three years from the date of the order of the Registrar and if the Tribunal is of the
opinion that the removal of the name of the company from the register of companies
is not justified in view of the absence of any of the grounds on which the order was
passed by the Registrar, it may order restoration of the name of the company in the
register of companies:

         Provided that before passing any order under this section, the Tribunal shall
give a reasonable opportunity of making representations and of being heard to the
Registrar, the company and all the persons concerned:

                                                      593
         Provided further that if the Registrar is satisfied, that the name of the company
has been struck off from the register of companies either inadvertently or on the
basis of incorrect information furnished by the company or its directors, which
requires restoration in the register of companies, he may within a period of three
years from the date of passing of the order dissolving the company under section
248, file an application before the Tribunal seeking restoration of name of such
company.

         (2) A copy of the order passed by the Tribunal shall be filed by the
company with the Registrar within thirty days from the date of the order and on
receipt of the order, the Registrar shall cause the name of the company to be
restored in the register of companies and shall issue a fresh certificate of
incorporation.

*  *  *  *  *  *  *    *  *  *  *                                 *  *

76.3. Reasons/Justification given by the Ministry for the proposed provisions:

"The amendment seeks to provide that applications for restoration of name of a
company filed within three years shall be made before the Regional Director, who
may pass an order upon satisfaction. This is intended to ensure a seamless and
time-bound process for restoration of companies and to de-burden the NCLT of such
routine matters."

76.4. Important Views/Suggestions given by Experts/Stakeholders:

Following are some of the important suggestions received from various stakeholders
during the deliberations of the Committee:

76.4.1. "The strike-off and restoration mechanism requires simplification."

76.4.2. "Restoration applications should be processed through a streamlined MCA
portal-based mechanism with minimal tribunal or manual intervention."

76.4.3. "The jurisdiction with respect to restoration under Section 252 may entirely
be vested with the Regional Director."

                  594
76.4.4. "A clarification needs to be provided in respect of the Appeals arising out of
the order of Regional Director. Expressly a forum should be specified to adjudicate
Appeal in cases where a party is aggrieved by the order of Regional Director."

76.4.5. "It is suggested to reinstate the earlier provision."

76.4.6.  "It is recommended that the clause be retained, subject to the insertion

of a provision for appeal to the Tribunal against a refusal by the Regional Director

within forty-five days, and a requirement that the Regional Director dispose of

restoration applications within sixty days by reasoned order."

76.5. Examination by the Committee:

76.5.1   Regarding the suggestions at para nos. 76.4.1 and 76.4.2 to simplify

the strike-off and restoration mechanism and introduce a streamlined MCA portal-

based application process, the Ministry noted the proposal and stated:

"The suggestion to include Restoration applications through a streamlined portal has
been noted, and will be considered while designing the next version of MCA21.
Hence, the provision in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 may be retained
without any change."

76.5.2.  Regarding the suggestion at para no.76.4.3 to vest the entire

jurisdiction with respect to restoration under Section 252 with the Regional Director,

the Ministry expressed its inability to accept the proposal and submitted:

"The suggestion seeks to vest the entire jurisdiction under Section 252 with the
Regional Director. The proposed amendment, however, transfers only the appellate
jurisdiction under Section 252(1), while retaining applications under Section 252(3)
before the Tribunal. Proceedings under Section 252(3) involve wider adjudicatory
powers, including applications by different classes of stakeholders, consideration of
restoration, and the issuance of consequential directions to restore the parties to
their original position. In view of the nature of such proceedings, it is appropriate that
they continue to be dealt with by the Tribunal. Hence, the provision in the Corporate
Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 may be retained without change."

                                     595
76.5.3.  Regarding the suggestion at para no. 76.4.4 requesting clarification on

the appellate forum for parties aggrieved by an order of the Regional Director, the

Ministry declined the proposal and submitted:

"The provision is itself an appeal mechanism against the order of Registrar passed
under Section 248(1)."

76.5.4.  Regarding the suggestion at para no. 76.4.5 to reinstate the earlier

provisions and retain restoration powers exclusively with the NCLT rather than

transferring them to the Regional Director, the Ministry declined to accept the

suggestion and stated:

"The amendment is intended to ease out restoration process for the struck off
companies and to unburden the NCLT. The grounds on which such application can
be made before the Regional Director is the absence of any grounds for striking off
the company from register of companies by ROC. This limited ground can be
adjudicated by the Regional Director. Hence, the provision in the Corporate Laws
(Amendment) Bill, 2026 may be retained without any change."

76.5.5.  Regarding the suggestion at para no. 76.4.6 to insert a provision for

appeal to the Tribunal within forty-five days against a refusal by the Regional Director

and mandate disposal of restoration applications within sixty days by reasoned order,

the Ministry declined to accept the suggestion.

76.6. Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

The Committee note that Clause 76 of the Bill seeks to amend Section 252 of
the Companies Act, 2013 by transferring routine restoration appeals (filed
within three years) from the NCLT to the Regional Director to unburden the
Tribunal.

The Committee concur with the Ministry that transferring routine restoration
appeals to the Regional Director will effectively decongest the NCLT. At the
same time, the Committee agree that complex restoration cases involving

                                                      596
wider stakeholder rights under Section 252(3) should continue to be
adjudicated by the Tribunal.
Accordingly, the Committee accept Clause 76 as proposed in the Bill. The
Committee further advise the Ministry to ensure a hassle-free restoration
process through relevant Rules and a streamlined portal mechanism under
MCA21.

                                                      597
                  CLAUSE - 77

77. Clause 77 of the Bill, 2026, proposes to amend Section 271 of the
         Companies Act, 2013

77.1. Provision proposed in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

In section 271 of the principal Act,--

(a) in clause (a), the words "by the Tribunal" shall be omitted;
(b) in clause (c), the words "by notification under this Act" shall be omitted.

77.2. Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (Companies Act, 2013):

271. A company may, on a petition under section 272, be wound up by the
Tribunal,--

(a) if the company has, by special resolution, resolved that the company be
wound up by the Tribunal;

*  *  *  *  *  *                        *  *  *  *  *                 *          *

(c) if on an application made by the Registrar or any other person authorised by
the Central Government by notification under this Act, the Tribunal is of the opinion
that the affairs of the company have been conducted in a fraudulent manner or the
company was formed for fraudulent and unlawful purpose or the persons concerned
in the formation or management of its affairs have been guilty of fraud, misfeasance
or misconduct in connection therewith and that it is proper that the company be
wound up;

*  *  *  *  *  *                        *  *  *  *  *                 *          *

77.3. Reasons/Justification given by the Ministry for the proposed provisions:

"The amendment in Section 271(a) to omit the words "by the Tribunal" and in section
271(c) to remove the words "by notification under this Act" to align the provision with
similar provisions in the Act."

                                                      598
77.4. Important Views/Suggestions given by Experts/Stakeholders:

Stakeholders expressed concern that provisions relating to winding up under Section
271(c) (on grounds of fraudulent conduct, misfeasance, or misconduct) and Section
271(e) (on the "just and equitable" clause) rely on broad and undefined terms. They
argued that companies face risks of winding up on subjective considerations even
when alternative remedies like restructuring are available, and suggested that
matters of financial mismanagement or debt default are more appropriately handled
under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016.

77.5. Examination by the Committee:

77.5.1  Regarding the suggestion to delete or modify Section 271(c) on the

grounds that winding up is not an appropriate remedy and that the Insolvency and

Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (IBC) is more suitable, the Ministry, while declining to accept

the suggestion, stated the following:

"Sub-clause 271(c) currently covers scenarios of the Registrar and/or any official of
the Central Government filing an application for winding up basis the opinion that
"affairs of the company have been conducted in a fraudulent manner or the company
was formed for fraudulent and unlawful purpose or the persons concerned in the
formation or management of its affairs have been guilty of fraud, misfeasance or
misconduct in connection therewith".

This provision is required to deal with the cases where the frauds committed by the
company result into wrongful loss to any person and when same is intended to be
recovered from the assets of the company.

Accordingly, the ambit of this sub-clause is different from the grounds for filing
insolvency under the extant provisions of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code,
2016. Under the IBC, financial and operational creditors are eligible to file
applications regarding non-payment of dues, which is currently not covered by sub-
clause 271(c) of the Companies Act, 2013. As the two provisions have two different
ambits, deleting or removing either provision may cause scenarios that the statutes
have not covered.

Hence, the provision in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 may be retained
without any change."

                                       599
77.6. Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:
The Committee note that Clause 77 seeks to amend Section 271 of the
Companies Act, 2013 by removing redundant phrasing--specifically omitting
"by the Tribunal" in clause (a) and "by notification under this Act" in clause
(c)--to align the section with standard terminology across the Act.
Addressing stakeholder concerns regarding potential overlap with the
Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (IBC), the Committee note the
Ministry's clarification that Section 271(c) serves a distinct regulatory function.
While the IBC governs creditor-led insolvency for debt defaults, Section 271(c)
enables statutory authorities to intervene in cases of corporate fraud and
misfeasance to safeguard public interest and recover wrongful losses from
company assets.
Agreeing with the Ministry's rationale and recognizing the imperative to
maintain statutory safeguards against corporate fraud, the Committee accept
Clause 77 as proposed in the Bill.

                                               CLAUSE - 78

78. Clause 78 of the Bill proposes to amend Section 361 of the Companies
         Act, 2013

78.1. Provision proposed in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

In section 361 of the principal Act,--

(a) in sub-section (1),--

         (i) for the words "under this Chapter", the words, brackets, letters and
         figures "in accordance with the provisions of this Chapter under the
         circumstances referred to in clauses (a), (b) and (d) of section 271" shall be
         substituted;

         (ii) in clause (i), for the word "and", the word "or" shall be substituted;

         shall--

                  (a) appoint the Official Liquidator as the liquidator of the company;
                  or

                  (b) appoint an insolvency professional registered under the
                  Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, as liquidator of the company to

(c) in sub-section (5),--

         (i) after the words "affairs of the company", the words "by the Official
         Liquidator or any officer not below the rank of Assistant Director as may be
         authorised by the Central Government in this behalf" shall be inserted;

         (ii) for the words "as may be specified", the words "as it may direct" shall
         be substituted;

                                                      601
(d) in sub-section (6), for the words "under the provision", the words "continued
under the provision" shall be substituted;

(e) after sub-section (6), the following Explanation shall be inserted, namely:--

Liquidator" shall include an insolvency professional registered under the

78.2. Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (Companies Act, 2013):

361. (1) Where the company to be wound up under this Chapter,-- (i) has
         assets of book value not exceeding one crore rupees; and

*  *  *  *  *  *    *  *  *  *                                        *  *

(2) Where an order under sub-section (1) is made, the Central
Government shall appoint the Official Liquidator as the liquidator of the
company.

*  *  *  *  *  *    *  *  *  *                                        *  *

(5) On receipt of the report under sub-section (4), if the Central
Government is satisfied that any fraud has been committed by the promoters,

into the affairs of the company and that a report shall be submitted within such

(6) After considering the investigation report under sub-section (5), the

*  *  *  *  *  *    *  *  *  *                                        *  *

               602
78.3. Reasons/Justification given by the Ministry for the proposed provisions:

"Clause 78 proposes to amend section 361 to enhance the scope of summary
liquidation so that the workload of the NCLT is reduced. The present scope, which
covers companies with (a) assets of book value less than one crore and (b) other
prescribed classes of companies, is proposed to be expanded by replacing the word
"and" with "or", so that either class of companies can avail such provisions.

It also enables appointment of an insolvency professional as liquidator, in addition to
the Official Liquidator, for carrying out the functions under this Part."

78.4. Important Views/Suggestions given by Experts/Stakeholders:

Stakeholders suggested enhancing the monetary and size eligibility thresholds
(currently capped at 1 crore asset size) to enable more small and medium-sized
companies to utilize the summary liquidation route. Additionally, stakeholders
recommended introducing a comprehensive document checklist, mandating a fully
digital filing interface via MCA21, and establishing a fixed outer timeframe (such as 3
to 6 months) to ensure summary proceedings do not drag on indefinitely.

78.5. Examination by the Committee:

78.5.1   Regarding the suggestions to raise the monetary threshold and

streamline the process through a digital framework, the Ministry accepted the

suggestions and stated:

"Threshold to be increased to Rs. 2 Crore or such higher amount as may be
prescribed. The suggestion also proposes a streamlined method for the summary
liquidation process to include the list of documents required as well as a digital filing
platform. This will be appropriately considered through Rules as well MCA21."

78.5.2.  Regarding the proposal to mandate a rigid time-bound completion

schedule for the summary liquidation process, the Ministry declined to prescribe

additional outer limits and submitted:

"....Any liquidation of assets and subsequent distribution to creditors and
shareholders involves process of sale, invitation of claims, their adjudication and
then distribution. All these require a due process to be followed and oversight of

                                                      603
quasi-judicial authority to ensure the integrity of the process. The timelines are
already prescribed in provisions of section 361 to 365 of the Act. The proposed
amendment provides for liquidation under circumstances referred in clause (a), (b)
and (d) of the Section 271 and summary procedure is provided in Part IV of Chapter
XX."

78.6. Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

78.6.1.  The Committee note that Clause 78 of the Bill seeks to expand the

scope of summary liquidation and permit the appointment of registered

Insolvency Professionals alongside Official Liquidators to reduce the burden

on the NCLT.

Accepting the Committee's observation on broadening accessibility and
streamlining administrative workflows, the Ministry of Corporate Affairs has
agreed to enhance the monetary threshold for summary liquidation (to 2 crore
or such higher amount as prescribed) and introduce standardized document
checklists on the MCA21 digital platform through relevant Rules.

Accordingly, clause (ii) of sub-section (1) of Section 361 of the Bill, may be
amended as follows:

" (ii) in clause (i), for the words "one crore rupees; and", the words
"two crore rupees or " shall be substituted;"

78.6.2.  To ensure that this fast-track exit mechanism functions

seamlessly on the ground, the Committee underscore the need for a well-

defined subordinate regulatory framework. The Committee, therefore,

recommend that the Ministry of Corporate Affairs finalize and notify the

requisite Rules--specifically detailing the operational guidelines for

Insolvency Professionals, digitized workflows on MCA21, and revised financial

thresholds--in an expeditious, transparent, and consultative manner with

relevant professional bodies and stakeholders.

              604
Subject to incorporation of amendment and prompt notification of the
subordinate rules and digital workflows, the Committee endorse the legislative
intent and accept Clause 78 of the Bill.

                     606
         CLAUSE - 80

80. Clause 80 of the Bill proposes to insert Section 365 A after Section 365
of the Companies Act, 2013

80.1. Provision proposed in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

After section 365 of the principal Act, the following section shall be inserted,
namely:-

"365A.   Any person aggrieved by an order of the Central Government under

this Part, may prefer an appeal within a period of forty-five days from the date of

receipt of such order by him, before the Appellate Tribunal in such manner and on

payment of such fee, as may be prescribed.".

80.2. Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (Companies Act, 2013):

Insertion of new Section 365 A after Section 365

80.3. Reasons/Justification given by the Ministry for the proposed provision:

"New section 365A being inserted to provide that appeal against order of the Central
Government in cases of summary liquidation shall lie before the NCLAT."

80.4. Important Views/Suggestions given by Experts/Stakeholders:

Following are some of the important suggestions received from various stakeholders
during the deliberations of the Committee:

80.4.1. "Clarify that the appeal shall lie before the Appellate Tribunal that passed the
           order under Section 365."

80.4.2.  "Insertion of the following proviso after Section 365 A "Provided that the
         Appellate Tribunal may entertain an appeal after the expiry of the said period
         of forty-five days, if it is satisfied that the appellate was prevented by
         sufficient cause from filing the appeal within the period."

         607
80.4.3. "1. Appeal before Appellate Tribunal within 45 days.

         2. Permit condonation of delay on sufficient cause."

80.5. Examination by the Committee:

80.5.1.  During the deliberation, when asked to clarify that an appeal shall lie

before the Appellate Tribunal that passed the order under Section 365--thereby

resolving jurisdictional ambiguity and facilitating smooth implementation--the

Ministry in its written submission declined the proposal, stating inter alia as follows:

"The National Company Law Appellate Tribunal as constituted under Section 410 of
the Companies Act, 2013 has 2 benches, the principal bench and the Chennai
bench. Both benches have specific territorial jurisdictions and admit, hear and
dispose of appeals accordingly. Orders by Tribunals under Section 365 of the
Companies Act, 2013 shall be appealable under the proposed insertion of Section
365A, in line with the territorial jurisdiction prescribed by Section 410 of the
Companies Act, 2013. Hence, the provision in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill,
2026 may be retained without any change.".

80.5.2.  It was suggested to the Ministry to insert a proviso to Section 365A

maintaining to accept the appeal after expiry of forty-five days on presentation of

sufficient cause which prevented the filing of such appeal. In response thereto, the

Ministry have agreed to accept the said suggestion.

80.6. Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

On the examination of Clause 80 of the Bill, the Committee note that the clause
seeks to insert Section 365A into the Companies Act, 2013, establishing a
statutory avenue of appeal before the National Company Law Appellate
Tribunal (NCLAT) against summary liquidation orders of the Central
Government.

The Committee also note the Ministry's clarification that territorial jurisdiction
between the Principal Bench at New Delhi and the Chennai Bench remains

                                                      608
fully anchored in Section 410 of the Act, thereby dispelling jurisdictional
ambiguity.

Nevertheless, the Committee emphasize that an equitable appellate
mechanism must balance administrative efficiency with procedural fairness. In
deference to the Committee's observation that an unyielding forty-five-day
limitation period could prejudice genuine litigants facing unforeseen
impediments, the Ministry of Corporate Affairs has agreed to amend Section
365A to explicitly provide for condonation of delay upon showing sufficient
cause.

Accordingly, the Committee recommend that proposed Section 365A be
incorporated into the Bill in the following modified form:

"365A.  Any person aggrieved by an order of the Central Government

under this Part, may prefer an appeal within a period of forty-five days from the

date of receipt of such order by him, before the Appellate Tribunal in such

manner and on payment of such fee, as may be prescribed.

         Provided that the Appellate Tribunal may entertain an appeal after the
expiry of the said period, but within a further period not exceeding forty-five
days, if it is satisfied that the appellant was prevented by sufficient cause from
filing the appeal within that period".

Subject to this modification, the Committee accept Clause 80 of the Bill.

       date of closing of the financial year:

                Provided further that if a company holds such first annual general
       meeting, it shall not be necessary for the company to hold any annual general
       meeting in the year of its incorporation:

                Provided also that";

         (b) sub-section (2) shall be omitted;

         (c) for sub-section (3), the following sub-section shall be substituted, namely:-

                  "(3) The Members shall adopt the articles of the Producer Company
         referred to in clause (b) of sub-section (1) of section 378G and appoint
         directors of its Board in the first annual general meeting.";

                                                      621
         (d) in sub-section (9), for the words "members of the Producer Company
shall", the words "members or one hundred members of the Producer Company,
whichever is less, shall" shall be substituted.

86.2 Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (The Companies Act, 2013):
         In section 378ZA of the principal Act,--

         (1) Every Producer Company shall in each year, hold, in addition to any other
meetings, a general meeting, as its annual general meeting and shall specify the
meeting as such in the notices calling it, and not more than fifteen months shall
elapse between the date of one annual general meeting of a Producer Company and
that of the next:

         Provided that the Registrar may, for any special reason, permit extension of
the time for holding any annual general meeting (not being the first annual general
meeting) by a period not exceeding three months.

         (2) A Producer Company shall hold its first annual general meeting within a
period of ninety days from the date of its incorporation.

         (3) The Members shall adopt the articles of the Producer Company and
appoint directors of its Board in the annual general meeting.

*  *  *  *    *  *                                                       *

         (9) Unless the articles of the Producer Company provide for a larger number,
one-fourth of the total number of members of the Producer Company shall be the
quorum for its annual general meeting.

*  *  *  *    *  *                                                       *

         622
86.3 Reasons / Justification given by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs for the
proposed provision :

         "This amendment is proposed to rationalize and align the provisions for
Producer Companies vis-à-vis other companies."

86.4 Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

The Committee find from the examination of Clause 86 of the Bill that it
amends Section 378ZA of the Companies Act, 2013 to streamline statutory
timelines for holding Annual General Meetings (AGMs) of Producer
Companies.

The clause removes the rigid requirement to hold the first AGM within ninety
days of incorporation. Instead, it allows the first AGM to be held within nine
months from the close of the first financial year, and subsequent AGMs within
six months.

Furthermore, it explicitly clarifies that members shall adopt the articles of
association and appoint directors at the first AGM, while revising the quorum
threshold to one-fourth of total members or one hundred members, whichever
is lower.

The Committee observe that these modifications successfully align the
governance framework of Producer Companies with general corporate
standards under the Act.

Replacing the restrictive setup deadline provides practical breathing space for
newly incorporated entities to organize their operations. Similarly, setting a
realistic quorum threshold prevents procedural deadlocks and ensures
smooth decision-making while preserving democratic member control.

                                                      623
The proposed amendments effectively resolve statutory ambiguities, eliminate
operational friction, and enhance ease of compliance. Accordingly, the
Committee recommend that Clause 86 may be accepted as proposed.

87 Clause 87 of the Bill seeks to amend Section 378ZF of the Companies
Act, 2013.

87.1 Provision proposed in The Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 :

For section 378ZF of the principal Act, the following section shall be substituted,
namely:--

         "378ZF. (1) Every Producer Company having an average annual turnover
exceeding five crore rupees or such other amount, as may be prescribed, in each of
the three consecutive financial years, shall be required to appoint an internal auditor,
who shall either be a chartered accountant or a cost accountant, or such other
professional as may be decided by the Board, to conduct internal audit of the
functions and activities of the Producer Company.

         (2) The manner and the intervals in which the internal audit shall be
conducted and reported to the Board, shall be such as may be prescribed.".

87.2 Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (The Companies Act, 2013):

378ZF. Internal audit.-- Every Producer Company shall have internal audit of its
accounts carried out, at such interval and in such manner as may be specified in
articles, by a chartered accountant as defined in clause (b) of sub-section (1) of
section 2 of the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949.

*  *  *  *            *  *                                              *

87.3 Reasons / Justification given by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs for the
proposed provision :

         625
         "This amendment is proposed to rationalize and align the provisions for
         Producer Companies vis-à-vis other companies."

87.4 Important Views/Suggestions given by Experts/Stakeholders:

Some of the suggestions given by experts / stakeholders are as follows :

         87.4.1 "The words "or such other amount, as may be prescribed" may be
        omitted."

        87.4.2 "It is suggested to specifically provide the term `Company Secretary' as
        under: "378ZF. (1) Every Producer Company having an average annual
        turnover exceeding five crore rupees or such other amount, as may be
        prescribed, in each of the three consecutive financial years, shall be required
        to appoint an internal auditor, who shall either be a chartered accountant or a
        cost accountant or company secretary, or such other professional as may be
        decided by the Board."

        87.4.3 "The proposed amendments do not appear necessary considering the
        existing compliance framework."

        87.4.4 "It is recommended that the term "other professional" be clearly
        defined, including minimum qualifications, relevant experience and eligibility
        criteria for appointment as an internal auditor. It is further recommended that
        compliance with recognised quality standards be included as part of the
        eligibility criteria for internal auditors, to ensure consistency, independence
        and quality in the conduct of internal audit engagements.

                  Require adherence to recognised quality management standards for
         internal audits of Producer Companies, and mandate internal audit and cost
         audit requirements only where the producer activity or cost-audited activity
         exceeds 10% of the company's turnover."

        87.4.5 "Raise threshold limit; link to size/shareholders; classify penalties as
        per type of company."

        87.4.6 One of the suggestions proposed that Section 378ZF(1) may be
        amended to include other parameters such as paid up share capital, of an
        amount as may be prescribed, to the threshold of Producer Companies
        instead of purely relying on an average annual turnover exceeding five crore.

                                                      626
87.5 Examination by the Committee:

87.5.1 While expressing inability in omitting the phrase "or such other amount, as
may be prescribed" concerning annual turnover of a Producer Company as
mentioned under Clause 87, the Ministry of Corporate Affairs cited that :

         "Producer Companies are being considered as a class of companies with
        specific compliance requirements under the Companies Act, 2013. Sections
        378P, 378Q, 378ZA, 378ZF are being considered to ensure parity with non-
        producer companies. Section 378ZF as amended by the Amendment Bill is
        parallel to Section 138 of the Companies Act and provides for internal audit
        provisions for companies. The financial thresholds are subject to periodic
        revision based on inflation, administrative cost, and market conditions.
        Embedding these in primary legislation would render the statute inflexible and
        quickly outdated. Further, the policy decision to impose a threshold is
        contained in the statute itself; only the quantum of its determination is
        delegated. As per Ministry of Corporate Affairs "Policy for Pre-Legislative
        consultation and comprehensive review of existing Rules and Regulations",
        the public consultation is held before issuing new Rules/Regulations or
        making changes in the Rules/Regulations made under the Companies Act,
        2013. The suggestions received from various stakeholders during such
        consultations are examined and accordingly new Rules/Regulations or
        amendments to existing Rules/Regulations are finalised. Further,
        Rule/Regulation making power is subject to Parliamentary approval. Thus, an
        apprehension regarding frequent changes through delegated legislation is
        unfounded. Hence, the provision in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill,
        2026 may be retained without any change."

87.5.2 While accepting the proposal regarding inclusion of `Company Secretary' as
an internal auditor in a Producer Company, the Ministry of Corporate Affairs stated
that :

        "The proposal to include words `Company Secretary' as part of internal
        auditors under Section 378ZF may be accepted to ensure that all statutorily
        recognised professionals are within the ambit of the section. A corresponding
        amendment will be proposed under Section 138 of the Companies Act, 2013
        to ensure seamless reading of the definition of `internal audit.'"

                                                      627
87.5.3 With respect to the suggestion calling the proposed amendments
unnecessary in the face of the existing compliance framework for Producer
Companies, the Ministry of Corporate Affairs reasoned that:

        "The proposed compliance requirement for Producer Companies to conduct
        internal audits is to ensure their sound functioning by maintaining accounting
        oversight of their functions and activities by professionals. The proposed
        amendment has been expressly added to maintain parity with non-Producer
        Companies who are currently obligated to conduct internal audits. Hence, the
        provision in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 may be retained
        without any change."

87.5.4 In explaining why it could not accept the suggestions to clearly define 'other
professionals' or to set recognized quality management standards as eligibility
criteria for internal auditors, the Ministry of Corporate Affairs stated that :

        "The words "or such other professionals as may be decided by the Board" are
        intended to enable Board to appoint any other person having similar
        qualifications or experience. This is aimed at providing flexibility to the Board
        of Directors. Similar provisions are provided in section 138. Section 378ZF
        pertains to internal audit of producer company and not cost audit. Further, the
        objects or activities of the producer company are clearly stipulated under
        section 378B. Thus, no further threshold based on activities seems
        necessary."

87.5.5 In rejecting suggestions to raise the annual turnover threshold for Producer
Companies, link compliance norms to company size or shareholder count and
categorize penalties by company type, the Ministry of Corporate Affairs submitted
that:

        "The amended Section 378ZF provides for lower compliance requirements by
        mandating internal audits for companies with a turnover exceeding INR 5
        crore. This amendment has been proposed keeping in mind the balance
        between promoting ease of doing business and ensuring internal audit
        compliance requirements."

                                                      628
87.5.6 In rejecting proposals to base a Producer Company's threshold on alternative
metrics--such as liabilities or paid-up share capital--rather than average annual
turnover, the Ministry of Corporate Affairs reasoned that:

        "The rationale behind mandating an internal audit based on turnover for
        Producer Companies (under Section 378ZF of the Companies Act) is based
        on section 378X wherein similar critieria has been used for appointment of
        company secretary. The turnover criteria is an accepted criteria to judge the
        scale of business operations."

87.5.7 During their oral deposition before the Committee, the representatives of the
Ministry of Corporate Affairs apprised that amendments in relevant Sections of the
Principal Act relating to management of Producer Companies were contained in
Clauses 83 to 87 of the Bill. In this regard, the representative of the Ministry of
Corporate Affairs submitted that :

        "... 83     ,       All of
        these amendments are aimed at rationalizing the provisions related to
        producer companies, aligning them with the standards of regular companies.
        Currently, the regulatory conditions for producer companies have become
        more stringent than those prescribed under the general provisions of the
        Companies Act. Therefore, we are attempting to bring all these provisions at
        par with normal companies. These changes relate to Clauses 83, 84, 85, 86,
        and 87. ..."

87.5.8 Further, apprising the Committee about the provisions under Clause 87
[Section 378ZF (1)] relating to financial threshold for Producer Companies to appoint
an internal auditor, the representative of the Ministry of Corporate Affairs also
submitted that :

        ",           ,     
         Clause 87 concerns the appointment of an internal auditor. Actually, even
        in regular companies, an internal auditor must be appointed once the
        company meets a certain financial threshold.      
                   

                                                      629
            There is a small threshold.      , 
               

                 ,          ,   
                     
                      
                    
              ,     
                       ..."

87.5.9 Provisions proposed under Clause 87 [Section 378ZF (2)] confer rule-making
power on the Central Government for prescribing the manner and interval in which
internal audit shall be conducted by the Producer Company. In this regard, the
Ministry stated that:

        "Clause 87 of the Bill empowers the Central Government to prescribe, under
        sub-section (1) of section 378ZF of the Companies Act, 2013 such other
        amount of average annual turnover in each of the three consecutive financial
        years for requiring a Producer Company to appoint an internal auditor. It
        further empowers the Central Government to prescribe, under sub section (2)
        of section 378ZF, the manner and the intervals in which the internal audit shall
        be conducted and reported to the Board."

87.5.10 Elaborating on the rationale behind this delegation of rule-making power, the
Ministry also apprised the Committee that these provisions demonstrate that the
delegation is directed at procedural flexibility and does not affect substantive
compliance of the law.

87.6 Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

87.6.1  The Committee find from the examination of Clause 87 of the Bill

that it substitutes Section 378ZF of the Companies Act, 2013. The substituted

provision mandates internal audits for Producer Companies having an average

annual turnover exceeding five crore rupees, or such other prescribed amount,

        630
in three consecutive financial years. It further empowers the Central
Government to prescribe rules regarding the manner and intervals for
conducting such audits.

The Committee observe that this amendment promotes ease of doing business
and establishes necessary parity between Producer and non-Producer
Companies. The Committee consider average annual turnover to be an
appropriate criterion for judging the scale of business operations.

While noting that delegating rule-making powers provides operational
flexibility without compromising the spirit of the law, the Committee emphasize
the need for robust execution. Accordingly, the Committee recommend that the
Ministry of Corporate Affairs ensure the subordinate legislative framework is
formulated in a timely, transparent, and consultative manner, with due regard
to inter-ministerial coordination and policy coherence for effective
implementation.

With regard to the appointment of internal auditors, the Committee emphasize
that Company Secretaries are statutorily recognized and fully authorized to
conduct internal audits. To ensure clarity and completeness, the Committee
recommend that the phrase "or a company secretary" be explicitly included in
Clause 87 [Section 378ZF (1)], and the sub-section be modified as follows:

"378ZF. (1) Every Producer Company having an average annual turnover
exceeding five crore rupees or such other amount, as may be prescribed, in
each of the three consecutive financial years, shall be required to appoint an
internal auditor, who shall either be a chartered accountant or a cost
accountant or a company secretary, or such other professional as may be
decided by the Board, to conduct internal audit of the functions and activities
of the Producer Company."

                                                      631
         Subject to the incorporation of the specified modification, the
Committee recommend that Clause 87 may be accepted as proposed.

87.6.2  Consequent to the modification recommended in Clause 87, the

Committee further recommend that in section 138 of the Principal Act, in sub-

section (1), after the words "or a cost accountant," the words "or a company

secretary," shall be inserted.

88 Clause 88 of the Bill seeks to amend Section 378ZM of the Companies
Act, 2013.

88.1 Provision proposed in The Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 :

In section 378ZM of the principal Act,--

(a) in sub-section (1), for the words "punishable with fine which may extend to ten
thousand rupees for every day during which such name has been used by him", the
words "liable to a penalty of one lakh rupees and in case of continuing failure, with a
further penalty of five hundred rupees for each day, after the first during which such
failure continues, subject to a maximum of five lakh rupees" shall be substituted;

(b) in sub-section (2), for the words "imprisonment for a term which may extend to six
months and with fine equivalent to five per cent. of the turnover of that Company
during the preceding financial year", the words "a penalty of twenty-five thousand
rupees and in case of continuing failure, with a further penalty of two hundred rupees
for each day, after the first during which such failure continues, subject to a maximum
of five lakh rupees" shall be substituted;

(c) for sub-section (3), the following sub-section shall be substituted, namely:--

         "(3) If a director or officer of a Producer Company--

                  (a) fails to hand over the custody of books of account and other
                  documents or property in his custody to the Producer Company of
                  which he is a director or officer; or

                  (b) fails to convene annual general meeting or other general meetings,

                                                      633
he shall be liable to a penalty of twenty-five thousand rupees and in case of
continuing failure, with a further penalty of two hundred rupees for each day, after the
first during which such failure continues, subject to a maximum of one lakh rupees.".

88.2 Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (The Companies Act, 2013):

378ZM. Penalty for contravention.--(1) If any person, other than a Producer
Company registered under this Chapter, carries on business under any name which
contains the words "Producer Company Limited", he shall be punishable with fine
which may extend to ten thousand rupees for every day during which such name has
been used by him.

(2) If a director or an officer of a Producer Company, who wilfully fails to furnish any
information relating to the affairs of the Producer Company required by a Member or
a person duly authorised in this behalf, he shall be liable to imprisonment for a term
which may extend to six months and with fine equivalent to five per cent. of the
turnover of that Company during the preceding financial year.

(3) If a director or officer of a Producer Company--

         (a) fails to hand over the custody of books of account and other documents or
property in his custody to the Producer Company of which he is a director or officer;
or

         (b) fails to convene annual general meeting or other general meetings,

he shall be punishable with fine which may extend to one lakh rupees, and in the
case of a continuing default or failure, with an additional fine which may extend to ten
thousand rupees for every day during which such default or failure continues.

88.3 Reasons / Justification given by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs for the
proposed provision :

                                                      634
         "This amendment is proposed to rationalise and align the provisions for
Producer Companies vis-à-vis other companies.

         Further, the amendment replaces the existing fine and imprisonment
provisions with a penalty framework for contraventions under this section. The
amendment is part of the broader decriminalization exercise under the Bill."

88.4 Important Views/Suggestions given by Experts/Stakeholders:

Some of the important suggestions given by stakeholders are as follows :

88.4.1 "A minor drafting correction has been recommended to replace the

pronoun "He" with "It".             [Batch - I, A-2, Sl. No.169]

88.4.2 "If someone who is not a Producer Company uses the words "Producer
Company Limited" in their business name, they can be fined up to Rs.10,000
for each day the name is used. If a director or officer of a Producer Company
deliberately fails to give information about the company's affairs when asked
by a member or an authorised person, they can face imprisonment up to 6
months and a fine equal to 5% of the company's turnover of the previous year.
If a director or officer: does not hand over books, documents, or property to
the company, or does not call annual or other general meetings, they can be
fined up to Rs.1,00,000, and if the failure continues, an extra fine of Rs.10,000
per day will apply. Reason: A fine of 5% of turn over for not furnishing
information is disproportionately high, especially for large companies. Even
minor lapses could lead to huge penalties, discouraging business. Routine
lapses like delay in handing over records or missing a meeting could lead not
Just to monetary fines but also imprisonment, which creates fear among
directors and officers. There are no producer companies coming into the forte
and this provision and other similar provisions are required to be deleted."

88.4.3 "Daily accumulating penalties frequently become punitive and
disproportionate. Fixed penalties would promote compliance while avoiding
excessive hardship."

88.5 Examination by the Committee:

88.5.1 While accepting the suggestion of a minor drafting correction to replace the
pronoun 'He' with 'It' when referring to a `Producer Company', the Ministry of
Corporate Affairs stated that the expression "Producer Company" is referred to as "it"
in Chapter XXIA of the Companies Act, while "he" is used for natural persons. Hence,

                                                      635
the Ministry assured that the semantic change would be included in the proposed
amendment and it would be formulated accordingly.

88.5.2 While declining the suggestion to delete this and other similar provisions from
the Bill due to disproportionate penalties that could potentially discourage business
and create fear among directors, the Ministry of Corporate Affairs submitted that:

         "The amendment replaces the existing fine and imprisonment provisions with
        a penalty framework for contraventions under this section. The amendment is
        part of the broader decriminalisation exercise under the Bill. The amendment
        also caps the monetary penalty payable by the defaulting person at INR
        5,00,000 (Indian Rupees Five Lakhs) for continuing contraventions. The
        contraventions laid out in Section 378ZM are serious in nature and cannot be
        removed from the ambit of the Companies Act, 2013. However, the proposed
        amendments under the Amendment Bill ensure a proportionate penalty for
        contravention by Producer Companies. Hence, the provision in the Corporate
        Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 may be retained without any change."

88.5.3 While turning down the suggestion for replacing daily accumulating penalties
with fixed penalties so as to avoid undue hardship, the Ministry of Corporate Affairs
reasoned that:

        "The daily penalty for continuing default is capped at maximum of INR 5 lakhs.
        The contraventions under Section 378ZM are materially different. They relate
        to misuse of the words "producer company limited", failure to furnish
        information and other continuing governance obligations. Such contraventions
        may not therefore be appropriately equated with procedural filing defaults.
        Penalty is commensurate with the gravity of the contravention."

88.6 Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

The Committee find from the examination of the contents of Clause 88 and the

parallel provisions of Section 378ZM of the Companies Act, 2013 that Clause

88 of the Bill suitably decriminalizes various offences relating to Producer

Companies by replacing criminal fines and imprisonment with a civil monetary

penalty framework. Specifically, it caps penalties for unauthorized use of the

                                                      636
company name and failure to furnish information at five lakh rupees, while
capping penalties for procedural defaults, such as failing to convene general
meetings or hand over records, at one lakh rupees.

The Committee observe that substituting custodial sentences and open-ended
daily fines with capped monetary penalties aligns with the broader legislative
objectives of decriminalizing corporate laws. This approach removes
unwarranted fear among directors and officers while preserving an effective
statutory deterrent against governance lapses.

With regard to sub-clause (a), the Committee note that the pronoun "he" is
inadvertently used when referring to "any person other than a Producer
Company". Since "any person other than a Producer Company" is a legal
entity consistently being referred to throughout Chapter XXIA of the Act, the
Committee recommend that the phrase "he shall be" be substituted with "that
person shall be" in Clause 88(a) to ensure statutory uniformity and drafting
precision and the sub-section be modified as follows:

"In section 378ZM of the principal Act,--

(a) in sub-section (1), for the words "he shall be punishable with fine which
may extend to ten thousand rupees for every day during which such name has
been used by him", the words "that person shall be liable to a penalty of one
lakh rupees and in case of continuing failure, with a further penalty of five
hundred rupees for each day, after the first during which such failure
continues, subject to a maximum of five lakh rupees" shall be substituted;"

                                                      637
Subject to the incorporation of the specified drafting correction, the Committee
recommend that Clause 88 may be accepted as proposed.

90 Clause 90 of the Bill seeks to amend Section 392 of the Companies Act,

90.1 Provision proposed in The Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 :

In section 392 of the principal Act, for the portion beginning with "shall be punishable

90.2 Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (The Companies Act, 2013):

392. Punishment for contravention.--Without prejudice to the provisions of section
391, if a foreign company contravenes the provisions of Chapter XXII, the foreign

but which may extend to three lakh rupees and in the case of a continuing offence,
with an additional fine which may extend to fifty thousand rupees for every day after

twenty-five thousand rupees but which may extend to five lakh rupees.
