90.3 Reasons / Justification given by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs for the
proposed provision :

         641
         "The amendment replaces the existing punishment with a penalty framework,
         including fixed and continuing penalties for contraventions by foreign
         companies and their officers. The amendment is part of the broader
         decriminalization exercise under the Bill."

90.4 Important Views/Suggestions given by Experts/Stakeholders:

Some of the important suggestions given by stakeholders are as follows:

         90.4.1 "Daily accumulating penalties frequently become punitive and
        disproportionate. Fixed penalties would promote compliance while avoiding
        excessive hardship."

        90.4.2 "If a foreign company violates any rules in Chapter XXII: 1. The
        company must pay a fine between Rs.1 lakh and Rs.3 lakh. 2. If the violation
        continues, an additional fine up to Rs.50,000 per day applies after the first
        day. Every officer of the foreign company who is responsible can also be fined
        Rs. 25,000 to 25 lakhs. Reason: The high fines, including daily continuing
        fines, can create significant financial burden for foreign companies, especially
        startups or small investors. Officers can face personal fines, making foreign
        investment and management in India riskier and potentially discouraging new
        business ventures."

        90.4.3 "Enforcement for offshore digital platforms handled via proposed
        Section 379A(5) -- geo-blocking plus prescribed penalty for continuing
        default."

90.5 Examination by the Committee:

90.5.1 While rejecting the suggestion to replace daily accumulating penalties with
fixed penalties to avoid excessive hardship and promote compliance, the Ministry of
Corporate Affairs submitted that:

         "The proposed amendment to Section 392 provides for a monetary penalty of
        INR 1,00,000 (Indian Rupees One Lakh) with a further penalty of INR 500 for
        each day subject to maximum of INR 5,00,000 (Indian Rupees Five Lakhs) for
        a continuing contravention by foreign companies. The proposed amendment
        is in line with penalties awarded to other class/classes of companies and are
        proportionate in nature given the seriousness of the contraventions. Hence,

                                                      642
        the provision in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 may be retained
        without any change."

90.5.2 While declining the suggestion to relax foreign company penalties under
Chapter XXII to lessen the financial burden on international investors, the Ministry of
Corporate Affairs stated that:

         "The revised penalty structure is proportionate and provides graded
        consequences for continuing contraventions, with prescribed limits, and is
        consistent with treatment of similar defaults under the Companies Act, 2013.
        The maximum penalty is capped at INR 5 Lakhs, Further, no separate
        framework is warranted for foreign companies, as entities carrying on
        business in India are required to comply with the same statutory requirements.
        Hence, the provision in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 may be
        retained without any change."

90.5.3 While stating that the suggestion regarding enforcement for offshore digital
platforms is in agreement with the proposed amendment, the Ministry of Corporate
Affairs elaborated on the definition of foreign company as given in the principal Act
and submitted as under:

         "The suggestion is in agreement with the proposed amendment. The definition
        of foreign company is provided in section 2(42) of the Act which covers the
        company having place of business in India through an agent, physically or
        through electronic mode and conducting any business activity in India in any
        other manner. The Companies (Specification of Definitions Details) Rules,
        2014 defines "electronic mode" and "business activity"."

90.6 Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

The Committee, on thorough examination of Clause 90 of the Bill, find that it

seeks to amend Section 392 of the Companies Act, 2013 to decriminalize

contraventions committed by foreign companies under Chapter XXII of the Act.

The amendment replaces criminal fines with a civil monetary penalty

framework. Under the revised provisions, a foreign company is liable to a

                                                      643
penalty of one lakh rupees, with a continuing daily penalty of five hundred
rupees, subject to a maximum cap of five lakh rupees. Additionally, every
officer in default is liable to a penalty of twenty-five thousand rupees, with a
continuing daily penalty of two hundred rupees, capped at two lakh rupees.
The Committee observe that the proposed framework establishes
proportionate and graded consequences for continuing defaults while capping
maximum monetary exposure. This aligns penalty structures for foreign
companies with standards applicable to other corporate entities under the Act,
ensuring equal regulatory treatment and encouraging cross-border
investment.
Having considered the concerns raised by stakeholders alongside the
clarifications submitted by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, the Committee
concur with the Ministry's position. After thorough deliberations, the
Committee accept the proposed amendment and recommend that Clause 90
may be accepted without any modification.

                                                      644
                                 INSERTION OF NEW PROVISION

90A New insertion of provisions in the Bill with regard to transfer of
registration of a company registered outside India.

90A.1 Examination by the Committee:

90A.1.1  On the issue of re-domiciliation of foreign-incorporated entities,

specifically shifting of foreign subsidiaries of Indian Company back to India, the

International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA) submitted written

submission as under :

"Many Indian entities in the business of ship leasing, aircraft leasing, funds,
insurance entities have established their subsidiaries in major foreign
jurisdictions. One of the main objective of IFSCA is to onshore such offshore
businesses into IFSC, however no enabling provision exists under the
Companies Act, to facilitate inward re domiciliation. Re-domiciliation enables
foreign-incorporated companies to migrate to the IFSC without winding up in
their home jurisdiction, while ensuring continuity of the entity/business. A
number of Indian entities have domiciled decades ago and many are willing to
redomicile back to Indian shores, provided an equivalent policy environment is
made available. Enabling inward re-domiciliation under the Companies Act,
would eliminate the need to incorporate a new entity and the requirement of
share/asset transfer-related costs. Major jurisdictions such as Singapore, UAE
(DIFC), Mauritius, Canada and Hong Kong provide for re-domiciliation under
their respective Companies Act. Accordingly, a new chapter namely, "Chapter
XVA - Transfer of Incorporation to IFSC" is recommended to be introduced
under the Companies Act."

90A.1.2  Further, the representatives of IFSCA deposed before the Committee

during oral evidence on the issue of re-domiciliation as follows :

"...many foreign jurisdictions have reciprocity provisions for re-domiciliation.
Some countries do not have the provision. So, our view is that after several
discussions inside with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, we have a feeling that
letting companies go out of India may not be a good idea. Therefore, from that
perspective, we decided not to keep the reciprocity provision. Therefore, we
will be able to redomicile companies which are in other countries and which
have a neutral provision for sending companies out without the requirement of
reciprocity. So, from that perspective, our proposal has been well thought-out
in this manner that we do not want to look at reciprocity provisions."

                                             645
90A.2 Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

The Committee note that re-domiciliation enables foreign-incorporated
companies to migrate seamlessly to an International Financial Services Centre
(IFSC) without undergoing winding-up or dissolution in their home jurisdiction,
thereby ensuring complete business and legal continuity.

The Committee observe that a significant number of Indian promoters with
offshore operations are desirous of returning to Indian shores, provided an
equivalent and enabling regulatory environment is established. In this regard,
the Committee are of the view that facilitating inward re-domiciliation under the
Companies Act, 2013 would eliminate the need to incorporate fresh entities
and significantly avoid onerous transaction costs associated with share or
asset transfers.

The Committee further note that while the IFSCA actively endeavours to
onshore offshore financial and business activities into the IFSC, the
Companies Act, 2013 currently lacks an explicit enabling statutory framework
for inward re-domiciliation. In order to facilitate the reverse-flipping and
shifting of foreign subsidiaries of Indian companies back to India, the
Committee feel that an enabling legal framework including provisions relating
to taxation, capital gains, stamp duty, transfer and vesting of assets and
liabilities, filing and compliance requirements, continuation of rights and
obligations, and other consequential or incidental matters arising from such
redomiciliation, is essential for seamless migration. Therefore, the Committee
recommend that the Central Government may, in consultation and
coordination with the Ministries, Departments and regulatory authorities
concerned, notify a comprehensive framework to facilitate the redomiciliation
of foreign-based entities and may also undertake or recommend suitable
amendments to the relevant laws, wherever necessary, to ensure a smooth and
seamless implementation of such redomiciliation.

         Accordingly, the Committee recommend that the following provisions be
incorporated after Clause 90 (after Section 393A of the Principal Act) as a new
`Chapter XXIIA - Transfer of registration of a company registered outside India'
in the Bill.

"Transfer of registration of a company registered outside India

393B. Eligibility for transfer of registration
                                                      646
Subject to the provisions of section 393C, a company incorporated outside
India and having share capital may, if it is authorised to do so by the laws of
the jurisdiction under which it was incorporated, apply for transfer of
registration under section 393D to the Registrar, as a company limited by
shares under this Act:

Provided that such company shall be allowed to register only within the
International Financial Services Centre, established under the Special
Economic Zones Act, 2005, and after it has obtained no objection from
International Financial Services Centres Authority.

393C. Conditions for making the application for transfer of registration

A company as referred to in section 393B, shall not apply for transfer of its
registration, if -

(a) it is formed for a purpose which is not lawful; or

(b) it is being struck off, wound up, or is in under liquidation or insolvency
proceedings under any law, or an application in this regard is pending before
any court or any other authority; or

(c) it is adjudged as insolvent; or

(d) a receiver, manager or administrator, by whatever name called, has been
appointed, whether by a court or in some other manner, in respect of any
property of such company; or

(e) it has filed an application for compromise or arrangement with its
members or creditors; or

(f) it does not comply with any other conditions as may be prescribed.

393D. Application to Registrar for transfer of registration

                                                      647
(1) An application by the company referred to in section 393B shall be made
under this Chapter in such form and manner, as may be prescribed and it shall
be accompanied by -

(a) a certified copy of the memorandum and articles, or other corresponding
instrument evidencing the formation of the company;

(b) a declaration of solvency which in accordance with the provisions of
Section 393E;

(c) the name under which it is proposed to register as a company under this
Act;

(d) evidence that the application, the proposed memorandum and articles
have been approved by a majority of the directors, or equity holders, or the
other persons who are authorised to exercise the powers over the company;

(e) evidence that the company is authorized by the laws of the jurisdiction
under which it is incorporated to make such application;

(f) a declaration that if the certificate of transfer of registration is issued under
this Chapter, it shall cease to be incorporated under the other jurisdiction
outside India;

(g) a declaration that it is not prevented from making this application under
any provisions of this Chapter; and

(h) such other documents as may be prescribed.

(2) The name so proposed under clause (c) of sub-section (1) shall be subject
to the provisions of sub-section (2) of section 4.

(3) All the documents required to be filed with the Registrar by such
company shall be in English language and where any such document is not in
English language, there shall be attached a translation thereof in English
language duly certified to be correct.

                                                      648
(4) The memorandum of a company applying under this Chapter shall, in
addition to the matters required to be stated under section 4, state--

(a) the name of the company at the date of the application and the name under
which it proposes to be registered;

(b) the place where it is incorporated, registered or formed; and

(c) the date on which it was incorporated, registered or formed at such place.

(5) The articles referred to in the Table F of Schedule I of this Act shall not
apply unless and except in so far as it is adopted by the members of such
company by way of special resolution.

393E. Declaration of solvency

A declaration of solvency shall be signed by each person, who is a director of
the company and shall state that having made full inquiry into the affairs of the
company, the directors have formed an opinion that the company is capable of
meeting its liabilities and will not be rendered insolvent within a period of one
year from the date of such declaration.

393F. Issue of certificate of transfer of registration.

(1) On compliance with the requirements of this Chapter, and on payment of
such fees, if any, as payable under section 403, the Registrar shall issue a
certificate of transfer of registration to the company referred to in section
393B.

(2) After the issuance of the certificate under sub-section (1), the Registrar
shall also immediately send a copy of it, through e-mail or by any other means
of communication to the appropriate official or public body in the jurisdiction
where such company was earlier registered and keep a copy of such
communication for the purposes of record.

393G. Effect of issue of certificate of transfer of registration.

                                                      649
(1) Upon the issue of the certificate of transfer of registration by the
Registrar under sub-section (1) of section 393F, the company referred to in
section 393B shall be registered under the provisions of this Act and on such
registration, the said company shall be governed by the provisions of this Act
and its earlier registration under the foreign jurisdiction shall cease to operate.
(2) The provisions of sections 368, 369 and 370 relating to vesting of property,
saving of existing liabilities and continuation of pending legal proceedings
shall apply mutatis mutandis to the company referred in sub-section (1)."

91 Clause 91 of the Bill seeks to amend Section 396 of the Companies Act,
2013.

91.1 Provision proposed in The Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

In section 396 of the principal Act,--

                  (a) in the marginal heading, for the word "offices", the words "and other
         offices" shall be substituted;

                  (b) after sub-section (1), the following sub-section shall be inserted,
         namely:--

                           "(1A) The Central Government may appoint such number of
                  Regional Directors, Additional Regional Directors or Joint Regional
                  Directors or Deputy Regional Directors as it considers necessary for
                  discharge of various functions under this Act, and the powers and
                  duties that may be exercisable by such officers shall be such as may
                  be prescribed.";

                  (c) in sub-section (2), after the words "Assistant Registrars", the words
         "or such other officers" shall be inserted;

                  (d) after sub-section (2), the following sub-section shall be inserted,
         namely:--

                           "(2A) The Central Government may authorise one or more
                  officers not below the rank of Assistant Director or Assistant Registrar
                  of that Government to exercise such powers and duties of the Regional

                                                      651
          Director or the Registrar and to discharge such functions under this Act
          as it may specify, by notification.".

91.2 Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (The Companies Act, 2013):
396. Registration offices.--

   (1) *     *     *       *     *     *

         (2) The Central Government may appoint such Registrars, Additional, Joint,
Deputy and Assistant Registrars as it considers necessary for the registration of
companies and discharge of various functions under this Act, and the powers and
duties that may be exercisable by such officers shall be such as may be prescribed.

*         *     *     *       *     *                                    *

91.3 Reasons / Justification given by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs for the
proposed provision:

         "The amendment to section 396 enables the Central Government to appoint
Regional Directors, Additional Regional Directors, Joint Regional Directors and other
officers, in addition to existing Registrar-level officers, and to authorise officers to
exercise specified powers and functions under the Act."

91.4 Important Views/Suggestions given by Experts/Stakeholders:

        A stakeholder suggested that clause 91 be retained, subject to the
modification that the authorisation under the proposed sub-section (2A) shall not
extend to adjudicatory or quasi- judicial functions of the Regional Director, which
shall be exercised only by officers of the rank of Regional Director or above.

                      652
91.5 Examination by the Committee:

91.5.1 While declining the suggestion related to modification of the rule-making
power of the Central Government, the Ministry of Corporate Affairs reasoned that :

         "The proposed framework already contains adequate institutional safeguards
        to ensure fairness and consistency in adjudication. The rank of adjudicating
        officers has been prescribed keeping in view the nature of in-house
        adjudication, the volume of cases, and the need for timely disposal. Further,
        prescribing a statutory timeline for notifying the transition Scheme and
        mandating its placement before Parliament is not considered necessary, as
        the Central Government retains the flexibility to notify the Scheme in a timely
        manner based on implementation requirements. Hence, the amendment
        under the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 may be retained without
        any change."

91.5.2 During the examination, the Ministry of Corporate Affairs apprised the
Committee that within sub-clause (c) of Clause 91, the officers being referred to in
the phrase "or such other officers" are already covered in sub-clause (b), namely,
Regional Directors, Additional Regional Directors or Joint Regional Directors or
Deputy Regional Directors. Therefore, the Ministry proposed that sub-clause (c) may
be deleted.

91.5.3 Further, provisions proposed under Clause 91(d) [Section 396] confer rule-
making power on the Central Government to authorize an officer for exercising
powers and duties of Regional Director under the Act. In this regard, the Ministry
stated that:

        "Clause 91 of the Bill empowers the Central Government to prescribe, under
        sub-section (1A) of section 396 of the Companies Act, 2013, the powers and
        duties that may be exercisable by the Regional Directors, Additional Regional
        Directors or Joint Regional Directors or Deputy Regional Directors, appointed
        by the Central Government for discharge of various functions under the
        Companies Act, 2013."

91.5.4 Elaborating on the rationale behind this delegation of rule-making power, the
Ministry also apprised the Committee as under:

                                                      653
        "This proposes to prescribe the powers and duties of the officers recognised in
        the statute. This is a form of domain specific delegation. While the law
        mandates the appointment of various regional directors to oversee the Act, it
        leaves the specific powers and duties of these officials to be prescribed by the
        Central Government, allowing for operational flexibility as administrative roles
        evolve."

91.6 Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

The Committee scrutinized the proposed Clause 91 thoroughly and find that it
provides for amendments to Section 396 of the Companies Act, 2013, by giving
statutory recognition to various cadres of Regional Directors and empowering
the Central Government to authorize officers not below the rank of Assistant
Director or Assistant Registrar to exercise the powers of a Regional Director or
Registrar. It also modifies the marginal heading of the Section to explicitly
cover centralized processing and specialized administrative offices.

The Committee observe that leaving the specific powers and administrative
duties of these officers to rules framed thereunder provides necessary
operational flexibility to handle expanding case volumes and evolving
governance needs.

While acknowledging the functional utility of this delegation, the Committee
emphasize that the subordinate legislative framework must strictly operate
within the boundaries of the parent statute without impinging upon the primary
legislative mandate. Accordingly, the Committee recommend that the Ministry
of Corporate Affairs ensure the subordinate legislative framework is

                                                      654
formulated in a timely, transparent, and consultative manner to facilitate
effective and coherent implementation.

The Committee further observe that sub-clause (c) proposing to insert the
phrase "or such other officers" is already covered in sub-clause (b).
Accordingly, the Committee recommend that sub-clause (c) be deleted;
consequently, sub-clause (d) be renumbered as sub-clause "(c)"; and Clause
91 be modified as follows :

"In section 396 of the principal Act,

         (a) in the marginal heading, for the word "offices", the words "and other
offices" shall be substituted;

         (b) after sub-section (1), the following sub-section shall be inserted,
namely:-

(1A) The Central Government may appoint such number of Regional Directors,
Additional Regional Directors or Joint Regional Directors or Deputy Regional
Directors as it considers necessary for discharge of various functions under
this Act, and the powers and duties that may be exercisable by such officers
shall be such as may be prescribed." ;

(c) in sub-section (2), after the words "Assistant Registrars", the words "or
such other officers" shall be inserted;

                                                      655
(cd) after sub-section (2), the following sub-section shall be inserted, namely:-
"(2A) The Central Government may authorise one or more officers not below
the rank of Assistant Director or Assistant Registrar of that Government to
exercise such powers and duties of the Regional Director or the Registrar and
to discharge such functions under this Act as it may specify, by notification."
Subject to the aforementioned modification, the Committee accept the
remaining provisions under Clause 91, as proposed.

                                                      656
                                               CLAUSE - 92

92 Clause 92 of the Bill seeks to insert a new Section 396A of the
Companies Act, 2013.

92.1 Provision proposed in The Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

After section 396 of the principal Act, the following section shall be inserted,
namely:-- "396A. Any person aggrieved by the decision of the Registrar under
section 4 or section 7, may prefer an appeal to an officer not below the rank of the
Joint Director as may be authorised by the Central Government, in such form and
manner, and within such period as may be prescribed.".

92.2 Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (The Companies Act, 2013):

No existing provision in the principal Act as this clause is proposed to be newly
inserted.

92.3 Reasons / Justification given by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs for the
proposed provision:

         "Through new section 396A, it is proposed that a person aggrieved by a
decision of the Registrar or the Central Registration Centre (CRC) on name
reservation or incorporation of companies may prefer an appeal to an officer not
below the rank of Joint Director, in the prescribed form, manner and within the
prescribed period."

92.4 Important Views/Suggestions given by Experts/Stakeholders:

Some of the important suggestions given by stakeholders are as follows :

         92.4.1 An appellate mechanism may be provided before High Courts against
        orders of Registrar of Companies (ROC) / Regional Directors (RD) / National
        Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT).

                                                      657
        92.4.2 The clause 92 may be retained, subject to the modification that the
        authorization under the proposed sub-section (2A) of Section 396 shall not
        extend to adjudicatory or quasi- judicial functions of the Regional Director,
        which shall be exercised only by officers of the rank of Regional Director or
        above.

92.5 Examination by the Committee:

92.5.1 While declining the suggestion to provide an appellate mechanism before
High Courts against orders passed by the ROC/RD/NCLAT, the Ministry of Corporate
Affairs reasoned that:

         "The Companies Act, 2013 already provides a structured appellate framework
        against orders passed by Registrars of Companies and Regional Directors,
        with appeals lying before the Regional Director, the National Company Law
        Tribunal (NCLT), the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT), or
        the Central Government, as applicable under the Act. The newly inserted
        Section 396A itself provides that any person aggrieved by a decision of the
        Registrar under section 4 or section 7 may prefer an appeal to an officer not
        below the rank of Joint Director, as authorised by the Central Government.
        Further, orders of the NCLAT are already appealable to the Supreme Court on
        questions of law under section 423 of the Act. Introducing an additional
        appellate forum before the High Courts for administrative or penal orders
        would create parallel appellate mechanisms, increase litigation, and be
        inconsistent with the existing statutory scheme. Hence, the provision in the
        Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 may be retained without any
        change."

92.5.2 While turning down the suggestion to modify sub-section (2A) of Section 396
to prohibit lower-ranked officers from exercising quasi-judicial functions, the Ministry
submitted that:-

         "Proposed section 396A provides for an appeal to an officer not below the
        rank of Joint Director on decision of ROC on name reservation or
        incorporation of companies."

92.5.3 During their oral deposition before the Committee, the representatives of the
Ministry of Corporate Affairs explained that if an applicant has a grievance because
their application for name reservation or incorporation is rejected, they currently lack
an appeal mechanism, therefore, this provision is being introduced.

                                                      658
92.5.4 Provisions proposed under Clause 92 [Section 396A] confer rule-making
power on the Central Government for prescribing the form and manner in which an
appeal can be made by an aggrieved person under this clause. In this regard, the
Ministry submitted that:

        "Clause 92 of the Bill empowers the Central Government to prescribe, under
        section 396A of the Companies Act, 2013, the form and manner in which and
        the period within which any person aggrieved by the decision of the Registrar
        under section 7 of the Companies Act, 2013, may prefer an appeal to an
        officer not below the rank of the Joint Director, as may be authorised by the
        Central Government."

92.5.5 Elaborating on the rationale behind this delegation of rule-making power, the
Ministry also apprised the Committee that this proposes to prescribe the form,
manner and period for filing appeals. These provisions demonstrate that the
delegation is directed at procedural flexibility and does not affect substantive
compliance of the law.

92.6 Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

On scrutinizing Clause 92 of the Bill, which seeks to insert a new Section 396A
into the Companies Act, 2013, the Committee find that it provides a dedicated
statutory appellate mechanism against decisions of the Registrar under
Section 4 or Section 7. Under this newly inserted provision, any aggrieved
person may prefer an appeal to an officer not below the rank of Joint Director.

The Committee note that this provision fills a crucial gap in administrative
redressal. Determining statutory appellate hierarchies falls squarely within the
legislative domain. Since the Act already provides established remedies
through the Regional Director, NCLT, NCLAT, and Supreme Court, creating a
parallel appellate route to High Courts is unnecessary and would disrupt the

                                                      659
existing statutory framework. The Committee, therefore, do not concur with the
suggestion to introduce an appellate forum before High Courts.
With regard to the rule-making power for prescribing the form, manner, and
time limits for filing appeals, the Committee observe that placing procedural
details in rules provides essential administrative flexibility. However, to ensure
that this appellate mechanism is fully effective and accessible, the Committee
desire that the Ministry formulate these procedural rules in timely consultation
with relevant stakeholders, keeping the appeal process simple, transparent,
and user-friendly.
Upon due consideration of the stakeholder representations alongside the
clarifications furnished by the Ministry, the Committee agree with the proposed
provisions and recommend that Clause 92 may be accepted without any
modification.

         INSERTION OF NEW PROVISION

92A New insertion proposed with regard to rectification in documents filed
with the Registrar.

92A.1 Examination by the Committee:

92A.1.1  During the examination of the Bill, the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, in

their written submissions, apprised the Committee of the procedural necessity to

provide with a statutory mechanism to rectify inadvertent clerical, arithmetical,

typographical, or factual errors and omissions in documents filed with the registry by

submitting a formal application.

92A.1.2  The Ministry further informed the Committee that such an enabling

provision needs to be inserted after Section 398 of the Principal Act, which relates to

the filing of applications, documents, and inspection, etc. in electronic form.

92A.2 Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

         The Committee observe that companies should be provided with an
appropriate and transparent statutory mechanism to rectify clerical,
arithmetical, typographical, or factual errors and omissions in documents or
information filed with the Registrar.

         The Committee are of the view that permitting such rectifications
through a prescribed application process would facilitate the prompt
correction of bona fide mistakes, significantly reduce unnecessary
administrative and legal burdens, and preserve the overall accuracy, integrity,
and reliability of statutory records maintained by the Registrar.

         Accordingly, the Committee propose that the following provisions be

suitably inserted after Clause 92 (after 398 of the Principal Act) of the Bill:
                                                      661
"398A. Rectification in documents filed with Registrar.

         (1) Where a company or any person has filed any document under the
provisions of the Act or rules made thereunder, after payment of fees in
accordance with section 403 (herein referred to as the "initial document"), and
it comes to the knowledge of the said company or such person, as the case
may be, that the initial document contains a clerical, calculation or
typographical error, the company or such person may, apply for rectification of
such error by filing an application and the rectified document with the
Registrar in such form and manner, and on payment of such fee, as may be
prescribed.

         (2) Unless otherwise directed by a competent court or Tribunal, the
initial document shall not be removed from the registry after the registration of
the rectified document.

         (3) No rectification under sub-section (1) shall be permitted where the
error -

                (a) is in relation to a company against which any proceeding under
                Chapter XIV is ongoing;

                (b) is in relation to creation, modification or satisfaction of charge,
                unless a prior approval of the charge-holder has been obtained;

                (c) is not apparent on the face of the initial document; and

                (d) in case, a period of one year has expired from the date of filing
                of the initial document.

         (4) Every rectified document filed under this section shall be
accompanied by a certificate from a director or the company secretary of the
company, and, where the initial document was certified by a company

                                                      662
secretary, chartered accountant or cost accountant, in practice, by such
practising professional, stating --

                (a) the nature of the error and the reason for its occurrence; and
                (b) that the rectification does not have the effect of
                misrepresenting the affairs of the company as they stood on the
                date of the initial document.
         (5) Nothing in this section shall --
                (a) apply to the revision of financial statements or report of the
                Board, which shall be governed by section 131;
                (b) be construed to limit or extinguish any liability of the company
                or of any officer in default, or any other person under any provision
                of this Act in respect of any error or omission, where such error or
                omission was not bona fide; or
                (c) entitle a company to any refund, set-off, or reduction of fee or
                additional fee already paid in respect of the initial document."

         INSERTION OF NEW PROVISION

92B New insertion proposed with regard to application of provisions of
Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023.

92B.1 Examination by the Committee:

92B.1.1  During the examination of the Bill, the Ministry of Electronics and

Information Technology (MeitY) submitted written suggestions regarding the

applicability of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 as under :

"Certain amendments may involve collection, storage and processing of digital
personal data relating to directors, shareholders, employees, auditors,
professionals and other individuals interacting with companies or regulatory
authorities.

MeitY notes that processing of digital personal data, wherever covered under
the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, would be required to comply
with the applicable provisions of that Act and the rules framed thereunder.
Accordingly, implementation frameworks developed under the Companies Act
may be designed in a manner that facilitates harmonised compliance with both
legislative frameworks.

The Ministry does not consider any amendment to the Bill necessary on this
account. Appropriate operational guidance may, wherever required, be
addressed through subordinate legislation or administrative instructions."

92B.1.2  Further, MeitY submitted the following observations regarding the

integration of cybersecurity protocols with statutory governance frameworks:

"Any directions, guidelines or circulars issued under the proposed provision
may, wherever digital systems are involved, appropriately incorporate
cybersecurity requirements, electronic record management practices and
technical safeguards consistent with applicable Government cybersecurity
policies.."

                                     664
92B.1.3  Regarding data protection and ensuring cyber security measures, the

representatives of MeitY, during their oral deposition, apprised the Committee as

under:

        "Overall, MeitY supports the Bill's digital transition. We are fully in line with
        whatever has been specified regarding electronic communication, websites,
        electronic service, video conferencing and other modes. It aligns with the
        overall Government's policy of pushing for more paperless governance and for
        the objective of Digital India. Thereafter, it is important also that electronic
        records, the chain of custody and the manner in which the records are dealt
        with, is important to preserve the accountability framework and that is
        something which needs to be maintained.

        Of course, there is an issue of processing of some personal data, including of
        directors, shareholders and other stakeholders of the company. Now, these
        need to comply with the provisions of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act,
        2023 wherever it is applicable. There are interfaces, and we are assuming that
        wherever such personal data is maintained, it will be maintained in
        accordance with the DPDP Act, which basically requires consent and the
        consent framework would be maintained.

        Any proposed rules which will eventually be put out need to be aligned with
        the detailed guidelines which CERT-In has issued on cyber security issues,
        which is why I requested that there should be a consultation with MeitY when
        the rules are finalised. Clearly, it is important that the IT systems are
        maintained in a very stable and secure fashion because the evidentiary value
        of these documents is important. Eventually, it becomes a part of that."

92B.1.4  During their deposition, the representatives of MeitY cautioned that

greater dependence on digital platforms may increase exposure to unauthorised

access, record manipulation, ransomware, phishing, credential compromise and

service disruption. They suggested safeguards such as - secure architecture,

encryption where appropriate, access controls, logging, vulnerability management,

business continuity and periodic security assessments. The representatives also

apprised that MeitY would provide technical assistance in the matter.

92B.1.5  MeitY further reiterated that as the amendments proposed under the

Bill involve processing personal data of directors, shareholders, employees, auditors

and professionals, compliance with the DPDP Act, 2023 where applicable must be

         665
ensured, with operational guidance through subordinate legislation or administrative
instructions.

92B.1.6  In addition, during the course of examination, the Ministry of Corporate

Affairs in their written submissions apprised the Committee that a provision is

required to be inserted in the Bill specifically, instead of inserting provisos to the

existing Sections 398 to 401, to ensure that any processing of personal data when

filing documents with the Registrar of Companies and right to inspect such records is

in line with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023.

92B.2 Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

92B.2.1 The Committee observe that with the accelerated digitalization of
corporate filings and electronic record management, it is paramount to ensure
that the collection, storage, and processing of digital personal data--
pertaining to directors, shareholders, employees, auditors, professionals, and
other stakeholders--are protected in strict conformity with the Digital Personal
Data Protection Act, 2023.

The Committee further emphasize that embedding robust cybersecurity
protocols, electronic record management standards, and technical safeguards
in line with applicable national cybersecurity policies is essential to preserve
system integrity and the evidentiary value of digital corporate records.

The Committee concur with the view that a dedicated statutory provision must
be inserted into the Bill to ensure that the processing of personal data during
document filings with the Registrar of Companies, as well as public access

         666
and inspection rights, strictly adheres to the mandates of the Digital Personal
Data Protection Act, 2023.

Accordingly, the Committee propose that the following provision be suitably
inserted in the Bill:

"Application of provisions of Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023.

         402A. All provisions of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
and the rules made thereunder relating to consent and the processing of
digital personal data, in so far as they are not inconsistent with this Act, shall
apply in relation to the records in electronic form specified under Sections 398
to 401."

To ensure a secure and legally sound digital framework, the Committee
recommend that the aforesaid provision may be inserted into the Bill as a new
`Clause 92B', immediately following Clause 90.

92B.2.2. With respect to the subordinate rule-making powers under
proposed `Clause 92B', the Committee observe that detailed rules, directions,
guidelines, and circulars will be required to govern the technical and security
operations of digital systems.

The Committee, therefore, recommend that the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, in
consultation with the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
(MeitY) and other relevant stakeholders, ensure that the subordinate legislative

                                                      667
framework is formulated in a timely and transparent manner, maintaining
necessary alignment and operational coherence to facilitate the effective
implementation of the proposed provisions.

                                               CLAUSE - 93

93 Clause 93 of the Bill seeks to amend Section 403 of the Companies Act,
2013.

93.1 Provision proposed in The Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 :

In section 403 of the principal Act, in sub-section (1),--

              (a) in the first proviso, for the words "shall not be less than one hundred
        rupees per day", the words "shall not be less than such amount per day as
        may be prescribed" shall be substituted;

              (b) in the second proviso, for the words "Provided further", the following
        shall be substituted, namely:--

                  "Provided further that the amount of additional fees shall not exceed
            two lakh rupees for such class or classes of companies, as may be
            prescribed:

                  Provided also".

93.2 Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (The Companies Act, 2013):

403. Fee for filing, etc.--(1) Any document, required to be submitted, filed, registered
or recorded, or any fact or information required or authorised to be registered under
this Act, shall be submitted, filed, registered or recorded within the time specified in
the relevant provision on payment of such fee as may be prescribed:

         Provided that where any document, fact or information required to be
submitted, filed, registered or recorded, as the case may be, under section 92 or 137
is not submitted, filed, registered or recorded, as the case may be, within the period
provided in those sections, without prejudice to any other legal action or liability
under this Act, it may be submitted, filed, registered or recorded, as the case may be,
after expiry of the period so provided in those sections, on payment of such

                                                      669
additional fee as may be prescribed, which shall not be less than one hundred
rupees per day and different amounts may be prescribed for different classes of
companies:

         Provided further that where the document, fact or information, as the case
may be, in cases other than referred to in the first proviso, is not submitted, filed,
registered or recorded, as the case may be, within the period provided in the relevant
section, it may, without prejudice to any other legal action or liability under this Act,
be submitted, filed, registered or recorded as the case may be, on payment of such
additional fee as may be prescribed and different fees may be prescribed for different
classes of companies:

*  *  *  *  *  *  *

93.3 Reasons / Justification given by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs for the
proposed provision:

         "This clause proposes to amend section 403 to provide flexibility in prescribing
the quantum of additional fees for delayed filings and to introduce a cap on such
fees. It enables prescription of lower daily additional fees for such class or classes of
companies, as may be prescribed, and limits the total additional fees to 2 lakh
rupees."

93.4 Important Views/Suggestions given by Experts/Stakeholders:

Some of the important suggestions given by stakeholders are as follows:

        93.4.1 "Cap fees to 1-5x of normal filing fee; remove daily penalties. Caps
        proposed are too high for small Companies."

         93.4.2 "Increase the cap and provide a mandatory fee-waiver "Downtime
        Certificate" when the MCA portal is officially unavailable."

         93.4.3 "Graduated Severity Ladder for Decriminalised Defaults (Section
         450/403) - The decriminalisation reform under Section 450 does not sort
         defaults by gravity, so genuinely harmful conduct may be under-deterred while
         trivial, curable lapses attract disproportionate penalties. A four-category
         graduated severity ladder (Schedule XX) is proposed distinguishing

                                                      670
         procedural/rectifiable defaults (additional fee only), governance/non-disclosure
         defaults (civil penalty), interested party/related-party defaults (enhanced civil
         penalty), and fraudulent or public-interest-harming conduct (prosecution only),
         with reasoned orders and a defined limitation period."

93.5 Examination by the Committee:

93.5.1 While declining the suggestion to remove daily penalties and cap additional
fees at 1-5 times the normal filing fee to reduce the burden on small companies, the
Ministry of Corporate Affairs submitted that:

         "The proposed amendment enables prescription of additional fee per day in
        subordinate legislation with different amount for different companies. Further,
        while the present regime does not prescribe an upper limit, the Amendment
        Bill proposes to cap the additional fee payable for delayed filing of financial
        statements under Section 137 and annual returns under Section 92 for
        prescribed classes of companies, including OPCs, small companies start ups
        and producer companies, as per the rationale accompanying the Amendment
        Bill. Accordingly, retaining continuous daily additional fees, subject to an upper
        ceiling, as is prescribed under the current Amendment Bill, may ensure
        proportionality of fees while promoting compliance under the Companies Act,
        2013."

93.5.2 While noting the suggestion to introduce a mandatory 'Downtime Certificate'
waiving additional fees during official MCA portal outages and adjusting fee caps, the
Ministry of Corporate Affairs responded that:

        "Suggestion will be considered appropriately during framing of subordinate
        legislation. The suggestion relates to operational aspects of the MCA filing
        portal, including provision of a downtime certificate and waiver of additional
        fees in cases of official system unavailability. As these matters pertain to the
        administration and implementation of the electronic filing system and do not
        require an amendment to the Act, they may be considered separately, as
        appropriate. Hence, the provision in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill,
        2026 may be retained without change."

93.5.3 While turning down the proposal for graduated severity ladder for
decriminalized defaults, the Ministry submitted that:

         "The proposed penalty framework under Section 450 is intended to provide a
        simple, uniform and proportionate mechanism for dealing with residual

                                                      671
        contraventions. Introducing multiple categories of defaults and separate
        penalty structures would add complexity and reduce consistency in
        enforcement. Serious violations involving fraud or public interest continue to
        be dealt with under the specific provisions of the Companies Act."

93.5.4 Detailing the long-term impact of the amendments proposed under Clause 93,
the representatives of the Ministry, during their oral deposition, explained that:

        "Clause 93, which amends Section 403 regarding filing fees. Currently, there
        are two primary returns - the annual return and the financial statement. If
        these two returns are not filed on time, there is an additional daily late fee of
        Rs. 100. This Rs. 100 delay fee accumulates for every single day of the delay
        without any upper limit. Because of this, small companies have been raising
        grievances that a delay of one or two years leads to an exorbitant
        accumulated penalty. They have requested a cap on this amount, which is
        what this proposal introduces. This will be highly beneficial for small
        companies."

93.5.5 Provisions proposed under Clause 93 (Section 403) confer rule-making power
on the Central Government for prescribing the amount payable per day regarding
contravention of the provisions as well as such class of companies for which the
additional fees is capped. In this regard, the Ministry has stated that:

        "Clause 93 of the Bill empowers the Central Government to prescribe, under
        the first proviso to sub-section (1) of section 403 of the Companies Act, 2013,
        the amount per day payable for submitting, filing, registering or recording any
        document, fact or information after expiry of the period provided under
        sections 92 or 137. It further empowers the Central Government to prescribe,
        under the second proviso to sub-section (1) of section 403, such class and
        classes of companies, for which the amount of additional fees shall not
        exceed two lakh rupees."

93.5.6 Elaborating on the rationale behind this delegation of rule-making power, the
Ministry also apprised the Committee as under:

        "This proposes to prescribe the amount per day payable for submitting, filing,
        registering or recording any document, fact or information after expiry of the
        period. It further proposes to prescribe such class and classes of companies,
        for which the amount of additional fees shall not exceed two lakh rupees. As
        far as prescription of fees is concerned, same is subject to periodic revision

                                                      672
        based on inflation, administrative cost, and market conditions. Embedding
        these in primary legislation would render the statute inflexible and quickly
        outdated. The use of "class or classes" is a well-established legislative device
        in corporate law, enabling dynamic calibration without frequent statutory
        amendments. The essential policy, i.e., that differential compliance may be
        warranted, is determined by the legislature; only the identification and periodic
        revision of such classes is delegated."

93.6 Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

On examining Clause 93 of the Bill, the Committee observe that it seeks to
amend sub-section (1) of Section 403 of the Companies Act, 2013, by replacing
the rigid minimum late fee of "one hundred rupees per day" for delayed filings
under Sections 92 and 137 with a flexible, prescribed daily amount.

Furthermore, it introduces an upper ceiling capping total additional fees at two
lakh rupees for prescribed classes of companies, thereby mitigating long-
standing concerns regarding disproportionate and endlessly accumulating
penalties on small enterprises.

Regarding operational grievances concerning technical outages on the MCA
filing portal, the Committee emphasize that stakeholders must not be
penalized for administrative or system failures beyond their control. While
taking note of the Ministry's assurance that relief--such as fee waivers during
official downtime--will be provided through subordinate legislation, the
Committee expect the Ministry to strictly abide by this commitment and
incorporate clear, mandatory procedural mechanisms in the rules to address
portal unavailability.

                                                      673
In delegating the authority to fix daily fees and categorize eligible entities, the
Committee note the necessity of balancing compliance deterrence with the
ease of doing business. The Committee accordingly urge the Ministry to frame
and notify these rules in a timely manner following meaningful consultation
with stakeholders, ensuring objective criteria are established so that Small
Companies, One Person Companies, Start-ups, and Producer Companies
obtain the full benefit of calibrated fees and the statutory ceiling.
In view of the assurances given by the Ministry and the overall merit of the
proposed statutory changes, the Committee, after thorough deliberations,
accept Clause 93 as proposed in entirety.

         INSERTION OF NEW PROVISION

93A New insertion proposed with regard to refund of fees or any other
payment.

93A.1 Examination by the Committee:

93A.1.1  The Ministry of Corporate Affairs, in their written submissions, apprised

the Committee of the necessity to provide statutory backing for the refund of fees

paid during the registration or filing of forms and documents. The Ministry stated that,

at present, cases where filing or registration cannot be completed due to technical

reasons are governed by an administrative refund manual. Therefore, in order to

provide statutory backing to this process, a new provision is required to be inserted

after Section 403 of the Companies Act, 2013.

93A.2 Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

93A.2.1 The Committee observe that it is essential to provide companies
with an explicit statutory entitlement to claim a refund of fees or payments
made for the registration or filing of forms and documents in situations where
such filings could not be successfully completed due to technical reasons or
operational glitches.

The Committee note that while such refund claims are currently governed by
an administrative refund manual issued by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs,
embedding a specific statutory framework into the Act would ensure greater
clarity, administrative transparency, and legal certainty, thereby preventing
avoidable financial burden on stakeholders.

                                                      675
To establish a transparent and seamless process for processing refunds, the
Committee propose that the following provisions may be inserted into the Bill
as a new `Clause 93A', following Clause 93 and after Section 403 of the
Principal Act :-

"403A. Refund of fees or any other payment.

         (1) An application may be filed for the refund of fees paid in pursuance
of section 403, or any payment made to the Consolidated Fund of India under
this Act, except in cases where such refunds are governed by any other
provisions of the Act or the rules made thereunder, on the following grounds,
namely :-

                 (a) fees is paid without successful filing of any form;
                 (b) penalty or fees has been paid twice for the same instance;
                 or
                 (c) other grounds as may be prescribed.
         (2) The application referred to in sub-section (1) shall be submitted in
such form and manner as may be prescribed.

         (3) No refund shall be paid, unless the application referred to in sub
section (1) is filed within a period of three years, or such other period, as may
be prescribed.

                                                      676
         (4) The Central Government may make rules for the purposes of this
section."
93A.2.2 With respect to the subordinate rule-making powers under the
proposed `Clause 93A', the Committee recommend that the Ministry of
Corporate Affairs, in consultation with relevant stakeholders, ensure that the
rules and operational procedures governing refund applications are
formulated and notified in a time-bound manner.

94A. Insertion of amendment to Section 415 of the Companies Act, 2013

94A.1.Examination by the Committee:

94A.4.1. During the course of examination of the Bill, with respect to the issue of
filing any casual vacancy for the post of President arising in NCLT or NCLAT, the
representatives of the Ministry of Corporate Affairs clarified that the senior most
Judicial member will preside over.

In this regard, the representatives of Ministry deposed as follows:

"    10         415    , 
             ,     
     ,    ,        ,
                
           ,      
  ,              
           ,      
"

94A.2.Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

The Committee note that presently there is no clear framework to deal with the
casual vacancy arsing for the post of President in NCLT or NCLAT which may
impact the functioning of the Tribunals.

The Committee further note that the express identification of the senior-most
Judicial Member as the acting head of the Tribunal or the Appellate Tribunal
would strengthen institutional certainty, ensure continuity in the
administration of justice, uphold the judicial character and independence of
these specialised fora and eliminate the scope for differing interpretations that
may otherwise arise under the existing provisions.

                                                      680
Therefore, the Committee, emphasise that an amendment to section 415 of the
Companies Act, 2013 is warranted to remove any ambiguity regarding the
person who shall assume charge during an interim vacancy. Thus, the word
"judicial" after the words "senior-most" in sub-sections (1) and (2) may be
inserted, so as to expressly provide that, in the event of a casual vacancy in
the office of the President of the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) or the
Chairperson of the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT), the
senior-most Judicial Member shall discharge the functions of the respective
office until a regular appointment is made.

Accordingly, the section 415 of the Companies Act, may be amended as
follows:

"In section 415 of the principal Act, --
(a) in sub-section (1), after the words "senior-most", the word "judicial" shall
be inserted;
(b) in sub-section (2), after the words "senior-most", the word "judicial" shall
be inserted."
The Committee, therefore, recommend that the proposed amendment to
section 415 of Companies Act, 2013 may be suitably inserted as Clause 94A in
the Bill.

by empowering the Chairperson to refer disputed points to additional
members, with the final outcome determined by a cumulative majority.

96.2. Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (The Companies Act, 2013):

419. Benches of Tribunal

(1)  *                     *       *       *  *

         (4) The Central Government shall, by notification, establish such number of
benches of the Tribunal, as it may consider necessary, to exercise the jurisdiction,
powers and authority of the Adjudicating Authority conferred on such Tribunal by or
under Part II of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016.

     *                     *       *       *  *

96.3. Reasons/Justification given by the Ministry for the proposed provisions:

                              684
"This clause proposes to enable constitution of Special Benches of the NCLT for
disposal of specific matters under the Act and the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code,
2016, including cases such as mergers."

96.4. Important Views/Suggestions given by Experts/Stakeholders:

         During the course of the examination of the Bill, various suggestions received
from the stakeholders are mentioned as under:

96.4.1.  "Insert the following proviso after Section 419(4):

`Provided that where circumstances so warrant, the President may, for reasons to be
recorded in writing, authorise any Bench of the Tribunal to exercise jurisdiction in
respect of matters arising within the territorial jurisdiction of any other Bench of the
Tribunal'."

96.4.2.  "It is recommended that the clauses be retained, subject to the

clarification that every Special Bench constituted under the proposed sub-section

(4A) shall include at least one Judicial Member."

96.5. Examination by the Committee:

96.5.1.  Regarding the suggestion in Para 96.4.1 for the Tribunal to record

reasons in writing, the Ministry declined to accept the proposal, clarifying that a

similar issue is currently pending before the Court and a decision on the matter will

be taken only after the judicial outcome.

96.5.2.  Further, regarding the suggestion in the above Para 96.4.2. related to

ensuring one Judicial Member as part of the Special Bench proposed under

proposed Section419(4A), the Ministry in its written response refused to accept the

suggestion as Section 419 (3) of Companies Act, 2013 provides that every bench

shall consist of two members out whom one shall be a judicial member. Hence, the

provision in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 may be retained without any

change.

                                           685
96.5.3.      Regarding the delegation of procedural details under newly inserted

Section 419(4A), the Ministry clarified that Clause 96 empowers the Central

Government to prescribe the manner in which the President may constitute Special

Benches to dispose of cases under the Companies Act, 2013 or the Insolvency and

Bankruptcy Code, 2016.

96.5.4       Elaborating on the rationale, the Ministry further stated that this

delegation is aimed purely at providing operational and procedural flexibility without

compromising substantive compliance with the law.

96.5.5.      Also, during the course of the examination of the Bill, on the specific

issue asked by the Committee regarding the increase in number of benches of the

Tribunals, the Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs deposed before the Committee

as follows:

"As far as number of benches have to be increased,     
........................       ,       
  /    ,       "

96.6. Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

96.6.1.      The Committee note that Clause 96 of the Bill amends Section

419(4) to cover all provisions of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016

and inserts sub-section (4A) empowering the President of NCLT to constitute

Special Benches for specific cases.

The Committee observe that this removes statutory loopholes, declutters
backlogs, and provides operational fluidity, provided that adequate staffing
and personnel training are prioritized.

                                     686
The Committee, therefore, emphasize that apart from regular benches dealing
with cases of corporate laws, mergers, acquisitions, specialised dedicated
Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC) Benches must be established through
a binding statutory obligation rather than an enabling administrative option. A
clear statutory separation of judicial architecture is essential to enforce
institutional accountability and achieve a balanced distribution of workload.
Dedicated Benches focused solely on insolvency matters would guarantee
strict adherence to statutory resolution timelines, which would significantly
help to avoid value erosion of distressed assets in IBC cases. Simultaneously,
this would insulate regular Benches from unplanned procedural urgencies,
thereby enabling them to devote focused attention to routine corporate
reorganizations, mergers, and conversions in a predictable and time-bound
manner.

In view of the foregoing, the Committee recommend that in the proposed sub-
section (4A) of Section 419, the words "may, if he considers appropriate," be
substituted by the words "shall" and the sub-section may be modified as
follows so as to establish specialised dedicated benches dealing with matters
related to IBC, 2016 apart from regular benches dealing with matters related to
Companies Act, 2013:

"(4A) The President may, if he considers appropriate shall constitute in such
manner as may be prescribed, one or more Special Benches of the Tribunal to
exercise the powers of the Tribunal for the disposal of any case or cases under
this Act, or under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016.

Provided that the President may, if he considers appropriate, constitute in
such manner as may be prescribed, one or more Special Benches of the
Tribunal to exercise the powers of the Tribunal for the disposal of any case or
cases under this Act."

Subject to the above amendments, the Committee recommend acceptance of
Clause 96.

                                                      687
96.6.2.  The Committee observe that time is of the essence in corporate

restructuring and insolvency resolution, and procedural delays inevitably lead

to severe asset value erosion. The Committee, therefore, recommend that the

Ministry of Corporate Affairs take urgent steps to increase the number of

benches of the Tribunals, thereby ensuring rapid disposal of backlogs, strict

adherence to statutory timeframes, and optimum value preservation.

                                 INSERTION OF NEW PROVISION

96A. Insertion of amendment to amend Section 439 of the Companies Act,
2013

96A.1.Examination by the Committee:

During the course of the examination of the Bill, in context of the issue of enabling
National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA) to file complaint against any other
person before the competent court, the Ministry of Corporate Affairs stated that the
issue will be addressed through suitable amendment in section 439 of the
Companies Act, 2013.

96A.2.Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

The Committee note that there is a need to remove ambiguity regarding the
filing of complaints against any other person who may be liable for offences
under the Companies Act, 2013 and to expressly confer statutory authority
upon the National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA) to initiate complaints
before the competent Court. This would facilitate timely and effective
prosecution of offences arising from its investigations, minimise procedural
uncertainties and reinforce the credibility of the regulatory and enforcement
mechanism.

The Committee, therefore, recommend that section 439 of the Companies Act,
2013 may be amended by inserting the words "or any other person" after the
words "any officer thereof" in sub-section (2) so that all persons who are liable
under the relevant provisions of the Act are subject to an unambiguous and
uniform procedural framework for prosecution.

Further, the Courts may also be empowered to take cognizance of offences
under clause (a) of sub-section (4A) of section 132 on a complaint in writing
made by a person authorised by the NFRA.

                                                      689
The Committee are of the considered view that these amendments would
promote legal certainty and strengthen the effectiveness of corporate
regulatory enforcement governing corporate financial reporting and audit
oversight. This would also facilitate coordinated action between investigative
and adjudicatory authorities without altering the substantive safeguards
available under the law.
Accordingly, section 439 of the Companies Act, may be amended as follows:
"In section 439 of the principal Act, -
(a) in sub-section (2), after the words "any officer thereof", the word "or any
other person" shall be inserted;
(b) in sub-section (2), the following proviso shall be inserted after the second
proviso -
Provided also that the Court may take cognizance of offences under clause (a)
of sub-section (4A) of Section 132 of this Act, on a complaint in writing, by a
person authorised by the National Financial Reporting Authority."
The Committee, therefore, after in-depth analysis, recommend suitable
insertion of amendments to section 439 of the Companies Act, 2013 as Clause
96A in the Bill.

                          CLAUSE - 97

97. Clause 97 of the Bill seeks to amend Section 441 of the Companies Act,
2013

97.1. Provision proposed in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

Amendment of Section 441

In section 441 of the principal Act, in sub-section (1), in clause (b), for the words
"does not exceed twenty-five lakh rupees", the words "does not exceed one crore
rupees" shall be substituted.

97.2. Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (The Companies Act, 2013):

441. (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973, any offence punishable under this Act (whether committed by a company or
any officer thereof) not being an offence punishable with imprisonment only, or
punishable with imprisonment and also with fine, may, either before or after the
institution of any prosecution, be compounded by--

*  *                      *  *         *  *

         (b) where the maximum amount of fine which may be imposed for such
offence does not exceed twenty-five lakh rupees, by the Regional Director or any
officer authorised by the Central Government, on payment or credit, by the company
or, as the case may be, the officer, to the Central Government of such sum as that
Tribunal or the Regional Director or any officer authorised by the Central
Government, as the case may be, may specify:

Provided that the sum so specified shall not, in any case, exceed the maximum
amount of the fine which may be imposed for the offence so compounded:

Provided further that in specifying the sum required to be paid or credited for the
compounding of an offence under this sub-section, the sum, if any, paid by way of
additional fee under sub-section (2) of section 403 shall be taken into account:

Provided also that any offence covered under this sub-section by any company or its
officer shall not be compounded if the investigation against such company has been
initiated or is pending under this Act.

                                                      691
        *            *       *       *  *                         *

97.3. Reasons/Justification given by the Ministry for the proposed provision:

"This clause seeks to increase the monetary threshold of fines for compounding of
offences by Regional Directors from Rs.25 lakhs to Rs.1 crore. This would enable
Regional Directors to handle a higher number of compounding applications and
reduce the burden on the NCLT."

97.4. Important Views/Suggestions given by Experts/Stakeholders:

97.4.1.    During the examination of the Bill, a stakeholder requested that all

Regional Director compounding orders and Section 454C settlement orders be made

publicly available.

97.5. Examination by the Committee:

97.5.1.    Regarding the suggestion mentioned in Para 97.4.1 to make

compounding and settlement orders public, the Ministry clarified that while the

measure promotes transparency and consistency, it is administrative in nature and

can be addressed through Rules without amending the primary Act. Accordingly, the

Ministry stated that the provision in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 may

be retained without change.

97.5.2.    Further, during the course of examination of the Bill, with regard to

Clause 97 of the Bill, the representatives of Ministry of Corporate Affairs deposed as

below:

reduce the load on NCLT.            25

                                                      692
97.5.3.  Continuing on the subject, the representatives of the Ministry further

deposed as under:

"............     ,  -     ,
