97.6. Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

The examination of the proposed Clause 97 of the Bill reveals that it provides
for the amendment of Section 441 of the Companies Act, 2013 to enhance the
monetary threshold for the compounding of offences by the Regional Director
or any officer authorized by the Central Government, raising the jurisdiction
from offences carrying a fine of Rs.25 lakh to those up to Rs.1 crore.

The Committee observe that this enhancement represents a progressive and
pragmatic reform. The Committee take special note of the Ministry's
submission during oral evidence that an estimated 90 per cent of all
compounding applications will now fall within the jurisdiction of the Regional
Directors. The Committee consider this shift a major step towards de-clogging
the Benches of the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), expediting the
disposal of compounding matters, and lowering compliance and litigation
costs for businesses without compromising regulatory oversight.

However, to ensure statutory consistency across Section 441, remove
interpretational ambiguity, and promote uniform enforcement, the Committee
recommend that the words "or any other person" be inserted after the word
"officer" wherever it appears in Section 441 (except where followed by the
words "authorised by the Central Government").

Further, the Committee are of the considered view that embracing digital

governance in compounding proceedings is an imperative necessity to
                                                      693
enhance operational efficiency, ensure transparency, and eliminate procedural
delays. In this context, the Committee strongly welcome the Ministry's
submission during oral deposition regarding the ongoing development of an e-
compounding portal and its intention to introduce an enabling statutory
provision for digital compounding. The Committee agree that an end-to-end
electronic platform--encompassing the filing of applications, submission of
documents, holding of hearings, passing of orders, and payment of fees--will
significantly enhance institutional accountability and improve the ease of
compliance.

Taking into account the above considerations and to give full effect to the e-
compounding mechanism, the Committee recommend that Clause 97 of the
Bill be rephrased as follows:

"In section 441 of the principal Act,-

(a) in whole section 441, after the word "officer" wherever it is appearing and
not being followed by word "authorised by the Central Government", the
words "or any other person" shall be inserted;

(b) in sub-section (1), in clause (b), for the words "does not exceed twenty-five
lakh rupees", the words "does not exceed one crore rupees" shall be
substituted.

(c) After sub section 3 of the Section 441 of the Companies Act, 2013, a
following sub section shall be inserted, namely:-

"(3A) Notwithstanding anything contained in this section, all proceedings for
compounding of offences before the Regional Director under clause (b) of sub-
section (1) (including filing of applications, submission of replies, documents
and evidence, holding of hearing, passing of orders of compounding, payment
of fee, etc.) shall take place in electronic mode only through such e-
compounding platform as may be developed by the Central Government for
this purpose:

Provided that where the electronic address of the applicant company or officer
is not available, service of notice may be affected by post at the last intimated
address or address available in the records and a record thereof shall be

                                                      694
preserved in the electronic records in the said electronic platform referred in
this sub section:
Provided further that the Central Government may, by notification, specify the
form, manner, and procedure for electronic filing, hearing, and disposal of
applications under this sub-section."
With regard to stakeholder representations advocating the public disclosure of
compounding and settlement orders, the Committee take note of the call for
greater transparency in administrative adjudications. The Committee are of the
considered opinion that while operational modalities in this regard are
administrative in nature and can be governed through subordinate legislation,
establishing systematic public accessibility is vital to foster institutional
integrity and enhance public trust. The Committee, therefore, recommend that
the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, in consultation with relevant stakeholders,
frame appropriate Rules to ensure that compounding and settlement orders
are regularly published and accessible on the MCA21 digital portal.

Subject to the above modifications in section 441 and timely framing of the
requisite subordinate rules to operationalize these procedural and
transparency safeguards, the Committee recommend the acceptance of Clause
97 in the Bill.

                            CLAUSE - 98

98.  Clause 98 of the Bill proposes to amend Section 446B of the

Companies Act, 2013

98.1. Provision proposed in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

Amendment of Section 446B.

In section 446B of the principal Act, for the words "liable to a penalty which shall not
be more than one-half of the penalty", the words "liable to a penalty of one-half, or
such per cent. not exceeding one-half, as may be prescribed, of the penalty" shall be
substituted.

98.2. Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (The Companies Act, 2013):

446B. Lesser penalties for certain companies-

446B. Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, if penalty is payable for non-
compliance of any of the provisions of this Act by a One Person Company, small
company, start-up company or Producer Company, or by any of its officer in default,
or any other person in respect of such company, then such company, its officer in
default or any other person, as the case may be, shall be liable to a penalty which
shall not be more than one-half of the penalty specified in such provisions subject to
a maximum of two lakh rupees in case of a company and one lakh rupees in case of
an officer who is in default or any other person, as the case may be.

Explanation.--For the purposes of this section,--

         (a) "Producer Company" means a company as defined in clause (l) of section
378A;

         (b) "start-up company" means a private company incorporated under this Act
or under the Companies Act, 1956 and recognised as start-up in accordance with the
notification issued by the Central Government in the Department for Promotion of
Industry and Internal Trade.

                            696
98.3. Reasons/Justification given by the Ministry for the proposed provisions:

"This amendment is to clarify that lesser penalties, i.e. one-half of the original penalty
or such lower percentage as may be prescribed, shall be leviable in case of four
classes of companies, namely One Person Companies (OPCs), Small Companies,
Start-up Companies and Producer Companies."

98.4. Examination by the Committee:

During the course of examination of the Bill, the Ministry clarified that delegating
power to the Central Government under Section 446B to prescribe reduced penalties
(up to one-half) for specified small entities provides essential statutory flexibility,
allowing penalty amounts to be periodically adjusted for inflation, administrative
costs, and market conditions without rendering the primary law rigid and outdated.

98.5. Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

The Committee note that Clause 98 of the Bill seeks to amend Section 446B of
the Companies Act, 2013, empowering the Central Government to prescribe
lower penalty limits--capped at one-half of the penalty specified under the
relevant provisions--for specified small entities such as One Person
Companies, small companies, start-ups, and Producer Companies.

The Committee observe that proportional penalties safeguard small
enterprises from excessive financial hardship, encourage voluntary
compliance, and grant necessary administrative flexibility to adapt to
economic changes through Rules.

Therefore, the Committee, after considered deliberation, recommend accepting
Clause 98 as proposed in the Bill.

                             CLAUSE - 99

99. Clause 99 of the Bill intends to amend Section 447 of the Companies
Act, 2013

99.1. Provision proposed in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

Amendment of Section 447

In section 447 of the principal Act,--

(a) for the words "ten lakh rupees", the words "twenty-five lakh rupees" shall be
substituted;

(b) in the second proviso, for the words "fifty lakh rupees", the words "one crore
rupees" shall be substituted.

99.2. Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (Companies Act, 2013):

447. Punishment for fraud.-

447. Without prejudice to any liability including repayment of any debt under this
Actor any other law for the time being in force, any person who is found to be guilty
of fraud, involving an amount of at least ten lakh rupees or one per cent. of the
turnover of the company, whichever is lower shall be punishable with imprisonment
for a term which shall not be less than six months but which may extend to ten years
and shall also be liable to fine which shall not be less than the amount involved in the
fraud, but which may extend to three times the amount involved in the fraud:

*  *                         *            *  *

Provided further that where the fraud involves an amount less than ten lakh rupees
or one per cent. of the turnover of the company, whichever is lower, and does not
involve public interest, any person guilty of such fraud shall be punishable with
imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years or with fine which may
extend to fifty lakh rupees or with both.

*  *                         *            *  *

                             698
99.3. Reasons/Justification given by the Ministry for the proposed provisions:
"Amendment in Section 447 is proposed as a consequential change pursuant to the
amendment in Section 441, which increases the monetary threshold for
compounding of offences by Regional Directors from Rs.25 lakhs rupees to Rs.1
crore. Accordingly, the thresholds in Section 447 are being revised to align with the
enhanced compounding limits."
99.4. Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:
The Committee note that Clause 99 of the Bill amends Section 447 of the
Companies Act, 2013 by raising the monetary thresholds for determining fraud
severity from Rs.10 lakhs to Rs.25 lakhs and Rs.50 lakhs to Rs.1 crore, serving
as a consequential update to align with the enhanced compounding
jurisdictional limits under Section 441 (raised from Rs.25 lakhs to Rs.1 crore).
The Committee observe that this amendment rationalizes the penal framework
by reserving the most severe penalties for major frauds involving public
interest, while treating minor violations proportionately, in line with the core
objectives of the Bill.
After careful deliberation, the Committee endorse the approval of Clause 99 as
proposed.

                                              CLAUSE - 100

100. Clause 100 of the Bill proposes to amend Section 453 of the Companies
Act, 2013

100.1. Provision proposed in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

Amendment of Section 453

In section 453 of the principal Act, for the words "punishable with fine which shall not
be less than five hundred rupees but may extend to two thousand rupees for every
day", the words "shall be liable to a penalty of one lakh rupees and in case of
continuing failure, with a further penalty of five hundred rupees for each day, after the
first during which such failure continues, subject to a maximum of five lakh rupees"
shall be substituted.

100.2. Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (The Companies Act, 2013):

453. Punishment for improper use of "Limited" or "Private Limited". -

453. If any person or persons trade or carry on business under any name or title, of
which the word "Limited" or the words "Private Limited" or any contraction or imitation
thereof is or are the last word or words, that person or each of those persons shall,
unless duly incorporated with limited liability, or unless duly incorporated as a private
company with limited liability, as the case may be, punishable with fine which shall
not be less than five hundred rupees but may extend to two thousand rupees for
every day for which that name or title has been used.

100.3. Reasons/Justification given by the Ministry for the proposed provisions:

"The amendment replaces the existing fine with a penalty framework, including fixed
and continuing penalties for misuse of the words "Limited" or "Private Limited". The
amendment is part of the broader decriminalisation exercise under the Bill."

100.4. Important Views/Suggestions given by Experts/Stakeholders:

100.4.1  A stakeholder suggested replacing the existing daily fine of Rs.500 to

Rs.2,000 under Section 453 of the Companies Act, 2013 with a structured penalty

framework: a standard penalty of Rs.1 lakh plus Rs.500 per day for continuing

         700
default (capped at 5 lakh), or alternatively, a concessional penalty of Rs.10,000 for
a first contravention rectified within 30 days of notice, and an upfront penalty of
Rs.25,000 plus Rs.500 per day (capped at 2 lakh) for continued non-compliance.

100.5. Examination by the Committee:

100.5.1. The Ministry of Corporate Affairs, while rejecting the stakeholder
suggestion regarding penalties for improper use of the words "Limited" or "Private
Limited", stated that the proposed penalty is intended to ensure effective compliance
with statutory naming requirements. The Ministry noted that prescribing lower
penalties or waivers for first-time defaults is unnecessary, as maintaining a uniform
penalty framework promotes consistency and certainty in enforcement.

100.6. Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

The Committee note that Clause 100 of the Bill seeks to amend Section 453 of
the Companies Act, 2013 by replacing criminal prosecution with civil financial
penalties for the improper use of the terms "Limited" or "Private Limited".

The Committee observe that decriminalizing such procedural defaults aligns
with the broader objective of rationalizing the enforcement framework through
in-house adjudication, while the upper limit on continuing penalties ensures
the punishment remains proportionate.

Having considered the stakeholder's suggestion and the Ministry's response,
the Committee accept Clause 100 as proposed.

101. Clause 101 seeks to amend Section 454 of the Companies Act, 2013

101.1. Provision proposed in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

Amendment of Section 454

In section 454 of the principal Act,--

(a) in sub-section (1), for the word "Registrar," the words "Assistant Registrar" shall

(b) after sub-section (1), the following sub-section shall be inserted, namely:--

(c) in sub-section (5),--

         "Provided that the Appellate Authority shall not be below the rank of Joint
Director.";

         (ii) in clause (ii), after the words "or with both", the words "by a Court and the
said Court shall also have the power to direct such officer or the other person to pay

(f) after sub-section (8), the following sub-sections shall be inserted, namely:--

"(9) The penalties realised under this section shall be credited to the Consolidated
Fund of India.

(10) On and from the commencement of the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Act,

amended to provide for adjudication under this section,--

(a) the manner of withdrawal of the complaint; and

(b) the manner of transfer of such matter for adjudication under this section,

in respect of such offence, whether pending in the Court or otherwise, shall be dealt
with in accordance with such Scheme as the Central Government may notify in this
behalf."

101.2. Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (The Companies Act, 2013):

454. Adjudication of penalties.-

454. (1) The Central Government may, by an order published in the Official
Gazette, appoint as many officers of the Central Government, not below the rank of
Registrar, as adjudicating officers for adjudging penalty under the provisions of this
Act in the manner as may be prescribed.

*  *                              *       *         *

(5) Any person aggrieved by an order made by the adjudicating officer under sub-
section (3) may prefer an appeal to the Regional Director having jurisdiction in the
matter.

*  *                              *       *         *

                                     703
(7) The Regional Director may, after giving the parties to the appeal an opportunity of
being heard, pass such order as he thinks fit, confirming, modifying or setting aside
the order appealed against.

(8) (i) Where company fails to comply with the order made under sub-section (3)
or sub-section (7), as the case may be, within a period of ninety days from the date
of the receipt of the copy of the order, the company shall be punishable with fine
which shall not be less than twenty-five thousand rupees but which may extend to
five lakh rupees.

         (ii) Where an officer of a company or any other person who is in default fails to
comply with the order made under sub-section (3) or sub-section (7), as the case
may be, within a period of ninety days from the date of the receipt of the copy of the
order, such officer shall be punishable with imprisonment which may extend to six
months or with fine which shall not be less than twenty-five thousand rupees but
which may extend to one lakh rupees, or with both.

101.3. Reasons/Justification given by the Ministry for the proposed provisions:

"This clause proposes insertion of enabling provisions in Section 454 for companies
and officers in default to make application to the adjudicating officer for adjudication
of defaults. It also enables the Central Government to designate an Appellate
Authority (not below the rank of Joint Director) in addition to the Regional Director for
hearing appeals, and to expand the pool of adjudicating officers.

This amendment is proposed to give power to the Court to direct the company and
officers in default to pay the amount of penalty in case of prosecution launched for
non-compliance of Registrar of Companies (RoC) or Regional Director order.

This amendment is to clarify that decriminalisation shall have a retrospective effect
and that the manner of withdrawal of complaint and transfer of such matters for
adjudication shall be provided through a scheme to be notified by the Central
Government."

101.4. Important Views/Suggestions given by Experts/Stakeholders:

         With regard to Clause 101 related to Amendment in Section 454, the various
suggestions received from stakeholders are produced as under:

                                                      704
101.4.1. "The adjudication mechanism should be strengthened with procedural
safeguards, opportunities for hearing and appellate remedies. Further, it is also
suggested that excessive concentration of adjudicatory powers without adequate
checks may adversely affect principles of natural justice. Powers are required to be
reduced substantially and no power of arrest or heavy fine without judicial approval
should be permitted."

101.4.2. "Adequate staffing, specialized training, clear operating procedures and
robust infrastructure needed."

101.4.3. "It is recommended that the clauses be retained, subject to the
following modifications: (i) adjudicating officers shall not be below the rank of
Registrar in respect of penalties exceeding Rs.5 lakh; and (ii) the transition Scheme
under sub-section (10) shall be notified within six months and laid before both
Houses of Parliament".

101.5. Examination by the Committee:

101.5.1. In response to the various suggestions on Clause 101, the Ministry of
Corporate Affairs consistently concluded that "the provision in the Corporate Laws
(Amendment) Bill, 2026 may be retained without any change."

101.5.2  Specifically, regarding the suggestion in Para 101.4.1 related to

strengthening the adjudication mechanism and addressing the reduction in powers,

the Ministry replied as below:

"....It is submitted that the framework proposed under the amended Section 454,
read together with the newly inserted Sections 454C and 454D, already incorporates
sufficient procedural safeguards consistent with the principles of natural justice. It
may be noted that the adjudicating officer is statutorily required to afford an
opportunity of being heard to the parties concerned prior to the imposition of any
penalty under sub-section (3) of the said section. Furthermore, an aggrieved person
has a substantive appellate remedy, being entitled to prefer an appeal either to the
Regional Director or to such Appellate Authority as may be notified by the Central
Government, provided that such Appellate Authority shall not be below the rank of
Joint Director, and a further opportunity of hearing is expressly contemplated at the
appellate stage under sub-section (7). It may additionally be noted that the newly
inserted Section 454D requires deposit of only ten per cent of the disputed penalty
amount as a pre-condition for filing an appeal, while Section 454C separately
provides for a voluntary settlement mechanism.

                                705
101.5.3. Further, regarding the suggestion in Para 101.4.2 pertaining to
adequate staffing and specialized training of adjudicating officers, the Ministry noted:

"The suggestion relates to staffing, specialized training, clear operating procedures
and robust infrastructure. As the suggestion pertains to an administrative measure
and does not require an amendment to the Act, it may be considered separately, as
appropriate.

101.5.4. Furthermore, with regard to the suggestion in Para 101.4.3 concerning
modifications in the rank of adjudicating officers where penalties exceed Rs.5 lakhs
and the transition scheme in sub-section (10), the Ministry stated:

"The proposed framework already contains adequate institutional safeguards to
ensure fairness and consistency in adjudication. The rank of adjudicating officers has
been prescribed keeping in view the nature of in-house adjudication, the volume of
cases, and the need for timely disposal. Further, prescribing a statutory timeline for
notifying the transition Scheme and mandating its placement before Parliament is not
considered necessary, as the Central Government retains the flexibility to notify the
Scheme in a timely manner based on implementation requirements.

101.5.5. Regarding devolving administrative and procedural implementation
under Clause 101 through subordinate legislation, the Ministry submitted that
empowering the Central Government to prescribe the form, manner, and fees under
Section 454(1A) ensures procedural flexibility without altering substantive
compliance. The Ministry further stated that delegating fee structures avoids
statutory rigidity, allowing timely adjustments based on inflation, administrative costs,
and market conditions.

101.5.6. As such, the representatives of the Ministry deposed before the Joint
Committee during the course of examination of the Bill as mentioned below:

"Sir, regarding Section 454 under Clause 101 - as we discussed in relation to LLPs -
this introduces a provision for suo motu adjudication. An application can be filed by a
company, a director, or an officer to initiate suo motu adjudication proceedings. This
is also intended to give retrospective effect to the decriminalisation of these
provisions. We are decriminalising 19 provisions in the Companies Act. This clause
enables both suo motu proceedings and ensures the retrospective application of

                                                      706
decriminalisation, which will provide significant relief. In fact, we have successfully
implemented a similar mechanism previously when we decriminalised 51 offences."

101.6. Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

The Committee note that Clause 101 of the Bill amends Section 454 of the
Companies Act, 2013 to strengthen and broaden the in-house adjudication
framework. The key modifications include expanding the pool of Adjudicating
Officers by lowering the threshold rank from Registrar to Assistant Registrar,
broadening Appellate Authorities to include Joint Directors alongside Regional
Directors, and empowering courts trying non-compliance prosecutions under
sub-section (8) to directly order recovery of unpaid administrative penalties.

The Committee observe that these amendments represent a major step toward
de-clogging the judicial system and facilitating swift compliance. Taking
special note of the oral evidence tendered by the Ministry before the
Committee, the Committee highlight that sub-section (1A) establishes an
enabling framework for suo motu adjudication, allowing companies and
individuals to proactively apply for penalty adjudication. Furthermore, the
Committee emphasize the significance of giving retrospective effect to
decriminalization across 19 provisions of the Act. This relief will be
operationalized through a Transition Scheme under sub-section (10) to transfer
or withdraw pending court complaints. The Committee note that this approach
draws upon the Ministry's successful past experience of decriminalizing 51
offences.

The Committee further note that delegating operational modalities--such as
forms, procedure, and fee structures under sub-section (1A)--to subordinate
rules provides necessary administrative flexibility to adapt to changing
economic and operational conditions without altering substantive statutory
compliance.

                                                      707
However, upon examining the newly proposed sub-section (1A) in Section 454,
the Committee are of the considered view that its scope needs to be broader
and legally precise. To ensure that the provision comprehensively
encompasses all categories of individuals who may be held liable for
contraventions across various sections of the Act, the Committee consider it
necessary to explicitly include "director, promoter" and "or any other person".
This textual refinement will eliminate interpretational ambiguity, avoid
unintended exclusions, and align sub-section (1A) with the liability language
used across the principal Act.

In light of the above, the Committee recommend that in section 454, after sub-
section (1), the newly proposed sub-section (1A) may be reworded as
following:

"(1A) A company, director, promoter, or its officer who is in default or any other
person, may make an application in such form and manner and on payment of
such fees, as may be prescribed under this section for adjudication of
penalty".

Regarding stakeholder suggestions for a fixed statutory timeframe to notify
the Transition Scheme under sub-section (10), the Committee accept the
Ministry's rationale that administrative flexibility is necessary. Nevertheless, to
ensure that pending prosecutions under the 19 decriminalized provisions
obtain timely relief without prolonged litigation, the Committee expect the
Ministry of Corporate Affairs, in consultation with relevant stakeholders, to
frame and to notify the Transition Scheme expeditiously upon enactment of the
Bill.

Subject to the statutory modification in sub-section (1A) and the timely
notification of the Transition Scheme and procedural Rules, the Committee
accept the Clause 101 as originally proposed.

                                                      708
                                              CLAUSE - 102

102. Clause 102 of the Bill proposes to amend Section 454 of the Companies
Act, 2013

102.1. Provision proposed in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

Amendment in Section 454A.

In section 454A of the principal Act, after the words "Regional Director", the words,
brackets and figures "or the Appellate Authority referred to in sub-section (5) of
section 454" shall be inserted.

102.2. Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (The Companies Act, 2013):

454A. Penalty for repeated default.-

Where a company or an officer of a company or any other person having already
been subjected to penalty for default under any provisions of this Act, again commits
such default within a period of three years from the date of order imposing such
penalty passed by the adjudicating officer or the Regional Director, as the case may
be, it or he shall be liable for the second or subsequent defaults for an amount equal
to twice the amount of penalty provided for such default under the relevant provisions
of this Act.

102.3. Reasons/Justification given by the Ministry for the proposed provisions:

"Amendment is proposed to allow hearing of appeals under section 454 by the
Appellate Authority, who can be an officer of appropriate rank authorised by the
Central Government. This would remove the necessity of Regional Directors only
hearing the appeals. Therefore, a consequential change in section 454A is also
being made."

102.4. Important Views/Suggestions given by Experts/Stakeholders:

Concerning Clause 102 of the Bill, certain suggestions made by stakeholders are
outlined as under:

                                                      709
102.4.1. "The proposed recovery powers confer extensive draconian
enforcement authority upon MCA Officers. Such provisions may lead to coercive
recovery actions without sufficient judicial oversight. Any review mechanism should
be subject to independent review and adequate appellate protection."

102.5. Examination by the Committee:

102.5.1. In response to stakeholder suggestions on Clause 102, the Ministry of
Corporate Affairs consistently maintained that "the provision in the Corporate Laws
(Amendment) Bill, 2026 may be retained without any change."

102.5.2  Specifically, concerning the suggestion in Para 102.4.1 regarding

independent review and adequate appellate protection, the Ministry disallowed the

proposal and responded:

"These provisions are proposed for companies and officers who neither pay the
penalty nor file an appeal against the order of Adjudicating officer rendering
adjudication process vitiated. This gap was noticed when Adjudicating Officers in
field offices of MCA came across such instances. The amendments are intended to
strengthen enforcement of final penalty orders and ensure effective compliance,
while remaining consistent with the objective of decriminalising procedural and
technical defaults by relying on civil penalties instead of criminal sanctions."

102.6. Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

The Committee note that Clause 102 of the Bill seeks to amend Section 454A of
the Companies Act, 2013 by inserting references to the "Appellate Authority"
alongside the "Regional Director". This amendment is consequential to the
changes proposed under Section 454(5), which broadens the appellate
structure by empowering the Central Government to notify additional Appellate
Authorities (not below the rank of Joint Director) to hear appeals alongside
Regional Directors.

The Committee observe that Section 454A distinguishes between first-time and
repeat violations by prescribing a penalty equal to twice the specified amount

                                                      710
for a subsequent default committed within three years of an earlier
adjudication order, serving as an effective deterrent against habitual non-
compliance.
However, to ensure accurate identification of repeat defaults and prevent
inadvertent or inconsistent application, the Committee expect the Ministry to
maintain robust, centralized digital records of all adjudication and appellate
orders.
Having carefully considered the suggestions from stakeholders as well as the
submissions of the Ministry, the Committee endorse acceptance of Clause 102
as proposed.

                                                      711
                                              CLAUSE - 103

103. Clause 103 of the Bill proposes to insert new sections after Section 454A
of the Companies Act, 2013

103.1. Provision proposed in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

Insertion of new Sections 454B, 454C and 454D.

After section 454A of the principal Act, the following sections shall be inserted,
namely:--

`454B. Recovery of Amounts

         (1) If a person fails to pay the penalty imposed under this Act, the Recovery
Officer may draw up under his signature a statement (herein referred to as
certificate) in the specified form specifying the amount due from the person and shall
proceed to recover from such person the amount specified in the certificate by one or
more of the following modes, namely:--

         (a) attachment and sale of movable property of such person;

         (b) attachment of bank accounts of such person;

         (c) attachment and sale of immovable properties of such person;

         (d) arrest of that person and his detention in prison;

         (e) appointing a receiver for the management of such movable or immovable
properties,

         and for this purpose, the provisions of sections 220 to 227, 228A, 229, 232,
the Second Schedule and Third Schedule to the Income-tax Act, 1961 and the
Income-tax (Certificate Proceedings) Rules, 1962, as in force from time to time, in so
far as may be, apply with necessary modifications as if the corresponding provisions
of the said Act and the rules made thereunder were the provisions of this Act and
referred to the amount due under this Act, instead of to income-tax under the
Income-tax Act, 1961.

                                                      712
Explanation 1.--For the purposes of this sub-section, the movable or immovable
property or monies held in bank accounts of the person, shall include any property or
monies held in bank accounts which has been transferred directly or indirectly on or
after the date when the amount specified in the certificate had become due, by the
person to his spouse or his minor child or son's wife or son's minor child, otherwise
than for adequate consideration, and which is held by, or stands in the name of, any
of his relations aforementioned; and so far as the movable or immovable property or
monies held in bank accounts so transferred to his minor child or his son's minor
child is concerned, it shall, even after the date of attainment of majority by such
minor child or son's minor child, as the case may be, continue to be included in the
movable or immovable property or monies held in bank accounts of such person for
recovering any amount due from him under this Act.

Explanation 2.--Any reference under the provisions of the Second Schedule or the
Third Schedule to the Income-tax Act, 1961 and the Income-tax (Certificate
Proceedings) Rules, 1962 to the assessee, shall be construed as a reference to the
person specified in the certificate.

Explanation 3.--Any reference to an appeal under Chapter XVIID and the Second
Schedule to the Income-tax Act, 1961, shall be construed as a reference to an
appeal before the Appellate Authority under sub-section (5) of section 454 of this Act.

Explanation 4.--The interest referred to in section 220 of the Income-tax Act, 1961
shall commence from the date the amount became payable by the person.

(2) The Recovery Officer shall have power to seek the assistance of the local district
administration while exercising the powers under sub-section (1).

Explanation.-- For the purposes of this section, the expression "Recovery Officer"
means an officer not below the rank of Assistant Registrar or Assistant Director
authorised by the Central Government in this behalf, by general or special order in
writing, to exercise the powers of a Recovery Officer.

454C. Settlement.-

(1) The contraventions which shall be liable for penalty under this Act may, subject to
the provisions of this section, eligible for settlement.

(2) The Central Government may constitute a Specified Authority comprising of an
officer or group of officers of the Central Government which may discharge the
functions of Specified Authority under this section.

                                                      713
(3) Any person, against whom any proceeding has been initiated for contravention of
any provision referred to in sub-section (1), may file an application in writing to the
Specified Authority in such form and manner, as may prescribed.

(4) An application under sub-section (3) may be submitted at any time before the
order of penalty is passed.

(5) The Specified Authority may, after taking into consideration the nature, gravity
and impact of contraventions, agree to the proposal for settlement, on payment of
such sum by the applicant or on such other terms and manner of implementation of
settlement and monitoring, as may be prescribed.

(6) If the Specified Authority is of the opinion that the settlement offered is not
appropriate in the circumstances, or if the Specified Authority and applicant
concerned do not reach an agreement on the terms of the settlement within such
time as may be prescribed, it shall by an order reject the application for settlement
and the proceedings initiated against the applicant shall be continued.

(7) The settlement proceedings under this section shall be conducted in such
manner as may be prescribed.

(8) No appeal shall lie against any order passed by the Specified Authority under this
section.

(9) All settlement amounts realised under this Act shall be credited to the
Consolidated Fund of India.

454D. Deposit of certain amount before appeal is entertained.-

No appeal by a person, who is required to pay any amount in terms of an order of -

         (a) the National Financial Reporting Authority under section 132; or

         (b) the Valuation Authority under section 247; or

         (c) the adjudicating officer under section 454

shall be entertained by the Appellate Tribunal or Regional Director or the Appellate
Authority referred to in sub-section (5) of section 454, as the case may be, unless the
appellant has deposited ten per cent. of that amount in the manner as directed by the

                                                      714
Appellate Tribunal or Regional Director, or the Appellate Authority, as the case may
be.

103.2. Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (The Companies Act, 2013):

Insertion of new Sections 454B, 454C and 454D after Section 454A.

103.3. Reasons/Justification given by the Ministry for the proposed provisions:

"The amendment proposes a new section 454B to provide an enabling framework
for recovery of unpaid penalties, including powers for attachment, sale, and other
recovery measures, on the lines of the recovery mechanism under the Income-tax
Act, 1961. The provision is intended for effective enforcement of penalty orders, on
the lines of the SEBI Act, 1992.

The amendment seeks to insert a new section 454C to provide a framework for
settlement of contraventions liable for penalty under the Act, including application,
consideration and disposal by Specified Authority on payment of settlement amount
or compliance with prescribed terms. It enables settlement of defaults covered under
section 454 through payment of monetary settlement fees, with a dedicated authority
to dispose of applications, while excluding matters to be decided by a criminal court.

The amendment seeks to insert a new section 454D to require a pre-deposit of ten
per cent of the penalty amount as a condition for filing an appeal against orders of
the NFRA, Valuation Authority or adjudicating officers."

103.4. Important Views/Suggestions given by Experts/Stakeholders:

         Pertinent to Clause 103 containing new insertions of Sections 454B, 454C
and 454D, some important suggestions or comments received from various
stakeholders and experts are summarised as follows:-

New Sub-Section 454B

103.4.1. With regard to Section 454B, "Request that power of arrest and
detention be removed and penalties be recovered through civil enforcement only
(attachment/sale of property, bank attachment) - to meet decriminalisation objective.
If considered necessary, request incorporation of safeguards (e.g. Section 14 of
FEMA) and minimum monetary thresholds."

                                                      715
103.4.2. "Any attachment of bank accounts or property by corporate authorities
shall be subordinate to the prior charge of secured financial creditors and
attachments must exclude operational cash-credit or working capital accounts
utilized for daily business operations."

103.4.3. "Restrict the coercive recovery toolkit (attachment, arrest and
detention) under new Section 454B to wilful, repeated, or fraud-linked non-payment
only, and provide an explicit instalment/settlement option before recourse to arrest,
mirroring the safeguards in Section 454C (settlement)."

103.4.4. "Proposed section 454B provides the power of arrest and detention to
the recovery officer. And for this purpose, provisions of section 220 to 227, Second
Schedule and Third Schedule to the Income-tax Act, 1961 have been applied. Vide
Finance Act, 2026, the provision related to arrest and detention by tax recovery
officer has been omitted from the Income-tax Act, 1961. Hence, the reference to
Income-tax Act, 1961 shall be replaced by Income-tax Act, 1961 (as it stood
immediately prior to its amendment by Finance Act, 2026)."

103.4.5. "It is recommended that the clause be modified as follows: (i) clause (d)
(arrest and detention) be deleted; in the alternative, a proviso be inserted that arrest
and detention shall not be resorted to unless the Recovery Officer records a finding,
after notice, that the defaulter has the means to pay and has wilfully refused, or has
dishonestly transferred or concealed property, and no order of detention shall be
executed without confirmation by the Regional Director; and (ii) Explanation 1 be
confined to transfers made after service of the adjudication notice."

103.4.6. "It is humbly proposed that a consolidated safeguard be inserted, by
proviso or Note on Clauses, to provide that where, in respect of the same act or
omission, penalty or recovery action has been or is being pursued under any law
administered by SEBI or IFSCA, no separate penalty or duplicate recovery shall be
imposed or pursued under the Companies Act to that extent, and the concerned
authorities shall coordinate to avoid multiplicity of proceedings.

Further, arrest and detention for default in payment of a civil penalty should not be
resorted to except in exceptional, recorded circumstances with due-process
protection."

New Sub-Section 454C

103.4.7. "Request that all Regional Director compounding orders and Section
454C settlement orders be made publicly available."

                                                      716
103.4.8. "The settlement mechanism is a welcome addition that will reduce
adjudication burden and incentivise voluntary compliance, and is strongly supported.
It is suggested that the scope of proposed section 454C relating to settlement of
contraventions liable for penalty under the Companies Act, 2013 should also
expressly include penalties imposed by the National Financial Reporting Authority
(NFRA) under section 132 of the Act. Accordingly, suitable amendment may be made
to provide that proceedings relating to penalties imposed under section 132 may also
be eligible for settlement under section 454C."

103.4.9. In context of the proposed Section 454C(2), it has been suggested,
"The Central Government may constitute a Specified Authority comprising of an
officer or group of officers of the central Government which may discharge the
functions of the Specified Authority under this Act.

Provided that for the purposes of penalties for contravention as provided under
Section 132 and Section 132D of this Act, the Specified Authority means the
Executive Body of the National Financial Reporting Authority, mentioned in sub-
section (3B) of Section 132 of this Act."

103.4.10. In connection with proposed Section 454C(3), it has been suggested
that "Replace 454(C) (3) with the following:

(3) Any person, against whom any proceeding has been initiated or may be initiated
for contravention of any provision referred to in sub-section (1), may file an
application in writing to the Specified Authority in such form and manner, as may be
prescribed."

103.4.11. Further, in connection with the proposed Section 454C(7), it has been
suggested, "The settlement proceedings under this section shall be conducted in
such manner as may be prescribed. Provided that the settlement proceedings
conducted by the Executive Body of the National Financial Reporting Authority as

as may be specified by the Authority by regulations."

103.4.12. "Compounding and settlements -

i) Publish Regional Director compounding orders and Section 454C settlement
orders.

ii) Permit settlement without admission of guilt and allow withdrawal before the final
order.

                                                      717
iii) Publish objective criteria for determining compounding amounts to improve
transparency and predictability."

103.4.13. "454C. (1) The contraventions which shall be liable for penalty under
this Act, including, for avoidance of doubt, contraventions that may attract
consequences under section 132(4) of this Act, may, subject to the provisions of this
section, eligible for settlement."

103.4.14. "It is recommended that the clause be retained, subject to the following
modifications: (i) an express provision that settlement shall be without admission or
determination of guilt, and that a settlement order shall not be treated as a "penalty
for default" for the purposes of section 164 or any other disqualification; (ii)

be published in such manner as may be prescribed; and (iv) a time-limit of ninety

New Sub-Section 454D

103.4.15. It has further been propounded that Section 132D may also be added

103.4.16. "Align with the Securities Appellate Tribunal regime; confirm the

103.4.17. "Provided further that where in any particular case, the Appellate
Tribunal or Regional Director or the Appellate Authority referred to in sub-section (5)
of section 454, as the case may be, is of the opinion that the deposit of such amount
would cause undue hardship to such person, the Appellate Tribunal or Regional
Director or the Appellate Authority referred to in sub-section (5) of section 454 may
dispense with such deposit subject to such conditions as it may deem fit to impose
so as to safeguard the realisation of the penalty. A mandatory pre deposit
requirement may prevent the appellant with genuine financial difficulties from
exercising its statutory right of appeal.

The suggested provision already exists in several Indian statutes governing appeals,
where appellate authorities are empowered to waive or modify pre-deposit
requirements in cases of undue hardship."

103.4.18. "Remove, or substantially lower (e.g. to a maximum of Rs.25,000 or 2%
of the penalty, whichever is less, rather than a flat 10%), the mandatory pre-deposit

                                                      718
required before an appeal against an NFRA, Valuation Authority or adjudicating-

103.4.19. "It is humbly proposed that a proviso (or Note on Clauses) be inserted

New Subsection 454B

103.5.1. Further, regarding the aforesaid suggestion in Para 103.4.1. and

Act, 1992 and the Income Tax Act, 2025. Section 28A (1) (b) of the SEBI Act, 1992
empowers the Recovery officer to recover amounts through attachment of bank
accounts. The proposed provision is intended to provide an effective recovery
mechanism. Therefore, altering the statutory priority of claims or creating exemptions
from attachment for specific categories of assets or bank accounts, may not be

Hence, the provision in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 may be retained

New Subsection 454D-

103.5.13. As such, with respect to the suggestion in Para 103.4.15 to include

"As an order of NFRA under newly proposed provision 132D is also appealable

                                                      723
103.5.14. Further, with regard to the suggestion in Para 103.4.16 appertaining to

follows:

"Section 454D discusses the conditions by which an appeal can be made under the
Companies Act, 2013 for grievances from orders passed by NFRA or the Valuation
Authority. It encompasses all possible appellate authorities present in the Companies
Act, 2013 to ensure uniform application of the statute. Each contravention and
grievance redressal mechanism has a relevant appellate authority specified in the
particular sections itself, and are therefore not ambiguous in nature."

103.5.15. Furthermore, in context of the suggestion in Para 103.4.17 dealing with
assigning power to the Appellate Authority or Reginal Director to waive off or reduce
the requirement for pre-deposit of ten per cent of penalty amount for appeals, the
Ministry while declining the suggestion in its written submission, stated as below:

"The suggestion seeks to empower the appellate authority to waive the mandatory
pre- deposit requirement in cases of undue hardship. The proposed provision
prescribes a uniform pre-deposit requirement to ensure certainty in the appellate
process while balancing the right of appeal with the need to safeguard recovery of
amounts due. Accordingly, the proposed framework may be retained without any
change. Such pre-deposit requirements are a well-recognised legislative mechanism
and exist under several statutes, including the Income-tax Act, 1961. Hence, the
provision in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 may be retained without any
change."

103.5.16. In connection with the suggestion in Para 103.4.18 referring to
removing or substantially lowering the requirement for pre-deposit before an appeal
along with completely exempting certain classes of Companies, the Ministry while
declining to accept the suggestion in its written response, stated as follows:

"It is submitted that the framework proposed under the amended Section 454, read
together with the newly inserted Sections 454C and 454D, already incorporates
sufficient procedural safeguards consistent with the principles of natural justice.
Section 454D requires deposit of only ten per cent of the disputed penalty amount as
a pre-condition for filing an appeal, while Section 454C separately provides for a
voluntary settlement mechanism."

                                                      724
103.5.17. Regarding the proposition received from stakeholder in para 103.4.19

"Same action may lead to different violations. If a consolidated bar was introduced, it

Defaulters may seek to expedite settlements or accept minimal penalties under the
most lenient regulatory regime purely to immunise themselves against more stringent

Section 413 of the Income Tax Act, 2025, as amended by the Finance Act, 2026, has

103.5.18. As such, with respect to enabling skeleton legislation with detailed
implementation left to statutory/subordinate instruments under Clause 103, the
Ministry in its written statement clarified as follows:

"Clause 103 of the Bill empowers the Central Government to prescribe, under sub-
section (3) of section 454C of the Companies Act, 2013, the form and manner of
filing an application for filing an application in writing to the Specified Authority by any
person, against whom any proceeding has been initiated for contravention of any
provision referred to in sub-section (1) of section 454C. It further empowers the
Central Government to prescribe, under sub-section (5) of section 454C of the
Companies Act, 2013, the terms and manner of implementation of settlement and
monitoring, and the sum on payment of which the Specified Authority may agree to
the proposal of settlement.

It also empowers the Central Government to prescribe, under subsection (6) of
section 454C of the Companies Act, 2013, the time within which the Specified

                                                      725
Authority and applicant concerned do not reach an agreement on the terms of
settlement, before it rejects the application for settlement the proceedings initiated
against the applicant are continued.

It also empowers the Central Government to prescribe, under subsection (7) of
section 454C of the Companies Act, 2013, the manner in which the settlement
proceedings under section 454C shall be conducted."

103.5.19. Moreover, expounding on the above subject of delegated legislation,
the Ministry further submitted as below:

"This proposes to prescribe the form, manner, term, time. As far as form, manner,
term and time is concerned these provisions demonstrate that the delegation is
directed at procedural flexibility and does not affect substantive compliance of the
law. The legislature is to determine the principle and the executive is merely tasked
with specifying how they are to be operationalised."

103.6. Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

103.6.1. The Committee note that Clause 103 of the Bill inserts new
Sections 454B, 454C, and 454D into the Companies Act, 2013 to establish a
statutory framework for penalty recovery, voluntary settlement of
contraventions, and pre-deposit conditions for appeals. The Committee
observe that these provisions will significantly strengthen the enforceability of
adjudication orders, discourage wilful default in penalty payments, ensure
efficient recovery, and deter frivolous or dilatory appeals.

Regarding Section 454B, the Committee take note of suggestions from various
stakeholders and experts advocating the removal of coercive recovery
measures--specifically the power of arrest and detention in prison under
proposed sub-section (1)(d)--to align with the broader objective of
decriminalization. The Committee also note the Ministry's explicit agreement to
align Section 454B with the statutory framework of the Income-tax Act, 2025
(as amended by the Finance Act, 2026), which has abolished arrest powers for
tax recovery officers. Furthermore, the Committee observe that legislative

                                                      726
references to the Income-tax Act, 1961 require updating to the Income-tax Act,
2025 and the Income-tax Rules, 2026.

In view of the above, the Committee recommend the omission of clause (d) of
Section 454B(1) and the updating of statutory cross-references. Accordingly,
the Committee recommend that sub-section (1) and Explanations 2, 3, and 4 of
Section 454B be reworded as follows:

"454B. (1) If a person fails to pay the penalty imposed under this Act, the
Recovery Officer may draw up under his signature a statement (herein referred
to as certificate) in the specified form specifying the amount due from the
person and shall proceed to recover from such person the amount specified in
the certificate by one or more of the following modes, namely:--

(a) attachment and sale of movable property of such person;

(b) attachment of bank accounts of such person;

(c) attachment and sale of immovable properties of such person;

(d) arrest of that person and his detention in prison;

(e)(d) appointing a receiver for the management of such movable or immovable
properties,

and for this purpose, the provisions of sections 220 to 227, 228A, 229, 232, the
Second Schedule and Third Schedule to the Income-tax Act, 1961 411 to 419,
421 and 422 of the Income-tax Act, 2025, and the Income-tax (Certificate
Proceedings) Rules, 1962 rules 153 and 225 of the Income-tax Rules, 2026 as
in force from time to time, in so far as may be, apply with necessary
modifications as if the corresponding provisions of the said Act and the rules
made thereunder were the provisions of this Act and referred to the amount

                                                      727
due under this Act, instead of to income-tax under the Income-tax Act, 1961
2025.

Explanation 1.--For the purposes of this sub-section, the movable or
immovable property or monies held in bank accounts of the person, shall
include any property or monies held in bank accounts which has been
transferred directly or indirectly on or after the date when the amount specified
in the certificate had become due, by the person to his spouse or his minor
child or son's wife or son's minor child, otherwise than for adequate
consideration, and which is held by, or stands in the name of, any of his
relations aforementioned; and so far as the movable or immovable property or
monies held in bank accounts so transferred to his minor child or his son's
minor child is concerned, it shall, even after the date of attainment of majority
by such minor child or son's minor child, as the case may be, continue to be
included in the movable or immovable property or monies held in bank
accounts of such person for recovering any amount due from him under this
Act.

Explanation 2.-- Any reference under the provisions of the Second Schedule
and Third Schedule to the Income-tax Act, 1961 and the Income-tax (Certificate
Proceedings) Rules, 1962 rules 153 and 225 of the Income-tax Rules, 2026, to
the assessee, shall be construed as a reference to the person specified in the
certificate.

Explanation 3.--Any reference to an appeal under Part D of Chapter XVIIID XIX
of the Income-tax Act, 2025 and the Second Schedule to the Income-tax Act,
1961 and rule 225 of the Income-Tax Rules, 2026, shall be construed as a
reference to an appeal before the Appellate Authority under sub-section (5) of
section 454 of this Act.

Explanation 4.--The interest referred to in section 411 220 of the Income-tax
Act, 2025 1961 shall commence from the date the amount became payable by
the person."

                                                      728
To better reflect the evolving legal landscape and ensure statutory inclusion of
specialized regulatory bodies, the Committee recommend adding the words
"or an officer of the National Financial Reporting Authority so" to the
Explanation following Section 454B(2). Accordingly, the Explanation after
Section 454B(2) may be re-casted as follows:

"Explanation.--For the purposes of this section, the expression "Recovery
Officer" means an officer not below the rank of Assistant Registrar or
Assistant Director or an officer of the National Financial Reporting Authority so
authorised by the Central Government in this behalf, by general or special
order in writing, to exercise the powers of a Recovery Officer."

103.6.2. The Committee are of the view that Section 454C introduces a
pivotal institutional mechanism for the settlement of specified contraventions
prior to the passing of a penalty order, which will significantly advance the
objective of Ease of Doing Business, reduce the burden of prolonged litigation,
and foster voluntary compliance. In this context, and taking note of
stakeholder suggestions, the Ministry agreed to expand the settlement
framework to cover penalties imposed by the National Financial Reporting
Authority (NFRA). Accordingly, the Committee recommend that sub-section (2)
of Section 454C may now be rephrased as below:

"454C(2): The Central Government may constitute a Specified Authority
comprising of an officer or group of officers of the Central Government which
may discharge the functions of Specified Authority under this section.

Provided that in case of contraventions liable for imposition of penalty by the
National Financial Reporting Authority, the Specified Authority comprising of
members of executive body of the National Financial Reporting Authority may
discharge the functions of Specified Authority under this section."

                                                      729
103.6.3. The Committee further note that introduction of new Section 454D
establishes a threshold of minimum pre-deposit of ten per cent before an
appeal is filed.

However, the Committee are of the view that the pre-deposit of ten percent of
the penalty amount as may be directed by the relevant authority for filing of
appeals, appears too harsh and is bound to lead to impediment in exercising
the statutory right of appeal as part of natural justice, especially for one-
person companies, small start-ups or other appellants with genuine financial
difficulties.

In view of the above, the Committee recommend reducing the minimum pre-
deposit of penalty amount from ten-percent to five percent in order to facilitate
appellants facing genuine fiscal restrictions and at the same time discouraging
wilful default in payment of penalties as well as ensuring efficient recovery
along with discouraging frivolous or dilatory appeals.

Further, to remove drafting ambiguity and ensure technical accuracy regarding
the nature of liabilities, the Committee are of the view that the term "penalty
imposed" may be inserted in place of "amount" in Section 454D. Additionally,
in Section 454D(a), the words "and 132D" may be added after Section 132 to
explicitly cover all appealable orders of the National Financial Reporting
Authority.

Furthermore, the Committee advocate firmly fixing the quantum of pre-deposit
at five per cent in the statute itself and standardizing its procedure, rather than
leaving the quantum or manner of deposit to individual appellate forums,
which risks inconsistent application and uncertainty for appellants. To ensure
predictability, equal treatment, and time-bound disposal of appeals, the
Committee recommend omitting the words "directed by the Appellate Tribunal
or Regional Director or the Appellate Authority, as the case may be" and
inserting "in such manner as may be prescribed" after Section 454D(c).

                                                      730
Accordingly, the proposed Section 454D as per Clause 103 may be restated in
the Bill as follows:

"After section 454A of the principal Act, the following sections shall be
inserted, namely:--

454D. No appeal by a person, who is required to pay any amount penalty
imposed in terms of an order of-

(a) the National Financial Reporting Authority under section 132 and 132D; or

(b) the Valuation Authority under section 247; or

(c) the adjudicating officer under section 454,

shall be entertained by the Appellate Tribunal or Regional Director or the
Appellate Authority referred to in sub-section (5) of section 454, as the case
may be, unless the appellant has deposited five ten per cent. of that amount in
such the manner as may be prescribed directed by the Appellate Tribunal or
Regional Director or the Appellate Authority, as the case may be.".

103.6.4. As such, with regard to stakeholder suggestion dealing with
publishing the settlement orders as well as compounding and settlement
mechanism, the Committee concur with the Ministry that such procedural
aspects are administrative in nature. Nevertheless, to foster institutional
integrity and maintain public trust in administrative adjudications, the
Committee emphasize the necessity of embedding clear transparency
standards within the subordinate regulatory framework.

The Committee, therefore, recommend that the Ministry of Corporate Affairs
exercise its rule-making powers and notify, in consultation with relevant
stakeholders, specific provisions in the relevant Rules governing the
systematic publication and public accessibility of compounding and
settlement orders on the MCA21 digital portal.

                                                      731
103.6.5. Subject to the specific modifications recommended in the
preceding paragraphs, the Committee recommend that the remaining
provisions of Clause 103 of the Bill may be retained as originally proposed.

104.2. Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (The Companies Act, 2013):

455. Dormant company. --

(1) Where a company is formed and registered under this Act for a future project
or to hold an asset or intellectual property and has no significant accounting

(B) in sub-clause (d), for the word "records.", the words "records; and" shall

(e) receipt or payment not relatable to the business or operations of the

                                                      739
                                              CLAUSE - 106

106. Clause 106 of the Bill proposes to insert new section after Section 466 of
the Companies Act, 2013

106.1. Provision proposed in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

Insertion of new Section 466A.

After section 466 of the principal Act, the following section shall be inserted,
namely:--

466A. Central Government to issue directions, guidelines or circulars

The Central Government may issue directions or guidelines or circulars, subject to
such conditions, as may be necessary, for the following purposes, namely: --

(a) clarifying the meaning or intent of any rule; and

(b) laying down any procedural requirement ancillary to any rule:

Provided that the Central Government shall hold consultation with expert bodies or
individuals in such manner, as may be prescribed, before issuing directions or
guidelines or circulars, under this section:

Provided further that where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is
necessary or expedient in the public interest that certain directions or guidelines or
circulars are required to be made urgently for the purposes of effective
implementation of the concerned rule, it may issue such directions or guidelines or
circulars, without consulting the expert bodies or individuals and record the reasons
for doing so in writing.

Explanation 1. -- The directions or guidelines or circulars issued under this section
shall be in addition to and not in derogation of any rule made under section 469 and
in case of any conflict, the rule shall prevail.

106.2. Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (The Companies Act, 2013):

                                                      740
Insertion of new section "466A. Central Government to issue directions, guidelines or
circulars".

106.3. Reasons/Justification given by the Ministry for the proposed provisions:

"This clause proposes to insert a new section 466A to enable the Central
Government to issue directions, guidelines or circulars to clarify the meaning or
intent of rules and to lay down procedural requirements for their implementation,
subject to prescribed consultation requirements."

106.4. Important Views/Suggestions given by Experts/Stakeholders:

Some suggestions pertaining to Clause 106 as received from stakeholders/experts
are worded as under:

106.4.1. "The Ministry notes proposed section 466A empowering the Central
Government to issue directions, guidelines or circulars to clarify the meaning or
intent of rules and to lay down ancillary procedural requirements, including urgent
issuance without prior consultation in specified circumstances.

While the provision may improve administrative responsiveness, the Ministry may
suggest that where such instruments have material compliance implications for
industry, consultation with concerned Ministries and stakeholders should ordinarily
be undertaken, except in genuinely urgent cases."

106.4.2. "Make SEBI a mandatory consultee where such circulars affect listed
entities /MIIs, and ensure no derogation from SEBI's framework."

106.4.3. "Clause 106 be retained, subject to the modification that every
direction, guideline or circular issued under section 466A be published on the
Ministry's website and laid before both Houses of Parliament in the manner provided
in section 470A for rules."

106.5. Examination by the Committee:

106.5.1. In response to stakeholder suggestions on Clause 106, the Ministry of
Corporate Affairs consistently maintained that "the provision in the Corporate Laws
(Amendment) Bill, 2026 may be retained without any change."

                                                      741
106.5.2  Specifically, regarding the suggestion in Para 106.4.1 concerning

consultations with Ministries and stakeholders when issuing directions, guidelines, or

circulars, the Ministry noted that that the proposed section already mandates

consulting expert bodies or individuals prior to issuance. The Ministry further clarified

that dispensing with consultation is restricted to cases of urgent public interest with

written reasons recorded, and where applicable, consultations are undertaken in

accordance with the Pre-Legislative Consultation Policy, 2014.

106.5.3  Further, in connection with the suggestion in Para 106.4.2 to make

SEBI a mandatory consultee for matters affecting listed entities or Market

Infrastructure Institutions (MIIs), the Ministry noted that the statutory requirement to

consult expert bodies adequately encompasses sector regulators such as SEBI,

balancing necessary stakeholder consultation with the imperative for timely

regulatory guidance.

106.5.4  Furthermore, regarding the suggestion in Para 106.4.3 to publish all

circulars issued under Section 466A and lay them before both Houses of Parliament,

the Ministry declined the proposal. The Ministry clarified that directions, guidelines,

and circulars under proposed Section 466A are purely administrative in nature,

intended to provide operational guidance and clarify the implementation of the Act

and the rules made thereunder.

106.5.5  Regarding procedural and operational implementation, the Ministry

submitted that Clause 106 of the Bill empowers the Central Government under the

proviso to Section 466A of the Companies Act, 2013 to prescribe the manner of

holding consultations with expert bodies or individuals prior to issuing directions,

guidelines, or circulars. The Ministry emphasized that this delegation is directed

solely at providing procedural flexibility and does not impact substantive compliance

under the law.

                                742
106.6. Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:
The Committee note that Clause 106 of the Bill seeks to insert a new Section
466A in the Companies Act, 2013, empowering the Central Government to
issue directions, guidelines, or circulars to clarify the intent of any rule and
establish ancillary procedural requirements.
The Committee observe with satisfaction that mandatory prior consultation
with experts and stakeholders ensures transparent, informed, and inclusive
decision-making.
Having carefully considered stakeholder suggestions and the submissions of
the Ministry, the Committee endorse acceptance of Clause 106 as proposed.

                                                      743
                          CLAUSE - 107

107. Clause 107 of the Bill intends to amend Section 469 of the Companies
Act, 2013

107.1. Provision proposed in the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026:

Amendment of Section 469

In section 469 of the principal Act, for sub-section (3), the following sub-section shall
be substituted, namely:--

"(3) Any rule made under sub-section (1) may provide that in case of contravention
thereof, the company, every officer of the company who is in default or any other
person, shall be liable to a penalty of an amount, as may be prescribed, which shall
not be more than five lakh rupees, and in case of continuing default, with a further
penalty of such amount, as may be prescribed, which shall not be more than five
thousand rupees for every day during which such default continues.".

107.2. Relevant Provision of the Principal Act (The Companies Act, 2013):

469. Power of Central Government to make rules.

469. (1) *  *             *                      *  *

         (3) Any rule made under sub-section (1) may provide that a contravention
thereof shall be punishable with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees and
where the contravention is a continuing one, with a further fine which may extend to
five hundred rupees for every day after the first during which such contravention
continues.

*           *             *                      *  *

107.3. Reasons/Justification given by the Ministry for the proposed provision:

"The amendment replaces the existing fine-based punishment with an enhanced and
flexible penalty framework, enabling prescription of higher penalties and continuing
penalties for contraventions of Rules. The amendment is part of the broader
decriminalisation exercise under the Bill."

                                                      744
107.4. Important Views/Suggestions given by Experts/Stakeholders:

         During the course of the analysis of the Bill, some important
suggestions/views received from various stakeholders and experts are summarised
as follows:

107.4.1. "Excessive delegation through subordinate legislation should be
avoided. Significant obligations, penalties and compliance requirements should be
incorporated in the statute itself rather than being left entirely to rule making powers."

107.4.2. "The Ministry notes that the substituted section 469(3) enables rules to
prescribe penalties up to five lakh rupees and continuing penalties up to five
thousand rupees per day for contravention of rules made under the Act. While a civil
penalty framework is preferable to criminal prosecution for procedural matters, the
Ministry may suggest that proportionality be expressly kept in view while framing the
relevant rules, particularly for small companies, start-ups and low-risk businesses."

107.4.3. "Clause 107 be reconsidered, and in any event the ceiling be reduced
to Rs.1 lakh, with a proviso that no rule shall provide a penalty for contravention of a
requirement unless the requirement is traceable to a specific provision of the Act."

107.5. Examination by the Committee:

107.5.1. In response to stakeholder suggestions on Clause 107, the Ministry of
Corporate Affairs consistently maintained that "the provision in the Corporate Laws
(Amendment) Bill, 2026 may be retained without any change."

107.5.2  Regarding the suggestion in Para 107.4.1 to avoid excessive

delegation through subordinate legislation, the Ministry noted that the proposed rule-

making powers are primarily procedural and subject to parliamentary oversight,

submitting that the concern will be appropriately addressed when framing the

subordinate legislation.

107.5.3. Further, concerning the suggestion in Para 107.4.2 regarding the need
to maintain proportionality of penalties while framing relevant rules--particularly for

                          745
small companies, startups, and low-risk businesses -- the Ministry declined to
accept the proposal and stated:

"....Under Section 446B of the Companies Act, 2013 small companies, startups, one
person companies and producer companies are already enjoying a proportional
penalty mechanism as they are subject to only one-half of the upper limit of penalty
or Rs. 2 lakh whichever is lower, prescribed under sections of the Companies Act,
2013. Therefore, this suggestion has already been incorporated under the current
regime".

107.5.4. Furthermore, regarding the suggestion in Para 107.4.3 to reduce the
statutory penalty ceiling to Rs.1 lakh, the Ministry clarified that:

"The amendment merely enhances the maximum statutory ceiling up to which
penalties may be prescribed under the rules. It does not mandate a penalty of Rs.5
lakh for every contravention. The actual penalty may be specified in the relevant
rules based on the nature of the default, subject to the statutory ceiling. Further,
under Section 446B of the Companies Act, 2013 small companies, start-ups, one
person companies and producer companies are already enjoying a proportional
penalty mechanism as they are subject to only one-half of the upper limit of penalty
or Rs. 2 lakh whichever is lower, prescribed under sections of the Companies Act,
2013."

107.5.5. Regarding the delegation of procedural and operational details under
subordinate legislation, the Ministry submitted that Clause 107 empowers the Central
Government under Section 469(3) of the Companies Act, 2013 to prescribe penalties
up to Rs.5 lakh, along with a further daily penalty up to Rs.5,000, for contravention of
rules framed under sub-section (1). Justifying this provision, the Ministry highlighted
that penalty amounts require periodic adjustments based on administrative costs,
and embedding specific figures within the primary statute would render the legislation
inflexible and quickly outdated.

107.6. Observations/Recommendations of the Committee:

107.6.1. The Committee note that Clause 107 of the Bill seeks to substitute
sub-section (3) of Section 469 of the Companies Act, 2013 to decriminalize rule
contraventions. As part of the broader decriminalization exercise, the
amendment replaces the existing fine-based criminal punishment with an
enhanced and flexible civil penalty framework, enabling the prescription of

                                                      746
higher penalties and continuing daily penalties for violations of rules framed
under the Act.

The Committee observe that transitioning to an administrative penalty
framework will promote greater voluntary compliance while remaining in
tandem with the broad objectives of the Bill.

After an exhaustive examination of stakeholder suggestions and the
responses of the Ministry, the Committee endorse acceptance of Clause 107 as
initially proposed.

107.6.2. Furthermore, during examination of the Bill, the Committee
observed that certain provisions of the Bill continue to refer to enactments and
authorities by their erstwhile names, notwithstanding that the relevant statutes
have since been renamed or substituted. For example, multiple lingering
references to the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 in the Companies Act, 2013
have been noticed.

The Committee are of the opinion that there should be a clean break from any
reference to the old Acts. As such, retaining references to outdated
nomenclature is inconsistent with the objective of ensuring clarity and
coherence in legislative drafting and may lead to avoidable ambiguity in
interpretation.

The Committee, therefore, recommend that the Ministry may undertake a
comprehensive review of both the principal Acts i.e. the Limited Liability
Partnership Act, 2008 and the Companies Act, 2013 to identify all such
references and appropriately substitute them with the current statutory
nomenclatures to align the legislation with the contemporary legal landscape.
