    CONSOLIDATED OBSERVATIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE
                                    JOINT COMMITTEE

S. Para    Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
           No.
No. No.    1       The Committee note that Clause 1 of the Corporate Laws
                   (Amendment) Bill, 2026 seeks to provide for the short title
1.  1.2.1          and commencement of the proposed legislation. The
                   Committee observe that the Clause empowers the Central
                   Government to bring the provisions of the proposed
                   legislation into force on such date as may be notified in
                   the Official Gazette. Further, it enables different provisions
                   of the proposed legislation to be brought into force on
                   different dates, and provides that any reference in any
                   provision of the Act to its commencement shall be
                   construed as a reference to the date on which that
                   particular provision comes into force.

                   The Committee are of the view that such an enabling
                   provision would provide the necessary flexibility to the
                   Government to implement the various provisions of the
                   Act in a phased manner, in accordance with administrative
                   and operational requirements. The Committee, therefore,
                   recommend that Clause 1 of the Bill be accepted without
                   any amendment.

2.  2.6.1  2       The Committee note that Clause 2 of the Corporate Laws
                   (Amendment) Bill, 2026 seeks to amend sub-section (1) of
                   Section 2 of the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008,
                   wherein definitions of the terms "International Financial
                   Services Centre", "International Financial Services

                                       749
S. Para    Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.    No.
                   Centres Authority", "permitted foreign currency" and
                   "Specified International Financial Services Centre LLP"
                   are proposed to be inserted. The Committee observe that
                   the Clause intends to adopt the meanings of "International
                   Financial Services Centre" and "International Financial
                   Services Centres Authority" from the International
                   Financial Services Centres Authority Act, 2019, thereby
                   ensuring consistency and uniformity across the legislative
                   framework. Further, it empowers the IFSCA to specify
                   permitted foreign currencies in consultation with the
                   Central Government and creates a distinct category of
                   "Specified International Financial Services Centre LLP" to
                   which the special IFSC provisions apply.

                   Keeping in view the justifications provided by the Ministry
                   of Corporate Affairs, examination of the suggestions
                   received from various stakeholders and experts, and after
                   thorough deliberations on the amendments proposed
                   under Clause 2, the Committee are of the opinion that the
                   proposed amendments are required in order to provide the
                   necessary definitional framework for implementation of
                   the special regulatory regime applicable to Limited
                   Liability Partnerships operating in International Financial
                   Services Centres. The Committee, therefore, accept the
                   proposed insertion of clauses (ma), (mb), (qa) and (tb) in
                   sub-section (1) of Section 2 of the Limited Liability
                   Partnership Act, 2008.

3.  2.6.2  2       Further, the Committee note that Clause 18 of the Bill
                   proposes to amend Section 2(28) of the Companies Act,

                                       750
S. Para    Clause  Observation/ Recommendation

                   2013, by substituting the words "the Cost and Works

4.  2.6.3  2       With respect to the proposed rule-making powers
                   conferred upon the concerned Authority under Clause 2,

                   regulations and procedural guidelines. Moreover, the

                   undertaken in close consultation and coordination with the

                                       751
S. Para    Clause  Observation/ Recommendation

5.  3.6.1  3       The Committee note that Clause 3 of the Bill seeks to
                   amend clause (c) and insert a new clause (d) in sub-
                   section (1) of section 11 of the Limited Liability
                   Partnership Act, 2008. The proposed amendment provides
                   that the requirement for a declaration by an advocate,
                   chartered accountant, cost accountant or company
                   secretary in practice at the time of formation or
                   incorporation of an LLP shall apply only where such
                   professional has been engaged for the purpose of
                   incorporation. The Clause also seeks to insert a new
                   proviso in clause (c) of sub-section (2) to provide that a
                   Specified International Financial Services Centre LLP shall
                   undertake only such financial services activities, as are
                   permitted under the framework of the International

                   752
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.     Financial Services Centres Authority.

                 The Committee observe that while the declaration by a
                 subscriber to the incorporation document shall continue
                 to remain mandatory, the requirement of a declaration by a
                 practicing professional has been made conditional upon
                 the engagement of such professional, thereby making
                 professional certification at the time of incorporation
                 optional. The Committee are of the view that the proposed
                 amendment strikes an appropriate balance between
                 maintaining necessary safeguards and reducing
                 procedural requirements. It would ease the incorporation
                 process by providing greater flexibility to LLPs, thereby
                 facilitating the ease of doing business without
                 compromising the integrity of the incorporation process.
                 Further, the Committee note the submission of the
                 Ministry of Corporate Affairs that the proposed
                 amendment emanated from the consultations held with the
                 Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade
                 (DPIIT) and the same is intended to align India's regulatory
                 framework with international best practices, which is
                 expected to have a positive bearing on global business
                 and competitiveness rankings.

                 Accordingly, taking into account the justifications and
                 clarifications furnished by the Ministry, the views and
                 suggestions received from stakeholders and experts, and
                 deliberations held by the Committee, the Committee
                 recommend that Clause 3 be accepted without any

                 753
S. Para    Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.    No.     amendment.

6.  4.6.1  4       The Committee note that Clause 4 of the Bill seeks to
                   insert a new proviso in sub-section (1) of section 13 of the
                   Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008, to provide that a
                   Specified International Financial Services Centre LLP
                   shall, at all times, have its registered office within an
                   International Financial Services Centre. The Committee
                   also note the clarification furnished by the Ministry of
                   Corporate Affairs that the amendment relates only to the
                   location of the registered office and does not restrict the
                   maintenance of disaster recovery (DR) sites or other
                   operational facilities outside the IFSC.

                   Having considered the justification furnished by the
                   Ministry, the views and suggestions received from
                   stakeholders and experts, and the deliberations held
                   thereon, the Committee observe that the proposed
                   amendment is intended to ensure that Specified IFSC LLPs
                   remain within the regulatory jurisdiction of the
                   International Financial Services Centre and operate in
                   accordance with the applicable regulatory framework.
                   Therefore, the Committee accept the Clause 4 of the Bill as
                   proposed.

7.  5.6.1  5       The Committee note that Clause 5 of the Bill seeks to
                   amend sub-section (1) of section 15 of the Limited Liability
                   Partnership Act, 2008 by inserting a proviso requiring
                   every Specified International Financial Services Centre
                   LLP to include the suffix "International Financial Services

                                       754
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 Centre LLP" as part of its name. The Committee observe
                 that the underlying objective of the proposed amendment
                 is to ensure that LLPs operating under the special
                 regulatory framework applicable to International Financial
                 Services Centres (IFSCs) are readily distinguishable from
                 other LLPs, thereby promoting ease of identification for
                 regulators, investors and other stakeholders. However,
                 during the course of examination, various stakeholders
                 and experts raised the concern before the Committee that
                 the mandatory use of the full suffix "International Financial
                 Services Centre LLP" may result in unduly long entity
                 names, creating practical difficulties in business
                 communications, branding and other commercial
                 operations. The Committee further observe that the
                 acronym "IFSC" has acquired widespread regulatory and
                 commercial recognition and it has been consistently used
                 in the regulations and circulars issued by the International
                 Financial Services Centres Authority. In view of its
                 established legal and commercial acceptance, the
                 Committee are of the considered opinion that permitting
                 the abbreviated suffix "IFSC LLP" would equally achieve
                 the legislative objective of clearly identifying Specified
                 IFSC LLPs, while at the same time reducing the practical
                 burden associated with lengthy names and enhancing
                 operational convenience.

                          Therefore, the Committee recommend that Clause 5
                 of the Bill should be modified to provide that a Specified
                 International Financial Services Centre LLP may use either
                 the suffix "International Financial Services Centre LLP" or
                 the suffix "IFSC LLP" as part of its name. Accordingly, the

                                     755
S. Para    Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.    No.     Clause 5 be amended as under:

                   In section 15 of the principal Act, in sub-section (1), the
                   following proviso shall be inserted, namely: --

                   `Provided that a Specified International Financial Services
                   Centre LLP shall have the suffix "International Financial
                   Services Centre LLP" or "IFSC LLP" as part of its name.'.

8.  6.6.1  6       The Committee note that Clause 6 of the Bill seeks to
                   insert a new proviso to sub-section (2) of section 23 of the
                   Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008, to provide that, in
                   case of such class or classes of LLPs regulated by the
                   Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) or the
                   International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA),
                   the requirement relating to filing of changes in the LLP
                   agreement shall be governed by such manner and
                   procedure, as may be prescribed in the rules. The
                   Committee also note that the proposed provision is
                   aligned with the broader policy objective reflected in the
                   amendments proposed under Clauses 7, 12, 13 and 17 of
                   the Bill, which intends to facilitate the establishment and
                   functioning of regulated entities, including Alternative
                   Investment Funds (AIFs), in the form of LLPs.

                   The Committee take note of the submission made by the
                   Ministry of Corporate Affairs that at present, all LLPs are
                   required to file any changes made in the LLP agreement
                   with the Registrar within a period of 30 days. The
                   Committee understand that this requirement has been

                                       756
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 identified as one of the factors contributing to the limited
                 adoption of the LLP structure by AIFs, as AIFs typically
                 witness frequent changes in their partner composition due
                 to entry and exit of large number of investors almost every
                 month, which necessitates corresponding changes in the
                 LLP agreement. Further, the Committee note that
                 stakeholders, including industry representatives, SEBI,
                 IFSCA and the Department of Economic Affairs (DEA),
                 have suggested that the filing requirement may be
                 rationalized by permitting such filings on a periodic basis,
                 such as annually or once in six months, instead of
                 requiring filing of every individual change within 30 days.

                 The Committee are of the view that a periodic filing
                 mechanism would reduce procedural burden on regulated
                 LLPs, while ensuring that necessary information remains
                 available with the regulatory authorities. The Committee,
                 therefore, recommend that the Clause 6 be suitably
                 modified to provide for annual filing of changes in the LLP
                 agreement in respect of such class or classes of LLPs
                 regulated by SEBI or IFSCA. Accordingly, the Committee
                 recommend that Clause 6 of the Bill be amended as under:

                 In section 23 of the principal Act, in sub-section (2), the
                 following proviso shall be inserted, namely: --

                 "Provided that in case of a class or classes of limited
                 liability partnerships regulated by the Securities and
                 Exchange Board of India, or by the International Financial
                 Services Centres Authority, as may be prescribed, the

                                     757
S. Para    Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.    No.
                   requirement of filing any changes in the limited liability
                   partnership agreement shall be on an annual basis, in
                   such form and manner, as may be prescribed.".

9.  6.6.2  6       Further, during the course of examination of the Bill, the
                   Committee received suggestions from various
                   stakeholders and experts regarding the need to ensure
                   confidentiality of investor-related information. The
                   stakeholders expressed the view that details of investors
                   should not become publicly searchable records, and
                   confidential filing mechanisms would enable regulators to
                   access necessary information, while protecting the privacy
                   and commercial interests of investors, particularly
                   sovereign funds, institutional investors, family offices and
                   strategic investors.

                   The Committee appreciate the concerns raised by the
                   stakeholders and are of the view that while regulatory
                   transparency and compliance requirements are essential,
                   adequate safeguards should also be maintained to protect
                   sensitive investor information. The Committee, therefore,
                   are of the opinion that suitable changes should be made in
                   the Act to provide for confidentiality of the details filed by
                   IFSC LLPs. Accordingly, the Committee recommend that
                   section 36 of the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008,
                   which provides for public inspection of documents kept by
                   Registrar, be amended as under:

                   In section 36 of the principal Act, the following proviso

                   758
S. Para    Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.    No.     shall be inserted, namely: --

                   "Provided that the requirements related to inspection of
                   documents under this section shall not apply in case of a
                   class or classes of limited liability partnerships registered
                   and regulated by the Securities and Exchange Board of
                   India, or by the International Financial Services Centres
                   Authority, as may be prescribed.".

10. 6.6.3  6       Moreover, the Committee observe that several documents
                   filed with the Registrar contain personal information of
                   partners, designated partners, investors, managers and
                   other individuals and many of these documents are
                   available for public inspection under the Limited Liability
                   Partnership Act, 2008. The Committee are of the view that
                   while transparency and public access to statutory records
                   are essential for maintaining corporate accountability,
                   such access should be balanced with the need to
                   safeguard personal data and protect the privacy of
                   individuals. Therefore, there is a need to ensure that
                   personal data contained in documents filed with the
                   Registrar of Companies is collected, processed, stored,
                   disclosed and made available for inspection in a manner
                   that is consistent with the provisions and principles of the
                   Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023.

                   The Committee also observe that LLPs should be provided
                   with an appropriate mechanism to rectify clerical,
                   arithmetical, typographical or factual errors or omissions
                   in documents or information filed with the Registrar. The

                                       759
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 Committee are of the opinion that permitting such
                 rectification through a prescribed application process
                 would facilitate correction of inadvertent errors, reduce
                 unnecessary compliance burden and ensure accuracy and
                 reliability of statutory records maintained by the Registrar.

                 Further, the Committee feel that LLPs should also be
                 provided with an appropriate provision for seeking refund
                 of fees paid for registration or filing of any form or
                 document in cases where such form or document could
                 not be registered or filed due to technical reasons. At
                 present, such matters are governed by the refund manual
                 issued by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs. Therefore, the
                 Committee are of the view that incorporating a specific
                 statutory provision for refund of fees in such cases would
                 provide greater clarity and certainty to LLPs and prevent
                 avoidable financial burden, particularly where the filing
                 could not be completed due to technical issues.

                 In view of the above, the Committee recommend that the
                 Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008 should be amended
                 as under:

                 After section 69 of the principal Act, the following sections
                 shall be inserted, namely: --

                 "69A. Refund of fees or any other payment.

                 For refund of fees or any other payment, the provisions of
                 section 403A of the Companies Act, 2013 (18 of 2013) shall

                                     760
S. Para    Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.    No.     mutatis mutandis apply."

                   "69B. Rectification in documents filed with the Registrar.

                   For rectification of the documents filed with the Registrar,
                   the provisions of section 398A of the Companies Act, 2013
                   (18 of 2013) shall mutatis mutandis apply."

                   "69C. Application of the provisions of Digital Personal
                   Data Protection Act, 2023.

                   All the provisions of the Digital Personal Data Protection
                   Act, 2023 and the rules made thereunder relating to
                   consent and processing of digital personal data, in so far
                   as they are not inconsistent with this Act, shall apply in
                   relation to the records in electronic form specified in
                   sections 36 and 68 of this Act."

12. 7.6.1  7       The Committee note that Clause 7 of the Bill seeks to
                   insert a new proviso to sub-section (2) of section 25 of the

                   regulated by the Securities and Exchange Board of India

                   intends to facilitate the adoption of the LLP structure by

                                       762
S. Para    Clause  Observation/ Recommendation

                   relaxation is limited to reporting of changes in partners
                   and does not affect the existing requirement under section

                   recommend that Clause 7 of the Bill be accepted without
                   any amendment.

13. 8.6.1  8       The Committee note that Clause 8 of the Bill seeks to
                   insert three new provisos in sub-section (2) of section 32
                   of the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008. The
                   proposed amendments provide that the monetary value of
                   contribution of each partner in a Specified IFSC LLP shall
                   be accounted for and disclosed in a permitted foreign
                   currency. The Clause further provides a transitional
                   framework for the Specified IFSC LLPs established before
                   the commencement of the Corporate Laws (Amendment)
                   Act, 2026, to convert the monetary value of the partners'
                   contributions from Indian Rupees to a permitted foreign
                   currency within the period and in the manner as specified
                   by the International Financial Services Centres Authority,
                   in consultation with the Central Government. It also
                   provides that, after the commencement of the proposed

                                       763
S. Para    Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.    No.
                   legislation, such LLPs shall not receive or accept any
                   monetary contribution from a partner unless the monetary
                   value of such contributions has first been converted into a
                   permitted foreign currency.

                   The Committee are of the opinion that the proposed
                   amendments are intended to bring uniformity and
                   consistency in the accounting and reporting practices of
                   Specified IFSC LLPs by ensuring that the monetary value
                   of partner contributions is maintained and disclosed in a
                   permitted foreign currency. Further, the transitional
                   provisions provided for existing IFSC LLPs would facilitate
                   a smooth transition to the proposed regulatory framework
                   without causing any disruption to their operations.

                   Accordingly, having considered the justification furnished
                   by the Ministry, the views and suggestions received from
                   stakeholders and experts, and the deliberations held
                   thereon, the Committee accept the Clause 8 of the Bill as
                   proposed.

14. 9.6.1  9       The Committee note that Clause 9 of the Bill seeks to
                   insert a new section 33A in the Limited Liability
                   Partnership Act, 2008, to provide that the provisions of
                   section 247 of the Companies Act, 2013, relating to
                   valuation by registered valuers, shall apply mutatis
                   mutandis to the valuation of a partner's contribution in an
                   LLP, or valuation of any property, assets, net worth or
                   liabilities of such LLP, or wherever such valuation is
                   required under the provisions of the Limited Liability

                                       764
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.     Partnership Act, 2008 or the rules made thereunder.

                 The Committee observe that while the Income-tax Act
                 increasingly relies upon fair market valuation principles
                 for determining tax implications in cases such as, partner
                 retirement and reconstitution of LLPs, the Limited Liability
                 Partnership Act does not presently provide for a
                 corresponding mechanism to ensure uniformity and
                 transparency in valuation. The Committee agree with the
                 contention of the Ministry of Corporate Affairs that, in the
                 absence of a specific statutory valuation framework under
                 the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008, there has been
                 a legislative gap in relation to valuation requirements
                 concerning partner contributions, assets, liabilities and
                 other financial aspects of LLPs. Therefore, the Committee
                 believe that the proposed amendment would address the
                 absence of a specific statutory valuation framework under
                 the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008, by providing a
                 consistent and legally recognized valuation mechanism for
                 LLPs.

                 The Committee are of the view that by adopting the
                 established framework under section 247 of the
                 Companies Act, 2013, the proposed amendment would
                 enhance transparency, ensure greater certainty in
                 valuation-related matters, facilitate better coordination
                 between corporate law and taxation provisions, and help
                 in reducing disputes and litigation arising from valuation
                 issues, while safeguarding the revenue interests of the
                 Government. Accordingly, the Committee recommend that

                                     765
S. Para    Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.    No.     Clause 9 of the Bill be accepted without any amendment.

15. 9.6.2  9       Further, the Committee note the submissions made by the

                                       766
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation

16. 10.6.1 10    The Committee note that Clause 10 of the Bill seeks to
                 insert two new provisos in sub-section (1) of section 34 of
                 the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008, to provide that
                 a Specified IFSC LLP maintaining its partners'
                 contributions in a permitted foreign currency, shall also
                 prepare and maintain its books of account, financial
                 statements and other records in permitted foreign
                 currency. The Clause further provides that such LLP may
                 prepare and maintain the aforesaid records in Indian
                 Rupees, if permitted by the International Financial
                 Services Centres Authority. The Clause also seeks to
                 decriminalize the offences under sub-sections (1) and (2)
                 of section 34 by rationalizing the applicable penalty
                 provisions.

                 The Committee observe that the proposed amendments
                 intend to align the accounting and record-keeping
                 requirements of Specified IFSC LLPs with the foreign
                 currency-based framework applicable to entities operating
                 within International Financial Services Centres, thereby

                                     767
S. Para   Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.   No.
                  ensuring consistency between their financial reporting
                  practices and the nature of their operations. At the same
                  time, the provision enabling IFSCA to permit preparation
                  of accounts and records in Indian Rupees, provides the
                  necessary flexibility and facilitates ease of compliance.
                  The Committee further observe that the proposed
                  rationalization of penalty provisions under section 34 aims
                  to simplify the compliance framework by avoiding
                  duplication and overlap in penal consequences, which is
                  in line with the objective of decriminalizing procedural
                  offences, while ensuring effective regulatory compliance.

                  In view of the above, the Committee are satisfied that the
                  proposed amendments would provide greater regulatory
                  clarity, facilitate ease of doing business for Specified IFSC
                  LLPs and ensure consistency with the regulatory
                  framework applicable to entities operating in International
                  Financial Services Centres. Therefore, the Committee
                  accept the Clause 10 of the Bill as proposed.

17. 11.6  11      The Committee find that the amendment proposed under
                  Clause 11 pertains to Section 38 of the LLP Act,2008. The
                  Committee note the suggestion that monetary penalties
                  under rules and amended provisions be calibrated
                  proportionately, especially for small companies, start-ups
                  and low-risk entities.

                  The Committee also note the reply of the Ministry that the
                  monetary penalties under the Amendment Bill have been
                  proposed after considering the nature and gravity of the

                                      768
S. Para   Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.   No.
                  defaults and the aspect of proportionality. The Ministry
                  has also stated that the Amendment Bill already
                  incorporates a calibrated penalty framework based on the
                  seriousness of the default.

                  Thus, after considering the replies of the Ministry and
                  noting that the proposed provision is aligned with the
                  stated object of ease of doing business and is likely to
                  reduce avoidable risk perception for investors, boards and
                  entrepreneurs in relation to non- substantive compliance
                  lapses, the Committee are of the view that the amendment
                  under Clause 11 is appropriate. Accordingly, the
                  Committee accept the amendment in its present form.

18. 12.6  12      The Committee note that Clause 12 of the Bill seeks to
                  insert a new subsection i.e. 57A after Section 57 of the
                  Principal Act. This amendment introduces a statutory
                  framework to enable specified trusts, registered by SEBI
                  or IFSCA having prescribed activities to convert into LLPs.
                  It facilitates the adoption of the LLP structure by
                  investment vehicles with provisions on eligibility and the
                  conversion process, thereby promoting flexibility in fund
                  structuring and improving ease of doing business.

                  The Committee note that various suggestions received
                  with respect to Clause 12 pertain to Schedule V being
                  introduced under Clause 17 of the Bill. However, the
                  Ministry, based on stakeholder suggestions received on
                  other associated Clauses, has accepted the need to bring
                  greater clarity with regard to the conversion process from

                                      769
S. Para   Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.   No.     Trust to LLP.

                  In this regard, as a step towards introducing clarity in
                  Clause 12, the Committee recommend that the Explanation
                  under Clause 12 be reframed to include in the meaning of
                  `Specified Trusts' those Trusts which are not only
                  registered but also regulated by Securities and Exchange
                  Board of India, or by the International Financial Services
                  Centres Authority. Thus, Clause 12 may be redrafted as
                  under:

                  "After section 57 of the principal Act, the following section
                  shall be inserted, namely: -- 57A. A specified trust may
                  convert into a limited liability partnership in accordance
                  with the provisions of this Chapter and the Fifth Schedule.

                  Explanation. --For the purposes of this section, the term
                  "specified trust" means a trust established under the
                  Indian Trusts Act, 1882 or under a Central Act or State Act,
                  and registered and regulated by the Securities and
                  Exchange Board of India, or by the International Financial
                  Services Centres Authority, as the case may be, having
                  such activities as may be prescribed.".

19. 13.6  13      The Committee note that Clause 13 of the Bill substitutes
                  Section 58 of the Principal Act. The Committee find that
                  this amendment expands the scope of conversion into
                  LLPs to include specified trusts by incorporating a new
                  Schedule V and aligning section 58(1) accordingly. It
                  facilitates the use of the LLP structure for Alternative

                                      770
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 Investment Funds by providing a statutory pathway for
                 their conversion, while also providing post-registration
                 intimation requirements.

                 The Committee also note the suggestion that the word
                 `Trustees' must be replaced with `Investors' and `Manager'
                 since Trustees are custodial/fiduciary intermediaries and
                 not economic stakeholders. Investors (LPs) are the
                 beneficial owners and capital contributors and therefore
                 must become LLP partners. Agreeing in principle with the
                 suggestion the Committee find that the investors
                 (beneficiaries) indeed possess the substantive economic
                 interest, reap the financial benefits, and ultimately assume
                 the risk. In contrast, the trustees generally act in a purely
                 fiduciary, administrative, or professional capacity. The
                 investors cannot be allowed to hide behind the trustees.
                 Because the investors reap the economic benefits, they, in
                 addition to the trustees, should be bound by the rules
                 governing the conversion. Moreover, since Managers are
                 responsible for all investment decisions and compliance
                 and they must be made liable in the scheme of conversion
                 as well.

                 Accordingly, in view of the above, the Committee
                 recommend that under Clause 13, Section 58 (2) be
                 reframed as follows:

                 "(2) Upon such conversion, the partners of the firm, the
                 shareholders of private company or unlisted public
                 company, or the trustees, investors and managers of the

                                     771
S. Para   Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.   No.
                  specified trust, as the case may be, the limited liability
                  partnership to which such firm or such company or such
                  specified trust has converted, and the partners of the
                  limited liability partnership, shall be bound by the
                  provisions of the Second Schedule, the Third Schedule,
                  the Fourth Schedule or the Fifth Schedule, as the case
                  may be, applicable to them."

20. 14.6  14      The Committee note that Clause 14 of the Bill seeks to
                  insert new provisos in section 68 of the principal Act, in
                  sub-section (1). The Clause aims to insert a specific filing
                  framework for Specified IFSC LLPs by permitting filings in
                  a permitted foreign currency, while ensuring that statutory
                  fees, fines and penalties continue to be payable in Indian
                  rupees. According to the Ministry, this is consistent with
                  the corresponding provisions proposed under section 43A
                  of the Companies Act, 2013.

                  The Committee find that stakeholders have suggested that
                  the treatment of existing approvals and pending matters,
                  valuation, and tax reporting be finalised in consultation
                  with the relevant stakeholders and published, before these
                  provisions are brought into force

                  The Committee note that the Ministry has stated that
                  Clause 14 of the Bill empowers the Central Government to
                  make rules under the proviso to sub-section (1) of section
                  68 of the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008, in respect
                  of the manner in which a Specified International Financial
                  Services Centres LLP shall use permitted foreign

                                      772
S. Para   Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.   No.
                  currency, for the purpose of filing, recording, or
                  registering any document under the said section. Further,
                  adding that the process of consultation with the Central
                  Government and other stakeholders, as considered
                  necessary, would be done while framing the relevant
                  subordinate legislation. The comments received from the
                  public, relevant Ministries/Departments, regulators and
                  other stakeholders shall be duly considered before the
                  Rules are finalised.

                  The Committee are of the view that the formulation of
                  these rules must be undertaken through inter-ministerial
                  coordination and stakeholder consultation to ensure
                  alignment with India's broader macroeconomic, trade, and
                  external sector policies. In view of the Ministry's reply that
                  extensive stakeholder consultation will take place before
                  framing of rules the Committee endorse the amendment
                  proposed in Clause 14.

21. 15.6  15      The Committee note that Clause 15 of the Bill seeks to
                  insert a new section after Section 68 A of the Principal Act.
                  The amendment introduces a formal appellate mechanism
                  against decisions of the Registrar relating to name
                  reservation and incorporation of LLPs. It enables
                  aggrieved persons to prefer an appeal before an
                  authorised officer of the Central Government, thereby
                  enhancing administrative accountability.

                  The Committee also observe that the clause currently
                  allows appeals to be made to any unspecified "officer of

                                      773
S. Para   Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.   No.
                  the Central Government." In this regard the Committee find
                  that it has been suggested that such as officer must hold
                  at least the rank of Joint Director.

                  The Committee are in agreement with the suggestion
                  proposed given that it would align the Appellate authority
                  in line of the similar provision under the Companies Act,
                  2013. Accordingly, The Committee recommend that Clause
                  15 may be reframed as under:

                  "After section 68A of the principal Act, the following
                  section shall be inserted, namely: --

                  "68B. Any person aggrieved by the decision of the
                  Registrar under section 12 or section 16, may prefer an
                  appeal to an officer not below the rank of the Joint Director
                  as may be authorized by the Central Government, in such
                  form and manner, and within such period, as may be
                  prescribed."

22. 16.6  16      The Committee note that Clause 16 of the Bill seeks to
                  insert new subsections after Sub-Section (1) and Sub-
                  Section (9), in section 76A of the principal Act. The new
                  Sub-Section 1A provides a statutory mechanism enabling
                  a limited liability partnership, or its partner or designated
                  partner, to make an application for adjudication of penalty
                  under section 76A of the Principal Act. The new sub-
                  section 10 is intended to clarify that the above
                  decriminalisation shall have a retrospective effect and the
                  relevant details (i.e. manner of withdrawal of

                                      774
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 complaint/prosecution, manner of transfer of such matter
                 for adjudication), shall be provided through a scheme to
                 be notified by the Central Government.

                 The Committee note the suggestion to retain the Clause,
                 provided that the transition Scheme under new sub-
                 section (10) is notified within six months of
                 commencement and laid before both Houses of
                 Parliament. The Committee further observes that the
                 Ministry agrees with this suggestion, finding it consistent
                 with the proposed amendment, and has stated that the
                 Scheme will be released following due consultation.

                 The Committee are of the opinion that apart from the
                 limited liability partnership, its partner or designated
                 partner, `any other person' may also be allowed to file the
                 application for adjudication of penalty under 76 A of the
                 Principal Act. This step will be in support of reducing
                 compliance burden and provide flexibility in procedural

                 partners.

                 Accordingly, the Committee recommend that in Clause 16
                 (1A) the words `any other person' be added and the Clause
                 be amended as follows:

                 "In section 76A of the principal Act, --

                 (a) after sub-section (1), the following sub-section shall

S. Para   Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.   No.     be inserted, namely: --

                       `(1A) A limited liability partnership or its partner or
                  designated partner or any other person may make an

                  adjudication of penalty'.";

23. 17.6  17      The Committee observe that the Clause 17 of the Bill seeks
                  to insert a new Schedule (Fifth Schedule) to the LLP Act,
                  2008 referred to in section 57A to specify the conditions
                  which would need to be fulfilled before conversion of a
                  specified trust into a limited liability partnership. The
                  provisions of Fifth Schedule are similar to conditions
                  provided under Second, Third and Fourth Schedules to the
                  Act. This amendment will facilitate conversion of
                  Alternative Investment Funds formed as trusts into LLPs.
                  The proposed Fifth Schedule comprises 17 paras
                  governing the conversion of specified trusts into limited
                  liability partnerships and providing for a smooth transition
                  upon such conversion. The Committee, after close
                  scrutiny and examination of Clause 17, taking into
                  consideration the views and suggestions received from
                  various stakeholders and their own deliberations, accept
                  the Clause subject to the amendments recommended in
                  respect of the relevant paras of the proposed Fifth
                  Schedule under it. The Committee have examined each of
                  the paras of the proposed Fifth Schedule separately and
                  their observations and recommendations are contained in

                  776
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.     the succeeding paras of this Report.

                 17.6.2  On the issue of delegation of legislative

                 powers proposed under Clause 17, the Committee

                 examined the justification furnished by the Ministry. The

                 Ministry has submitted that the matters proposed to be

                 prescribed under para 4(a) of the Fifth Schedule relate to

                 the form, manner and fee for filing the statement

                 containing the prescribed particulars while the matters

                 proposed under para 5 relate to the form and manner in

                 which the resulting limited liability partnership is required

                 to intimate the concerned authority of the conversion and

                 furnish the particulars of the limited liability partnership. It

                 has been further stated that these delegations are

                 procedural in nature and are intended only to prescribe the

                 operational modalities for implementation of the proposed

                 provisions. The Committee, after examining the

                 justification furnished by the Ministry, are satisfied that the

                 proposed delegation relates only to procedural and

                 operational matters.

24. 17(1).6 17   The Committee note that para 1 of the proposed Fifth
                 Schedule seeks to define the key expressions governing
                 the proposed framework for conversion of specified trusts
                 into limited liability partnerships. During the examination
                 of the Bill, stakeholders suggested that the manager/fund
                 manager should also be recognized in the proposed
                 conversion framework.

                 The Committee are of the view that, once the manager is
                                     777
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 proposed to be assigned a role under the Fifth Schedule,
                 the expression `manager' or `fund manager' should also be
                 specifically defined with reference to the applicable SEBI
                 and IFSCA regulations to ensure legal certainty and
                 consistency with the regulatory framework governing
                 Alternative Investment Funds.

                 The Committee, therefore, accept the para 1 of the
                 proposed Fifth Schedule subject to the following
                 amendments. Insert the following clause after clause (b):

                 "(ba) "manager" means a manager as defined under the
                 Securities and Exchange Board of India (Alternative
                 Investment Funds) Regulations, 2012 made under the
                 Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992 and
                 includes fund manager or fund management entity as
                 defined under the International Financial Services Centres
                 Authority (Fund Management) Regulations, 2025 made
                 under the International Financial Services Centres
                 Authority Act, 2019;"

25. 17(2).6 17   The Committee note that para 2 of the proposed Fifth
                 Schedule provides the enabling framework for conversion
                 of a specified trust into a limited liability partnership and
                 specifies the persons who shall be bound by the
                 provisions of the proposed Schedule upon such
                 conversion. The Committee further note that the Ministry
                 has accepted the suggestion to broaden the category of
                 persons bound by the provisions of the Fifth Schedule and
                 has agreed to suitably amend the provision in consultation

                                     778
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 with the Department of Economic Affairs, the Securities
                 and Exchange Board of India and the International
                 Financial Services Centres Authority.

                 The Committee are of the view that such amendment would
                 ensure consistency with the revised conversion framework
                 by extending the application of the proposed Fifth
                 Schedule to all persons through whom the conversion may
                 be effected and would appropriately reflect the operational
                 structure of Alternative Investment Funds.

                 Accordingly, the Committee propose following
                 amendment:

                 In paragraph 2(2) of the proposed Fifth Schedule, for "the
                 trustees of the specified trust", shall be substituted with
                 "the trustees, investors and managers of the specified
                 trust".

                 17(2).6.2 The Committee note that the proposed
                 framework does not clearly address the conversion of
                 multi-scheme Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) into
                 limited liability partnerships. The Committee also note the
                 clarification furnished by the Ministry that the proposed
                 framework is intended primarily to facilitate conversion of
                 specified trusts having a single scheme and that the
                 substantial majority of Alternative Investment Funds
                 registered with SEBI, or regulated by IFSCA, fall within this
                 category. The Ministry has explained that an individual
                 scheme of a multi-scheme Alternative Investment Fund

                                     779
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 does not possess a separate legal identity distinct from the
                 trust and that permitting scheme-wise conversion would
                 give rise to complexities. The Committee, however, are of
                 the view that there is a need to provide enabling framework
                 for conversion of specified trust with multiple schemes
                 also.

                 The Committee, therefore, recommend that the

                 Government should provide for a carve out, by way of an

                 enabling framework for conversion of such specified trust

                 as are registered or regulated by SEBI or IFSCA, and which

                 operate or maintain multiple schemes.  Further,

                 keeping in view the larger aim to facilitate conversion of

                 specified trust to LLP, the Committee recommend that the

                 Government may provide a detailed framework to address

                 the consequential issues arising out of such conversion,

                 like filing taxation, capital gains, stamp duty implications,

                 etc. If required, suitable amendments may be carried out in

                 the relevant Acts.

                 Accordingly, the following sub-para may be inserted after
                 sub-para (2) of para 2 of the Fifth Schedule:

                 "(2A) Notwithstanding anything contained in this Schedule,
                 where a specified trust operates or maintains multiple
                 schemes, or such other structure which is not already
                 covered under this Schedule, a framework may be
                 provided for conversion of such trusts into a limited
                 liability partnership, subject to such conditions, and

                 780
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.     procedure, as may be prescribed.

                 (2B) The Central Government may, in consultation and
                 coordination with the Ministries, Departments and
                 regulatory authorities concerned, notify a comprehensive
                 framework to facilitate the conversion of specified trusts
                 into limited liability partnerships, including provisions
                 relating to taxation, capital gains, stamp duty, transfer and
                 vesting of assets and liabilities, filing and compliance
                 requirements, continuation of rights and obligations, and
                 other consequential or incidental matters arising from such
                 conversion.

                 (2C) The Central Government may also undertake or
                 recommend suitable amendments to the relevant laws,
                 wherever necessary, to ensure a smooth and seamless
                 implementation of such conversion."

                 Subject to the amendments recommended above, the
                 Committee accept the para 2 of the Fifth Schedule.

26. 17(3).6 17   The Committee note that para 3 of the proposed Fifth
                 Schedule prescribes the eligibility conditions for
                 conversion of a specified trust into a limited liability
                 partnership. The Committee have carefully considered the
                 views of the stakeholders, the written replies furnished by
                 the Ministry and the clarifications given during the oral
                 evidence. The Committee also note that the original
                 provision restricted eligibility for conversion to cases
                 where the partners of the resulting limited liability

                                     781
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.     partnership were only the trustees of the specified trust.

                 17(3).6.2 During the examination of the Bill, several
                 stakeholders submitted that the proposed restriction did
                 not adequately reflect the operational structure of
                 Alternative Investment Funds. They further stated that
                 limiting eligibility only to trustees excluded managers and
                 investors from the conversion framework at the threshold
                 stage, thereby making the proposed conversion
                 mechanism less practical and flexible. The Committee are
                 of the considered view that omission of the said restriction
                 would provide the necessary flexibility in the conversion
                 process and substantially address the concerns expressed
                 by the stakeholders. Accordingly, the Committee
                 recommend that para 3 of the proposed Fifth Schedule be
                 amended by omitting the following:

                 "only if the partners of the limited liability partnership into
                 which the specified trust is to be converted, are trustees of
                 such specified trust and no one else."

                 17(3).6.3 The Committee further are of the view that
                 requiring a prior No Objection Certificate from the
                 Securities and Exchange Board of India or the International
                 Financial Services Centres Authority, as the case may be,
                 would ensure that the conversion process remains subject
                 to appropriate regulatory oversight. Accordingly, the
                 Committee recommend that para 3 of the proposed Fifth
                 Schedule be amended by inserting, after the words "in

                 782
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.     accordance with this Schedule", the following:

                 " only if the Securities and Exchange Board of India, or by
                 the International Financial Services Centres Authority, as
                 the case may be, has given their no objection to such
                 conversion"

27. 17(4).6 17   The Committee note that para 4 of the proposed Fifth
                 Schedule prescribes the statements and documents
                 required to be filed for conversion of a specified trust into
                 a limited liability partnership. After considering the views
                 expressed by the stakeholders, the written replies
                 furnished by the Ministry and the clarifications given
                 during the oral evidence, the Committee recommend that
                 para 4 of the proposed Fifth Schedule be adopted subject
                 to the following amendments.

                 The Committee are of the opinion that the application for
                 conversion should be filed only by a person duly
                 authorised by investors holding not less than three-fourths
                 in value. Such a requirement would ensure that the
                 application is instituted only with the authority of the
                 investors competent to approve the proposed conversion.
                 Accordingly, the Committee recommend that in paragraph
                 4(a) of the proposed Fifth Schedule, for the words "a
                 statement by all of its trustees", the words "a statement by
                 the applicant duly authorised by the investors representing
                 not less than three-fourth in value of the investments in the
                 specified trust" shall be substituted.

                 783
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 17(4).6.2 The Committee are also of the view that
                 conversion of specified trusts regulated by the Securities
                 and Exchange Board of India or the International Financial
                 Services Centres Authority should remain subject to
                 appropriate regulatory oversight. In view of the
                 Committee's recommendation that conversion should be
                 undertaken only after obtaining a prior No Objection
                 Certificate from the concerned regulator, the Committee
                 consider it necessary that the application for conversion
                 should also be accompanied by a copy of such No
                 Objection Certificate. Accordingly, the Committee
                 recommend that paragraph 4(a) of the proposed Fifth
                 Schedule be amended by inserting the following new
                 clause after clause (ii):

                 "(iia) a copy of the no objection referred to in paragraph 3;

                 17(4).6.3 The Committee feel that the application should
                 clearly disclose the period from which the specified trust
                 has remained subject to the regulatory framework of the
                 Securities and Exchange Board of India or the International
                 Financial Services Centres Authority, as the case may be.
                 Such disclosure would facilitate verification of the
                 regulatory status of the specified trust at the time of
                 conversion.

                 The Committee, therefore, recommend that in the clause
                 relating to the regulatory registration of the specified trust,
                 the provision be amended to substitute the words "the date
                 on which the specified trust was registered with" with the

                                     784
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 words "the date from which the specified trust has been
                 registered and regulated by".

                 17(4).6.4 The Committee further note that stakeholders
                 had suggested that investor consent for conversion should
                 be determined on the basis of the value of their interests
                 rather than merely their numerical strength. The Committee
                 are of the considered view that requiring the consent of
                 investors holding three-fourths in value would better
                 reflect the economic interests of investors and provide a
                 more appropriate basis for determining investor consent in
                 the case of specified trusts regulated as Alternative
                 Investment Funds.

                 Therefore, they recommend that in clause (a)(iv) relating to
                 investor consent "the consent of three-fourths of the
                 investors of the trust;" shall be substituted with "the
                 consent of three-fourths of the investors in value of the
                 trust;"

28. 17(5).4 17   The Committee note that the proposed provision provides
                 for registration of the conversion by the Registrar,
                 issuance of a certificate of registration specifying the
                 effective date of conversion and requires the limited
                 liability partnership to intimate the concerned authority
                 with which the specified trust was established within
                 fifteen days of such registration. The Committee are of the
                 view that the proposed provision facilitates an orderly and
                 transparent conversion process and ensures that the
                 concerned authority is duly informed of the conversion.

                                     785
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 The Committee, therefore, recommend that para 5 of the
                 proposes Fifth Schedule may be adopted as it is.

29. 17(6).4 17   The Committee note that the proposed provision
                 empowers the Registrar to refuse registration where he is
                 not satisfied with the particulars or other information
                 furnished under the Act. It also provides for appeal against
                 such refusal before the Tribunal and also empowers the
                 Registrar to require verification of the prescribed
                 documents. The Committee further note the concern
                 expressed by a stakeholder that despite the facility of
                 resubmission, an applicant may be apprehensive of refusal
                 of registration without a reasoned order. The Committee
                 also note the Ministry's clarification that there is a
                 mechanism for resubmission of forms in cases of
                 deficiencies. The Committee, therefore, are of the opinion
                 that the proposed provision, read with the appellate
                 remedy before the Tribunal, provides adequate safeguards.
                 Accordingly, the Committee recommend that para 6 of the
                 Fifth Schedule may be adopted without any amendment.

30. 17(7).6 17   The Committee note that the para 7 of the Fifth Schedule
                 under Clause 17 seeks to provide that upon registration of
                 conversion, all tangible and intangible property, assets,
                 interests, rights, privileges, liabilities and obligations of the
                 specified trust shall vest in the resulting limited liability
                 partnership by operation of law and that the specified trust
                 shall stand dissolved. The Committee further note the
                 Ministry's clarification that such vesting takes place by
                 operation of law without requiring execution of any

                                     786
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 separate deed. Having considered the views expressed by
                 the stakeholders and the response of the Ministry, the
                 Committee are satisfied that the proposed provision
                 adequately provides for the legal consequences of
                 conversion. In view of this, the Committee accept para 7 of
                 the proposed Fifth Schedule without any modification.

                 17(7).6.2 The Committee, however, recommend that the
                 Central Government may frame suitable Rules, in
                 consultation with the Securities and Exchange Board of
                 India (SEBI), the International Financial Services Centres
                 Authority (IFSCA) and the Registrar of Companies to
                 ensure time-bound processing of applications for
                 conversion and seamless coordination amongst the
                 concerned authorities to facilitate timely updation of

                 hardships for entities.

31. 17(8).4 17   The Committee note that Clause 17 seeks to insert the Fifth
                 Schedule in the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008 and
                 para 8 thereof requires the limited liability partnership to
                 notify the concerned authority of the conversion and
                 update the registration of property vested in it consequent
                 upon such conversion. The Committee observe that the
                 proposed provision is necessary to facilitate updation of
                 statutory records relating to property and ensure
                 continuity of title consequent upon conversion. Therefore,
                 the Committee accept the para 8 of the proposed Fifth
                 Schedule as it is.

32. 17(9).4 17   The Committee observe that para 9 of the proposed Fifth

                 Schedule, inserted by Clause 17 of the Bill, provides that

                 all proceedings by or against the specified trust or its

                 trustees, pending before any Court, Tribunal or other

                 authority on the date of conversion, shall continue and

                 may be completed and enforced by or against the resulting

                 limited liability partnership. The Committee observe that

                 the intention of the provision is to ensure that the

                 conversion does not interrupt or prejudice pending

                 proceedings and that the rights and liabilities of the

                 parties thereto continue unaffected. The Committee,

                 therefore, recommend that para 9 of the proposed Fifth

33. 17(10).4 17  The Committee note that para 10 of the proposed Fifth
                 Schedule provides for the continued enforceability of any
                 conviction, ruling, order or judgment notwithstanding the
                 conversion of a specified trust into a limited liability
                 partnership. The Committee further note that in the
                 preceding paras of the proposed Fifth Schedule, they have
                 recommended recognition of managers as persons
                 through whom the conversion may be effected and who
                 would be bound by the provisions of the proposed Fifth
                 Schedule.

                 The Committee are, therefore, of the view that the
                 proposed provision should also extend to managers acting
                 on behalf of the specified trust, in addition to trustees, so
                 as to maintain consistency with the revised conversion
                 framework and ensure continuity in respect of actions

                                     788
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 undertaken by such managers prior to conversion.
                 Accordingly, the Committee recommend that in para 10 of
                 the proposed Fifth Schedule, after the words "its
                 trustees,", the words "or its managers" be inserted.

34. 17(11).4 17  The Committee note that para 11 of the proposed Fifth
                 Schedule, inserted by Clause 17 of the Bill, provides that
                 every agreement to which the specified trust was a party
                 immediately before the date of registration shall continue
                 to have effect as if the resulting limited liability partnership
                 were a party thereto in place of the specified trust. The
                 Committee are of the view that the proposed provision is
                 necessary to preserve contractual continuity and avoid
                 disruption of existing legal relationships merely on
                 account of the conversion. The Committee, therefore,
                 accept para 11 of the proposed Fifth Schedule without any
                 amendment.

35. 17(12).4 17  The Committee note that para 12 of the proposed Fifth
                 Schedule, inserted by Clause 17 of the Bill, provides that
                 all deeds, contracts, schemes, bonds, agreements,
                 applications, instruments and arrangements subsisting
                 immediately before the date of registration shall continue
                 in force and remain enforceable by or against the resulting
                 limited liability partnership. The Committee find that the
                 proposed provision is necessary to ensure seamless
                 continuity and enforceability of all existing legal and
                 commercial arrangements notwithstanding the
                 conversion. The Committee, therefore, recommend that
                 para 12 of the proposed Fifth Schedule may be adopted

36. 17(13).4 17  The Committee note that para 13 of the proposed Fifth

37. 17(14).6 17  The Committee note that para 14 seeks to provide for

38. 17(15).6 17  The Committee note that para 15 of the proposed Fifth

                 (iv) To insert new clause (74A) to define the term

                 (v) To amend sub-clauses (i) and (ii) of clause (85) to

                      The Committee note that the proposed changes in
                 clause (28), seeks to alter foundational definition by
                 replacing the title "Cost and Works Accountants" with
                 "Cost Accountants" in Section 2(28). As the existing text
                 mentions outdated legislative reference for financial
                 professionals, the amendment rectifies this by substituting
                 the reference with the correct and appropriate legal title
                 which removes nomenclature ambiguities and ensures
                 systemic legal harmony.

                     The Committee note that the proposed proviso to
                 clause (41) seeks to enable companies and body
                 corporates to realign their financial year to 31 March in
                 certain cases, subject to Central Government approval.
                 Under the current framework, shifting away from a uniform
                 April-to-March financial cycle involves complex legal

                                     794
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 hurdles. The proposed amendment empowers the Central
                 Government to permit corporate bodies to shift their
                 financial year closures based on applications citing
                 legitimate corporate structures or distinct "commercial
                 considerations". This is a pro-business flexibility which
                 will greatly benefit Indian companies operating with
                 foreign parent companies or global joint ventures.

                       The Committee observe that while "Regional
                 Directors" exercise significant delegated enforcement and
                 adjudicative authority under the Companies Act, the
                 insertion of the definition for "Regional Director" formally
                 confirms the title of "Regional Director" which would
                 reduce institutional friction and provide statutory backing,
                 as the Ministry shifts from criminal trials to localized
                 monetary penalty structures.

                      The Committee also note the statutory formalisation of
                 the "Registered Valuer" by inserting a new clause (74A)
                 defining the term "Registered Valuer". The Committee
                 agrees with views of the Ministry that this is for clarity and
                 consistency to valuation-related provisions for providing a
                 single point of reference that seamlessly aligns across
                 valuation-related provisions by linking the term to the
                 certificate of registration under section 247.

                    Further, under Clause (85) the definition of "Small
                 Company" doubles the paid-up capital threshold from 10
                 crore to 20 crore and the turnover threshold from 100
                 crore to 200 crore. The Committee underscores this as a

                                     795
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 vital milestone for MSMEs. By expanding these
                 boundaries, a vast cohort of mid-sized firms automatically
                 enters a reduced-compliance landscape, boosting market
                 liquidity and reducing operational overheads. A
                 significantly larger number of private companies will now
                 qualify as "small companies" and gain access to abridged
                 compliance obligations facilitating ease of doing business
                 for small sized Companies.

                      After considering the suggestions of stakeholders,
                 responses thereto, views of experts, and deliberations
                 held, the Committee recommend that Clause 18 be
                 accepted without any amendment. The Committee in this
                 regard, however note that under clause (28), the title "Cost
                 and Works Accountants" has been proposed to be
                 replaced with legally correct title of "Cost Accountants"
                 for ensuring systemic legal harmony with "The Cost

                 recommend that in line with the proposed amendment in

                 update the nomenclature of "Cost Accountant' . Therefore,
                 the Committee recommend the following amendments in

                 `in clause (h), for the words "the Cost and Works

                 substituted.';
