42. 19.4  19      19.4.1 The Committee note that Clause 19 of the Bill seeks
                  to amend section 4(5)(ii)(a) of the Companies Act 2013 to
                  provide for a fixed penalty amount of fifty thousand rupees
                  where companies default in compliance with such
                  provisions. The proposed provision Replaces the
                  discretionary fine "which may extend to one lakh rupees"
                  with a fixed penalty "of fifty thousand rupees" for improper
                  use of a company name reserved under Section 4. This is
                  a broader shift from variable, court-adjudicated fines to
                  fixed, in-house penalties continuing the decriminalisation
                  and rationalisation agenda. The fixed penalty provided
                  under Section 4 removes adjudicating discretion and
                  litigation for making enforcement faster and more
                  predictable. Therefore, after having examined the amended
                  provision and justifications submitted by the Ministry, the
                  Committee are of the view that Clause 19 may be retained
                  as proposed without any modification.

44. 21.6  21      21.6.1 The Committee note that Clause 21 of the Bill seeks
                  to insert a new section 12A in the Companies Act, 2013 to
                  provide that the prescribed class or classes of companies
                  shall maintain a website, an email address and other
                  modes of communication in such form and manner as may
                  be provided by rules. It further provides that these details
                  and the changes therein shall be intimated to the Registrar
                  in such form and within such period as may be provided
                  by rules. The Committee acknowledge that the proposed
                  amendment seeks to provide an express statutory basis,
                  in respect of prescribed classes of companies, to maintain
                  a functional website, an e-mail address or other mode of
                  communication, in order to have transparency and ease of
                  communication. The provision covers a class of
                  companies, and the specifics of form/manner, are to be
                  taken up while framing Rules. The Committee note that
                  this operationalises the Bill's broader push toward
                  electronic governance.

                  In this regard, the Committee further note from the
                                      799
S. Para   Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.   No.
                  Ministry's submissions that mentioning of "E-Mail" along
                  with Website and other modes of communication affirms
                  the objective that these modes of information-sharing and
                  communication for large companies are recognized in the
                  Act itself. The Committee endorse the intent of the
                  Ministry. However, it is also of the view that the Ministry's
                  proposal to prescribe only certain classes of companies
                  for compliance with this provision would exempt all other
                  companies also from the basic requirement of maintaining
                  an email-ID. Since maintaining an email ID is a standard
                  and essential practice for carrying out day-to-day business
                  operations in an increasingly digital environment, the
                  Committee are of the opinion that this requirement should
                  not be limited only to the prescribed classes of
                  companies. The Committee however, after having
                  examined the amended provision, justifications submitted
                  by the Ministry and deliberations held, accept Clause 21 as
                  proposed without any modification.

                  to insert a proviso after sub-section (2) of section 20 of

                  companies to their members shall take place only through
                  electronic mode in such manner as may be provided by
                  rules. Since electronic communication is cost-effective
                  and convenient mode for dispatching and delivering
                  documents the proposed amendments seeks to allow
                  communication in such form. The manner in which
                  members would be entitled to receive physical copies of
                  the prescribed classes of documents would be provided in

                                      800
S. Para   Clause  Observation/ Recommendation

                  the words "annual general meeting", with the words
                  "general meeting" to allow determination of fees for
                  delivery of any document to a member through a particular
                  mode in the extraordinary general meetings also. The
                  Committee further note and agree with the justifications
                  submitted by the Ministry that the proposed amendment
                  intends to promote digital communication, reduce
                  compliance costs and facilitate timely service of
                  documents by enabling prescribed classes of companies
                  to serve prescribed classes of documents through

49. 26.6  26      26.6.1 The Committee note that Clause 26 of the Bill seeks
                  to amend section 42 of the Companies Act 2013 in the
                  following manner:

                  (i) The marginal heading of section 42 by substituting
                           the word "shares" with the word "securities".

                  (ii) Sub-section (2) to insert the words "or such other
                           scheme linked to the value of the share capital of
                           a company", after the words, "employee stock
                           option", in order to recognise instruments such
                           as Restricted Stock Units and Stock Appreciation
                           Rights, in addition to Employee Stock Option
                           Plans, as executive compensation to be issued
                           with approval of shareholders.

                  (iii)Sub-section (10) to replace the words "which may
                           extend to", with the words "equivalent to" to
                           bring in more transparency in levy of penalties.

                  804
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 26.6.2 The Committee after examining the suggestions
                 and the responses thereto of the Ministry, are of the
                 opinion that the marginal heading correction reflects that
                 Section 42 is substantively concerned with private
                 placement of securities, and the marginal heading is being
                 aligned accordingly. Further, section 42 already governs
                 the private placement of all securities, not just shares, and
                 this removes a longstanding drafting inconsistency.
                 Further, the extension to "other schemes linked to share
                 value" in order to recognise instruments such as
                 Restricted Stock Units and Stock Appreciation Rights is a
                 forward-looking change to accommodate emerging equity-
                 linked instruments. Further, the move to a fixed penalty
                 formula in sub-section (10) again reflects the broader shift
                 away from open-ended, discretionary fines.

                       The Committee further note the concerns raised in
                 respect of the lack of requisite clarity on the scope and
                 coverage of schemes under the expression "or such other
                 scheme linked to the value of the share capital of a
                 company" in section 26(2). The Committee in this regard,
                 agree with the justification and clarifications submitted by
                 the Ministry that proposed amendment is intended to
                 enable companies to issue securities under schemes
                 linked to the value of the share capital of a Company, while
                 the detailed framework governing such schemes,
                 including their applicability and eligibility criteria, is to be
                 prescribed separately under the Rules . The Committee
                 acknowledges that the issue needs to be adequately
                 addressed, so that genuine employee incentive schemes,
                 are covered and appropriate safeguards prevent their

                                     805
S. Para   Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.   No.
                  misuse. The Committee desire that the aforementioned
                  concerns of the stakeholders seeking clarity on the
                  Schemes to be covered must be satisfactorily addressed
                  by timely formulation of clear and comprehensive rules,
                  regulations and procedural guidelines. The Committee
                  after detailed scrutiny of the suggestions received and
                  responses submitted by the Ministry, accept the proposed
                  provisions under this clause, in entirety, without any
                  modification.

50. 27.6  27      27.6.1 The Committee note that Clause 27 of the Bill
                  seeks to insert new section 43A in the Companies Act to
                  provide for the requirements in respect of issue and
                  maintenance of share capital, preparation and
                  maintenance of books of account, filing, submitting or
                  delivering documents by companies set up and
                  incorporated in the IFSC jurisdiction in a permitted foreign
                  currency. The `Notes on Clauses' of the Ministry informs
                  that presently, the Companies Act does not include
                  specific provisions to enable companies to prepare
                  accounts or financial statements in foreign currencies.
                  Therefore, considering the nature of companies set up in
                  IFSC jurisdiction, new section 43A has been proposed.
                  The Committee observe that it provides a framework for
                  existing companies to transition from Indian rupees to
                  such foreign currency enabling maintenance of books of
                  account and financial statements in that currency and
                  provides definitional clarity by incorporating definition
                  references to the International Financial Services Centres

                  806
S. Para   Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.   No.     Authority Act, 2019.

                       The Committee observe that this is a substantial and
                  enabling structural change for IFSC incorporated
                  companies and responds to the practical difficulty for
                  companies operating in the IFSC whose business,
                  investor base, and functional currency is foreign-currency-
                  denominated were nonetheless required to maintain share
                  capital and records in Indian rupees, creating currency-
                  mismatch. Therefore, upon examination and after
                  threadbare analysis of the views of the Ministry and
                  stakeholders, the Committee are of the considered view
                  that the amendment proposed in Clause 27 is a forward
                  looking provision to bring the company's-law treatment of
                  IFSC entities into closer alignment with international
                  financial centre practice and address a practical difficulty
                  faced by companies operating in the IFSC, that would help
                  promoting the ease of doing Business. Therefore, the
                  Committee concurs with the justifications of the Ministry
                  and accept the Clause 27 as proposed without any
                  modification.

51. 28.6  28      28.6.1 The Committee note that Clause 28 of the Bill seeks
                  to amend clause (b) of sub-section (1) of section 62 of the

                  scheme linked to the value of the share capital of the

                  compensation. It will help in recognising schemes such as
                  Restricted Stock Units (RSUs) and Stock Appreciation

                     The Committee note that Clause 29 of the Bill seeks to
                 substantially amend Section 68 of Company law 2013 to
                 provide flexibility in buy-back offers for such class or
                 classes of companies as may be prescribed. Buy-back
                 through tender offers is an efficient way of returning
                 surplus funds to shareholders and it is proposed to allow
                 prescribed class of companies to avail such mechanism.

                 allowing a higher limit for buy-back permitting an
                 additional buy-back offer within a year, subject to a
                 minimum gap of six months between two offers. The
                 Committee observe that eligible companies gain
                 meaningfully greater flexibility in capital management
                 through additional buy-backs and, potentially, higher buy-
                 back ceilings.

                 omission of the requirement for verification of the
                 declaration of solvency by affidavit is provided for ease of
                 compliance. Removing the affidavit requirement reduces
                 procedural cost. The amendment under Section 68(8)
                 seeks to include securities issued under schemes linked
                 to the value of the share capital of a company, in line with
                 similar amendments to section 62. Further, the amendment
                 to Section 68(11) replaces the existing fine-based
                 punishment with a penalty framework as part of broader

                 810

                 drawbacks.

                  charges, in the interest of ease of compliances. The
                  Committee take note that the proposed amendment
                  intends to provide additional time for registration of
                  charges under section 77 for class or classes of
                  companies in category of small companies which may
                  benefit from the relaxed compliance requirements for ease
                  of doing business. The Committee, however, are of the
                  view that the use of class of companies in section instead
                  of specific mention of class intended to be benefitted,
                  itself do not bring out clear legislative intent to extend the
                  relaxation to small companies or such or others in the

                                      814
S. Para   Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.   No.
                  category. The Committee, therefore, while supporting the
                  core objectives of the proposed amendments, recommend
                  that section 77 may be reworded and now be read as given
                  under:

                  "In section 77 of the principal Act, in sub-section (1), after
                  the second proviso, the following proviso shall be
                  inserted, namely:--

                  `Provided also that for such class or classes of small
                  companies, as may be prescribed, the period of "sixty
                  days" referred to in clause (b) of the second proviso shall
                  be read as "one hundred and twenty days.' "

54. 31.6  31      31.6.1 The Committee note that Clause 31 of the Bill seeks
                  to insert a new sub-section (2A) in section 88 of the
                  Companies Act to provide that no notice of any Trust,
                  whether express, implied, or constructive, shall be entered
                  in the register of members or debenture holders as
                  maintained under sub-section (1) of the said section.
                  Accordingly, the trustee shall be recorded as the legal
                  owner in the register, while the trust may be entered as the
                  beneficial owner as per the relevant provisions of the Act.
                  The Committee however, at the same time, underscores
                  that there is a need for clarity regarding the treatment of
                  notices of trust that have already been entered in the
                  register of members or debenture holders prior to the
                  commencement of the proposed amendment. In the
                  absence of requisite clarity, uncertainty may persist
                  whether the existing entries to be removed or should they

                                      815
S. Para  Clause   Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                  continue to remain in the register notwithstanding the
                  amendment. The Committee, therefore, while
                  acknowledging the need of procedural streamlining
                  recommend for providing a transitional period under
                  which trusts already registered as members are struck
                  from the register pursuant to the amendment. Thus, after
                  threadbare analysis of the justification of the Ministry and
                  stakeholder's submissions, the Committee recommend
                  that in section 88 of the principal Act, after sub-section (2),
                  the following sub-section shall be inserted, namely:-

                  "(2A) No notice of any trust, whether express, implied or
                  constructive, shall be entered in the register of members
                  or debenture holders maintained under sub-section (1):

                  Provided that every company, existing on or before the
                  commencement of the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Act,
                  2026, which is required to comply with the provisions of
                  this sub-section, shall make necessary changes in the
                  entries in the register referred to in sub-section (1) within a
                  period of one year from the date of such commencement.".

58. 35.6.8 35      35.6.1 The Committee note that Clause 35 amends the
          35.6.9   proviso to section 101(1) to permit a shorter notice period,
          35.6.10  not less than seven days, or such other period as may be
                   prescribed, uniformly for extraordinary general meetings
                   conducted wholly through video conferencing or audio-
                   visual means under the new section 100(7).

                   35.6.2 The Committee note that the Ministry had accepted
                   the suggestion, based on SEBI's recommendation, and
                   agreed to provide that for listed companies such EGMs
                   would require a notice period of not less than fifteen days
                   rather than seven, having regard to the nature of
                   resolutions typically placed before an EGM, such as
                   schemes of arrangement, material related-party
                   transactions and appointment of directors, which may
                   require shareholders and proxy advisors additional time
                   for scrutiny.

                   35.6.3 During deliberations, concern was raised that an
                                       821
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 extraordinary general meeting is, by definition, meant for
                 extraordinary or urgent situations, and that a longer notice
                 period of fifteen days could give a company additional
                 time to divert funds before shareholders are able to act;
                 even for listed companies, the notice period should
                 accordingly remain at seven days.

                 35.6.4 The Committee note SEBI's clarification that, in
                 situations involving fraud, diversion of funds or serious
                 governance failure, it is unlikely that the management
                 responsible for such conduct would itself convene an
                 EGM to address its own misconduct, and that the existing
                 proviso to section 101(1), which permits an EGM to be
                 called at shorter notice where members holding not less
                 than ninety-five per cent of the voting power have
                 consented, already provides a safeguard for genuine
                 emergencies.

                 35.6.5 The Committee further note SEBI's submission, with
                 reference to the OECD Corporate Governance Factbook
                 2025, that only nineteen per cent of surveyed jurisdictions
                 prescribe a notice period of under twenty days, and that
                 comparator jurisdictions such as Singapore, the United
                 Kingdom and Hong Kong prescribe differentiated notice
                 periods depending on the type of resolution or meeting
                 involved. Having regard to the nature of resolutions
                 typically placed before an EGM of a listed company, and to
                 the safeguard already available under section 101(1) for
                 genuinely urgent matters, the Committee are of the view
                 that the case for a differentiated, fifteen-day notice period

                                     822
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 for listed companies has been sufficiently made out, and
                 recommend that Clause 35 be modified accordingly.

                 35.6.6 The Committee take note of the suggestions
                 regarding, respectively, shorter notice for physical/hybrid
                 EGMs and the postal ballot mechanism under section 110,
                 and the Ministry's clarifications that the existing statutory
                 framework already accommodates these concerns; the
                 Committee see no need for further amendment on these
                 points.

                 35.6.7 The Committee note the suggestions for extending
                 the shortened notice period to wholly virtual AGMs, and
                 the Ministry's clarification that AGM business is ordinarily
                 routine in nature and warrants the existing twenty-one-day
                 notice regardless of meeting mode; the Committee concur
                 with this distinction between AGMs and EGMs.

                 35.6.8 The Committee note the Ministry's position that the
                 procedural and operational framework for hybrid/virtual
                 EGMs, including the matter raised in the suggestion that
                 Rules be framed in consultation with SEBI, would be
                 appropriately addressed through the Rules, in
                 consultation with the concerned regulators, wherever
                 necessary, and recommend that the Rules under this
                 Clause be framed accordingly.

                 35.6.9 The Committee, therefore, recommend that Clause
                 35 of the Bill be modified as follows:

63. 40.6.1 40    The Committee note that Clause 40 seeks amendment of
                 Section 132 of the Companies Act. Clause 40(d) seeks to
                 insert new sub-sections (3C) and (3D) after Section 132
                 (3B) of the parent act.

                 The Committee understand that Section 132 (3B) of the
                 Companies Act creates an executive body of the National
                 Financial Reporting Authority consisting of the
                 Chairperson and full-time Members of such Authority for
                 efficient discharge of its functions under sub-section (2)
                 [other than clause (a) and sub-section (4). The Committee
                 also note that sub-section (2) outlines the core
                 responsibilities of the NFRA regarding corporate financial
                 reporting and sub-section (4) equips the NFRA with the
                 authority needed to act as a strict regulator, granting it
                 significant investigative and penal powers.

                 Thus, Section 132 (3B) distinctly identifies the function of
                 the Executive Body vis a vis the General Body. During

                                     830
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 examination of the suggestions, it was highlighted that the
                 present formulation of Section 132(3B) of the Act, has
                 missed out incorporating the relevant proposed sections
                 132A, 132C, 132D, 132I, 132J, 132K, and 454C in the
                 functions of the Executive Body. Similarly, suggestions
                 were also received from stakeholders asking for the
                 clarification in the role and functions of Executive Body
                 and full NFRA. The Committee arrived at the considered
                 opinion that the role and functions of Executive Body and
                 full NFRA must be clearly specified in the statue. The
                 Ministry were in agreement with the view of the
                 Committee. Accordingly, after extensive discussions with
                 the Ministry and in view of the suggestions of the
                 stakeholders the Committee recommend that a new sub-
                 clause, namely, 40(ca) be added after Clause 40 (c) to
                 make necessary changes in Section 132, sub-section (3B)

                 "(ca) in sub-section (3B), for the words, brackets, figures
                 and letter "functions under sub-section (2) [other than
                 clause (a)] and sub-section (4)", the following shall be
                 substituted, namely:--

                 "functions under--

                 (i) sub-section (2) [other than clause (a)], sub-sections (4)
                 and (4A), sub-section (10) in respect of meetings of the
                 Executive Body, sub-section (11) and sub-section (17), of
                 section 132;

                 831
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.     (ii) section 132A;

                 (iii) sub-section (2) of section 132C (2); and

                 (iv) section 132D.";

64. 40.6.2 40    The Committee also note that under Clause 40, the
                 proposed Section 132(3C) vests the Chairperson with
                 powers of general superintendence and permits the
                 exercise of powers delegated by the Executive Body, while
                 Section 132(3D) enables further delegation of powers by
                 the Executive Body. The Committee note with concern that
                 present framework provides that substantive decision
                 making and regulatory functions are exercised by a limited
                 subset of members. The Committee feel such
                 concentration of powers may dilute the benefits of
                 collective decision-making, institutional checks and
                 balances, and the diverse expertise intended to be
                 represented within the Authority. The Committee therefore
                 recommend that the power of delegation through `General'
                 order may not be vested in the Executive Body.
                 Accordingly, the Committee desire the removal of the
                 words `general or' from the text of the Clause 40 (d) (3D).

65. 40.6.3 40    The Committee note that Clause No. 40(e) seeks to
                 strengthen NFRA's enforcement framework by clarifying
                 the scope of investigable misconduct, allowing it to issue
                 graded remedial measures, and enabling the Central
                 Government to define the classes subject to investigation
                 while NFRA specifies the investigative procedure by

                                     832
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 regulations. Clause 40(e) amends Section 132 (4) (a) of the
                 Companies act which provides NFRA the power to
                 investigate in such manners may be prescribed by the
                 Central Government. It seeks to substitute the words *"in
                 such manner as may be prescribed"*, with the words ", *as
                 may be prescribed, and in such manner as may be
                 specified by regulations by the said Authority"*.

                 The Committee find that the substitution of the words as
                 stated above enhances the power of NFRA to determine
                 the manner of investigation under Section 132 (4)(a). In
                 this regard, concerned about the expansion of NFRAs
                 investigative powers, the stakeholders have suggested
                 that the words "as may be prescribed" be restored in
                 Section 132(4)(a) to enable the manner and procedure of
                 investigation to be prescribed through rules. The
                 Committee understand that in the context of the
                 Companies Act, "prescribed" refers to rules made by the
                 Central Government, as opposed to "specified by
                 regulations" which refers to the Authority. The Ministry
                 accepted the proposed suggestion and stated that the
                 amendment pertaining to clause (a) of sub-section (4) may
                 be omitted as the power of prescribing manner of
                 investigation is to be retained with Central Government on
                 lines of proposed provision of section 132D (under Clause
                 41) which seeks to empower Central Government to
                 prescribe manner of inquiry.

                 In view of the reply furnished by the Ministry of Corporate
                 Affairs and after due consideration of the suggestions

                                     833
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 received the Committee recommend that in the Corporate
                 Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026, in clause 40, in sub clause
                 (e), item (i) may be omitted.

66. 40.6.4 40    With regard to the investigative powers of the NFRA In
                 Section 132(4) (a), the Committee further note the
                 suggestion regarding Section 132(4)(a) to omit the words
                 `where the National Financial Reporting Authority has
                 initiated an investigation under this Section' from the
                 proviso to the said clause. The Committee understand that
                 this proviso was originally intended to address the period
                 of transition when the National Financial Reporting
                 Authority (NFRA) was first established.

                 The Committee observe that the Ministry has stated that
                 jurisdiction of the NFRA over specific classes of
                 companies is clearly defined under the legislative mandate
                 and the NFRA Rules. However, the Committee are apprised
                 that despite this demarcation, there are instances where
                 the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI) has
                 continued to exercise disciplinary powers and initiate
                 actions against entities that squarely fall under the NFRA's
                 jurisdiction, leading to regulatory duplication and
                 jurisdictional conflict. The Committee are of the firm view
                 that the statutory framework must provide absolute clarity
                 regarding the powers to be exercised by respective
                 regulators, leaving no ambiguity as to whether a matter
                 falls under the purview of the ICAI or the NFRA. The
                 Ministry on its part have accepted that the omission of the
                 relevant words would bring clarity in the respective roles

                                     834
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 of NFRA and other bodies. Therefore, to prevent parallel
                 proceedings and in view of the Ministry's agreement on
                 the issue, the Committee agrees with the proposed
                 modification. Thus, the Committee recommend that in
                 clause 40, in sub clause (e), item (i) to be omitted may be
                 replaced by

                 "(i) in clause (a), in the proviso, the words "where the
                 National Financial Reporting Authority has initiated an
                 investigation under this section" shall be omitted;"

67. 40.6.5 40    The Committee further note that Clause 40(e) (iii) seeks to
                 substitute the Explanation under Section 132 Sub-section
                 (4). The proposed amendment seeks to define the
                 expression "professional or other misconduct" and state
                 that it shall include the meaning assigned to it under
                 section 22 of the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949, and
                 shall further include `such acts or omissions which
                 constitute a contravention of the provisions of this Act, or
                 the rules or regulations made thereunder, in so far as such
                 provisions relate to matters within the jurisdiction,
                 functions, or regulatory remit of the National Financial
                 Reporting Authority'. The Committee note the suggestion
                 that the broadened definition of "professional or other
                 misconduct" should be refined to cover only violations
                 related to auditor duties.

                 The Committee also observe that the Ministry has
                 accepted the need to limit the definition of professional or

                 835
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.     other misconduct to audit matters.

                 The Committee therefore recommend that the Explanation
                 be suitably modified and be read as under:

                 "Explanation.--For the purposes of this sub-section, the
                 expression "professional or other misconduct" shall
                 include the meaning assigned to it under section 22 of the
                 Chartered Accountants Act, 1949, and shall further include
                 such acts or omissions which constitute a contravention
                 of the provisions of this Act, or the rules or regulations
                 made thereunder, in so far as such provisions relate to
                 audit matters within the jurisdiction, functions, or
                 regulatory remit of the National Financial Reporting
                 Authority."

68. 40.6.6 40    The Committee note that Clause 40(f) seeks to strengthen
                 NFRA's enforcement by penalising non-compliance with
                 its orders or failure to pay penalties within the prescribed
                 period, including through imprisonment, fines and
                 additional debarment. The Committee note that the
                 provision allowing imprisonment for failure to comply with
                 orders of NFRA is not in consonance with the larger
                 objective of decriminalisation of the present legislation.
                 The Committee therefore recommend that the provision for
                 imprisonment for non-compliance with the orders of the
                 NFRA or failure to pay penalties be deleted and the
                 punishment restricted to a fine. This would ensure that the
                 enforcement mechanism retains adequate deterrence
                 while aligning the clause with the broader legislative intent

                                     836
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 of decriminalisation. Thus, the Committee desire that
                 under Clause 40 (f) the Sub-section 4A(a)(i) the words `with
                 imprisonment which may extend to six months or' may be
                 removed so that the amended 4A(a)(i) reads as under:

                 "(i) with fine which shall not be less than one lakh rupees
                 but which may extend to five lakh rupees, if such person is
                 an individual; or"

69. 40.6.7 40    The Committee note that Clause 40(g) of the Bill seeks to
                 amend sub-section (10) of Section 132 of the Principal Act,
                 inter-alia substituting the word "prescribed" with
                 "specified by regulations by the said Authority." The
                 Committee observe that this amendment is intended to
                 transfer the power to determine the time, place, and rules
                 of procedure for the meetings of the National Financial
                 Reporting Authority (NFRA) from the Central Government
                 to the Authority itself.

                 The Committee note the apprehensions expressed by
                 various stakeholders regarding the excessive delegation
                 of powers to the Authority, with concerns being raised
                 about potential regulatory overreach. While the Committee
                 recognise the need to restrict the delegation of broad
                 substantive powers, they are of the considered view that
                 the transaction of business at internal meetings is strictly
                 a procedural and administrative matter. The Committee
                 feel that such internal procedures do not impact the
                 substantive rights, liabilities, or compliance burdens of the
                 regulated entities. The Committee, therefore, agrees that

                                     837
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 granting the Authority the requisite flexibility to govern its
                 own day-to-day internal workings through regulations is
                 administratively beneficial. Similar operational autonomy
                 is granted to independent regulators, and is not equivalent
                 to an excessive delegation of legislative power. The
                 Committee therefore desire that Clause 40(g) seeking
                 amendment to sub-section (10) of Section 132 of the
                 Principal Act be read as under:

                 "(g) in sub-section (10),--

                 (i) after the words "National Financial Reporting
                 Authority", the words "and Executive Body" shall be
                 inserted;

                 (ii) for the word "prescribed", the words "specified by
                 regulations by the said Authority" shall be substituted;"

70. 40.6.8 40    The Committee observe that Clause 40 (h) seeks to
                 provide powers to Authority regarding appointment of
                 secretary and other employees by making changes in sub-
                 section 11 of Section 132. During examination the
                 Committee received suggestions that the power under
                 Section 132(11) should to be retained with the Central
                 Government and should not be delegated. Multiple
                 stakeholders also expressed their apprehensions
                 regarding the excessive delegation of powers to the NFRA
                 by the Central Government. The Committee after careful
                 consideration of the views of the stakeholders with
                 particular regard to the issue of excessive delegation feel

                                     838
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 that the Central Government should consider keeping the
                 power to appoint the Secretary and other employees of the
                 Authority under Section 132(11) vested with itself, rather
                 than delegating it to the NFRA. This will address the
                 concerns that allowing a regulatory body completely
                 unchecked administrative hiring power can negatively
                 impact accountability checks and general oversight. The
                 Committee accordingly recommend that Clause 40(h) may
                 be omitted in entirety.

71. 40.6.9 40    The Committee also note that Section 132(3) of the
                 Companies Act, 2013 deals with the composition of the
                 National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA). Section
                 132(3) provides that the NFRA shall consist of A
                 Chairperson, appointed by the Central Government, who
                 must be a person of eminence with expertise in
                 accountancy, auditing, finance, or law. However, the act
                 does not specify the qualifications of the Members. The
                 Ministry under Clause 40 (i) seeks to insert sub-section 16
                 and 17 after sub-section 15 of section 132 of Companies
                 Act, 2013. The proposed section (17) provides that The
                 National Financial Reporting Authority may, in such
                 manner as may be `specified by regulations', engage such
                 number of experts and professionals who have special
                 knowledge of, and experience in, accounting standards,
                 auditing standards, economics, law, business or such
                 other disciplines related to its functions.

                 The Committee observe that the Bill does not prescribe
                 any qualifications for the Members of the Executive Body.

                                     839
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 The Committee are of the considered view that the
                 Members of NFRA particularly the Executive Body should
                 be drawn from a diverse mix of backgrounds across
                 administration, business, finance, and corporate law.

                 In this regard the Committee recommend that in Clause 40
                 (i) (f) the words `specified by regulations' may be replaced
                 with the words `prescribed' so that the power to determine

                 "(17) The National Financial Reporting Authority may, in

                 functions under this Act.".

72. 40.6.10 40   The Committee further recognise the need for amending

                 and "other charges" through regulations, without any
                 principles, limits, or legislative safeguards, which may
                 lead to arbitrary imposition and regulatory overreach. The
                 Committee also considered the reply of the Ministry that
                 these provisions are consistent with those conferred on

                 intended to establish NFRA as an independent audit

                                     848
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation

                 sectoral regulator with comprehensive powers necessary

81. 41.6.9 41    The Committee note the provisions under Clause 41 of the
                 Bill, specifically the proposed Section 132J, grants
                 regulation-making powers to the National Financial
                 Reporting Authority (NFRA). The provision grants wide
                 and residuary powers to the National Financial Reporting
                 Authority to frame regulations "for carrying out its
                 functions," including matters relating to investigation,
                 reporting, fees, and enforcement. During examination the
                 Committee were apprised that NFRA does not presently
                 have explicit powers akin to Securities and Exchange
                 Board of India (SEBI) under Section 469 of the Companies
                 Act, 2013 to frame and lay regulations before Parliament.
                 In the absence of such enabling provision, the validity of
                 NFRA issuing regulations, particularly those intended to
                 have statutory effect may be open to legal challenge.

                 Stakeholders have raised concerns that such broad and
                 open-ended delegation, may result in excessive delegation
                 of legislative powers and enable creation of a parallel
                 regulatory framework without adequate legislative
                 oversight. The Committee are of the considered opinion

                                     849
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 that scope of regulation making powers be clearly defined
                 and limited primarily to procedural and operational
                 aspects. Substantive matters such as the manner of
                 investigation, and the recovery of penalties may be
                 governed through rules framed by the Central
                 Government, subject to Parliamentary oversight, rather
                 than through regulations framed by NFRA itself, in order to
                 avoid excessive delegation and preserve legislative
                 accountability

                 The Committee observe that substantive changes have
                 been recommended by the Committee to the regulation
                 making provisions of NFRA. In particular the manner of
                 investigation under clause (a) of sub-section (4) of section
                 132 and the manner of recovery of the amount of penalty
                 under sub-section (3) of section 132D.

                 Accordingly, pursuant to the changes accepted in
                 respective substantive provisions necessary changes in
                 the regulation making provisions have to be carried out
                 under section 132J.

                 Consequently, the Committee recommend that in clause
                 41, in the proposed section 132J in sub-section (2), sub-
                 clauses (a), (c), (d), (e) and (f) shall be omitted and the
                 other sub-clauses be renamed accordingly.

82. 41.6.10 41   In this regard the Committee note that it has recommended
                 changes in Clause 41 to grant requisite flexibility to NFRA
                 to govern its own day-to-day internal workings w.r.t the

                                     850
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation

83. 41.6.11 41   The Committee note that NFRA was originally envisaged
                 as an oversight authority with a limited and clearly defined
                 mandate in relation to accounting and auditing standards
                 for public interest entities, while regulation of the
                 Chartered Accountancy profession continued under the
                 Chartered Accountants Act, 1949.

                 However, the Committee feel that the expanded powers for
                 registration, investigation, delegated regulation-making
                 powers and the proposed body corporate status may
                 broaden NFRA's role beyond its original oversight
                 function. In the considered opinion of the Committee this
                 may result in overlap with the statutory functions of ICAI,
                 leading to regulatory duplication, institutional
                 fragmentation, increased compliance burden, and
                 uncertainty regarding jurisdictional boundaries.

                 The Committee thus recommend that the Ministry take
                 steps to ensure that amendments to the Companies Act do

                                     851
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 not dilute or override the statutory autonomy granted to
                 ICAI under the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949. Instead,
                 the legislative framework must allow a harmonious
                 coexistence where NFRA's role under the Companies Act
                 remains strictly focused on corporate financial oversight,
                 leaving professional development, standard-drafting
                 foundations, and primary domain matters to the statutory
                 purview of ICAI.

84. 41.6.12 41   The Committee observe that Clause 41, seeks to insert a
                 new section 132K to provide for transparency and periodic
                 review in the regulation-making process of the NFRA,
                 including prior public consultation and review of
                 regulations at regular intervals, with an exception for
                 urgent or internal matters. In this regard, the Committee
                 find that stakeholders have suggested that the public at
                 large should be provided a minimum of thirty days to
                 respond to the draft regulations under section 132K and
                 these features should be expressly mentioned in the Act
                 while leaving the detailed process to be prescribed by the
                 rules. The Committee agree with the view that the scope of
                 regulation making power vested with NFRA should
                 preserve important safeguards to prevent their misuse.
                 The Committee therefore recommend that the proviso to
                 section 132K after sub-clause (b) may be removed in
                 entirety.

86. 42.6.1 42    The Committee note that the amendment proposed under
                 Clause 42 to section 134(3) of the Companies Act, 2013
                 seeks to enhance transparency in the Board's Report by
                 requiring the Board to provide explanations or comments
                 on specified observations, qualifications, reservations or
                 adverse remarks made by the auditors and to disclose the
                 composition of the Audit Committee, along with reasons
                 where any recommendation of the Audit Committee has
                 not been accepted by the Board.

                 The Committee note the concern raised by stakeholders
                 that the expressions "every observation or comment of the
                 auditors" and "any qualification, reservation or adverse
                 remark" are broad and subjective. It was pointed out that
                 auditors' reports contain observations and statements
                 arising under different statutory and professional
                 frameworks, including applicable auditing standards, the
                 Companies (Auditor's Report) Order, internal financial
                 control reporting requirements and other applicable laws.
                 The Committee are of the view that the absence of clarity
                 regarding the precise scope of the Board's obligation may
                 result in uncertainty, overlapping reporting requirements
                 and avoidable compliance burdens.

                 The Committee, therefore, recommend that the rules and
                                     853
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 prescribed reporting formats under section 134 clearly
                 specify the categories of audit observations,
                 qualifications, reservations and adverse remarks requiring
                 a response from the Board. The terminology used should,
                 as far as practicable, be aligned with the relevant auditing
                 standards and prescribed auditor reporting formats. The
                 framework should also clearly distinguish between
                 matters requiring a substantive explanation by the Board
                 and routine or technical observations already addressed
                 through other statutory reporting requirements.

                 The Committee also note the suggestion that the proposed
                 AI and Digital Risk Statement should not remain a mere
                 self-declaration by the Board and should be subject to
                 appropriate self-certification or verification. In view of the
                 increasing use of artificial intelligence and digital
                 technologies in financial reporting and corporate decision-
                 making, the Committee recommend that the applicable
                 rules prescribe appropriate standards for Board-level
                 oversight, verification and accountability in respect of
                 such disclosures. The Committee further recommend that
                 the need for appropriate certification or self-certification of
                 such statements be considered, wherever necessary, to
                 ensure that such disclosures are supported by adequate
                 verification and that accountability for the accuracy and
                 integrity of material AI-driven or digitally generated
                 financial information is clearly established.

                 The Committee further recommend that the above
                 requirements be suitably incorporated in the rules and

                                     854
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 prescribed reporting formats under section 134 to ensure
                 clarity, consistency and effective implementation. The
                 Committee recommend that Clause 42 of the Corporate
                 Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 be accepted without
                 amendment.

87. 43.5.1 43    The Committee note that the proposed amendments to
                 Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013 seek to rationalise
                 the Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) framework by
                 easing the compliance requirements on small companies,
                 enhancing the threshold for applicability of CSR from a net
                 profit of 5 crore to 10 crore, providing additional time for
                 transfer of unspent CSR amounts to the designated
                 account, enhancing the threshold for constitution of the
                 CSR Committee, and enabling exemption of such class or
                 classes of companies as may be prescribed. The
                 Committee observe that the revision of the CSR threshold
                 would reduce the compliance requirements for a large
                 number of small and medium-sized companies, enabling
                 them to devote greater resources towards business
                 expansion and operational efficiency, while ensuring that
                 the CSR framework remains focused on companies with
                 relatively greater financial capacity. However, the
                 Committee are of the view that the proposed power to
                 exempt "such class or classes of companies as may be
                 prescribed" is broad and lacks statutory guidance, thereby
                 amounting to excessive delegation of legislative power.
                 The Committee, therefore, recommend that the words "as
                 may be prescribed" be omitted. The Committee further
                 note that the consequential amendments proposed under
                 Clause 43(c) and Clause 43(d), relating to the extension of

                                     855
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 the timeline for transfer of unspent CSR amounts to the
                 designated account and the enhancement of the threshold
                 for constitution of the CSR Committee, are intended to
                 provide greater operational flexibility and simplify
                 compliance processes without diluting corporate
                 accountability towards CSR obligations. The Committee
                 are of the view that these amendments strike an
                 appropriate balance between regulatory facilitation and
                 preserving the underlying objectives of the CSR
                 framework. Accordingly, the Committee accept the
                 provisions contained in Clause 43(a), 43(c) and 43(d) of the
                 Bill as proposed.

                 The Committee also observe that, while Clause 43
                 proposes to extend the period for transferring the unspent
                 CSR amount remaining at the end of a financial year from
                 thirty days to ninety days, no corresponding amendment
                 has been proposed in respect of the transfer of the
                 unspent amount earmarked for an ongoing project after
                 the completion of the third financial year. The Committee
                 are of the view that both provisions govern analogous
                 procedural requirements and should provide a uniform
                 compliance timeline. In order to ensure consistency in the
                 statutory framework and to provide companies with a
                 reasonable timeframe for effecting such transfers, the
                 Committee recommend that the corresponding provision
                 relating to ongoing projects be amended on similar lines
                 by substituting, for the words "specified in Schedule VII,
                 within a period of thirty days", the words "specified in

                 856
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.     Schedule VII, within a period of ninety days".

                 The Committee are in agreement that CSR funds should
                 not be utilised through any implementing agency,
                 including organisations, trusts, societies, non-
                 governmental organisations and Section 8 companies, that
                 is in contravention of any law for the time being in force or
                 is prohibited from receiving such funds under any
                 statutory provision or order of a competent authority. The
                 Committee are of the considered view that any CSR
                 contribution made to an entity included in a duly notified
                 negative list should not qualify as CSR expenditure for the
                 purposes of compliance under Section 135 of the
                 Companies Act, 2013. The Committee further recommend
                 that the criteria for inclusion of any entity in such a
                 negative list should be objective, transparent and based
                 solely on statutory provisions or orders passed by a
                 competent authority, so as to ensure certainty, fairness
                 and uniform application. The Committee also recommend
                 that the restriction should operate only for the period and
                 subject to the conditions specified in the relevant
                 notification, and that an appropriate statutory mechanism
                 be provided for removal of an entity from the negative list
                 upon the cessation of the grounds that led to its inclusion.
                 Accordingly, the Committee recommend that Clause 43 of
                 the Bill may be suitably modified to incorporate the above
                 safeguards within the statutory framework.

                 Clause 43, and prescribing a negative list of entities

                 such contributions are capable of generating greater

                 disaster management. The Committee also note that the
                 proposal of the National Disaster Management Authority
                 (NDMA) to treat the free-of-cost supply of products for
                 disaster relief as eligible CSR expenditure is presently
                 under consideration and that valuation principles under
                 the GST framework have been suggested for determining
                 the value of such contributions.

                 regulated, has the potential to enhance the effectiveness,

                 Committee recognise that such a framework must
                 adequately address concerns relating to objective
                 valuation, transparency, auditability and accountability.
                 The Committee, therefore, recommend that the
                 Government examine the feasibility of permitting CSR
                 contributions in kind through an appropriate statutory or
                 regulatory framework, incorporating robust safeguards,
                 including objective valuation norms, independent
                 verification, appropriate disclosure and reporting
                 requirements, and effective monitoring mechanisms, so as
                 to prevent misuse or overvaluation while ensuring that the
                 objectives and integrity of the CSR framework are fully
                 preserved.

88. 44.6.1 44

                 The Committee note that Clause 44 of the Bill seeks to
                 insert a new sub-section (12) in Section 139 of the
                 Companies Act, 2013 to enable the Central Government to
                 exempt such class or classes of companies, subject to
                 such conditions as may be prescribed, from the
                 requirement of appointing statutory auditors. The
                 Committee observe that the proposed amendment is
                 intended to reduce the compliance requirement on low-
                 risk and small companies, particularly newly incorporated
                 and micro enterprises, for whom the cost of mandatory
                 statutory audit may be disproportionate to the scale of
                 their operations. The Committee further note that the
                 preparation and filing of financial statements, annual

                                     861
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 returns and other statutory compliances would continue to
                 remain mandatory and that the conditions governing such
                 exemption would be prescribed through subordinate
                 legislation, taking into account relevant factors, such as
                 borrowings, assets and other appropriate parameters, so
                 as to balance the objective of ease of doing business with
                 the need to preserve financial discipline, transparency and
                 stakeholder confidence.

                 The Committee, however, are of the view that extending
                 the enabling provision to all classes of companies may
                 have unintended implications for transparency and
                 stakeholder protection. In the opinion of the Committee,
                 the proposed exemption should be confined to private
                 companies only, as such companies generally have a
                 limited shareholder base and comparatively lower public
                 interest implications. Restricting the exemption to private
                 companies would achieve the objective of reducing
                 compliance burden for small businesses, while ensuring
                 that the public companies, whose affairs have a wider
                 bearing on investors, creditors and other stakeholders,
                 continue to remain subject to statutory audit requirements.

                 The Committee, therefore, recommend that Clause 44 of
                 the Bill be modified to provide that the power of the
                 Central Government to exempt companies from the
                 requirement of appointing statutory auditors shall be
                 exercisable only in respect of such class or classes of
                 private companies, subject to such conditions as may be
                 prescribed. This would adequately balance the objective of

                                     862
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 ease of doing business with the need to safeguard
                 transparency, accountability and stakeholder confidence
                 in the corporate sector.

                 Accordingly, Clause 44 of the Bill be modified as under:

                 44. In section 139 of the principal Act, after sub-section
                 (11), the following sub-section shall be inserted, namely:--

                 "(12) Such class or classes of private companies, which
                 fulfil such conditions as may be prescribed, shall not be
                 required to appoint auditors under this Chapter and the
                 reference to the requirement of having audited financial
                 statements for determining any financial information in
                 accordance with the provisions of the Act or the rules
                 made thereunder shall be construed accordingly, as if
                 there is no requirement for audit.".

                 The Committee further recommend that, while framing the
                 Rules, suitable clarity may be provided regarding the use
                 and applicability of the expressions "audited", "statutory
                 auditor" and "audit report" in relation to companies
                 exempted from the requirement of statutory audit, so as to
                 avoid ambiguity in the implementation of the proposed
                 exemption.

89. 45.6.1 45

                 The Committee note that Clause 45 of the Corporate Laws
                 (Amendment) Bill, 2026 seeks to amend Section 141(1) of
                 the Companies Act, 2013, by inserting a proviso requiring

                                     863
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 that every partner of an audit firm shall be a person
                 registered with a statutory institute or body established
                 under a law in India.

                 The Committee observe that stakeholders and
                 professional bodies raised strong concerns against this
                 proposed blanket mandate, emphasizing that the existing
                 framework under Section 141 of the Companies Act, 2013,
                 already provides sufficient safeguards. Currently, where a
                 firm or Limited Liability Partnership (LLP) is appointed as
                 an auditor, a majority of the partners practicing in India
                 must be qualified Chartered Accountants, and only
                 partners who are Chartered Accountants are authorized to
                 act and sign on behalf of the firm.

                 The Committee are of the considered view that mandating
                 Indian statutory registration for every partner in an audit
                 firm is unnecessary and counterproductive as it will affect
                 the constitution of multi-disciplinary partnership firms.
                 The Committee feel such a rigid restriction would
                 adversely affect Multidisciplinary Partnerships (MDPs) by
                 preventing them from inducting domain experts such as IT
                 specialists, MBAs, forensic analysts, or foreign-qualified
                 professionals who may not be registered with an Indian
                 statutory body. This would create operational friction,
                 increase compliance burdens, and contradict the
                 Government's ongoing initiative to encourage holistic and
                 multidisciplinary partnership firms.

                 Accordingly, the Committee recommend that the proposed
                                     864
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 proviso to Section 141(1) of the Companies Act, 2013, as
                 contained in Clause 45 of the Bill, may not be accepted
                 and is to be omitted from the Bill.

90. 46.6.1 46    The Committee note that Clause 46 of the Bill seeks to
                 amend Section 144 of the Companies Act, 2013, by
                 introducing additional restrictions on the provision of non-
                 audit services by auditors or audit firms of such class or
                 classes of companies as may be prescribed. The proposed
                 amendment further provides for a three-year restriction on
                 the provision of non-audit services to the company, its
                 holding company or subsidiary company after the
                 completion of the auditor's term, besides providing a
                 transitional period for auditors already rendering such
                 services.

                 The Committee observe that the proposed amendments
                 seek to strengthen auditor independence and address
                 potential conflicts of interest arising from the provision of
                 non-audit services. The Committee, however, note the
                 concerns raised by various stakeholders regarding the
                 broad scope of the proposed restrictions, the absence of
                 clarity regarding the class of companies to which the
                 enhanced restrictions would apply and the categories of
                 services that would be regarded as non-audit services.
                 The Committee further note that a blanket prohibition on
                 all non-audit services may unnecessarily restrict legitimate
                 and low-risk professional services and may create
                 uncertainty regarding the services intended to be covered

                 865
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.     by the restriction.

                 The Committee are, therefore, of the considered opinion
                 that the implementation of the proposed restrictions
                 should adopt a calibrated and risk-based approach, with
                 due regard to the need to preserve auditor independence
                 while avoiding unintended restrictions on legitimate
                 professional services, particularly in the case of small
                 companies, MSMEs and smaller audit practices. The
                 Committee, accordingly, recommend that the Ministry
                 utilise its delegated rule-making powers to restrict the
                 application of the enhanced prohibitions on non-audit
                 services to specified high-risk entities or Public Interest
                 Entities, thereby safeguarding small companies, MSMEs
                 and smaller audit practices from disproportionate
                 administrative and compliance burdens.

                 The Committee further note that the proposed first proviso
                 prohibits auditors or audit firms from providing "any non-
                 audit services" to the company or its holding or subsidiary
                 company. The Committee are of the view that the scope of
                 such prohibition should be clearly defined to ensure legal
                 certainty and prevent inconsistent interpretation and
                 implementation. The Committee, therefore, recommend
                 that the words "as may be prescribed" be inserted after
                 the words "any non-audit services", thereby enabling the
                 prescription of specific categories of non-audit services to
                 which the restriction would apply. The Committee further
                 recommend that the subordinate legislative framework
                 clearly identify the services covered by the prohibition

                                     866
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 and, where appropriate, permit legitimate and low-risk
                 professional services, subject to appropriate safeguards
                 to protect auditor independence and prevent actual or
                 perceived conflicts of interest. The Committee further
                 recommend that the expression "management services"
                 be replaced with "management functions" so as to provide
                 greater clarity regarding the scope of the restriction. The
                 Committee, therefore, recommend that Clause 46 be
                 suitably amended to provide that the prohibition shall
                 apply to such non-audit services "as may be prescribed"
                 and to replace the expression "management services"
                 with "management functions".

                 With regard to the proposed three-year restriction on the
                 provision of non-audit services after completion of the
                 auditor's term, the Committee note the concerns raised by
                 various stakeholders regarding the length and scope of
                 the proposed cooling-off period and its possible
                 implications for the availability of professional expertise,
                 choice of service providers and the cost of compliance.
                 The Committee further note that the proposed three-year
                 restriction may be particularly onerous in cases involving
                 group companies, joint audits, mid-term resignation or
                 non-reappointment of auditors.

                 The Committee are of the considered view that a
                 proportionate and risk-based approach would balance the
                 objective of safeguarding auditor independence with the
                 need to preserve access to specialised professional
                 services. The Committee, therefore, recommend that the

                                     867
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 proposed three-year cooling-off period be reduced to one
                 year. The Committee, therefore, recommend that Clause 46

                 following changes:

                 In section 144 of the principal Act,-

                 (a) for the words and brackets "(h) management services;

                 and" shall be substituted;
