91. 47.6.1  47      The Committee note that Clause 47 of the Bill seeks to
                    amend Section 147 of the Companies Act, 2013, as part of
                    the broader objective of decriminalising procedural and
                    technical defaults under the Companies Act, 2013. The
                    proposed amendment provides for the substitution of
                    criminal fines with monetary penalties in respect of
                    specified contraventions relating to auditor appointment
                    and related compliance requirements, while also expressly
                    including contraventions of Section 143, other than sub-
                    section (12), and Section 146 within the scope of sub-
                    section (2) of Section 147.

                    The Committee observe that the proposed amendment
                    seeks to establish a more calibrated enforcement
                    framework by distinguishing between procedural and
                    technical non-compliances, which may appropriately be
                    addressed through monetary penalties, and serious
                    misconduct warranting criminal consequences. The
                    Committee further note the Ministry's submission that the
                    Companies Act, 2013 already follows such a differentiated
                    enforcement approach, wherein imprisonment is generally
                    reserved for serious offences involving fraud, false
                    statements and other wilful misconduct, while procedural
                    and technical defaults are increasingly dealt with through
                    civil penalties and in-house adjudication. The Committee
                    also note that Section 446B provides for lesser penalties in
                    respect of certain classes of companies, including small
                    companies, One Person Companies, start-up companies
                    and producer companies.

                    869
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 The Committee have also examined the concerns
                 regarding the possible exposure of auditors to parallel
                 proceedings under Section 147 of the Companies Act,
                 2013 and the regulatory framework administered by the
                 National Financial Reporting Authority or the Institute of
                 Chartered Accountants of India. The Committee note the
                 Ministry's clarification that the jurisdiction and scope of
                 proceedings under Section 147 and Section 132 operate
                 under distinct statutory frameworks, with the jurisdiction
                 of the National Financial Reporting Authority being
                 specified under the relevant Rules, while Section 147
                 applies generally to auditors in respect of specified
                 contraventions under the Companies Act, 2013. The
                 Committee also note the Ministry's submission that a
                 separate compliance framework under the Companies Act,
                 2013 for digital asset-related start-ups may not be
                 appropriate at this stage, as such activities, wherever
                 applicable, are subject to sector-specific regulatory
                 frameworks.

                 The Committee, while taking note of the views and
                 suggestions received from stakeholders and the
                 clarifications furnished by the Ministry, are of the view that
                 the proposed amendment appropriately advances the
                 objective of decriminalising procedural and technical
                 defaults while retaining criminal sanctions for serious
                 misconduct and culpable violations. The Committee
                 further observe that the proposed framework, read with
                 the existing provisions providing for proportionate
                 penalties for specified classes of companies, seeks to
                 balance the objectives of effective enforcement, corporate

                                     870
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.     accountability and ease of doing business.

                 Accordingly, taking into account the justifications and
                 clarifications furnished by the Ministry, the views and
                 suggestions received from stakeholders and experts, and
                 the deliberations held by the Committee, the Committee
                 recommend that Clause 47 be accepted without any
                 amendment.

93. 49.6.1  49      The Committee note that Clause 49 of the Bill seeks to
                    amend Section 149 of the Companies Act, 2013, relating to
                    the eligibility, continuing independence and tenure of
                    independent directors. The proposed amendments seek to
                    extend certain independence-related restrictions to the
                    current financial year; replace the reference to "company
                    secretaries in practice" with "secretarial auditors"; enable
                    the prescription of a lower pecuniary threshold for
                    transactions involving legal or consulting firms; require
                    independent directors to continue to satisfy the prescribed
                    eligibility conditions during their tenure; extend the
                    cooling-off restriction to the holding, subsidiary and
                    associate companies of the company; permit a limited
                    exception in respect of transactions of legal or consulting
                    firms below the prescribed threshold; and provide that the
                    tenure served as an additional director shall be counted
                    towards the tenure of an independent director.

                    The Committee observe that the proposed amendments
                    seek to strengthen the continuing independence of
                    independent directors, prevent circumvention of the
                    prescribed tenure and cooling-off requirements, and
                    provide regulatory flexibility to calibrate the materiality
                    threshold for assessing potential conflicts of interest. The
                    Committee also note the concerns raised regarding the
                    possible premature cessation of the tenure of independent
                    directors in group companies, the extension of the
                    cooling-off restriction across the corporate group, the
                    proposed delegation of power to prescribe a lower
                    pecuniary threshold, and the absence of corresponding
                    amendments to Section 161 and Schedule IV. The

                                        874
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 Committee, however, note the clarifications furnished by
                 the Ministry that the proposed extension of the cooling-off
                 restriction is intended to preserve the actual and perceived
                 independence of independent directors across a corporate
                 group; that the existing threshold is not being altered but
                 may be calibrated through subordinate legislation in
                 response to regulatory and market developments; and that
                 Section 161 already enables the appointment of any
                 eligible person as an additional director, while the
                 proposed amendment merely clarifies that such tenure
                 shall be counted for the purposes of determining the
                 tenure of an independent director.

                 The Committee further note the concern that prescribing
                 specific technical expertise for independent directors of
                 entities regulated by the International Financial Services
                 Centres Authority may not be appropriate, as the skill
                 requirements may vary depending upon the nature and
                 activities of the concerned entity and may be addressed,
                 wherever necessary, through sector-specific regulatory
                 requirements. The Committee also note the Ministry's
                 assurance that the manner of compliance with the
                 continuing eligibility requirement under proposed sub-
                 section (6A), including the role of the declaration under
                 sub-section (7), would be considered at the rule-making
                 stage. The Committee are of the view that the subordinate
                 legislative framework should ensure that the continuing
                 compliance requirement does not result in the creation of
                 a separate or duplicative certification mechanism.

                 875
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 Accordingly, taking into account the justifications and
                 clarifications furnished by the Ministry of Corporate
                 Affairs, the views and suggestions received from
                 stakeholders and experts, and the deliberations held by
                 the Committee, the Committee are of the opinion that the
                 proposed amendments seek to strengthen the framework
                 governing the independence, eligibility and tenure of
                 independent directors while providing the necessary
                 regulatory flexibility to address evolving corporate and
                 market circumstances. The Committee, therefore,
                 recommend that Clause 49 of the Corporate Laws
                 (Amendment) Bill, 2026 be accepted without amendment.

                 and other specified situations. It also provides that a
                 reasonable opportunity of being heard shall be given
                 before cancellation of a DIN on the ground of false or
                 incorrect information or suppression of material facts.

                 The Committee note the concerns regarding the scope of
                 discretion in the deactivation or cancellation of DINs and
                 the need for clear grounds and adequate procedural
                 safeguards to prevent arbitrary action. The Committee are
                 of the view that, given the significant consequences
                 associated with the deactivation or cancellation of a DIN,
                 the statutory framework should clearly define the grounds
                 and consequences of such action and ensure that the
                 power is exercised in a transparent, reasoned and
                 proportionate manner. The Committee further emphasise
                 that the principles of natural justice should be adequately
                 safeguarded and that a reasonable opportunity of being
                 heard should be provided, wherever the circumstances
                 permit, before any adverse action resulting in the
                 deactivation or cancellation of a DIN is taken. The
                 Committee also recommend that the subordinate
                 legislative framework should prescribe clear procedures
                 for a fair, transparent and time-bound procedure for notice,
                 rectification and reactivation of a DIN, particularly in cases
                 of procedural or verification-related non-compliance.

                 878
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 The Committee further note that the proposed amendment
                 to Section 154 establishes a comprehensive statutory
                 framework governing the deactivation and cancellation of
                 Director Identification Numbers. Being the principal
                 provision governing the subject, Section 154 should
                 comprehensively regulate all matters relating to
                 deactivation and cancellation of DINs. The Committee are
                 of the view that the corresponding provisions of Sections
                 152 and 167 should be harmonised with the amended
                 Section 154 so as to ensure statutory consistency, avoid
                 duplication and provide legal clarity.

96. 51A.2 51A    The Committee note that the Director Identification
                 Number serves as a unique and permanent identifier for
                 individuals acting as directors and constitutes an
                 important element of the corporate regulatory framework
                 for maintaining accurate records of directorships and
                 ensuring effective regulatory oversight. The Committee
                 observe that while section 155 of the Companies Act, 2013
                 prohibits an individual from obtaining or possessing more
                 than one Director Identification Number, the Act does not
                 presently provide an express statutory mechanism
                 requiring the surrender of additional Director Identification
                 Numbers where an individual is already in possession of
                 multiple DINs. Consequently, persons holding duplicate
                 DINs, including those arising on account of inadvertent

                                     882
S. Para   Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.   No.
                  allotment, legacy records or administrative errors, lack a
                  clear statutory process for regularising their position.

                  The Committee are of the view that providing an express
                  statutory obligation to surrender every additional Director
                  Identification Number would facilitate cleansing of the DIN
                  database, preserve the integrity of the identification
                  framework, prevent duplication of records and strengthen
                  regulatory oversight. The Committee further note that
                  prescribing the manner and time within which such
                  surrender is to be made through rules would provide the
                  necessary administrative flexibility while ensuring uniform
                  implementation.

                  The Committee, therefore, recommend the insertion of the
                  proposed proviso to section 155 of the principal Act, as
                  under:

                  In section 155 of the principal Act, the following proviso
                  shall be inserted, namely:-

                  "Provided that an individual in possession of more than
                  one Director Identification Number, shall make an
                  application to surrender every such additional Director
                  Identification Number in such manner within such time as
                  may be prescribed."

97. 52.6  52      The Committee note that Clause 52 of the Bill seeks to
                  amend Section 159 of the Companies Act, 2013, by
                  replacing the expression "which may extend to" with the

                                      883
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 expression "of", thereby providing for a fixed penalty of
                 50,000 for defaults in complying with Sections 152, 155
                 and 156 of the Act. The Clause further seeks to introduce a
                 maximum ceiling of 5 lakh on the additional penalty
                 leviable for continuing defaults.

                 The Committee have considered the suggestion that a
                 minimum penalty of 25,000 may be prescribed while
                 retaining 50,000 as the maximum penalty, in view of the
                 fact that the existing provision does not prescribe a
                 minimum penalty and leaves the quantum of penalty to be
                 determined, up to the prescribed maximum, having regard
                 to the facts and circumstances of each case. The
                 Committee also note the Ministry's submission that the
                 proposed amendment seeks to bring certainty and
                 uniformity in the quantum of penalty by removing
                 adjudicatory discretion and, at the same time, introducing
                 a cap on the continuing penalty, which may otherwise
                 accumulate without an upper limit.

                 The Committee are of the view that while certainty and
                 uniformity in the levy of penalties are important objectives,
                 a fixed penalty may, in certain cases, result in
                 disproportionate consequences, particularly where the
                 nature, duration and circumstances of the default may
                 vary. Considering that the proposed amendment is
                 intended to bring greater transparency and certainty in the
                 levy of penalties and that the continuing penalty is now
                 proposed to be subject to an overall ceiling of 5 lakh, the
                 Committee accept the amendment proposed under Clause

                                     884
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 52 and recommend that the same may be retained without
                 modification.

98. 53.6.1 53    The Committee note that Clause 53 of the Bill seeks to
                 amend Section 161 of the Companies Act, 2013, relating to
                 the appointment of additional directors and directors
                 appointed against casual vacancies. The proposed
                 amendment seeks to provide that an additional director
                 and a director appointed to fill a casual vacancy shall hold
                 office up to the date of the next general meeting or for a
                 period of three months from the date of appointment,
                 whichever is earlier. The Clause further seeks to provide
                 that a person whose appointment as a director could not
                 be considered or was not approved by the members in a
                 general meeting shall not thereafter be appointed by the
                 Board as an additional director, alternate director or
                 director against a casual vacancy without the prior
                 approval of the members.

                 The Committee observe that the proposed amendment
                 seeks to strengthen shareholder oversight by ensuring
                 that appointments made by the Board are placed before
                 the members for approval within a specified and
                 reasonable timeframe. The Committee also note the
                 concerns expressed by stakeholders that the requirement
                 of convening a general meeting within three months may
                 impose additional procedural and financial burdens,
                 particularly on small and unlisted companies, and the
                 suggestion that the period may be extended to six months
                 or that such directors may be permitted to continue until

                                     885
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 the next Annual General Meeting. However, the Committee
                 further note the Ministry's submission that permitting such
                 directors to continue until the next Annual General
                 Meeting may dilute the objective of timely shareholder
                 approval and may enable prolonged continuation of
                 appointments without effective shareholder oversight. The
                 Committee also note the Ministry's clarification that the
                 proposed period of three months is considered sufficient
                 for obtaining the approval of members and that the
                 availability of virtual general meetings would mitigate the
                 concerns relating to additional cost and logistical burden.

                 The Committee are of the view that timely approval of
                 appointments by shareholders is an important corporate
                 governance safeguard and that the proposed three-month
                 period seeks to ensure that directors appointed by the
                 Board do not continue in office for an extended period
                 without shareholder approval. The Committee further
                 observe that the proposed provision under sub-section (5),
                 which prevents the Board from reappointing a person
                 whose appointment as a director has not been approved
                 by the members without their prior approval, appropriately
                 reinforces shareholder primacy and prevents the
                 circumvention of an adverse decision of the members.

                 Accordingly, taking into account the justifications and
                 clarifications furnished by the Ministry, the views and
                 suggestions received from stakeholders and experts, and
                 the deliberations held by the Committee, the Committee
                 recommend that Clause 53 be accepted without any

                                     886
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.     amendment.

99. 54.6.1 54

                 The Committee note that Clause 54 seeks to strengthen
                 the disqualification framework for directors by, inter alia,
                 reducing the threshold for disqualification on account of
                 continuous non-filing of financial statements or annual
                 returns from three consecutive financial years to two
                 financial years, introducing a cooling-off period for certain
                 professionals associated with the company before their
                 appointment as directors, expanding the scope of
                 disqualification under Section 164(1)(g), introducing a "fit
                 and proper person" criterion, and providing for
                 consequential vacation of office under Section 167.

                 The Committee further note the concerns expressed by
                 stakeholders that extending disqualification to cases
                 where a person has merely been subjected to a monetary
                 penalty under Section 188 would be inconsistent with the
                 objective of decriminalisation, since technical defaults no
                 longer constituting criminal offences should not attract the
                 serious civil consequence of disqualification. The
                 Committee also note the concern that, given the diverse
                 categories of directors under the Act, it would be difficult
                 to objectively determine what constitutes a "fit and proper
                 person", and the proposed criterion may lead to subjective
                 and arbitrary application. The Committee further note the
                 concerns that the proposed "fit and proper person"
                 criterion, to be prescribed through subordinate legislation,
                 confers an excessively broad delegated power in a matter
                 involving significant civil consequences. The Committee

                                     887
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 further note the concerns regarding the inclusion of
                 registered valuers within the proposed cooling-off
                 framework, having regard to the assignment-based nature
                 of their engagement.

                 The Committee are of the view that the proposed
                 amendment under sub-clause (A) of clause (g) of sub-
                 section (1), seeking to substitute the words "dealing with
                 related party transactions" with the words "or subjected to
                 penalty for default", is inconsistent with the objective of
                 decriminalisation, as technical defaults attracting civil
                 penalties should not automatically result in the serious
                 consequence of disqualification from holding office as a
                 director. The Committee are of the view that the
                 Companies Act, 2013 recognises different categories of
                 directors each performing distinct roles and
                 responsibilities. In the absence of objective statutory
                 parameters, it would be difficult to prescribe a uniform
                 standard for determining what constitutes a "fit and proper
                 person" across such diverse categories of directors. The
                 Committee are of the view that such a broad and
                 undefined criterion may lead to subjective interpretation,
                 inconsistent application and the possibility of arbitrary
                 exercise of power in matters involving significant civil
                 consequences. The Committee further consider that the
                 proposed "fit and proper person" criterion under clause
                 (k), being left to be prescribed through subordinate
                 legislation, involves excessive delegation of essential
                 legislative functions. The Committee also consider that a
                 cooling-off period of two years for auditors, secretarial
                 auditors, cost auditors, registered valuers and insolvency

                                     888
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.

                 professionals would adequately          safeguard the
                 independence of the Board while         avoiding undue
                 restrictions on such professionals.

                 The Committee, therefore, recommend that the proposed
                 amendment under sub-clause (A) of clause (g) of sub-
                 section (1), seeking to substitute the words "dealing with
                 related party transactions" with the words "or subjected to
                 penalty for default", be omitted. The Committee further

100. 55.6  55      55.6.1 On scrutinizing Clause 55 of the Bill, which seeks to
                   amend Section 165 of the Companies Act, the Committee
                   note that it empowers the Central Government to notify a
                   lower maximum number of directorships for specific
                   classes of companies or directors.

                   The Committee acknowledge that calibrating directorship
                   caps is a progressive measure intended to ensure greater
                   active participation, diligence, and board oversight by
                   corporate leaders.

                   The Committee, however, observe that the proposed
                   enabling provision does not specify a transitional
                   mechanism, which could lead to inadvertent non-
                   compliance and trigger abrupt vacation of office under
                   Section 167 of the Act the moment a lower cap is notified.

                   To prevent administrative hardship and operational
                   disruption, the Committee expect the Ministry to
                   incorporate a clear compliance window in the rules,
                   allowing affected directors a reasonable time period to
                   bring their directorships within the revised ceilings
                   without being exposed to vacation proceedings under
                   Section 167 during such period.

                   55.6.2. Regarding the calibration of lower ceilings--
                   including separate limits for public and listed entities--the
                   Committee emphasize that the power delegated to the
                   Central Government must be exercised judiciously. The
                   Committee accordingly desire that the Ministry, while

                                       891
S. Para    Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.    No.
                   framing statutory rules, take into account realistic
                   operational requirements, consult key regulators such as
                   SEBI and other relevant stakeholders, and maintain
                   balanced standards that do not unduly constrain
                   legitimate corporate group structures.

                   55.6.3 Subject to the incorporation of these procedural
                   safeguards in the rules, and upon due consideration of the
                   stakeholder representations alongside the Ministry's
                   assurances, the Committee concur with the proposed
                   statutory changes and recommend the adoption of Clause
                   55 without any modification.

101. 56.6  56      The Committee note that Clause 56 rationalizes the
                   enforcement of directors' fiduciary duties under Section
                   166 of the Companies Act, 2013 by decriminalizing routine
                   defaults, while preserving criminal liability and
                   disgorgement mechanisms for grave breaches involving
                   wrongful enrichment under sub-section (5).

                   The Committee observe with satisfaction that empowering
                   courts to order the recovery of undue gains under sub-
                   section (7) and introducing non-criminal penalties under
                   sub-section (8) fills a critical legislative gap, establishing a
                   balanced, proportionate, and enforceable compliance
                   framework.

                   Regarding stakeholder concerns over subjecting non-
                   procedural duties--such as acting in good faith,
                   exercising due care, skill, diligence, and independent

                                       892
S. Para    Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.    No.
                   judgment under sub-sections (2) and (3)--to monetary
                   penalties, the Committee are firmly of the view that
                   excluding these core fiduciary duties from sub-section (8)
                   would compromise board accountability. The Committee,
                   therefore, emphasize that all statutory obligations under
                   Section 166 must remain backed by civil penalties, while
                   expecting adjudicating authorities to exercise judicious
                   discretion to distinguish between bona fide business

                   recommend the adoption of Clause 56 without any
                   modification.

103. 58.6  58      58.6.1 The Committee note that Section 173(5) of the
                   Companies Act, 2013 currently requires One Person

                   the two meetings. The proviso exempts One Person
                   Companies with only one director from this requirement.
                   The Committee further note that the proposed amendment
                   collapses this into a simpler requirement of at least one
                   Board meeting in a calendar year for these classes of
                   companies, thereby removing the rigid ninety-day gap
                   stipulation.

                   58.6.2 The Committee recognize that the earlier
                   requirement imposed disproportionate procedural burdens
                   on companies with minimal scale and limited operations.
                   The Committee are of the view that the amendment eases
                   compliance for very small entities by reducing

                                       895
S. Para    Clause  Observation/ Recommendation

                   Board-meeting requirements to a single annual meeting,
                   thereby aligning governance obligations with practical
                   realities while still preserving minimum oversight.

                   be considered separately through Rules. The Committee

                   meeting frequency.

104. 59.6  59      59.6.1  The Committee note that Section 184(1)

                   interest in any company, body corporate, firm or

                   first Board meeting of every financial year, in addition to

                   disclosing at the first meeting in which he participates as

                   director and whenever there is a change. The Committee

                   further note that the proposed amendment in Clause 59

                   seeks to remove the recurring annual disclosure

                   obligation, so that disclosures will now be required only

                   (a) at the first Board meeting attended by a director, and

                   (b) upon any change in previously declared interests.

                           896
S. Para    Clause  Observation/ Recommendation

                   amendment eliminates a recurring, often perfunctory

                   annual compliance step that added limited governance

                   value when no change in interest had occurred, making

                   disclosure event-driven rather than calendar-driven and

                   thereby aligning the obligation more closely with its

                   substantive purpose. The Committee concur that Clause

107. 62.4  62      62.4.1  The Committee note that Section 189 of the

                   Companies Act 2013 requires companies to maintain a

                   register recording particulars of contracts/arrangements in

                   which directors have an interest under section 184. The

                   Committee further note that the unamended section did

                   not contain a self-contained penalty provision for non-

                   compliance with section 189 specifically. Clause 62 seeks

                   to insert a dedicated penalty thereby creating explicit and

                   standalone enforceability for the register-maintenance

                   obligation under Section 189. The Committee find merit in

                   the insertion of a dedicated penalty provision, as it

                   removes ambiguity about which penalty applies to defaults

                   under Section 189 and strengthens enforceability of the

                   register-maintenance obligation.

                   62.4.2  The Committee further note that the penalty

                   structure imposes a flat 2 lakh penalty on the company,

                   without a per-day continuing default formula or

                   officer-level liability, thereby treating non-maintenance as

                   a one-time compliance lapse rather than an ongoing

                   default. The Committee recognize that this approach

                   reflects the nature of the lapse while avoiding

                   disproportionate exposure for companies and officers. The

                   Committee, therefore, after examining the Clause and

                   considering the justification given by the Ministry, accept

                   the amendment to Clause 62 without any modification.

109. 63.6  63      63.6.1 The Committee note that while the Companies Act,
                   2013 provides a structured mechanism for resignation of
                   directors under section 168, there is presently no
                   corresponding statutory framework governing the
                   resignation of whole-time key managerial personnel (KMP)
                   who are not directors. The proposed insertion of section
                   203A, therefore, seeks to address this legislative gap and
                   enhance regulatory transparency by mandating formal
                   intimation of such resignations to the Registrar.

                   63.6.2 The Committee further note that the proposed
                   provision lays down a clear procedural framework, inter
                   alia, providing that: (i) resignation shall be tendered by
                   way of a written notice; (ii) the Board shall take note of
                   such resignation and intimate the Registrar within the
                   prescribed time; (iii) in case of failure by the company, the
                   KMP may independently file such resignation with
                   reasons; (iv) the effective date of resignation is linked to
                   receipt of notice or a specified later date; and (v) liability
                   for acts during the tenure continues even after resignation.

                   63.6.3 The Committee note the concerns that the current
                                       902
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 drafting of Section 203A could be misread as permitting
                 resignation of a whole-time key managerial personnel on a
                 bare one day's notice, which would undermine governance
                 stability. The Committee observe that the legislative intent
                 of Section 203A is to provide a statutory mechanism for
                 disclosure and regulatory visibility of KMP resignations,
                 not to override or shorten contractual or policy-based
                 notice periods. The Committee find merit in clarifying that
                 the provision should expressly state that the notice period
                 for resignation of a whole-time KMP shall be such period
                 as may be agreed upon in the employment contract or be
                 mutually agreed upon between the KMP and the company.
                 Such clarification will prevent misuse of the provision,
                 ensure accountability remains tied to the individual's
                 tenure, and preserve professional certainty without
                 creating conflict with contractual arrangements.
                 Accordingly, the Committee recommend that the clause be
                 suitably amended to make clear that Section 203A governs
                 disclosure and intimation to the Registrar, while the length
                 of notice period continues to be determined by
                 employment contract, thereby safeguarding governance
                 stability and avoiding unintended interpretation of one day
                 resignations.

                 63.6.4 The Committee also recommend that it may be
                 specified, by way of an explanatory clarification
                 accompanying Section 203A or in the Rules to be
                 prescribed thereunder, that Section 203A is intended to
                 govern the disclosure and intimation of such resignation
                 to the Registrar, and not to override or shorten any

                 903
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.     contractually or internally prescribed notice period.

                 63.6.5 The Committee note the suggestion that the proviso
                 to Section 203A may be suitably modified to limit post-
                 resignation liability of whole-time KMPs to a reasonable
                 and specified period, with the objective of balancing
                 accountability and professional certainty. The Committee
                 observe that while this proposal seeks to provide clarity
                 and fairness, they concur with the Ministry's clarification
                 that prescribing such a limitation could undermine
                 accountability for defaults committed during the
                 individual's tenure. Accordingly, the Committee
                 recommend that Section 203A be retained in its present
                 form on this point, with liability firmly anchored to acts
                 committed while in office, thereby ensuring accountability
                 without introducing arbitrary post-resignation periods.

                 63.6.6. Concerns have been raised about aligning of
                 timelines relating to resignation and reporting under
                 Section203A with that of SEBI's requirements relating to
                 KMP appointment and resignation. The Committee, feel
                 that the official filing window under the Companies Act
                 should align with broader market disclosure structures to
                 eliminate discrepancies between stock exchange
                 notifications and public registry records. The committee
                 therefore recommend that the Ministry, either in the
                 provisions or the rules formulated thereunder, should
                 specify the timelines to be followed by the Company and
                 the Key Managerial Personnel regarding intimation to the
                 Registrar thus eliminating any confliction with the SEBI

                                     904
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.     guidelines.

                 63.6.7 Accordingly, after considering the suggestions
                 received and the submissions of the Ministry as well as
                 detailed deliberation in the matter, the Committee
                 recommend that the clause be amended as under :-

                 "After section 203 of the principal Act, the following
                 section shall be inserted, namely:--

                 "203A. (1) A whole-time key managerial personnel of a
                 company, who is not a director, may resign from his office
                 by giving a notice in writing to the company, and the
                 Board shall, on receipt of such notice, take note of the
                 same and shall intimate the Registrar of such resignation
                 in such form and manner and within such time, as may be
                 prescribed:

                 Provided that where the company fails to intimate the
                 Registrar under this sub-section within such time the said
                 key managerial personnel may forward a copy of his
                 resignation along with detailed reasons for his resignation
                 to the Registrar in such manner, as may be prescribed.

                 (2) The resignation of a key managerial personnel under
                 sub-section (1) shall take effect from the date as mutually
                 agreed by such key managerial personnel and the
                 company or the date arrived at based on the contract of
                 employment between such key managerial personnel and

                 905
S. Para    Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.    No.     the company whichever is earlier.

                   Provided that such key managerial personnel who has
                   resigned shall be liable even after his resignation for the
                   default for which he was liable during his tenure.".

110. 64.6  64      64.6.1 The Committee note that the proposed amendment
                   seeks to formally align the terminology under section 204
                   by substituting the expression "company secretary in
                   practice" with "secretarial auditor", while retaining the
                   substantive requirement that such auditor shall be a
                   company secretary in practice. The Committee note that
                   this brings the framework for secretarial audit in line with
                   the provisions relating to statutory auditors and cost

                   ensuring consistency across audit functions.

                   insertion of sub-section (1A) enables appointment of
                   secretarial auditors in the name of a firm, subject to the
                   condition that a majority of partners are practising in India
                   and are eligible for such appointment. This provides
                   statutory recognition to multi-disciplinary partnership
                   structures.

                   64.6.3 The Committee note the suggestion that the
                   appointment and tenure of Secretarial Auditors be aligned
                   with the framework prescribed under SEBI (LODR)
                   Regulation 24A(b), including fixed terms and shareholder

                 recommend separately empowering SEBI to prescribe the

111. 65.4  65      65.4.1 The Committee note that the proposed amendment
                   seeks to substitute sub-section (7) of section 206 with a
                   revised penalty framework for failure to furnish any
                   information or explanation, or to produce any document,
                   required under the said section. The Committee observe
                   that the existing provision prescribes a fine which may
                   extend to one lakh rupees on the company and every
                   officer in default, with an additional fine of up to five
                   hundred rupees for each day of continuing failure, without
                   any prescribed cap.

                   65.4.2 The Committee further note that the proposed sub-
                   section (7) replaces this fine-based punishment with a
                   structured, capped penalty. The company shall be liable to
                   a penalty of one lakh rupees, with a further penalty of five
                   hundred rupees per day of continuing failure, subject to a
                   maximum of five lakh rupees; and every officer in default
                   shall be liable to a penalty of twenty-five thousand rupees,
                   with a further penalty of two hundred rupees per day of

                                       909
S. Para    Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.    No.
                   continuing failure, subject to a maximum of one lakh
                   rupees. The Committee note that, as stated by the Ministry,
                   this amendment is part of the broader decriminalisation
                   exercise under the Bill.

                   65.4.3 The Committee recognize that the proposed
                   amendment provides certainty on maximum exposure
                   through express caps, while preserving a meaningful daily
                   deterrent for continuing non-compliance with Registrar
                   inquiries. The Committee further note that this also
                   strengthens the Registrar's practical enforcement leverage
                   in information-gathering and inspection proceedings, by
                   making non-cooperation a quantifiable, swiftly ad
                   judicable civil wrong rather than a criminal offence
                   requiring prosecution.

                   65.4.4  The Committee find that the proposed

                   framework brings certainty and proportionality to the

                   penalty structure under section 206 by prescribing

                   distinct, capped penalties for the company and its officers

                   in place of the earlier open-ended fine. The Committee,

                   having examined the provisions of the Clause, accept

                   Clause 65 as proposed, without any modification.

113. 67.6  67      67.6.1 The Committee note that Clause 67 seeks to amend
                   Section 230 of the Companies Act, 2013 to provide for a
                   single jurisdictional bench of the National Company Law
                   Tribunal (NCLT) for schemes of compromise, arrangement
                   and amalgamation, and to omit references to the
                   Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016. The Committee
                   further note that, with effect from commencement of the
                   Amendment Act, every application under section 230 or
                   sections 231 to 233 must be filed before the NCLT bench
                   having jurisdiction over the transferee or resultant
                   company, with such bench exercising all powers of the
                   Tribunal for all companies involved in the scheme, while
                   applications already pending as on the date of
                   commencement will continue under the pre-amendment
                   regime. The Committee are of the view that this measure
                   will reduce multiplicity of proceedings, compress
                   timelines, and lower cost and procedural duplication in
                   multi-state mergers, demergers and amalgamations, while
                   the savings clause preserves certainty for schemes
                   already in process. The Committee also note that the
                   amendment aligns this framework with the existing fast-

                                       911
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 track approach under Rule 25(4)(a) of the Companies
                 (Compromises, Arrangements and Amalgamations) Rules,
                 2016.

                 67.6.2 The Committee considered the suggestions
                 received for a mechanism to transfer proceedings between
                 Benches, or to constitute a Special Bench, having regard
                 also to concerns raised during deliberations regarding
                 NCLT pendency and a further suggestion for a separate,
                 specialised tribunal for mergers and acquisitions. The
                 Committee note the Ministry's response that a single
                 bench hearing merger schemes ensures efficiency and
                 avoids parallel proceedings, that provision for Special
                 Benches already exists under section 419 read with Clause
                 96 of the Bill, and that the question of inter-Bench transfer
                 of proceedings is presently sub judice before the Hon'ble
                 Supreme Court, for which reason the Ministry has
                 refrained from legislating on the point. The Committee
                 accept this position, while recommending that NCLT
                 capacity be augmented, including through additional
                 Benches and members, given that capacity constraints
                 remain a root cause of delay. The Committee urge the
                 Ministry to revisit the question of inter-Bench transfer
                 once the pending matter before the Supreme Court is
                 decided.

                 67.6.3 The Committee note that the deletion of the
                 Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code cross-reference in sub-
                 sections (1) and (6) confines schemes under Section 230
                 to the Companies Act framework and sharpens the

                                     912
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 jurisdictional boundary between the two statutes. In this
                 connection, the Committee considered the suggestion that
                 applications under section 230 be barred during the
                 corporate insolvency resolution process, subject to the
                 Tribunal's discretion post-liquidation, and a query raised
                 during deliberations on reconciling the relaxed
                 merger/demerger process with parallel IBC proceedings
                 involving a holding or subsidiary company. The
                 Committee note the Ministry's clarification that the

115. 69.6  69      69.6.1  The Committee note that the Section 233 of

                   the Companies Act 2013 provides a simplified, Regional-

                   Director-sanctioned fast-track merger route for prescribed

                   categories of companies (e.g., small companies, holding-

                   wholly owned subsidiary mergers, and other prescribed

                   classes), as an alternative to the full NCLT process under

                   sections 230-232.

                   69.6.2  The Committee also note that as per the

                   current amendment the scheme must now be approved by

                   a majority of members or class of members present and

                   voting at the meeting (in the prescribed manner) who hold

                   at least 75% of the value in shares held by such members

                           916
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 present and voting. This is a marked relaxation from the
                 requirement of a 90% (nine-tenths) shareholder approval
                 threshold under the unamended provision and is expected
                 to materially increase the practical usability of section 233.
                 The Committee accept that the safeguard of a members'
                 meeting, whether physical, hybrid, or through e-voting,
                 may continue to be mandatory in order to preserve
                 transparency and stakeholder participation in the merger
                 process.

                          However, the Committee are of the considered view
                 that the reduction of the approval threshold from 90% to
                 75%, taken together with the built-in safeguard of
                 publication of the scheme for stakeholder comment, is not,
                 by itself, a sufficient answer to the concerns raised
                 regarding minority shareholder protection. Therefore, the
                 Committee recommend that a statutory exit right for
                 dissenting/non-voting shareholders may be provided
                 explicitly safeguarding minority shareholders' ability to
                 object, particularly where foreign institutional investors
                 and promoters may have a different investment horizon
                 than small shareholders.

                          Accordingly, the Committee recommend that the
                 Ministry, within the Act itself may provide a clear and
                 enforceable mechanism such as a fair-value exit or buyout
                 option for shareholders who dissent from a fast-track
                 merger or amalgamation, so that the interests of minority
                 shareholders, including retail and non-institutional
                 shareholders, are not subordinated to the interests of

                                     917
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 majority or institutional shareholders. The Committee
                 therefore, recommend that under Section 233(1) after (b)
                 the following provision may be inserted:

                                  "Provided that a fair-value exit or buyout
                         option for shareholders who dissent from a fast-
                         track merger or amalgamation may be provided in
                         such manner as may be prescribed:"

116. 70.6  70      70.6.1  The Committee note that, historically, under

                   schemes of compromise/arrangement sanctioned prior to

                   the commencement of the Companies Act, 2013, some

                   transferee companies ended up holding shares in their

                   own name, directly or via trusts, as part of the

                   restructuring -- a practice that effectively created a form

                   of treasury stock, which is prohibited under Indian

                   company law, as shares cannot generally be held by a

                   company in itself. The Committee observe that this new

                   insertion of section 233A creates a mandatory, time-bound

                   mechanism to deal with this legacy position.

                   70.6.2  The Committee find that this amendment

                   closes a long-standing structural anomaly in Indian

                   company law by giving companies a definite three-year

                   window to regularize legacy treasury-shareholdings

                   arising from pre-2013-Act schemes. The Committee are of

                   the view that the automatic, deemed-capital-reduction

                   consequence for non-disposal provides a self-executing

                   backstop, reducing reliance on case-by-case Tribunal

                   intervention to address non-compliant treasury holdings.

                   70.6.3  The Committee further observe that the

                   uncapped, per-day penalty for continuing non-compliance

                   with the cancellation obligation, unlike many other

                   penalties in the Bill, which are capped, signals that

                           920
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 continued retention of treasury shares beyond the
                 cancellation trigger is treated as a serious, ongoing
                 governance failure.

                 70.6.4 The Committee are of the view that companies,
                 particularly older listed and unlisted entities that
                 underwent pre-2013 mergers or restructurings, would
                 benefit from conducting a shareholding audit to identify
                 any legacy self-held or trust-held shares, and recommend
                 that the Rules require such identification and planning for
                 disposal well within the three-year window once the
                 provision is notified. The Committee also recognize the
                 merit in the suggestion that the Rules provide for
                 restrictions on voting and dividend rights during the
                 disposal window, and for exchange-based sale in the case
                 of listed companies, an approach consistent with the
                 Ministry's own submission that SEBI had already acted to
                 curb this practice for listed companies from 2021, and
                 recommend that the Ministry give due consideration to
                 this suggestion while framing the Rules.

                 70.6.5 During their deliberation, a concern was raised
                 regarding the shares bought back and extinguished,
                 remaining unpaid/unclaimed for over 7 years, go to the
                 Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF), but there's
                 currently no equivalent provision for unclaimed
                 consideration in delisted companies. The representatives
                 of the Ministry confirmed that an amendment is being
                 brought to address the "amount in respect of shares
                 bought back and extinguished remaining unpaid or

                                     921
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 unclaimed" while expressly stating that this is a distinct
                 issue (buyback/IEPF) rather than the self-held/treasury-
                 share extinguishment provision. The Committee therefore
                 recommend that the provision in itself must remove this
                 ambiguity which connects the extinguishment of treasury
                 shares to the provisions under section 66 of the
                 Companies Act.

                 70.6.6 In view of the above, the Committee recommend that
                 Clause 70 may be amended as follows:-

                 After section 233 of the principal Act, the following section
                 shall be inserted, namely:--

                 "233A. (1) Where a transferee company, as a result of a
                 compromise or an arrangement which has taken place
                 prior to the commencement of the Companies Act, 2013,
                 has held any shares in its own name or in the name of any
                 trust (whether on its behalf or on behalf of any of its
                 subsidiary or associate companies), such shares shall,
                 within a period not exceeding three years from the date of
                 commencement of the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Act,
                 2026, be dealt with or disposed of in such manner, as may
                 be prescribed.

                 (2) Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, if a
                 company fails to deal with or dispose of the shares
                 referred to in sub-section (1), such shares shall be
                 cancelled and extinguished by the company in such
                 manner, as may be prescribed, and such cancellation and

                                     922
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation

                 (3) If the company fails to comply with the provisions of
                 sub-section (2), the company and every officer of the

                 ten thousand rupees for every day during which the
                 default continues.

117. 70A.2 70A   70A.2.1 The Committee note that the current provisions of
                 the Section 240 ensures that an officer-in-default of a
                 transferor company cannot escape liability for offences
                 committed before a merger/amalgamation/acquisition
                 simply because the merger took place -- the officer's
                 personal liability survives the corporate restructuring.

                 70A.2.2 The Committee further note that the existing
                 provision is silent on what happens to the transferor
                 company's own pending legal proceedings. Since the
                 transferor company ceases to exist upon merger, it's
                 ambiguous whether ongoing prosecutions/ proceedings
                 that were initiated against the company itself (as opposed
                 to against individual officers) can continue -- and if so,
                 against whom.

                 70A.2.3 The Committee feel that addressing the
                 treatment of ongoing prosecutions/proceedings initiated
                 against the company itself, is of vital importance.
                 Therefore, the Committee recommend that the following

                                     923
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.     provision may be suitably incorporated in the Bill:

                 In section 240 of the principal Act,-

                 (a) in the marginal heading, -

                 (i) the word "of officers" shall be omitted;

                 (ii) after the word "offences", the word "default" shall be
                 inserted;

                 (b) for the words "the liability in respect of offences
                 committed under this Act by the officers in default, of the
                 transferor company prior to its merger, amalgamation or
                 acquisition shall continue", the following words, brackets,
                 letters and figures

                 "(i) the liability of the officers in default of the transferor
                 company in respect of offences and default committed
                 under this Act prior to its merger, amalgamation or
                 acquisition shall continue; and

                 (ii) the proceedings in respect of offences and default
                 committed under this Act prior to its merger,
                 amalgamation or acquisition against the transferor
                 company, shall be continued against the transferee
                 company," shall be substituted.

118. 71.6  71      71.6.1 The Committee note that Clause 71 omits sub-
                   section (8) of section 242, thereby removing the existing
                   criminal fine provision for contravention of Tribunal orders
                   passed under sub-section (5), as part of the Bill's broader
                   decriminalization exercise.

                   71.6.2 The Committee note the suggestion that a new civil
                   penalty and enforcement framework be introduced in place
                   of the omitted provision, and the countervailing
                   suggestion that section 242(8) be retained so that
                   Tribunals continue to have the power to penalise non-
                   compliant companies. The Committee observe that neither
                   suggestion has been accepted by the Ministry, since
                   existing mechanisms for execution and enforcement of
                   Tribunal orders, including the Tribunal's contempt powers
                   under section 425 of the Companies Act, 2013, are
                   considered adequate, obviating the need either for a new
                   civil penalty regime or for retention of the criminal
                   provision being omitted.

                   71.6.3 The Committee find that the Ministry's reliance on
                   the Tribunal's existing contempt powers under section 425
                   is a reasonable basis for the omission, and are satisfied
                   that the decriminalization of section 242(8) does not leave
                   a gap in the enforcement of Tribunal orders.

                   71.6.4 The Committee, therefore, accept Clause 71 as
                   proposed, without any modification.

119. 72.4  72      72.4.1 The Committee note that Clause 72 makes a cross-
                   reference correction to section 245(1), substituting the
                   reference to "sub-section (2)" with "sub-section (3)". The
                   Committee observe that the requisite number of members
                   or depositors entitled to file a class action application
                   under sub-section (1) is, in fact, prescribed in sub-section
                   (3) of section 245, whereas sub-section (2) deals with the
                   liability of an audit firm and its partners in respect of
                   damages or compensation claimed against them. The
                   Committee find that the existing cross-reference in sub-
                   section (1) is, therefore, misdirected, and that Clause 72
                   corrects this error so as to ensure that sub-section (1)
                   accurately refers to the sub-section actually prescribing
                   the threshold numbers.

                   72.4.2 The Committee find that this is a purely technical,
                   drafting-correction amendment with no independent
                   substantive policy effect.

                                       926

121. 73.6.2 73   Regarding stakeholder suggestions on the central tracking
                 of valuation reports, the Committee observe that the

                 Number (VRIN) is essential to enhance authenticity,
                 traceability, and prevent misuse.

                 In pursuance of the Committee's observation, the Ministry
                 of Corporate Affairs has agreed to explicitly mandate the
                 provision for VRIN generation at the time of framing
                 regulations by the Valuation Authority.

                 The Committee further stress that this subordinate

                 transparent, and consultative manner with relevant
                 stakeholders to ensure policy coherence and seamless

                 927
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.     implementation.

122. 73.6.3 73   The Committee also note and accept the detailed
                 justification provided by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs
                 on various structural and policy suggestions raised by
                 stakeholders regarding the governance of valuers:

                 (i) Designation of IBBI as the Valuation Authority: The
                 Committee note that designating the Insolvency and
                 Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) leverages an established
                 statutory regulator with existing administrative
                 infrastructure, thereby preventing institutional duplication
                 and avoiding the need to constitute a separate statutory
                 body.

                 (ii) Designation of NCLAT as Appellate Forum: The
                 Committee accept that since Section 247 specifically
                 governs valuations required under the Companies Act,
                 2013, the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal
                 (NCLAT) is the appropriate specialized judicial body to
                 hear appeals against orders of the Valuation Authority,
                 making a separate appellate tribunal unnecessary.

                 (iii) Adoption of Valuation Standards: The Committee
                 note that framing valuation standards and policies
                 (including consideration of ICAI standards) is properly
                 within the purview of the Valuation Authority to
                 recommend to the Central Government via
                 Rules/Regulations, rather than embedding specific

                 928
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.     institutional standards rigidly into primary legislation.

                 (iv) Recognition of Valuers under Other Enactments
                 (SEBI Act, Wealth Tax Act, etc.): The Committee accept
                 that Section 247 is meant strictly for valuations under the
                 Companies Act, 2013, and that other sectoral regulators
                 (such as SEBI or RBI) or revenue authorities may align
                 their respective rules or regulations to recognize IBBI-
                 registered valuers as deemed fit by them.

                 The Committee observe that the regulatory and
                 institutional architecture proposed under Clause 73 is
                 balanced, cohesive, and adequate. The Committee,
                 therefore, recommend that the provisions as proposed in
                 the Bill as introduced regarding these matters suffice and
                 do not necessitate further change.

123. 73.6.4 73   Furthermore, the Committee observe that prior
                 consultation with stakeholders is critical to ensuring
                 objectivity, predictability, and transparency in the
                 valuation regulatory process. The Committee, therefore,
                 recommend that after sub-section 9 of Section 247, the
                 following new sub-section 9A shall be inserted:

                 "(9A) The Valuation Authority shall, prior to making
                 regulations under sub-section (9),--

                 (a) ensure transparency by publishing the draft regulations
                 along with all relevant details on its website and inviting
                 public comments for such period as may be specified

                                     929
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.     therein; and

                 (b) review such regulations at least once in three years:

                 Provided that if the Valuation Authority is of the opinion
                 that it is necessary or expedient to make, or amend, any
                 regulations urgently in public interest, or where the
                 subject matter of the regulations relates solely to the
                 internal functioning of the Valuation Authority, it may, for
                 reasons to be recorded in writing, make or amend such
                 regulations without following the procedure specified in
                 clause (a)."

124. 73.6.5 73   Subject to incorporation of the above amendments, the
                 Committee accept Clause 73 of the Bill.

139. 86.4  86      The Committee find from the examination of Clause 86 of
                   the Bill that it amends Section 378ZA of the Companies
                   Act, 2013 to streamline statutory timelines for holding
                   Annual General Meetings (AGMs) of Producer Companies.

                   The clause removes the rigid requirement to hold the first
                   AGM within ninety days of incorporation. Instead, it allows
                   the first AGM to be held within nine months from the close

                                       941
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 of the first financial year, and subsequent AGMs within six
                 months.

                 Furthermore, it explicitly clarifies that members shall
                 adopt the articles of association and appoint directors at
                 the first AGM, while revising the quorum threshold to one-
                 fourth of total members or one hundred members,
                 whichever is lower.

                 The Committee observe that these modifications
                 successfully align the governance framework of Producer
                 Companies with general corporate standards under the
                 Act.

                 Replacing the restrictive setup deadline provides practical
                 breathing space for newly incorporated entities to
                 organize their operations. Similarly, setting a realistic
                 quorum threshold prevents procedural deadlocks and
                 ensures smooth decision-making while preserving
                 democratic member control.

                 The proposed amendments effectively resolve statutory
                 ambiguities, eliminate operational friction, and enhance
                 ease of compliance. Accordingly, the Committee
                 recommend that Clause 86 may be accepted as proposed.

140. 87.6.1 87   The Committee find from the examination of Clause 87 of

                 Act, 2013. The substituted provision mandates internal
                 audits for Producer Companies having an average annual

                                     942
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation

                 operational flexibility without compromising the spirit of
                 the law, the Committee emphasize the need for robust

                 effective implementation.
