142. 88.6  88      The Committee find from the examination of the contents
                   of Clause 88 and the parallel provisions of Section 378ZM
                   of the Companies Act, 2013 that Clause 88 of the Bill
                   suitably decriminalizes various offences relating to
                   Producer Companies by replacing criminal fines and
                   imprisonment with a civil monetary penalty framework.
                   Specifically, it caps penalties for unauthorized use of the
                   company name and failure to furnish information at five

                                       944
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 lakh rupees, while capping penalties for procedural
                 defaults, such as failing to convene general meetings or
                 hand over records, at one lakh rupees.

                 The Committee observe that substituting custodial
                 sentences and open-ended daily fines with capped
                 monetary penalties aligns with the broader legislative
                 objectives of decriminalizing corporate laws. This
                 approach removes unwarranted fear among directors and
                 officers while preserving an effective statutory deterrent
                 against governance lapses.

                 With regard to sub-clause (a), the Committee note that the
                 pronoun "he" is inadvertently used when referring to "any
                 person other than a Producer Company". Since "any
                 person other than a Producer Company" is a legal entity
                 consistently being referred to throughout Chapter XXIA of
                 the Act, the Committee recommend that the phrase "he
                 shall be" be substituted with "that person shall be" in
                 Clause 88(a) to ensure statutory uniformity and drafting
                 precision and the sub-section be modified as follows:

                 "In section 378ZM of the principal Act,-- (a) in sub-section
                 (1), for the words "he shall be punishable with fine which
                 may extend to ten thousand rupees for every day during
                 which such name has been used by him", the words "that
                 person shall be liable to a penalty of one lakh rupees and
                 in case of continuing failure, with a further penalty of five
                 hundred 22 rupees for each day, after the first during
                 which such failure continues, subject to a maximum of five

                                     945
S. Para    Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.    No.     lakh rupees" shall be substituted;"

                   Subject to the incorporation of the specified drafting
                   correction, the Committee recommend that Clause 88 may
                   be accepted as proposed.

143. 89.4  89      The Committee find that the proposed Clause 89
                   associated with Section 378ZS of the Companies Act, 2013
                   seeks to decriminalize contraventions occurring during
                   the re-conversion of Producer Companies into inter-State
                   cooperative societies. Specifically, it replaces criminal
                   fines with a civil monetary penalty framework for defaults
                   under sub-section (4) of the said Section.

                   The Committee observe that this provision serves as a
                   necessary consequential amendment under the broader
                   policy of corporate law reform. Replacing criminal
                   sanctions with monetary penalties enhances compliance
                   while directly supporting the ease of doing business.

                   Finding the proposed amendment well-aligned with the
                   objectives of the Bill, the Committee recommend that
                   Clause 89 may be accepted in its entirety without any
                   modification.

144. 90.6  90      The Committee, on thorough examination of Clause 90 of
                   the Bill, find that it seeks to amend Section 392 of the
                   Companies Act, 2013 to decriminalize contraventions
                   committed by foreign companies under Chapter XXII of the

                   946
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.     Act.

                 The amendment replaces criminal fines with a civil
                 monetary penalty framework. Under the revised
                 provisions, a foreign company is liable to a penalty of one
                 lakh rupees, with a continuing daily penalty of five
                 hundred rupees, subject to a maximum cap of five lakh
                 rupees. Additionally, every officer in default is liable to a
                 penalty of twenty-five thousand rupees, with a continuing
                 daily penalty of two hundred rupees, capped at two lakh
                 rupees.

                 The Committee observe that the proposed framework
                 establishes proportionate and graded consequences for
                 continuing defaults while capping maximum monetary
                 exposure. This aligns penalty structures for foreign
                 companies with standards applicable to other corporate
                 entities under the Act, ensuring equal regulatory treatment
                 and encouraging cross-border investment.

                 Having considered the concerns raised by stakeholders
                 alongside the clarifications submitted by the Ministry of
                 Corporate Affairs, the Committee concur with the
                 Ministry's position. After thorough deliberations, the
                 Committee accept the proposed amendment and
                 recommend that Clause 90 may be accepted without any
                 modification.

145. 90A.2 New   The Committee note that re-domiciliation enables foreign-
                 incorporated companies to migrate seamlessly to an

                                     947
S. Para  Clause     Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
         insertion  International Financial Services Centre (IFSC) without
                    undergoing winding-up or dissolution in their home
                    jurisdiction, thereby ensuring complete business and legal
                    continuity.

                    The Committee observe that a significant number of Indian
                    promoters with offshore operations are desirous of
                    returning to Indian shores, provided an equivalent and
                    enabling regulatory environment is established. In this
                    regard, the Committee are of the view that facilitating
                    inward re-domiciliation under the Companies Act, 2013
                    would eliminate the need to incorporate fresh entities and
                    significantly avoid onerous transaction costs associated
                    with share or asset transfers.

                    The Committee further note that while the IFSCA actively
                    endeavours to onshore offshore financial and business
                    activities into the IFSC, the Companies Act, 2013 currently
                    lacks an explicit enabling statutory framework for inward
                    re-domiciliation. In order to facilitate the reverse-flipping
                    and shifting of foreign subsidiaries of Indian companies
                    back to India, the Committee feel that an enabling legal
                    framework including provisions relating to taxation, capital
                    gains, stamp duty, transfer and vesting of assets and
                    liabilities, filing and compliance requirements,
                    continuation of rights and obligations, and other
                    consequential or incidental matters arising from such
                    redomiciliation, is essential for seamless migration.
                    Therefore, the Committee recommend that the Central
                    Government may, in consultation and coordination with

                                        948
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation

                 the Ministries, Departments and regulatory authorities
                 concerned, notify a comprehensive framework to facilitate
                 the redomiciliation of foreign-based entities and may also
                 undertake or recommend suitable amendments to the
                 relevant laws, wherever necessary, to ensure a smooth
                 and seamless implementation of such redomiciliation.

147. 92.6  92      On scrutinizing Clause 92 of the Bill, which seeks to insert
                   a new Section 396A into the Companies Act, 2013, the
                   Committee find that it provides a dedicated statutory
                   appellate mechanism against decisions of the Registrar
                   under Section 4 or Section 7. Under this newly inserted
                   provision, any aggrieved person may prefer an appeal to
                   an officer not below the rank of Joint Director.

                   The Committee note that this provision fills a crucial gap
                   in administrative redressal. Determining statutory
                   appellate hierarchies falls squarely within the legislative
                   domain. Since the Act already provides established
                   remedies through the Regional Director, NCLT, NCLAT,

                                       956
S. Para     Clause     Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.     No.
                       and Supreme Court, creating a parallel appellate route to
                       High Courts is unnecessary and would disrupt the existing
                       statutory framework. The Committee, therefore, do not
                       concur with the suggestion to introduce an appellate
                       forum before High Courts.

                       With regard to the rule-making power for prescribing the
                       form, manner, and time limits for filing appeals, the
                       Committee observe that placing procedural details in rules
                       provides essential administrative flexibility. However, to
                       ensure that this appellate mechanism is fully effective and
                       accessible, the Committee desire that the Ministry
                       formulate these procedural rules in timely consultation
                       with relevant stakeholders, keeping the appeal process
                       simple, transparent, and user-friendly.

                       Upon due consideration of the stakeholder
                       representations alongside the clarifications furnished by
                       the Ministry, the Committee agree with the proposed
                       provisions and recommend that Clause 92 may be
                       accepted without any modification.

155. 94A.2 -       The Committee note that presently there is no clear
                   framework to deal with the casual vacancy arsing for the
                   post of President in NCLT or NCLAT which may impact the

                                       965
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.     functioning of the Tribunals.

                 The Committee further note that the express identification
                 of the senior-most Judicial Member as the acting head of
                 the Tribunal or the Appellate Tribunal would strengthen
                 institutional certainty, ensure continuity in the
                 administration of justice, uphold the judicial character and
                 independence of these specialised fora and eliminate the
                 scope for differing interpretations that may otherwise arise
                 under the existing provisions.

                 Therefore, the Committee, emphasise that an amendment
                 to section 415 of the Companies Act, 2013 is warranted to
                 remove any ambiguity regarding the person who shall
                 assume charge during an interim vacancy. Thus, the word
                 "judicial" after the words "senior-most" in sub-sections (1)
                 and (2) may be inserted, so as to expressly provide that, in
                 the event of a casual vacancy in the office of the President
                 of the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) or the
                 Chairperson of the National Company Law Appellate
                 Tribunal (NCLAT), the senior-most Judicial Member shall
                 discharge the functions of the respective office until a
                 regular appointment is made.

                 Accordingly, the section 415 of the Companies Act, may
                 be amended as follows:

                 "In section 415 of the principal Act, --

                 (a) in sub-section (1), after the words "senior-most", the
                                     966
S. Para    Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.    No.     word "judicial" shall be inserted;

                   (b) in sub-section (2), after the words "senior-most", the
                   word "judicial" shall be inserted."

                   The Committee, therefore, recommend that the proposed
                   amendment to section 415 of Companies Act, 2013 may be

                 compromising regulatory oversight.

162. 100.6 100   The Committee note that Clause 100 of the Bill seeks to
163. 101.6 101   amend Section 453 of the Companies Act, 2013 by

                 The Committee note that Clause 101 of the Bill amends
                 Section 454 of the Companies Act, 2013 to strengthen and
                 broaden the in-house adjudication framework. The key

                                     976
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 modifications include expanding the pool of Adjudicating
                 Officers by lowering the threshold rank from Registrar to
                 Assistant Registrar, broadening Appellate Authorities to
                 include Joint Directors alongside Regional Directors, and
                 empowering courts trying non-compliance prosecutions
                 under sub-section (8) to directly order recovery of unpaid
                 administrative penalties.

                 The Committee observe that these amendments represent
                 a major step toward de-clogging the judicial system and
                 facilitating swift compliance. Taking special note of the
                 oral evidence tendered by the Ministry before the
                 Committee, the Committee highlight that sub-section (1A)
                 establishes an enabling framework for suo-motu

                 retrospective effect to decriminalization across 19
                 provisions of the Act. This relief will be operationalized
                 through a Transition Scheme under sub-section (10) to
                 transfer or withdraw pending court complaints. The
                 Committee note that this approach draws upon the
                 Ministry's successful past experience of decriminalizing 51
                 offences.

                 The Committee further note that delegating operational
                 modalities--such as forms, procedure, and fee structures
                 under sub-section (1A)--to subordinate rules provides
                 necessary administrative flexibility to adapt to changing
                 economic and operational conditions without altering

                                     977
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation

                 However, upon examining the newly proposed sub-section
                 (1A) in Section 454, the Committee are of the considered
                 view that its scope needs to be broader and legally
                 precise. To ensure that the provision comprehensively
                 encompasses all categories of individuals who may be
                 held liable for contraventions across various sections of
                 the Act, the Committee consider it necessary to explicitly
                 include "director, promoter" and "or any other person".
                 This textual refinement will eliminate interpretational

                 may be prescribed under this section for adjudication of

                 Regarding stakeholder suggestions for a fixed statutory

                 frivolous or dilatory appeals.

                 inserted, namely:--

                 (e) receipt or payment not relatable to the business or
                 operations of the company."

                 Apart from the above drafting correction, the Committee
                 accept the Clause 104 as proposed.

167. 105.4 105   The Committee note that Clause 105 of the Bill seeks to
                 amend Section 457 of the Companies Act, 2013 to provide
                 statutory protection against compelled disclosure of the
                 identity or source of informants before any court, Tribunal,
                 or other authority in connection with investigations into
                 company affairs (under Section 210) and serious fraud
                 investigations conducted by the Serious Fraud

                 989
S. Para  Clause    Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.       Investigation Office (SFIO under Section 212).

                   The Committee consider this protection essential to
                   encourage the reporting of corporate fraud, financial
                   irregularities, and serious violations without fear of
                   retaliation or victimization. Accordingly, after careful
                   examination, the Committee recommend that Clause 105
                   be accepted as proposed.

168. 106.6 106     The Committee note that Clause 106 of the Bill seeks to
                   insert a new Section 466A in the Companies Act, 2013,
                   empowering the Central Government to issue directions,
                   guidelines, or circulars to clarify the intent of any rule and
                   establish ancillary procedural requirements.

                   The Committee observe with satisfaction that mandatory
                   prior consultation with experts and stakeholders ensures
                   transparent, informed, and inclusive decision-making. The
                   Committee observe with satisfaction that mandatory prior
                   consultation with experts and stakeholders ensures
                   transparent, informed, and inclusive decision-making.

                   Having carefully considered stakeholder suggestions and
                   the submissions of the Ministry, the Committee endorse
                   acceptance of Clause 106 as proposed.

169. 107.6.1. 107  The Committee note that Clause 107 of the Bill seeks to
          and      substitute sub-section (3) of Section 469 of the Companies
          107.6.2  Act, 2013 to decriminalize rule contraventions. As part of
                   the broader decriminalization exercise, the amendment

                                       990
S. Para  Clause  Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                 replaces the existing fine-based criminal punishment with
                 an enhanced and flexible civil penalty framework, enabling
                 the prescription of higher penalties and continuing daily
                 penalties for violations of rules framed under the Act.

                 The Committee observe that transitioning to an
                 administrative penalty framework will promote greater
                 voluntary compliance while remaining in tandem with the
                 broad objectives of the Bill. After an exhaustive
                 examination of stakeholder suggestions and the
                 responses of the Ministry, the Committee endorse Clause
                 107 as initially proposed.

                 Furthermore, during examination of the Bill, the Committee
                 observed that certain provisions of the Bill continue to
                 refer to enactments and authorities by their erstwhile
                 names, notwithstanding that the relevant statutes have
                 since been renamed or substituted. For example, multiple
                 lingering references to the Code of Criminal Procedure,
                 1973 in the Companies Act, 2013 have been noticed.

                 The Committee are of the opinion that there should be a
                 clean break from any reference to the old Acts. As such,
                 retaining references to outdated nomenclature is
                 inconsistent with the objective of ensuring clarity and
                 coherence in legislative drafting and may lead to avoidable
                 ambiguity in interpretation.

                 The Committee, therefore, recommend that the Ministry
                 may undertake a comprehensive review of both the

                                     991
S. Para  Clause        Observation/ Recommendation
No. No.  No.
                       principal Acts i.e. the Limited Liability Partnership Act,
                       2008 and the Companies Act, 2013 to identify all such
                       references and appropriately substitute them with the
                       current statutory nomenclatures to align the legislation
                       with the contemporary legal landscape.

2. At the outset, the Chairperson welcomed the Members to the First Sitting of
the Committee and also congratulated them for having been nominated for the `Joint
Committee on Corporate Law (Amendment) Bill, 2026'. Then, he drew attention of
the Members to the fact that the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026, which

                                                      1003
seeks further to amend the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008 and the
Companies Act, 2013, was introduced in Lok Sabha on 23rd March, 2026 and
referred to this Joint Committee to examine and report to the House by the last day
of the first week of the Monsoon Session, 2026. He also briefly apprised the
Members of the procedure followed by a Joint Committee on a Bill and invited their
kind attention to Direction 81(1) of the `Directions by the Speaker Lok Sabha'
regarding submission of memoranda on Bills by Members.
3. Thereafter, the Committee deliberated on the future course of action for the
examination of the said Bill, including deliberations with stakeholder/experts and
study visits to be undertaken in this regard. The Committee, with a view to obtain
broader views and suggestions on the Bill, also decided to invite memoranda from
experts, industries, associations, organizations and other stakeholders through a
Press Communiqué which will be published on the Secretariat's social media
platforms and displayed as a scroll on Sansad TV.

3. The Secretary, Ministry of MSME, informed the Committee that his Ministry
had engaged in structured consultations with MSME associations in January and
April 2025. He stated that the proposed amendments are largely aligned with the
concerns raised by the MSME sector, particularly regarding the reduction of
compliance burdens and costs. During the presentation, the Ministry highlighted the
sector's contribution to GDP and employment and expressed support for the revised
thresholds for small companies. The Ministry also proposed three additional
suggestions regarding the Limited Liability Partnership (LLP) Act, including aligning
thresholds with the MSME Act, introducing provisions for disclosing liabilities toward
MSMEs, and providing flexibility for Designated Partner Identification Numbers
(DPIN).

4. During the subsequent deliberations, the Committee raised several concerns
which, inter-alia, included the impact of raising the CSR net profit threshold from Rs.
5 crore to Rs. 10 crore on grassroots-level social initiatives in mining-affected and
underdeveloped regions, even as some Members felt the revised threshold merely
adjusted for inflation; whether CSR contribution should be computed on post-tax
rather than pre-tax profit, along with a suggestion for an additional `Corporate
Research Responsibility' contribution; the implications of exempting small companies

                                                      1013
from mandatory statutory audit on financial discipline and the risk of "vanishing
companies", with alternatives such as aligning the audit threshold with the Income-
Tax Act or a compliance certificate from a practising Company Secretary; the need to
synchronize the definitional and compliance framework across the Companies Act,
the MSME Act, and the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951, since
several MSME-registered entities are governed by more than one statute; and the
need to preserve the distinct policy objectives of the two frameworks despite
overlapping eligibility of the same unit as both a `small company' and an MSME.
5. The Committee also sought clarifications on various other issues relating to
the subject, including the mechanism for preventing larger corporate entities from
availing of fiscal benefits and other privileges intended for genuine micro and small
enterprises, and the balance to be maintained between regulatory relaxation and
protection of stakeholder interests, and the witnesses responded to some of those
queries. The Chairperson then directed the representatives to furnish written replies
to queries, which remained unanswered during the deliberations, to the Secretariat
within seven days.

                                      The witnesses then withdrew.

2. At the outset, the Hon'ble Chairperson welcomed the representatives of the
National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA) and informed that the Sitting had
been called for deliberations with the representatives of NFRA on various provisions
of the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026. Further, the Chairperson highlighted
the changes related to NFRA proposed in the Bill through amendments in Section
132 of the Companies Act, 2013 and insertion of 11 new Sections from 132A to
132K, which envisage fundamental structural and functional overhaul of NFRA,
transforming it into a fully autonomous regulator with powers to make regulations,
issue directions, impose penalty, levy fees or other charges. The Hon'ble
Chairperson also drew attention of the witnesses to the `Confidentiality' of the
Proceedings of the Joint Committee as stipulated in Direction 55(1) of the Directions
by Speaker, Lok Sabha.

3. During the discussion, the representatives from NFRA gave their presentation
and put forth their suggestions which, inter-alia, included additional amendments to
Section 132(3B) - Executive Body for discharge of NFRA's functions; Section
132(3C) - powers of Chairperson and Executive Body; Section 132(4)(a) - overriding
powers of NFRA's proceedings to bring more clarity in the statutory framework and
avoid ambiguity and jurisdictional overlap; Section 132(4)(c) - existing principle of
levy of monetary penalty in cases of proved misconduct must be maintained and the
other actions may supplement the monetary penalty; Section 454C - power to do
settlement should be vested with NFRA; Section 132(4A) and Section 439 - to
initiate proceedings under sub-section (a) of Section 132 (4A), there has to be a
provision allowing NFRA to make application to the Special Court, so as to enable
special court to take cognizance of the offense under 132(4A)(a), hence, Section 439
of the Act needs to be amended to include NFRA as an applicant and the
Auditor/Audit Firm as a person/entity who has committed an offense under the Act;

                                                      1030
Section 132A(1) - intimation of registration details by Auditors before appointment;
Section 132A (3) and (4) - penalty for failure to furnish registration details or
incorrect details; Section 132C - power of NFRA to issue directions; Section 132D(1)
- power of Authority to hold inquiry; Section 132D(3) - manner of recovery of various
Penalties; Section 132J - power of Authority to make Regulations; Section 454D -
requirement to deposit certain amount before appeal is entertained, etc.

4. After the presentation, the Committee deliberated upon various points which,
inter-alia, included the following:

         i) likely impact of the proposed reforms on NFRA's effectiveness,
         accountability and regulatory outcomes;
         ii) need for consistency between the broader objective of
         decriminalization and ease of doing business and proposed provision for
         imprisonment upto six months for failing to comply with the orders of NFRA or
         failing to pay the penalty;
         iii) need to strike a balance between provisions of this Bill and the
         Chartered Accountants Act, 1949;
         iv) rationale for requiring auditors and audit firms to obtain a separate
         registration with NFRA;
         v) specific regulatory deficiencies which necessitated this separate
         registration and disciplinary framework under NFRA;
         vi) need to avoid duplication of compliance requirements, increased
         regulatory burden and potential jurisdictional overlap between NFRA and
         ICAI;
         vii) need for the regulator to maintain a clear separation between the
         functions of investigation and adjudication;
         viii) balancing the need for practical domain expertise in the executive body
         with the necessity of maintaining strict independent oversight free from
         industry conflict;
         ix) need to prescribe limitation period for initiation of enquiries by NFRA in
         line with Income Tax Act, 2025 and GST Act, 2017;
         x) need to establish a clear, rule-based framework limiting firm-wide bans
         strictly to exceptional cases, involving systemic collusion;

                                                      1031
         xi) possibility of introducing an annual white-list of highly compliant audit
         firms in order to leverage market-based incentives to drive audit quality, rather
         than relying solely on the threat of punishment;
         xii) delegation by the executive body should be for a specific purpose,
         work, or duration under Section 132(3C); etc.
5. The Committee also sought clarifications on various other issues relating to
the subject and the witnesses responded to some of those queries. The Chairperson
then directed the representatives to furnish written replies to queries, which remained
unanswered during the deliberations, to the Secretariat within seven days.

1. At the outset, the Hon'ble Chairperson welcomed the representatives of
the Department of Financial Services (DFS), the Reserve Bank of India (RBI),
and the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI).
After outlining the objects of the Bill, the Chairperson observed that several
entities covered under its provisions are also subject to regulation by DFS,
RBI, and IRDAI. He accordingly invited the witnesses to share their views on
the consistency of the Bill with existing regulatory frameworks and areas
requiring coordination, and drew their attention to Direction 55(1) of the

                                                      1034
Directions by the Speaker, Lok Sabha, regarding the confidentiality of
Committee proceedings.

2. The representative of DFS informed the Committee that its suggestions,
given after consultation with RBI, had been incorporated in the Bill to the
extent found appropriate, and that the Department concurred with the
amendments. Provisions of the Bill, bearing on banks and financial institutions
were highlighted by the representative inter-alia including designation of IBBI
as the Central Statutory Valuation Authority, the enabling provision for IFSC
companies and LLPs to maintain accounts in foreign currency, automatic
vesting of assets on conversion of trusts into LLPs, enhanced digital
compliance, strengthening of NFRA, and the bar on liquidating companies
pursuing mergers. The Committee was informed that the DFS welcomed
decriminalization of procedural defaults, and suggested extending mandatory
registration of charges to LLPs and barring wilful defaulters from directorships.

3. The representative of RBI stated that RBI concurred with the
amendments and the suggestions made by DFS, and submitted that the
provision permitting IFSC entities to maintain accounts in foreign currency
should be confined to entities regulated by the International Financial Services
Centres Authority (IFSCA).

4. The representative of IRDAI welcomed the decriminalization of
procedural defaults, suggesting periodic review of penalty quantum through
subordinate legislation,. It was also informed that IRDAI welcomed the
increase in the CSR net profit threshold from Rs. 5 crore to Rs. 10 crore. The
Committee was apprised that certain provisions of the Companies Act and the
Insurance Act--such as recognition of stock appreciation rights and ESOPs,
appointment and remuneration of whole-time directors and KMPs, and the `fit
and proper' criteria for directors--are also governed by IRDAI regulations It
was suggested that corresponding carve-outs be explicitly recorded despite
the general primacy of sectoral regulation. IRDAI welcomed statutory
recognition of NFRA as an autonomous body and the simplification of annual
disclosure requirements for directors. Further suggestions included: (i)
reconsidering Section 101(1) to provide 21 days' notice for an Extraordinary
General Meeting in the interest of minority shareholders; and (ii) clarifying
under Section 135(9) that net profit for CSR purposes in insurance companies

                                                      1035
be computed as defined under the Insurance Act, 1938 given differences in
calculation methods.
5. The members sought clarification on the submissions made by the
witnesses. The representatives from the Department of Financial Services
(DFS), the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the Insurance Regulatory and
Development Authority of India (IRDAI) responded to the same. The
Chairperson directed that the written replies on matters requiring further
examination be furnished to the Secretariat within five to seven working days.

                                        MINUTES OF SITTING

        At the outset, the Chairperson welcomed the Members and Witnesses to
the Committee Sitting convened for Briefing/Presentation by the representatives
of the Ministry of Finance (Department of Revenue), the Central Board of Direct
Taxes (CBDT) and the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC). In
his opening remarks, the Chairperson highlighted the significance of the Bill,
especially with respect to its impact on corporate governance, compliance
frameworks, and the broader `Ease of Doing Business' initiative, and drew the

                                                      1038
attention of the Witnesses to the confidentiality of the proceedings of the Joint
Committee as stipulated in Direction 55(1) of the Directions by the Speaker, Lok
Sabha.

2. Secretary (Revenue), while welcoming the positive features of the Bill --
namely compliance relief for one-person, small, start-up and producer
companies, simplified voluntary strike-off, AGMs/EGMs via video-conferencing,
and a strengthened National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA) -- informed
the Committee that the Bill had not come to the Department of Revenue for inter-
ministerial consultation. He flagged four specific concerns for the Committee's
consideration: recovery provisions in the amended Bill; the provision permitting
IFSC companies and LLPs to maintain books in foreign currency; exemption of
certain classes of companies from audit; and provisions relating to Fast-Track
Merger and Demerger.

3. During the deliberations that followed, the Committee sought clarifications
on the binding nature of valuations conducted by IBBI, the newly designated
Central Statutory Valuation Authority, for mergers, amalgamations, and share
swaps/buybacks for the purposes of the Income-tax Act, vis-à-vis independent
valuation by the Income Tax Department; the safeguards being developed to
identify ultimate beneficial ownership in new IFSC LLPs, including measures to
prevent the conversion of tax-exempt trusts into profit-oriented LLPs for tax
planning or avoidance and the consistency of such conversions with the IBC and
public policy; the safeguards proposed against misuse of arrest and detention
powers by Recovery Officers; along with pre-exit tax clearance or PAN-linkage
measures to prevent accelerated strike-off or summary liquidation from defeating
pending tax assessments; the desirability of maintaining uniform corporate
governance and compliance norms from the inception of a company rather than
varying them by size or stage of growth; the nature of the Registrar's power to
refuse registration when `not satisfied', including the requirement to record
reasons; and the tax implications of automatic vesting of trust property in an LLP
at less than market value under the Income-tax Act, noting that the Bill is silent on
the issue.

                                                      1039
4. The witnesses responded to the issues raised by the Members. The
Chairperson directed that the written replies on matters requiring further
examination be furnished to the Secretariat within five to seven working days.

2. At the outset, the Hon'ble Chairperson welcomed the representatives of the
Bharat Web3 Association and India Blockchain Forum and informed that the Sitting
had been called for deliberations on various provisions of the Corporate Laws
(Amendment) Bill, 2026. Further, the Chairperson highlighted that Bharat Web3
Association and India Blockchain Forum represent an emerging Sector that is
expected to play an important role in India's digital economy, as these technologies
are increasingly finding applications in corporate governance, tokenization of real-
world assets, digital identity, supply-chain management, audit trails, smart contracts,
compliance automation and secure record-keeping. The Hon'ble Chairperson also
drew attention of the witnesses to the `Confidentiality' of the proceedings of the Joint
Committee as stipulated in Direction 55(1) of the Directions by Speaker, Lok Sabha.

3. During the discussion, the representatives from Bharat Web3 Association
gave their presentation and put forth their suggestions which, inter-alia, included
information about regulatory journey of VDAs in India; challenges regarding digital
jurisdiction; global approaches to VDAs; recognition of digital assets as a distinct
property class - Section 2; mandatory registration of foreign digital platform entities -
Section 379A; inclusion of token incentive schemes - Section 62(1)(b); enablement
of DLT for shareholder voting and corporate records - Section 108 and 120;
introduction of statutory proof-of-reserves requirement - Section 128, etc.

4. Thereafter, a presentation was also given by a representative from India
Blockchain Forum which, inter-alia, highlighted the use cases of VDAs and
blockchain technology in the Indian economy; economic case for regulating VDA and
blockchain companies; global benchmarking - EU (MiCA), UAE (VARA) and
Singapore (MAS); IFSCA's Gift City sandbox and why it should lead over NFRA for
this sector; need for creation of a Digital/Virtual Asset Valuation Standard; need to

                                                      1045
publish a public, machine-readable registry of Specified IFSC LLPs/companies
cross-referenced with the FIU-IND VDASP registry; extension of filing relaxations
under LLP Act (Section 23 and 25) explicitly to LLP-SPVs holding tokenized/digital
fund assets; need for clarification regarding treatment of stablecoin-denominated
LLP/company contributions under Section 32 of LLP Act and Section 43A of
Companies Act, etc.

5. After the presentations, the Committee deliberated upon various points which,
inter-alia, included the following:

    i) issues related to establishment of beneficial ownership and control by the
         regulators, given the pseudonymous nature of many blockchain transactions;
         ii) challenges against mandating blockchain-based corporate filings or
         disclosures for certain categories of companies;
         iii) in a blockchain ecosystem involving decentralized actors, who should
         bear legal responsibility when compliance failures occur, the developers,
         validators, token holders, promoters or platform operators;
         iv) safeguards for addressing risks arising from tokenized investment
         products and digital asset-linked corporate structures;
         v) likely impact of amendment to Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013
         on concerned companies/entities/service providers in Indian Blockchain
         Industry;
         vi) need for governance mechanisms to manage cyber security risks
         arising out of blockchain systems;
         vii) need to address conflicts between domestic regulatory requirements
         and governance protocols embedded in global blockchain networks, etc.

6. The Committee also sought clarifications on various other issues relating to

         At the outset, the Chairperson welcomed the Joint Treasurer, Laghu Udyog

company', decriminalises certain procedural defaults, and provides relaxations in
statutory audit, meeting and Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) requirements. He
also drew the attention of the Witnesses to the 'Confidentiality' of the Proceedings of
the Joint Committee as stipulated in Direction 55(1) of the Directions by Speaker, Lok
Sabha.

2. The representative of Laghu Udyog Bharati, informed the Committee about
the work of the organisation. He welcomed the revised small-company threshold of
Rs. 20 crore and the increase in the CSR net-profit threshold to Rs. 10 crore, while
seeking further relaxations, including dispensing with the mandatory professional
declaration at incorporation, exempting one-person and dormant companies from
mandatory website maintenance, retaining a physical option for service of notices,
exempting small companies from NFRA registration, easing the three-yearly
mandatory rotation of auditors, permitting tax and statutory audits to be combined,
capping penalties in proportion to paid-up capital, keeping physical AGMs optional
rather than mandatory, and recognising local effluent-treatment and industrial-
infrastructure spend as permissible CSR expenditure.

3. The representatives of NSIC, stated that the Corporation, as the sole Central
Public Sector Enterprise dedicated to the MSME sector, welcomed the revised paid-
up capital and turnover thresholds proposed for small companies, and suggested
that the definitions of a 'small company' under the Companies Act and of an LLP be
aligned with the thresholds prescribed under the MSMED Act, 2006. It was also
proposed that the requirement to maintain a website and email address be made
advisory rather than mandatory for micro enterprises, that greater flexibility be
allowed in the mode of service of documents, and that a separate, lower fee and
penalty structure be prescribed for small companies.

                                                      1052
4. During the subsequent deliberations, the Committee raised several concerns
which, inter-alia, included the apparent tension between seeking higher compliance
thresholds while simultaneously seeking exemption from professional declarations
and NFRA oversight, and whether corresponding regulatory safeguards ought to
accompany any such relaxation; whether extensive exemptions from statutory audit
and financial reporting could reduce transparency, increase credit risk for public
sector lenders, or weaken accountability to minority shareholders; whether greater
reliance on electronic and hybrid meetings could disadvantage shareholders in rural
areas without reliable internet connectivity; whether raising LLP thresholds could
expose the MSME ecosystem to greater third-party credit risk; and whether easing
CSR compliance could reduce funding available for local grassroots and skilling
initiatives.
5. The Committee also sought clarifications on various other issues relating to
the subject, including whether a compliance certificate from a practising professional
could meaningfully substitute full statutory audit for small companies, whether a
single annual board meeting would be adequate for family-run companies with
external investors, and whether NSIC possessed compliance-cost data that could
assist the Committee in calibrating the proposed thresholds. The Chairperson then
directed the Witnesses to furnish written replies to queries, which remained
unanswered during the deliberations, to the Secretariat within three days.

                                    The witnesses then withdrew.
                     A copy of the verbatim proceedings is placed on record.

    2. At the outset, the Chairperson welcomed the Members and Witnesses to the
    Committee Sitting convened to have briefing by the representatives of the National
    Law School of India University (Bangaluru), National Law University (Delhi), and
    Nalsar University of Law (Hyderabad). Further, the Chairperson in his opening
    remarks drew attention of the Witnesses to the scope and ambit of the Bill and to
    the `Confidentiality' of the Proceedings of the Joint Committee as stipulated in
    Direction 55(1) of the Directions by Speaker,LokSabha.

    3. Thereafter, the representatives of National Law School briefly presented their
    views on the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026, emphasizing on removal of
    the reference to the IBC from Sections 230(1) and 230(6); rationale behind
    requirement of three-year cooling-off period for the auditors u/s 144; definition of
    small companies and exclusion of holding and subsidiary companies therefrom;
    need for valuation-fairness check under proposed section 43A; inclusion of
    guidance criteria under clause 43(d) to avoid excessive delegation of legislative

                                                          1055
function; provision of guidance criteria for reducing the directorship cap under
clause 55, etc.

4. Afterwards, the representative of National Law University briefly presented
their views on Bill and interalia apprised the Committee about the subjection of
formation and incorporation of LLPs to higher compliance requirement; definition
of the Specified IFSC LLP under Section 2(iii) of the Bill; the need for adopting dual
approach of presenting the books of account in indian rupee for domestic
regulatory and tax compliances, failure in intimation of registration details of
auditors and filing of returns and discretion in penalty imposition; the legislative
intent and rationale behind the 75% majority approval for scheme of mergers u/sec
233 etc. Then, the representative from Nalsar University, briefed the Committee on
various provisions of the Bill and put forth their suggestions thereon. Some of them
are, proposed flexibility u/sec 2(41) in alignment of financial year and its
consequences across tax, accounting and regulatory regimes; excessive fee
levying power of NFRA u/sec 132; exclusion of companies having net profits of 5
crores to 10 crores from the applicability of CSR U/sec 135 and its adverse impact
on the society as a whole etc.

5. After the presentation, the Committee, deliberated inter-alia upon the following
points:

(i) Co-existence of constitutional morality and political philosophies pertaining to
CSR in a democracy;

(ii) Consequences of conferring excessive rule-making powers on the Executive and
need of clear regulatory guidelines governing exercise of delegated power without
discretionary considerations;

(iii) Ease and speed of doing business vis-vis dual intimation of appointment of
auditors to NFRA and RoC;

(iv) Impact of new definition of small companies on private investments.

(v) Excessive delegation of powers to NFRA for levying fee;

(vi) Precautions and safeguards to ensure that ease of doing business does not
create a vulnerable ecosystem leading to ease of defrauding;

(vii) Encumbrances and benefits of Trusts under Indian Trusts Act and operational
safeguards and challenges in the conversion process, appropriateness of entrusting
executive the power to permit and oversee these conversions of Trusts;

(vii) Areas of jurisdictional overlap between the existing powers of NCLT and
adjudication mechanism proposed in this Bill;

(viii) Expansion of the National Financial Reporting Authority's enforcement powers
over auditors and audit firms and jurisdictional overlap with ICAI's disciplinary
authority over individual chartered accountants, and primacy in overlapping cases;

                                                      1056
(ix) Constitutionally sustainable basis for differential corporate governance
standards for companies incorporated within International Financial Services
Centres (IFSCs) from mainland companies;

(x) threshold raise for small companies and risk creating a class of mid-sized
companies escaping governance safeguards disproportionate to their actual
economic footprint etc..

6. The Committee also sought clarifications on various other issues relating to the
subject and the witnesses responded to some of those queries. The Chairperson
then directed the representatives to furnish written replies to the remaining points,
which could not be readily replied by them during the discussion to the Secretariat
within three days.

of the Committee and the representatives of the Ministry of Corporate Affairs to the
sitting convened for the oral evidence of the Ministry officials in connection with the
clause-by-clause examination of the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026.

3. After the introductory remarks, which highlighted the Committee's thorough
engagement with the Bill, the Hon'ble Chairperson underscored the extensive
deliberations undertaken over several weeks and the large number of suggestions
received from diverse stakeholders. Emphasis was placed on the consultative
process adopted by the Committee, reflecting its inclusive approach to examination
of the Bill. The Chairperson then drew the attention of the witnesses to Direction
55(1) of the Directions by the Speaker regarding confidentiality of Committee
proceedings.

4. The Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs, in her opening remarks,
submitted that the Ministry had made concerted efforts to incorporate stakeholder
suggestions received across the 107 clauses under examination in the Bill. The
Committee were informed that suggestions covering about 41 sections had been
accepted, while those requiring further consultation were kept open and marked as
`under examination' for consideration after the day's discussion.

                                                      1061
5. Thereafter, the Bill was discussed clause by clause. The Ministry made a
clause-wise presentation on the proposed amendments to the LLP Act (Clauses 1-
17) inter-alia covering the introduction of definitions of IFSC and permitted foreign
currency; making professional certification of incorporation documents optional;
permitting use of the IFSC acronym in LLP names; relaxation of filing timelines for
IFSC/SEBI-regulated AIF LLPs; introduction of valuation requirements under the new
Section 33A with corresponding changes to Section 247 of the Companies Act;
ensuring confidentiality of contributor details; and the mechanism under Section 57A
and the Fifth Schedule for conversion of specified AIF trusts into LLPs.
5.1 Thereafter, the presentation proceeded to the amendments to the Companies
Act, 2013, commencing Clause 18 which inter-alia covers correction of nomenclature
to "Cost Accountant," revision of small company thresholds for paid-up capital and
turnover, introduction of flexibility in financial year conversion beyond foreign
subsidiaries to commercial considerations, definition of Regional Director. The
Committee were informed that in Clause 19, on penalties, ROC discretion is being
removed, with penalties system-calculated through the e-adjudication portal. It was
further informed that mandatory declarations are being made optional on LLP
incorporation.
6. The Ministry also acknowledged concerns on excessive delegation. It was
submitted that a list of delegated areas has been prepared and would be shared.
7. During the course of the presentation, Members sought clarifications on
certain clauses of the Bill. The representatives of the Ministry responded to the
queries, providing explanations and assurances where required.

2. At the outset, the Hon'ble Chairperson welcomed the Members to the Twenty-
Fourth Sitting of the Joint Committee on the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026
convened for internal deliberations on the Bill. The Hon'ble Chairperson informed the

                                                      1070
Committee that after extensive deliberations and a wide-ranging consultative process
with various stakeholders, the Committee had concluded the examination of the Bill
by having a clause-by-clause discussion with the representatives of the Ministry of
Corporate Affairs. The Ministry had explained the rationale for the proposed
provisions and responded to the concerns and suggestions raised by the Members.
It was further informed that while the Ministry had accepted a number of suggestions
made by the Committee, certain issues had been kept pending for further
deliberation until additional information and clarifications are received from the
Ministry. The Hon'ble Chairperson stated that the Ministry had since furnished notes
on the issues kept pending for further deliberation for the consideration of the
Committee and requested the Hon'ble Members to deliberate upon those issues and
offer their considered views so as to enable the Secretariat to finalise the Draft
Report for consideration and adoption by the Committee. The Hon'ble Chairperson
further requested the Hon'ble Members to indicate whether there were any other
issues or provisions of the Bill which, in their considered view, merited further
deliberation or recommendation by the Committee.

3. Thereafter, the Committee, inter alia, discussed on issue viz. Delegation of
legislative powers under the Bill, Framework for conversion of Alternative Investment
Fund (AIF) trusts into Limited Liability Partnerships, Assessment of Directors on the
basis of the 'fit and proper' criteria, Enhancement of the threshold for exemption of
certain companies from statutory audit, Provisions relating to Corporate Social
Responsibility (CSR), Proposal relating to buy-back of securities, issues related to
NCLT, Proposal relating to registration of charges, Provisions relating to mandatory
official e-mail addresses and websites for companies, Role of Registrar of
Companies, Ease of Doing Business, Composition of National Financial Reporting
Authority (NFRA), Notice period for calling Extraordinary General Meeting (EGM)
and Annual General Meeting (AGM), Cooling off Period for Auditors, etc.

4. At the end, the Hon'ble Chairperson thanked the Members for their valuable
suggestions and constructive deliberations on the various issues arising out of the
examination of the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026. The Hon'ble
Chairperson stated that the views expressed by the Members would be duly taken
into consideration while finalising the Draft Report of the Committee. The Hon'ble

                                                      1071
Chairperson further informed the Members that the Secretariat would incorporate the
decisions taken by the Committee during the day's deliberations and circulate the
Draft Report to all the Members for their consideration. The Hon'ble Chairperson also
requested the Hon'ble Members to furnish any further suggestions or comments, if
any, in writing within two days so that the same could be appropriately considered
while finalising the Draft Report.

                                  The Committee then adjourned.

              17. After the Fourth Schedule to the principal Act, the following Schedule shall be
              inserted, namely:--

                                               `THE FIFTH SCHEDULE

                                                     (See section 57A)

                    CONVERSION FROM SPECIFIED TRUST INTO LIMITED LIABILITY PARTNERSHIP

              1. Interpretation.--In this Schedule, unless the context otherwise requires,--

              (a) "convert", in relation to a specified trust converting into a limited liability
              partnership, means a transfer of the property, assets, interests, rights, privileges,
              liabilities, obligations and the undertaking of the specified trust to the limited
              liability partnership in accordance with this Schedule;

              (b) "investor" means an investor to the funds of the specified trust in accordance
              with the relevant regulations made by the Securities and Exchange Board of India,
              or by the International Financial Services Centres Authority, as the case may be;
              [***]

              (ba) "manager" means a manager as defined under the Securities and
              Exchange Board of India (Alternative Investment Funds) Regulations, 2012
              made under the Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992 and
              includes fund manager or fund management entity as defined under the
              International Financial Services Centres Authority (Fund Management)
              Regulations, 2025 made under the International Financial Services Centres
              Authority Act, 2019;

              (c) "specified trust" shall have the meaning assigned to it in the Explanation to
              section 57A.

              2. Conversion from specified trust into limited liability partnership.--(1) A
              specified trust may convert into a limited liability partnership by complying with
              the requirements as to the conversion set out in this Schedule.

              (2) Upon such conversion, the trustees, investors and managers of the specified
              trust shall be bound by the provisions of this Schedule that are applicable to them.

              (2A) Notwithstanding anything contained in this Schedule, where a specified
              trust operates or maintains multiple schemes, or such other structure which is

                                                       1090
not already covered under this Schedule, a framework may be provided for
conversion of such trust into a limited liability partnership, subject to such
conditions, and procedure, as may be prescribed.

(2B) The Central Government may, in consultation and coordination with the
Ministries, Departments and regulatory authorities concerned, notify a
comprehensive framework to facilitate the conversion of specified trusts into
limited liability partnerships, including provisions relating to taxation, capital
gains, stamp duty, transfer and vesting of assets and liabilities, filing and
compliance requirements, continuation of rights and obligations, and other
consequential or incidental matters arising from such conversion.

(2C) The Central Government may also undertake or recommend suitable
amendments to the relevant laws, wherever necessary, to ensure a smooth and
seamless implementation of such conversion.

3. Eligibility for conversion.--A specified trust may apply to convert into a
limited liability partnership in accordance with this Schedule, [***] only if the
Securities and Exchange Board of India, or the International Financial
Services Centres Authority, as the case may be, has given its no objection to
such conversion.

4. Statements to be filed.--A specified trust may apply to convert into a limited
liability partnership by filing with the Registrar,--

(a) a statement by [***] the applicant duly authorised by the investors
representing not less than three-fourth in value of the investments in the
specified trust in such form and manner and accompanied by such fee, as may be
prescribed, containing the following particulars, namely:--

(i) the name and registration number, if applicable, of the specified trust;

(ii) the date on which the specified trust was established under the Indian Trusts
Act, 1882 (2 of 1882) or under a Central Act or State Act;

(iia) a copy of the no objection referred to in paragraph 3;

(iii) the date [***] from which the specified trust [***] has been registered and
regulated by [***] the Securities and Exchange Board of India, or by the
International Financial Services Centres Authority, as the case may be, in terms of
the relevant regulations issued in this regard; and

(iv) the consent of three-fourths of the investors in value of the trust; and

(b) the incorporation document and statement referred to in section 11.

5. Registration of conversion.-- On receiving the documents referred to in
paragraph 4, the Registrar shall, subject to the provisions of this Act, register the
documents and issue a certificate of registration in such form, as the Registrar may
determine, stating that the limited liability partnership is, on and from the date
specified in the certificate, registered under this Act:

Provided that the limited liability partnership shall, within fifteen days of the date
of registration, inform, the concerned authority with which specified trust was
established under the provisions of the Indian Trusts Act, 1882 (2 of 1882) or
under a Central Act or State Act, about the conversion and of the particulars of the
limited liability partnership in such form and manner, as may be prescribed.

6. Registrar may refuse to register.--(1) Nothing in this Schedule shall be
construed as to require the Registrar to register any limited liability partnership, if
he is not satisfied with the particulars or other information furnished under the
provisions of this Act:

Provided that an appeal may be made before the Tribunal in case of refusal of

                                         1091
registration by the Registrar.

(2) The Registrar may, in any particular case, require the documents referred to in
paragraph 4 to be verified in such manner, as he considers fit.

7. Effect of registration.--On and from the date of registration specified in the
certificate of registration issued under paragraph 5,--

(a) there shall be a limited liability partnership by the name specified in the
certificate of registration registered under this Act;

(b) all tangible (movable and immovable) property as well as intangible property
vested in the specified trust, all assets, interests, rights, privileges, liabilities,
obligations relating to the specified trust and the whole of the undertaking of the
specified trust shall be transferred to and shall vest in the limited liability
partnership without further assurance, act or deed; and

(c) the specified trust shall be deemed to be dissolved.

8. Registration in relation to property.--If any property to which
sub-paragraph (b) of paragraph 7 applies is registered with any authority, the
limited liability partnership shall, as soon as practicable after the date of
registration, take all necessary steps as required by the relevant authority to notify
the authority of the conversion and of the particulars of the limited liability
partnership in such medium and form, as the authority may specify.

9. Pending proceedings.--All proceedings by or against the specified trust or its
trustee, on behalf of the specified trust, which are pending in any Court or
Tribunal or before any authority on the date of registration may be continued,
completed and enforced by or against the limited liability partnership.

10. Continuance of conviction, ruling, order or judgment.--Any conviction,
ruling, order or judgment of any Court, Tribunal, or other authority, in favour of or
against the specified trust, or its trustees, or its managers acting on behalf of the
specified trust may be enforced by or against the limited liability partnership.

11. Existing agreements.--Every agreement, to which the specified trust was a
party immediately before the date of registration, whether or not of such nature
that the rights and liabilities thereunder could be assigned, shall have effect as
from that date, as if--

(a) the limited liability partnership were a party to such an agreement instead of
the specified trust; and

(b) for any reference to the specified trust, there were substituted in respect of
anything to be done on or after the date of registration a reference to the limited
liability partnership.

12. Existing contracts, etc.--All deeds, contracts, schemes, bonds, agreements,
applications, instruments and arrangements, subsisting immediately before the
date of registration relating to the specified trust or to which the specified trust is a
party, shall continue in force on and after that date as if they relate to the limited
liability partnership and shall be enforceable by or against the limited liability
partnership, as if the limited liability partnership were named therein or were a
party thereto instead of the specified trust.

13. Continuance of employment.--Every contract of employment to which
paragraph 11 or paragraph 12 applies, shall continue to be in force on or after the
date of registration, as if the limited liability partnership were the employer
thereunder instead of the specified trust.

[***]

                                         1092
Amendment of  15. Application of paragraphs 7 to [***] 13.--The provisions of paragraphs 7 to            18 of 2013.
section 2.    [***] 13 (both inclusive) shall apply to any approval, permit or licence issued to
              the specified trust under any other [***] law, which is in force immediately before
              the date of registration of the limited liability partnership, subject to the provisions
              of such other [***] law under which such approval, permit or licence has been
              issued.

              16. Partner liable for liabilities and obligations of specified trust before
              conversion.--(1) Notwithstanding anything in paragraphs 7 to [***] 13, every
              trustee and manager of a specified trust that has converted into a limited liability
              partnership, shall continue to be personally liable (jointly and severally with the
              limited liability partnership) for the liabilities and obligations of the specified trust
              which were incurred prior to the conversion or which arose from any contract
              entered into prior to the conversion.

              (2) If any such trustee or manager discharges any liability or obligation referred
              to in sub-paragraph (1), he shall be entitled (subject to any agreement with the
              limited liability partnership to the contrary) to be fully indemnified by the limited
              liability partnership in respect of such liability or obligation.

              17. Notice of conversion in correspondence.--(1) The limited liability partnership
              shall ensure that for a period of twelve months commencing not later than fourteen
              days after the date of registration, every official correspondence of the limited
              liability partnership bears the following, namely:--

              (a) a statement that it was, as from the date of registration, converted from a
              specified trust into a limited liability partnership; and

              (b) the name and registration number, if applicable, of the specified trust, from
              which it was converted.

              (2) Any limited liability partnership which contravenes the provisions of sub-
              paragraph (1) shall be punishable with fine which shall not be less than ten
              thousand rupees but which may extend to one lakh rupees and with a further fine
              which shall not be less than fifty rupees but which may extend to five hundred
              rupees for every day after the first day after which the default continues.'.

                  132D. (1) The National Financial Reporting Authority may, after holding inquiry,

                  in such manner as may be prescribed and after giving a reasonable opportunity of

                  being heard, impose such penalty under  sub-section (4) of section 132A

                  or sub-section (2) of section 132C, as it may consider appropriate.

                  (2) While holding an inquiry, the National Financial Reporting Authority shall
                  have power to summon and enforce the attendance of any person acquainted with
                  the facts and circumstances of the case to give evidence and examine them on
                  oath or to produce any document, which in the opinion of the said Authority, may
                  be useful for or relevant to the subject matter of the inquiry and if, on such inquiry,
                  it is satisfied that the person has failed to comply with the provisions of any of the
                  sections specified in sub-section (1), it may impose such penalty as it considers
                  appropriate in accordance with the provisions of any of those sections.

                  (3) The amount of any penalty imposed under section 132 and sub-section (3) of
                  section 132A and this section, if not paid, may be recovered by the National
                  Financial Reporting Authority in accordance with section 454B [***].

                  (4) All sums realised by way of penalties under this section shall be credited to the
                  Consolidated Fund of India.

                  (5) Any person aggrieved by an order of the National Financial Reporting
                  Authority under this section may prefer an appeal before the Appellate Tribunal
                  within a period of forty-five days from the date on which a copy of the order of the
                  said Authority is made available, in such manner and on payment of such fee, as
                  may be prescribed.

                 132H. (1) If at any time, the Central Government is of the opinion--

                 (a) that on account of grave emergency, the National Financial Reporting
                 Authority is unable to discharge the functions and duties imposed on it by or under
                 the provisions of this Act; or

                 (b) that the National Financial Reporting Authority has persistently not complied
                 with any direction given by the Central Government under this Act or in the
                 discharge of the functions and duties imposed on it by or under the provisions of
                 this Act, and as a result of such non-compliance, the financial position or the
                 administration of such Authority has deteriorated; or

                 (c) that circumstances exist which render it necessary in the public interest so to
                 do,

                 the Central Government may, by notification, supersede the National Financial
                 Reporting Authority for such period, not exceeding six months, as may be
                 specified in the notification.

                 (2) Upon the publication of a notification under sub-section (1) superseding the
                 National Financial Reporting Authority,--

                 (a) the Chairperson and all the members shall, as from the date of supersession,
                 vacate their offices as such;

                 (b) all the powers, functions and duties which may, by or under the provisions of
                 this Act, be exercised or discharged by or on behalf of the National Financial
                 Reporting Authority shall, until the said Authority is reconstituted under sub-
                 section (3), be exercised and discharged by such person or persons as the Central
                 Government may direct; and

                 (c) all properties owned or controlled by the National Financial Reporting
                 Authority shall, until the said Authority is reconstituted under sub-section (3), vest
                 in the Central Government.

                 (3) On the expiration of the period of supersession specified in the notification
                 issued under sub-section (1), the Central Government may reconstitute the
                 National Financial Reporting Authority by a fresh appointment, and in such case,
                 any person or persons who vacated their offices under clause (a) of the said
                 sub-section, shall not be deemed disqualified for appointment:

                 Provided that the Central Government may, at any time, before the expiration of

                                                          1103
                 the period of supersession, take action under this sub-section.

                 (4) The Central Government shall cause a notification issued under  sub-

                 section (1) and a full report of any action taken under this section and the

                 circumstances leading to such action to be laid before each House of Parliament at

                 the earliest.

                  and impact of contraventions, agree to the proposal for settlement, on payment of
                  such sum by the applicant or on such other terms and manner of implementation of
                  settlement and monitoring, as may be prescribed.

                  (6) If the Specified Authority is of the opinion that the settlement offered is not
                  appropriate in the circumstances, or if the Specified Authority and applicant
                  concerned do not reach an agreement on the terms of the settlement within such
                  time as may be prescribed, it shall by an order reject the application for settlement
                  and the proceedings initiated against the applicant shall be continued.

                  (7) The settlement proceedings under this section shall be conducted in such
                  manner as may be prescribed.

                  (8) No appeal shall lie against any order passed by the Specified Authority under
                  this section.

                  (9) All settlement amounts realised under this Act shall be credited to the
                  Consolidated Fund of India.

                  454D. No appeal by a person, who is required to pay any penalty imposed [***]
                  in terms of an order of--

                  (a) the National Financial Reporting Authority under section 132 or section 132D;
                  or

                  (b) the Valuation Authority under section 247; or

                  (c) the adjudicating officer under section 454,

                  shall be entertained by the Appellate Tribunal or Regional Director or the
                  Appellate Authority referred to in sub-section (5) of section 454, as the case may
                  be, unless the appellant has deposited [***] five per cent. of that amount in such
                  [***] manner as may be prescribed [***].'.

              106. After section 466 of the principal Act, the following section shall be inserted,
              namely:--

              "466A. The Central Government may issue directions or guidelines or circulars,
              subject to such conditions, as may be necessary, for the following purposes,
              namely:--

              (a) clarifying the meaning or intent of any rule; and

              (b) laying down any procedural requirement ancillary to any rule:

              Provided that the Central Government shall hold consultation with expert bodies
              or individuals in such manner, as may be prescribed, before issuing directions or
              guidelines or circulars, under this section:

              Provided further that where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is
              necessary or expedient in the public interest that certain directions or guidelines or
              circulars are required to be made urgently for the purposes of effective
              implementation of the concerned rule, it may issue such directions or guidelines or
              circulars, without consulting the expert bodies or individuals and record the
              reasons for doing so in writing.

              Explanation.--The directions or guidelines or circulars issued under this section
              shall be in addition to and not in derogation of any rule made under
              section 469 and in case of any conflict, the rule shall prevail.".
              107. In section 469 of the principal Act, for sub-section (3), the following sub-
              section shall be substituted, namely:--
              "(3) Any rule made under sub-section (1) may provide that in case of
              contravention thereof, the company, every officer of the company who is in
              default or any other person, shall be liable to a penalty of an amount, as may be
              prescribed, which shall not be more than five lakh rupees, and in case of
              continuing default, with a further penalty of such amount, as may be prescribed,
              which shall not be more than five thousand rupees for every day during which
              such default continues.".
